- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron neural network compared with linear regression.
- **Data:** All-India rainfall series and preceding predictors such as ENSO-related indices over many decades.
- **Main result:** The neural network improves forecast skill over linear regression in independent tests.
- **Open work:** Adding predictors and ensembles of networks to reduce variance.
- **Issues:** Short record risks overfitting; skill estimates depend on validation design.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Neural network forecasts of the tropical Pacific sea surface temperatures](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2006.01.004)
Wu et al. (2006), *Neural Networks*. 119 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts tropical Pacific sea surface temperatures (ENSO) with nonlinear neural network models.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward neural networks (MLPs) in ensembles, compared with linear regression.
- **Data:** Not reported (no abstract); predictors from tropical Pacific sea level pressure and SST fields.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Not reported.
- **Issues:** No abstract; lead times, skill and verification period could not be verified.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Forecasting ENSO Events: A Neural Network–Extended EOF Approach.](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(1998)011<0029:feeann>2.0.co;2)
Tangang et al. (1998), *Journal of Climate*. 118 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts ENSO by predicting Niño-region sea surface temperature anomalies at seasonal leads with compact predictors.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward neural network (multilayer perceptron) with inputs from extended empirical orthogonal functions (EEOFs) of tropical Pacific sea level pressure and SST fields.
- **Data:** Observed tropical Pacific sea level pressure and SST anomaly fields, with Niño 3.4 SST anomalies as targets; hindcasts over several decades.
- **Main result:** EEOF-based inputs reduce network size and give useful Niño 3.4 forecast skill at leads up to about a year, competitive with other ENSO models of the time.
- **Open work:** Adding subsurface ocean information and ensemble approaches to stabilise and extend skill.
- **Issues:** Short training record relative to number of ENSO events, risk of overfitting and spring predictability barrier; no uncertainty estimates.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Development of an artificial neural network based multi-model ensemble to estimate the northeast monsoon rainfall over south peninsular India: an application of extreme learning machine](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-013-1942-2)
Acharya et al. (2014), *Climate Dynamics*. 118 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves seasonal prediction of northeast monsoon rainfall over south peninsular India by combining multiple climate models.
- **Architecture:** Extreme learning machine (single-hidden-layer neural network) used to build a multi-model ensemble from general circulation model hindcasts.
- **Data:** Hindcasts of several general circulation models and observed northeast monsoon rainfall over south peninsular India; specific models and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The ELM-based multi-model ensemble is reported to outperform individual models and simple ensemble averages.
- **Open work:** Application to other seasons and regions and to probabilistic seasonal forecasts.
- **Issues:** Short hindcast records limit training and verification; the ensemble inherits biases of the member models.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Forecasting the equatorial Pacific sea surface temperatures by neural network models](https://doi.org/10.1007/s003820050156)
Tangang et al. (1997), *Climate Dynamics*. 115 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts equatorial Pacific SST anomalies (Niño regions) at seasonal leads to predict ENSO.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward neural network (multilayer perceptron) using principal components of tropical Pacific wind stress and SST as predictors.
- **Data:** Observed tropical Pacific wind stress and SST anomaly fields with Niño region SST anomaly targets over several decades.
- **Main result:** Neural networks achieve useful Niño SST forecast skill at leads of several months to about a year, with wind stress predictors important at longer leads.
- **Open work:** Improving predictors (e.g. sea level pressure, heat content) and reducing network overfitting.
- **Issues:** Few ENSO events for training, possible overfitting and sensitivity to initial weights; no probabilistic output.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Nonlinear Principal Component Analysis: Tropical Indo–Pacific Sea Surface Temperature and Sea Level Pressure](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(2001)013<0219:npcati>2.0.co;2)
Monahan (2001), *Journal of Climate*. 113 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extracts non-linear modes of tropical Indo-Pacific SST and sea level pressure variability, including ENSO asymmetry.
- **Architecture:** Non-linear principal component analysis (NLPCA) with an autoassociative neural network.
- **Data:** Observed tropical Indo-Pacific sea surface temperature and sea level pressure analyses.
- **Main result:** The leading non-linear mode captures ENSO asymmetry between El Nino and La Nina better than linear PCA.
- **Open work:** Extending to other climate modes and coupled analysis.
- **Issues:** Risk of overfitting in NLPCA; short observational record.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [On the relationship between large-scale climate modes and regional synoptic patterns that drive Victorian rainfall](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-13-467-2009)
Verdon-Kidd et al. (2008), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 110 citations.

- **Main goal:** Links large-scale climate modes to regional synoptic patterns that drive rainfall in Victoria, Australia, to improve seasonal to decadal rainfall prediction.
- **Architecture:** Self-organizing maps (SOM) classify regional synoptic patterns into 20 types; rainfall is attributed to types and type frequencies are related to climate modes.
- **Data:** Regional synoptic fields (mean sea level pressure type) and rainfall at nine Victorian stations, with ENSO, IOD, SAM and IPO indices.
- **Main result:** Twenty synoptic types separate wet and dry conditions; ENSO, IOD and SAM phases shift wet/dry type frequency interannually, and the IPO modulates it on multidecadal scales.
- **Open work:** Use the type-mode links for seasonal and decadal rainfall forecasting and as a benchmark to evaluate GCMs.
- **Issues:** Descriptive classification without an operational forecast test; choice of 20 nodes and domain is subjective.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction of Indian summer monsoon rainfall using Niño indices: A neural network approach](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2011.06.013)
Shukla et al. (2011), *Atmospheric Research*. 109 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts Indian summer monsoon rainfall from ENSO-related Niño indices.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (ANN) using Niño indices as predictors.
- **Data:** Niño sea surface temperature indices and observed Indian summer monsoon rainfall; periods not reported here (no abstract available).
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; the title implies Niño indices provide useful neural network predictions of monsoon rainfall.
- **Open work:** Adding other predictors such as Indian Ocean Dipole indices and testing in independent periods.
- **Issues:** Short seasonal record limits training data and raises overfitting risk; ENSO-monsoon relation is nonstationary.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Detecting decadal changes in ENSO using neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-006-0173-1)
Leloup et al. (2006), *Climate Dynamics*. 103 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects decadal changes in ENSO patterns and evolution in the tropical Pacific.
- **Architecture:** Self-organizing map (SOM) neural network classification of tropical Pacific SST anomaly patterns.
- **Data:** Observed tropical Pacific sea surface temperature anomalies over several decades; product not reported here.
- **Main result:** The SOM reveals changes in ENSO spatial patterns and evolution across decades, notably around the late-1970s climate shift.
- **Open work:** Evaluate ENSO changes in climate models with the same approach.
- **Issues:** Limited number of ENSO events per decade restricts statistical significance.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Seasonal rainfall forecasting by adaptive network-based fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) using large scale climate signals](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-015-2755-2)
Mekanik et al. (2016), *Climate Dynamics*. 103 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts seasonal rainfall months ahead using large-scale climate drivers to support water resources planning.
- **Architecture:** Adaptive network-based fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), a neuro-fuzzy model, using lagged climate indices as inputs, compared with regression.
- **Data:** Station rainfall in Victoria, Australia, with large-scale climate indices such as ENSO and Indian Ocean Dipole indicators.
- **Main result:** ANFIS using combined climate signals gives better seasonal rainfall forecasts than linear regression approaches.
- **Open work:** Inclusion of additional climate drivers and evaluation over more regions and seasons.
- **Issues:** Short records limit training and validation; skill depends on the stability of teleconnections.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Subseasonal Forecasts of Opportunity Identified by an Explainable Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020gl092092)
Mayer et al. (2021), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 92 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies subseasonal forecasts of opportunity for North Atlantic midlatitude circulation via tropical-extratropical teleconnections.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network classifier using tropical inputs, with prediction confidence to select opportunities and layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) for explanation.
- **Data:** Tropical input fields and North Atlantic (40°N, 325°E) circulation target at 22-day lead; the dataset source is not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Higher-confidence predictions are more accurate; LRP highlights tropical hot spots matching known teleconnection source regions and suggests a new pattern.
- **Open work:** Testing in observations/reanalysis and other regions and leads; using opportunities in operational subseasonal forecasts.
- **Issues:** Classification of sign only at a single location; LRP interpretations can be method-sensitive.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Using network theory and machine learning to predict El Niño](https://doi.org/10.5194/esd-9-969-2018)
Nooteboom et al. (2018), *Earth System Dynamics*. 91 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extends ENSO warm-phase prediction skill beyond 6 months to up to 1 year.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid of ARIMA and an artificial neural network with attributes derived from physical knowledge and climate network topological properties.
- **Data:** Zebiak–Cane-type model output and observations.
- **Main result:** Up to 6 months the hybrid is slightly better than the NCEP CFSv2 ensemble; 12-month lead skill is similar to shorter leads.
- **Open work:** Robust evaluation over more events and assessment of the spring predictability barrier.
- **Issues:** Short observational record risks overfitting; limited verification sample of El Niño events; skill measures not detailed in the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Skill Comparisons between Neural Networks and Canonical Correlation Analysis in Predicting the Equatorial Pacific Sea Surface Temperatures](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(2000)013<0287:scbnna>2.0.co;2)
Tang et al. (2000), *Journal of Climate*. 91 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether nonlinear neural networks add skill over linear methods for seasonal prediction of equatorial Pacific SST.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network compared with canonical correlation analysis and linear regression.
- **Data:** Equatorial Pacific SST indices (Nino1+2, Nino3, Nino3.4, Nino4) with large-scale predictor fields; cross-validated evaluation.
- **Main result:** Neural network skill is comparable to linear regression and CCA; differences are not significant at the 5% level, suggesting nearly linear seasonal dynamics.
- **Open work:** Exploring nonlinear methods at other time scales and with longer records where nonlinearity may matter.
- **Issues:** Short records limit neural network training and the power of significance tests.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction of monthly rainfall on homogeneous monsoon regions of India based on large scale circulation patterns using Genetic Programming](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2012.05.033)
Kashid et al. (2012), *Journal of Hydrology*. 91 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts monthly rainfall over homogeneous monsoon regions of India from large-scale ocean-atmosphere circulation patterns.
- **Architecture:** Genetic programming (symbolic regression) linking large-scale climate indices to regional monthly rainfall.
- **Data:** Monthly rainfall for homogeneous Indian monsoon regions and large-scale circulation indices (ENSO and equatorial Indian Ocean indices); periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** Genetic programming models capture rainfall variability with useful skill using circulation predictors; exact metrics not reported here.
- **Open work:** Adding further climate drivers and extending to longer lead times and finer spatial scales.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; monthly rainfall predictability from indices is modest and may not hold for extremes or under nonstationary teleconnections.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Prediction of all India summer monsoon rainfall using error-back-propagation neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1007/bf01029704)
Venkatesan et al. (1997), *Meteorology and Atmospheric Physics*. 90 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts all-India summer monsoon rainfall seasonally from predictor parameters.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward neural network (multilayer perceptron) trained with error back-propagation.
- **Data:** Historical all-India summer monsoon rainfall and predictors from India Meteorological Department records.
- **Main result:** The neural network gives better prediction skill than statistical regression models; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Updating predictors and testing in operational forecasting.
- **Issues:** Short record and predictor stationarity issues; overfitting risk.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Improving Subseasonal Forecasting in the Western U.S. with Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.1145/3292500.3330674)
Hwang et al. (2018), *Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining*. 89 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves subseasonal (weeks 3-4 and 5-6) temperature and precipitation forecasts for western US water management, in the Subseasonal Climate Forecast Rodeo.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble of two nonlinear regression models: multitask feature selection over many predictors, and a weighted local linear regression with multitask nearest-neighbor features.
- **Data:** SubseasonalRodeo dataset of meteorological measurements and dynamical forecasts (including CFSv2), 2011-2018 evaluation.
- **Main result:** Each model beats debiased CFSv2; the ensemble exceeds the top Rodeo competitor; combining with debiased CFSv2 improves its skill by 40-50% for temperature and 129-169% for precipitation.
- **Open work:** Extending to other regions and leads, and using richer dynamical model ensembles.
- **Issues:** Absolute subseasonal skill remains low; evaluation limited to western US; relative skill gains can look large from low baselines.

### [Nonlinear Canonical Correlation Analysis of the Tropical Pacific Climate Variability Using a Neural Network Approach](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(2001)014<2528:nccaot>2.0.co;2)
Hsieh (2001), *Journal of Climate*. 87 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyzes nonlinear coupled variability of tropical Pacific SST and sea level pressure.
- **Architecture:** Nonlinear canonical correlation analysis (NLCCA) implemented with neural networks.
- **Data:** Tropical Pacific SST and sea level pressure anomaly fields.
- **Main result:** NLCCA reveals nonlinear asymmetric modes between El Nino and La Nina not captured by linear CCA; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Applying NLCCA to forecasting and other climate fields.
- **Issues:** Neural network nonlinear methods are prone to overfitting with short records.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Unified deep learning model for El Niño/Southern Oscillation forecasts by incorporating seasonality in climate data.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scib.2021.03.009)
Ham et al. (2021), *Science Bulletin*. 85 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves deep learning ENSO forecasts by accounting for seasonality, avoiding separate per-season models that give inconsistent forecast time series.
- **Architecture:** All-season CNN (A_CNN) that includes calendar-season information in one unified model across target seasons and lead times; activation maps are used for diagnosis.
- **Data:** Training and testing follow Ham et al. (2019): CMIP5 historical simulations and reanalysis for training, observations for validation. The details are not given in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Improves correlation skill of the ENSO index, especially for boreal spring target seasons (the spring predictability barrier). Activation maps show clear time evolution of precursors with lead time.
- **Open work:** Use the model as a diagnostic tool for ENSO precursors, and extend to ENSO diversity and spatial patterns.
- **Issues:** Few independent observed ENSO events for validation, and depends on CMIP biases in training data.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Prediction of the Summer Rainfall over South Africa](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(1995)008<1511:potsro>2.0.co;2)
Hastenrath et al. (1995), *Journal of Climate*. 85 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops statistical seasonal prediction of summer rainfall over South Africa from predictors available before the rainy season.
- **Architecture:** Empirical statistical prediction from large-scale climate indices, comparing linear regression with a neural network approach.
- **Data:** South African summer rainfall index with preceding circulation and sea surface temperature indices (including ENSO-related indicators); exact period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Pre-season indices give useful skill for summer rainfall prediction; quantitative skill measures are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Operational testing on independent seasons and refined predictor selection are natural next steps.
- **Issues:** Short records limit training and validation; statistical relationships may be non-stationary.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deep learning for bias correction of MJO prediction](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-23406-3)
Kim et al. (2021), *Nature Communications*. 84 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves subseasonal MJO prediction, which falls short of its potential predictability partly because of systematic errors in dynamical models.
- **Architecture:** Deep learning bias correction that blends dynamical forecasts with observations to correct forecast MJO amplitude and phase (RMM-based indices) over lead times up to four weeks.
- **Data:** Multi-model operational subseasonal reforecasts (S2S project models) and observed MJO indices.
- **Main result:** Over four weeks, the correction reduces multi-model errors in MJO amplitude by about 90% and in phase by about 77%. The largest gains are for events starting in the Indian Ocean and crossing the Maritime Continent.
- **Open work:** Extend the correction to real-time operational forecasts and to full fields rather than indices, and test how it affects downstream teleconnection skill.
- **Issues:** Corrects the index rather than the model physics. Reforecast samples are limited, so overfitting is a risk, and the gains depend on stationary model bias.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Multi-task machine learning improves multi-seasonal prediction of the Indian Ocean Dipole](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-35412-0)
Ling et al. (2022), *Nature Communications*. 75 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extending Indian Ocean Dipole prediction skill beyond the roughly three-month limit of current models.
- **Architecture:** Multi-task deep learning model (MTL-NET); the specific network family is not stated in the abstract.
- **Data:** Hindcasts of IOD events over the past four decades, compared with dynamical forecast models.
- **Main result:** MTL-NET predicts the IOD well up to 7 months ahead, outperforming most dynamical models compared, and identifies predictor importance and nonlinear links.
- **Open work:** Operational use and extension to other climate modes.
- **Issues:** Few independent IOD events in four decades; risk of overfitting and sensitivity to predictor choice.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Using Artificial Neural Networks for Generating Probabilistic Subseasonal Precipitation Forecasts over California](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-20-0096.1)
Scheuerer et al. (2020), *Monthly Weather Review*. 74 citations.

- **Main goal:** Producing reliable probabilistic subseasonal (weeks 1-4) precipitation forecasts over California, where NWP skill is low.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (ANN) predicting category probability shifts relative to climatology, plus a convolutional neural network (CNN) extension using images of large-scale predictors.
- **Data:** ECMWF ensemble reforecasts and gridded observed 7-day precipitation accumulations over California, up to 4-week leads.
- **Main result:** Both methods compare favorably with a state-of-the-art postprocessing technique, with positive skill everywhere, though skill is low at weeks 3 and 4.
- **Open work:** Exploring additional sources of subseasonal predictability.
- **Issues:** Low week-3/4 skill; a single region.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Objective Identification of Nonlinear Convectively Coupled Phases of Monsoon Intraseasonal Oscillation: Implications for Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1175/2007jas2474.1)
Chattopadhyay et al. (2008), *Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences*. 73 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies the nonlinear phases of the monsoon intraseasonal oscillation objectively to improve understanding and prediction of active and break spells.
- **Architecture:** Self-organizing map clustering of large-scale convection and circulation fields to define intraseasonal oscillation phases, compared with linear methods.
- **Data:** Observed outgoing longwave radiation and reanalysis circulation fields over the Indian monsoon region; periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** The SOM captures nonlinear convectively coupled phases better than linear decompositions, suggesting improved potential for extended-range prediction of monsoon spells.
- **Open work:** Building SOM-based prediction schemes for monsoon intraseasonal variability.
- **Issues:** Phase identification depends on SOM size and input fields; prediction implications are demonstrated only partly.

### [Long-term precipitation forecast for drought relief using atmospheric circulation factors: a study on the Maharloo Basin in Iran](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-18-1995-2014)
Sigaroodi et al. (2013), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 72 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts monthly precipitation in the drought-prone Maharloo Basin in southern Iran using large-scale climate indices to support water management.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network compared with stepwise multiple regression, with predictors chosen by cross-correlation and stepwise selection from 40 climate indices.
- **Data:** Monthly observed precipitation in the Maharloo Basin and 40 atmospheric circulation indices such as NAO, PNA and ENSO.
- **Main result:** The ANN outperforms multiple regression; NAO, PNA and El Nino are the key predictors, with best accuracy in September and worst in March.
- **Open work:** Adding other climatic and physiographic factors such as wind and topography is suggested.
- **Issues:** Coarse data and high system complexity introduce uncertainty; many candidate predictors raise overfitting risk.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Predicting the cloud patterns of the Madden‐Julian Oscillation through a low‐order nonlinear stochastic model](https://doi.org/10.1002/2014gl060876)
Chen et al. (2014), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 71 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts the cloud patterns of the Madden-Julian Oscillation at intraseasonal lead times using a simple model of its spatial modes.
- **Architecture:** Not machine learning: a low-order nonlinear stochastic model with hidden variables and energy-conserving nonlinear interactions, fitted to MJO modes from nonlinear Laplacian spectral analysis.
- **Data:** MJO modes extracted from satellite infrared brightness temperature data (CLAUS) over the tropics.
- **Main result:** The stochastic model gives skillful predictions of the MJO cloud patterns at lead times of several weeks and captures intermittency of MJO events.
- **Open work:** Applying the approach to other intraseasonal modes and to ensemble data assimilation is a natural extension.
- **Issues:** The low-order model captures only large-scale patterns and depends on the mode extraction; skill varies between strong and weak MJO years.

### [Sub-Seasonal Climate Forecasting via Machine Learning: Challenges, Analysis, and Advances](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i1.16090)
He et al. (2020), *AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence*. 70 citations.

- **Main goal:** Systematically assesses ML approaches for sub-seasonal (2 weeks to 2 months) temperature forecasting, a difficult and understudied range.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of 10 ML methods including linear models, XGBoost, and deep learning models (e.g., LSTM, CNN-type encoder-decoders).
- **Data:** A new sub-seasonal dataset over the contiguous US with atmospheric, oceanic and land variables, released with code.
- **Main result:** Well-chosen ML models such as XGBoost capture some sub-seasonal predictability and beat climatology; deep learning models barely match the best results.

- **Issues:** Limited observational sample; skill measured relative to climatology rather than operational S2S systems.

### [A graphical sensitivity analysis for statistical climate models: application to Indian monsoon rainfall prediction by artificial neural networks and multiple linear regression models](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.811)
Cannon et al. (2002), *International Journal of Climatology*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a graphical sensitivity analysis to interpret statistical climate prediction models, which are often treated as black boxes.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural networks and multiple linear regression, analysed with a graphical input-sensitivity method.
- **Data:** Indian summer monsoon rainfall with large-scale climate predictors (e.g., ENSO-related indices).
- **Main result:** The graphical analysis reveals nonlinear predictor-response relations in the neural networks that linear regression misses, while forecast skill differences are modest.
- **Open work:** Applying the interpretation tool to other climate prediction problems.
- **Issues:** Short seasonal records limit training; sensitivity plots depend on the fitted ensemble.

### [Forecasts of Tropical Pacific Sea Surface Temperatures by Neural Networks and Support Vector Regression](https://doi.org/10.1155/2009/167239)
Aguilar-Martinez et al. (2009), *International Journal of Oceanography*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether nonlinear regression improves seasonal forecasts of tropical Pacific SST anomalies over linear regression.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian neural network (BNN) and support vector regression (SVR) compared with linear regression, using PCA-compressed predictors.
- **Data:** Sea level pressure and SST predictors for 1950–2005 and 1980–2005, the latter adding equatorial Pacific warm water volume; lead times 3–15 months.
- **Main result:** Nonlinear models give only modest gains over linear regression; SVR does not beat BNN; nonlinearity appears mainly in the second SST PCA mode; WWV adds slight, linear skill.
- **Open work:** Better use of nonlinear predictors and longer records to exploit nonlinearity.
- **Issues:** Short records limit nonlinear model training; few ENSO events; skill gains are marginal.

### A novel neural network design for long range prediction of rainfall pattern
Goswami et al. (1996), *Current Science*. 68 citations.

### [The Nonlinear Patterns of North American Winter Temperature and Precipitation Associated with ENSO](https://doi.org/10.1175/jcli3372.1)
Wu et al. (2005), *Journal of Climate*. 64 citations.

- **Main result:** Reveals nonlinear, asymmetric teleconnection patterns: the North American temperature and precipitation responses to warm and cold ENSO phases are not mirror images, beyond what linear analysis shows.

Badr et al. (2014), *Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology*. 59 citations.

### [A deep learning model for forecasting global monthly mean sea surface temperature anomalies](https://doi.org/10.3389/fclim.2022.932932)
Taylor et al. (2022), *Frontiers in Climate*. 58 citations.

- **Main result:** High skill in equatorial and subtropical Pacific; skill up to 18 months for 2019-2020 El Nino and 2016-2018 La Ninas; long-lead skill for the northeast Pacific Blob.
- **Open work:** Including subsurface ocean information to capture events like the 2015-2016 El Nino.
- **Issues:** Weak prediction of the 2015-2016 extreme El Nino; short-lead skill only for Ningaloo Nino; surface-only inputs; limited independent test period.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Forecasting regional sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific by neural network models, with wind stress and sea level pressure as predictors](https://doi.org/10.1029/97jc03414)
Tangang et al. (1998), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*. 58 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts sea surface temperature anomalies over equatorial Pacific Niño regions with neural networks, to improve ENSO prediction at long leads.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network (MLP) ensembles, averaging 20 runs with random initial weights; one model type uses sea level pressure and another wind stress as predictors.
- **Data:** Tropical Pacific sea level pressure, wind stress and SST anomalies; cross-validation over 1952–1993 and out-of-sample forecasts for 1982–1993.
- **Main result:** SLP-based models show usable skill to 12-month lead and beat wind-stress models at 9–12 months; Niño 3.5 out-of-sample correlations are 0.78, 0.80 and 0.75 at 9, 12 and 15 months.
- **Open work:** Improving skill in eastern boundary regions and adding ocean predictors such as heat content follow naturally.
- **Issues:** Short record for training nonlinear models; skill is lower in the eastern Pacific and forecasts are deterministic without uncertainty.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A Nonlinear Analysis of the ENSO Cycle and Its Interdecadal Changes](https://doi.org/10.1175/jcli3466.1)
An et al. (2005), *Journal of Climate*. 56 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyses the nonlinear structure of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation cycle and how it changed between decades.
- **Architecture:** Nonlinear principal component analysis implemented with an autoassociative neural network (MLP-based NLPCA).
- **Data:** Observed tropical Pacific sea surface temperature and upper-ocean thermocline or heat content fields over recent decades.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; NLPCA reveals asymmetric, nonlinear ENSO behaviour that became stronger after the late 1970s regime shift.
- **Open work:** Linking the detected nonlinearity changes to ENSO dynamics and testing them in coupled climate models.
- **Issues:** Short observational record for interdecadal comparison and sensitivity of NLPCA to regularization and overfitting.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [The Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Improve El Niño Prediction Skill](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphy.2019.00153)
Dijkstra et al. (2019), *Frontiers in Physics*. 55 citations.

- **Main goal:** Review how machine learning can improve El Nino prediction beyond the roughly 6-month skill limit of classical methods.
- **Architecture:** Review of neural-network-based ENSO prediction, including attribute selection from complex network approaches.
- **Data:** Reviewed studies use observational and reanalysis tropical Pacific data and climate model output.
- **Main result:** Early ML results show enhanced skill for lead times beyond 12 months.
- **Open work:** Critical outlook on further developments, including better predictors and robust validation.
- **Issues:** Review predates many later deep learning ENSO studies; small observational sample size limits skill verification.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Seasonal to Inter-annual Climate Prediction Using Data Mining KNN Technique](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-89853-5_7)
Jan et al. (2008), *International Multi Topic Conference on Wireless Networks, Information Processing and Systems*. 53 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts seasonal to inter-annual climate variables with a data-mining approach.
- **Architecture:** K-nearest neighbour (KNN) data-mining technique using historical analogues.
- **Data:** Historical meteorological records (e.g. temperature and precipitation); region and period are not reported here.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; KNN gives reasonable seasonal predictions.
- **Open work:** Comparison with dynamical and other statistical models and use of climate indices as predictors.
- **Issues:** Analogue methods are limited by record length and cannot extrapolate beyond past climate.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Regional Rainfall Forecasting using Large Scale Climate Teleconnections and Artificial Intelligence Techniques](https://doi.org/10.1515/jisys.2007.16.4.307)
Kumar et al. (2007), *Journal of Intelligent Systems*. 53 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts monthly and seasonal summer monsoon rainfall over Orissa, India, exploiting lagged teleconnections with large-scale climate indices.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (MLP-type ANN) whose architecture is optimized with a genetic optimizer (genetic algorithm), using lagged climate indices as inputs.
- **Data:** Monthly Orissa rainfall for June to September plus ENSO, EQUINOO and Ocean-Land Temperature Contrast (OLTC) indices; separate training and testing periods (years not reported in the abstract).
- **Main result:** Reasonably good accuracy for both individual monsoon months and total JJAS rainfall; large-scale teleconnection indices are shown to carry useful predictive information.
- **Open work:** Extend predictor sets and compare with dynamical seasonal forecasts and other statistical baselines; test robustness to changing teleconnections.
- **Issues:** Short monsoon record and small sample; skill reported only qualitatively in the abstract; no uncertainty quantification or comparison with climatology given.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Predicting summer rainfall in the Yangtze River basin with neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.1588)
Hartmann et al. (2008), *International Journal of Climatology*. 52 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts summer rainfall in the Yangtze River basin months ahead, where floods and droughts cause major impacts.
- **Architecture:** Backpropagation neural networks (MLP) using climate indices and large-scale predictors.
- **Data:** Station precipitation in the Yangtze basin and large-scale predictors such as SST, ENSO indices and Tibetan Plateau snow; exact selection not reported here.
- **Main result:** The networks provide useful skill for summer rainfall prediction over parts of the basin; quantitative scores not reported here.
- **Open work:** Refine predictor selection and test in operational seasonal forecasting.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; short records relative to network complexity; risk of overfitting and nonstationary teleconnections.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Probabilistic Forecasting of El Niño Using Neural Network Models](https://doi.org/10.1029/2019gl086423)
Petersik et al. (2020), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 51 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides probabilistic ENSO forecasts with direct estimates of predictive uncertainty from statistical models.
- **Architecture:** Ensembles of Gaussian density neural networks and quantile regression neural networks; layer type not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** ENSO indices and predictors over 1963–2017 for evaluation; specific datasets not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Mean/median forecasts reach correlation of 0.5 at 12-month lead (1963–2017); Gaussian density networks estimate uncertainty better than a standard method over 1982–2017.
- **Open work:** Combining with dynamical models and reducing the spring predictability barrier.
- **Issues:** Short observational record limits training; skill at long leads remains modest.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [The nonlinear Northern Hemisphere winter atmospheric response to ENSO](https://doi.org/10.1029/2003gl018885)
Wu et al. (2004), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 49 citations.

- **Main goal:** Characterizes the nonlinear, asymmetric Northern Hemisphere winter atmospheric response to ENSO, which linear methods such as CCA or composites cannot fully capture.
- **Architecture:** Neural-network-based nonlinear canonical correlation analysis (NLCCA) relating tropical Pacific SST anomalies to extratropical winter circulation anomalies.
- **Data:** Tropical Pacific SST and Northern Hemisphere winter 500 hPa geopotential height anomalies from the NCEP/NCAR reanalysis over recent decades.
- **Main result:** The extratropical response is clearly nonlinear: the El Niño and La Niña patterns are not mirror images, with the warm-event response displaced eastward relative to the cold-event response.
- **Open work:** Extending the nonlinear analysis to other fields, seasons and coupled model output, and attributing the nonlinearity to physical mechanisms.
- **Issues:** Few strong ENSO events in the record limit the robustness of nonlinear modes; NLCCA can overfit and its results depend on network settings and ensemble selection.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Deep Residual Convolutional Neural Network Combining Dropout and Transfer Learning for ENSO Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021gl093531)
Hu et al. (2021), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 48 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves ENSO amplitude and type forecasts with limited training data.
- **Architecture:** Deep residual convolutional neural network (ResNet CNN) with dropout and homogeneous and heterogeneous transfer learning.
- **Data:** Evaluation 1984–2017; training datasets not named in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Predicts Niño3.4 up to 20 months ahead, three more than the previous best; ONI up to 18 months; 83.3% accuracy for 12-month El Niño type.
- **Open work:** Further improvement of ENSO diversity and probabilistic forecasts.
- **Issues:** Short observational record; small evaluation sample for El Niño type.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Seasonal prediction of winter extreme precipitation over Canada by support vector regression](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-15-65-2011)
Zeng et al. (2010), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 48 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts winter maximum 5-day accumulated precipitation over Canada at seasonal lead times of 3–12 months.
- **Architecture:** Support vector regression (nonlinear and linear) compared with a nonlinear Bayesian neural network and multiple linear regression; K-means clustering groups stations into regions.
- **Data:** 118 Canadian stations, 1950–2007; predictands are leading principal components of regional anomalies; predictors are quasi-global SST anomalies, Northern Hemisphere 500 hPa height anomalies and six climate indices (Nino-3.4, NAO, PNA, PDO, Scandinavia, East Atlantic).
- **Main result:** Robust SVR models generally beat MLR and BNN, with nonlinear SVR slightly better than linear SVR; the Prairies show the highest skill and strongest nonlinearity, the Arctic the second highest skill.
- **Open work:** Extending to other extremes and seasons and improving skill in regions with weak predictability.
- **Issues:** Seasonal extreme precipitation skill is modest overall; limited sample of winters for training nonlinear models.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Long Range Forecasting Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfallby a Hybrid Principal Component Neural Network Model](https://doi.org/10.1007/s007030050059)
Guhathakurta et al. (1999), *Meteorology and Atmospheric Physics*. 46 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts all-India summer monsoon rainfall at long range, where linear regression models have limited skill.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid principal component neural network: principal components of predictors are fed to a feed-forward neural network.
- **Data:** Seasonal monsoon rainfall and long-range predictors from India Meteorological Department records; exact period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The hybrid model is reported to forecast Indian summer monsoon rainfall with skill comparable to or better than operational regression models; numbers not reproduced here.
- **Open work:** Testing on more independent years and updating predictors whose relationships with the monsoon change over time.
- **Issues:** Short record (a few decades of seasons) for training a neural network risks overfitting; predictor relationships are non-stationary.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Improving Seasonal Forecast Using Probabilistic Deep Learning](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021ms002766)
Pan et al. (2020), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 45 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves and benchmarks seasonal forecasts, where large GCM ensembles are costly and limited observations hinder verification and diagnosis.
- **Architecture:** Conditional Generative Forecasting (CGF): a probabilistic deep learning generative model that explicitly models internal variability and GCM formulation differences; the exact network family is not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** 52,201 years of climate model simulations (GCM output) for training; applied to real-world global seasonal forecasts of precipitation and 2 m air temperature.
- **Main result:** CGF faithfully represents GCM-encoded seasonal predictability and achieves performance competitive with dynamical forecasts; it reveals that insufficient ensemble spread sampling limits a dynamical system's skill.
- **Open work:** Combine multiple GCMs in CGF-based ensemble strategies to exploit their complementary strengths.
- **Issues:** Learned relationships inherit GCM biases; skill in observation space is only competitive with, not clearly better than, dynamical forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [ENSO analysis and prediction using deep learning: A review](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2022.11.078)
Wang et al. (2022), *Neurocomputing*. 44 citations.

- **Main goal:** Survey deep learning approaches for analysing and predicting the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, a key source of seasonal-to-interannual predictability.
- **Architecture:** Literature review; per the title it covers deep learning methods (likely CNNs, recurrent networks and related models) used for ENSO analysis and prediction.
- **Data:** Review; covered studies typically use observations, reanalysis and climate-model (e.g. CMIP) simulations. Not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Abstract not available; the paper presumably synthesizes reported skill and methods of deep-learning ENSO forecasts.
- **Open work:** Likely includes extending skillful lead times, interpretability and handling limited observational records.
- **Issues:** Content cannot be verified from an abstract; summary is inferred from the title only.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Long lead monsoon rainfall prediction for meteorological sub-divisions of India using deterministic artificial neural network model](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00703-008-0335-2)
Guhathakurta (2008), *Meteorology and Atmospheric Physics*. 42 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides long-lead prediction of summer monsoon rainfall for the meteorological sub-divisions of India.
- **Architecture:** Deterministic artificial neural network model; network type not specified beyond this.
- **Data:** Historical monsoon rainfall records for Indian meteorological sub-divisions; period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; the model produces sub-divisional long-lead forecasts with reported useful skill.
- **Open work:** Adding large-scale climate predictors and probabilistic forecasts.
- **Issues:** Short records for many sub-divisions; deterministic forecasts without uncertainty.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Nonlinear interdecadal changes of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-003-0361-1)
Wu et al. (2003), *Climate Dynamics*. 41 citations.

- **Main goal:** Examines nonlinear interdecadal changes in the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, in particular around the late-1970s climate shift.
- **Architecture:** Nonlinear principal component analysis using an autoassociative neural network, compared with linear PCA.
- **Data:** Tropical Pacific SST and related fields from observational analyses for periods before and after the late 1970s; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** ENSO is found to show stronger nonlinearity after the late-1970s shift than before.
- **Open work:** Physical mechanisms of the change in nonlinearity and implications for ENSO prediction.
- **Issues:** Short sub-periods limit statistical robustness; NLPCA can overfit.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Low‐order stochastic model and “past‐noise forecasting” of the Madden‐Julian Oscillation](https://doi.org/10.1002/grl.50991)
Kondrashov et al. (2013), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 41 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts the Madden–Julian Oscillation with a low-order data-driven stochastic model, providing a cheap alternative to dynamical models.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML statistical method: multilevel empirical model reduction (stochastic inverse model) with past-noise forecasting that uses estimated past noise.
- **Data:** Observed MJO indices (e.g., RMM index time series); period not reported here.
- **Main result:** No abstract is available; past-noise forecasting improves MJO prediction skill over standard stochastic forecasts.
- **Open work:** Combining with dynamical forecasts and extending to other intraseasonal modes.
- **Issues:** Abstract missing; low-order index-based model cannot represent full spatial structure; skill numbers unverified.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Hybrid coupled models of the tropical Pacific – II ENSO prediction](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-002-0231-2)
Tang et al. (2002), *Climate Dynamics*. 40 citations.

- **Main goal:** Uses hybrid coupled models of the tropical Pacific to predict ENSO.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid coupled model combining a dynamical ocean model with a neural network (MLP) atmospheric model that maps SST to wind stress.
- **Data:** Observed tropical Pacific SST and wind stress data; period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The hybrid coupled models show useful ENSO forecast skill at seasonal leads, comparable to other intermediate models.
- **Open work:** Improved initialization and ensemble forecasting.
- **Issues:** Simplified ocean; short training records.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Artificial neural network models for forecasting intermittent monthly precipitation in arid regions](https://doi.org/10.1002/met.127)
Dahamsheh et al. (2009), *Meteorological Applications*. 38 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts intermittent monthly precipitation in arid regions with neural networks.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks such as feed-forward networks compared with regression models; types not confirmed here.
- **Data:** Monthly precipitation records from stations in arid Jordan; details not confirmed here.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; neural networks give reasonable forecasts but struggle with intermittency.
- **Open work:** Better treatment of zero months.
- **Issues:** Intermittent series hard to model; limited records.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Robust nonlinear canonical correlation analysis: application to seasonal climate forecasting](https://doi.org/10.5194/npg-15-221-2008)
Cannon et al. (2008), *Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics*. 38 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves nonlinear canonical correlation analysis on noisy datasets such as seasonal climate forecasts.
- **Architecture:** Robust nonlinear canonical correlation analysis neural network using biweight midcorrelation and mean absolute error cost functions.
- **Data:** Synthetic dataset and tropical Pacific SST and sea level pressure fields; source datasets not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Biweight midcorrelation improves performance, especially with a strong common event; mae helps on synthetic data but only at the longest lead on climate data.
- **Open work:** Problem-dependent choice of cost functions.
- **Issues:** Limited to one climate application; small sample sizes.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Coupled Ocean-Atmosphere Dynamics in a Machine Learning Earth System Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08632)
Wang et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 37 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a fast coupled AI ocean-atmosphere model for large-ensemble seasonal forecasts.
- **Architecture:** Ola: separate autoregressive Spherical Fourier Neural Operator (SFNO) models for ocean and atmosphere at 0.25 degree, coupled together.
- **Data:** Atmospheric and ocean reanalysis fields at 0.25 degree; exact products and periods not reported in the abstract; ENSO skill compared with GFDL SPEAR.
- **Main result:** Learns coupled dynamics including tropical ocean waves with correct phase speeds and an internally generated ENSO with realistic amplitude and structure; ENSO forecast skill compares favourably to SPEAR.
- **Open work:** Fuller seasonal skill assessment, large ensembles and longer stable climate runs.
- **Issues:** Initial evidence only; skill comparison limited; reanalysis training inherits biases and the ocean record is short.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Nonlinear multichannel singular spectrum analysis of the tropical Pacific climate variability using a neural network approach](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001jc000957)
Hsieh et al. (2002), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*. 36 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extracting nonlinear spatio-temporal modes of tropical Pacific climate variability, generalising linear singular spectrum analysis.
- **Architecture:** Nonlinear multichannel singular spectrum analysis (NLSSA): SSA for dimension reduction, then a nonlinear PCA autoencoder neural network with a circular bottleneck node combining the leading SSA PCs.
- **Data:** Tropical Pacific sea surface temperature anomaly and sea level pressure anomaly fields, 1950–2000.
- **Main result:** NLSSA mode 1 shows shorter, more intense warm periods than cool periods as in ENSO, with eastern-Pacific warm and central-Pacific cool peaks; mode 2 reveals a quasi-triennial wave of about 39 months.
- **Open work:** Application to other climate fields and phenomena, and use of nonlinear modes for prediction.
- **Issues:** Results depend on the SSA truncation and network settings; nonlinear PCA can overfit with short records.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Skilful global seasonal predictions from a machine learning weather model trained on reanalysis data](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01198-3)
Kent et al. (2025), *npj Climate and Atmospheric Science*. 35 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses whether an ML weather model trained on reanalysis can produce skilful global seasonal forecasts.
- **Architecture:** ACE2, an autoregressive ML atmosphere emulator (spherical Fourier neural operator) with 6-hourly steps, run as a lagged ensemble with persisted SST and sea-ice anomalies.
- **Data:** ACE2 trained on ERA5; seasonal hindcasts initialised around 1 November for winters 1993/94 to 2015/16, compared with a leading physics-based seasonal system.
- **Main result:** Skilful winter NAO prediction (correlation 0.47, p = 0.02), realistic skill distribution and spread, predictability patterns like the physics model, and a signal-to-noise error.
- **Open work:** Coupling to an interactive ocean, better representing extremes beyond the training data, and studying the signal-to-noise paradox with ML models.
- **Issues:** Persisted SST and sea-ice anomalies; limited skill for extreme seasons outside training data such as winter 2009/2010; only one start date per year.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Learning forecasts of rare stratospheric transitions from short simulations](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-21-0024.1)
Finkel et al. (2021), *Monthly Weather Review*. 35 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts rare sudden stratospheric warmings, computing event probability and lead time from short simulations instead of long integrations.
- **Architecture:** Non-deep-learning data-driven method: transition operator estimation from short trajectories (dynamical Galerkin approximation) to compute committor probabilities and expected lead times.
- **Data:** Short simulations of a stochastically forced Holton-Mass stratospheric model.
- **Main result:** Efficiently computes probability and lead time of SSWs and relates them to a few interpretable physical variables, suggesting optimal measurements.
- **Open work:** Applying to high-dimensional models and observations and to other rare events.
- **Issues:** Highly idealized model; scalability to full atmospheric models not demonstrated.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [ENSO‐GTC: ENSO Deep Learning Forecast Model With a Global Spatial‐Temporal Teleconnection Coupler](https://doi.org/10.1029/2022ms003132)
Mu et al. (2022), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 34 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts ENSO by learning global SST teleconnections among ocean basins.
- **Architecture:** ENSO-GTC: graph neural network with probability graph convolution layers on an ocean-patch dynamics graph, with a graph total-variation loss penalty.
- **Data:** Global SST fields over the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans; training and validation datasets not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Nino3.4 correlation skill of 0.79/0.66/0.51 at 6/12/18 months (iterative) and above 0.6 within 20 months (direct), outperforming other models; learned links match ENSO theory.
- **Open work:** Monitoring meridional modes and inter-basin teleconnections to further improve forecasts.
- **Issues:** Short observational record and model training data limitations; skill claims depend on validation period.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Representation of the quasi‐biennial oscillation in the tropical stratospheric wind by nonlinear principal component analysis](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001jd001250)
Hamilton et al. (2002), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 34 citations.

- **Main goal:** Representing the quasi-biennial oscillation (QBO) of tropical stratospheric winds with a one-dimensional nonlinear description.
- **Architecture:** Circular nonlinear principal component analysis (NLPCA.cir), an autoencoder neural network with a circular bottleneck node for quasiperiodic phenomena.
- **Data:** Near-equatorial station zonal winds at 70–10 hPa, 1956–2000.
- **Main result:** NLPCA.cir yields a better one-dimensional representation of the QBO than linear PCA and a single QBO phase series, which correlates strongly with boreal winter high-latitude stratospheric temperatures.
- **Open work:** Using the QBO phase index in studies of stratosphere-troposphere coupling and predictability.
- **Issues:** One-dimensional representation cannot capture all QBO irregularities; based on a limited set of station levels.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Transformer for EI Niño-Southern Oscillation Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1109/lgrs.2021.3100485)
Ye et al. (2022), *IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters*. 33 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improve multi-season ENSO prediction by capturing long-range, basin-scale precursors that the local receptive field of convolutional networks struggles to represent.
- **Architecture:** ENSO transformer (ENSOTR), a transformer model using self-attention over global ocean-atmosphere fields to predict the monthly Niño3.4 index, compared against a CNN baseline.
- **Data:** Training and evaluation datasets are not reported in the abstract; evaluation includes historical events such as the 1997–1998 El Niño.
- **Main result:** Skillful Niño3.4 prediction up to about 18 months ahead, strong El Niño events such as 1997–1998 predicted more than a year in advance, and higher skill than the CNN.
- **Open work:** Assess robustness across decades and in the spring predictability barrier, interpret the attention patterns physically, and compare with operational dynamical forecasts.
- **Issues:** Short letter with limited detail on data and validation; few strong El Niño events limit robust skill assessment, and no probabilistic or uncertainty information is given.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Multivariate forecast of winter monsoon rainfall in India using SST anomaly as a predictor: Neurocomputing and statistical approaches](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crte.2010.06.004)
Chattopadhyay et al. (2009), *Comptes Rendus. Géoscience*. 33 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasting average winter monsoon rainfall over India from previous-year rainfall and sea surface temperature anomalies.
- **Architecture:** MLP neural network with sigmoid nonlinearity and genetic algorithm-based variable selection, compared with a multiple exponential regression fitted by Levenberg-Marquardt.
- **Data:** Indian winter monsoon rainfall and SST anomalies of previous-year winter monsoon months; SST product not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Linear and polynomial trends explain little variance; judged by Willmott's index, percentage error and prediction yield, the ANN outperforms the exponential regression.
- **Open work:** Testing additional predictors and longer independent validation periods.
- **Issues:** Short annual series give few samples for training and testing; no comparison with dynamical forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [The nonlinear association between ENSO and the Euro-Atlantic winter sea level pressure](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-004-0470-5)
Wu et al. (2004), *Climate Dynamics*. 32 citations.

- **Main goal:** Investigates whether the Euro-Atlantic winter sea level pressure response to ENSO is nonlinear, differing between El Nino and La Nina.
- **Architecture:** Nonlinear projection using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network mapping an ENSO index onto the leading principal components of winter sea level pressure.
- **Data:** Observed or reanalysis winter sea level pressure over the Euro-Atlantic sector with a tropical Pacific ENSO index over several decades.
- **Main result:** A clear nonlinear (largely quadratic) response is found: both strong El Nino and La Nina produce NAO-like anomalies with patterns not simply opposite in sign.
- **Open work:** Testing in model simulations and examining dynamical mechanisms of the asymmetric teleconnection.
- **Issues:** Short observational record with few strong ENSO events; statistical association does not establish causality; potential overfitting of nonlinear fits.

### [Assessing Decadal Predictability in an Earth‐System Model Using Explainable Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021gl093842)
Toms et al. (2021), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 31 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identify oceanic regions that provide decadal predictability of continental surface temperature, using explainable neural networks as a discovery tool.

Zhang et al. (2024), *Science Bulletin*. 31 citations.

Wang et al. (2023), *Ocean-Land-Atmosphere Research*. 30 citations.

- **Main goal:** From the title, develops a deep learning model for ENSO forecasting that is interpretable, to link predictive skill to physical precursors.

### [Reconstruction of the El Niño attractor with neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1007/bf00228027)
Grieger et al. (1994), *Climate Dynamics*. 30 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs the low-dimensional dynamics (attractor) of El Niño–Southern Oscillation from time series and uses it for prediction.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (feedforward) trained on time-delay embeddings of ENSO indices to approximate the dynamical map.
- **Data:** ENSO time series (e.g. Niño SST index) from observations and/or coupled model output; details not reported.
