- **Main result:** Shows the QRNN gives a flexible nonlinear quantile regression suitable for downscaling mixed discrete–continuous precipitation.
- **Open work:** Extending to multisite and multivariate downscaling.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; independently fitted quantiles can cross.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Statistical downscaling of precipitation using machine learning techniques](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2018.05.022)
Sachindra et al. (2018), *Atmospheric Research*. 320 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compare machine learning techniques for downscaling reanalysis data to monthly station precipitation across climate regimes.
- **Architecture:** Four ML methods compared: genetic programming, artificial neural networks, support vector machines and relevance vector machines, built per station and calendar month.
- **Data:** Reanalysis predictors and monthly precipitation at 48 stations in Victoria, Australia (wet, intermediate, dry regimes); calibration 1950-1991, validation 1992-2014.
- **Main result:** All methods capture the mean better than variability, underestimate the standard deviation and maxima, overestimate low-to-mid percentiles and underestimate high percentiles; RVM/ANN recommended for floods, RVM for droughts, polynomial kernels best for SVM/RVM.
- **Open work:** Bias correction of extremes and application to GCM projections for future precipitation.
- **Issues:** Monthly resolution only; systematic underestimation of extremes; stationarity of predictor-precipitation relationships under climate change is untested.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Downscaling temperature and precipitation: a comparison of regression‐based methods and artificial neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.655)
Schoof et al. (2001), *International Journal of Climatology*. 307 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares statistical downscaling methods for daily and monthly surface temperature and precipitation, to judge whether artificial neural networks beat regression for local climate projections.
- **Architecture:** Multiple linear regression-based downscaling compared with feed-forward artificial neural networks (MLP), using large-scale circulation predictors, partly reduced by principal component analysis.
- **Data:** Large-scale predictors from NCEP/NCAR reanalysis and station observations at a single US site (Indianapolis, Indiana).
- **Main result:** Temperature is downscaled with reasonable skill by both approaches, while precipitation is reproduced much less well; neither method clearly dominates for all variables and time scales.
- **Open work:** Applying the downscaling models to GCM output and testing additional predictors and stations.
- **Issues:** Single-station study; precipitation skill is low; no abstract available, so details rely on recollection and should be checked.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Adversarial super-resolution of climatological wind and solar data](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1918964117)
Stengel et al. (2020), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences*. 290 citations.

- **Main goal:** Super-resolve global climate model wind and solar outputs to scales needed for renewable energy resource assessment under climate scenarios.
- **Architecture:** Fully convolutional generative adversarial super-resolution network, trainable on small domains and applicable to arbitrarily sized inputs.
- **Data:** High-resolution wind (NREL WIND Toolkit) and solar (NSRDB) data for training; applied to CMIP5 / IPCC AR5 climate scenario output.
- **Main result:** Achieves up to 50x resolution enhancement; outputs are robust to input noise, reproduce turbulent spectra and solar irradiance statistics, and remain consistent with coarse fields.
- **Open work:** Apply to more variables and scenarios and assess impacts on energy-system planning decisions.
- **Issues:** GAN outputs may hallucinate fine-scale detail; training on present-day high-resolution data assumes the coarse-to-fine relationship holds under future climates.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Multisite simulation of daily precipitation and temperature in the Rhine Basin by nearest‐neighbor resampling](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001wr000291)
Buishand et al. (2001), *Water Resources Research*. 288 citations.

- **Main goal:** Simulates daily precipitation and temperature simultaneously at many sites for hydrological impact studies in the Rhine basin.
- **Architecture:** Non-parametric nearest-neighbour (k-NN) resampling weather generator (non-deep statistical method).
- **Data:** Daily precipitation and temperature records from multiple stations in the Rhine basin.
- **Main result:** Nearest-neighbour resampling reproduces spatial correlation and many daily statistics, but some variability of multi-day precipitation totals is underestimated.
- **Open work:** Improving reproduction of long-term variability and extremes, and climate change scenarios.
- **Issues:** Resampling cannot generate values outside the observed record; underestimates variability at longer time scales.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Configuration and intercomparison of deep learning neural models for statistical downscaling](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-2019-278)
Baño-Medina et al. (2019), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 278 citations.

- **Main goal:** Systematically assess the added value of CNNs for continental-scale statistical downscaling, including extrapolation relevant to climate change.
- **Architecture:** CNN models of increasing complexity compared with linear and generalized linear benchmarks within the VALUE validation framework.
- **Data:** Large-scale reanalysis predictors (ERA-Interim) and gridded observations (E-OBS) over Europe for temperature and precipitation; a warm test period as a surrogate for future climate.
- **Main result:** CNNs add value for temperature mainly in reproducing extremes, and outperform classical methods for precipitation in most aspects; they can be applied to whole continents without predictor selection.
- **Open work:** Application to GCM predictors for climate-change projections, e.g. within CORDEX, and further tests of extrapolation.
- **Issues:** Perfect-prognosis setup with reanalysis predictors; a warm historical period is only a partial proxy for future climate; deterministic models.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A technique for generating regional climate scenarios using a nearest‐neighbor algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1029/2002wr001769)
Yates et al. (2003), *Water Resources Research*. 274 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generates plausible regional daily climate scenarios for impact studies without running a climate model.
- **Architecture:** K-nearest neighbor resampling weather generator with conditional selection to produce shifted scenarios (e.g. warmer or wetter); a non-parametric statistical method.
- **Data:** Multi-station daily weather observations (precipitation and temperature) for a US region; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The nearest-neighbor approach produces scenarios that preserve spatial and cross-variable correlations while shifting climate statistics as specified.
- **Open work:** Linking scenario shifts to climate-model projections and generating values outside the historical record.
- **Issues:** Resampling cannot produce values outside the observed range; scenarios are user-specified rather than physically derived.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Statistical downscaling of daily precipitation using support vector machines and multivariate analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2010.01.021)
Chen et al. (2010), *Journal of Hydrology*. 244 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales daily precipitation from large-scale circulation for local hydrological impact studies.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine (classification of wet/dry days and support vector regression of amounts) combined with multivariate analysis for predictor reduction.
- **Data:** Large-scale reanalysis predictors (NCEP/NCAR) and daily station precipitation, likely in Taiwan; details not given here.
- **Main result:** The SVM-based approach reproduces daily precipitation statistics better than a multiple linear regression benchmark.
- **Open work:** Applying the model to GCM scenarios for future precipitation projections.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; study region, predictors and scores are not verified here; extremes likely underestimated, as is typical for regression downscaling.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Downscaling precipitation to river basin in India for IPCC SRES scenarios using support vector machine](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.1529)
Anandhi et al. (2008), *International Journal of Climatology*. 242 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales monthly precipitation to a river basin in India under IPCC SRES scenarios.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine regression (least-squares SVM) statistical downscaling model.
- **Data:** NCEP/NCAR reanalysis predictors for calibration and CGCM2 GCM output for SRES scenarios; Malaprabha basin, India.
- **Main result:** The SVM downscaling reproduces observed precipitation well and projects changes in basin precipitation under the SRES scenarios.
- **Open work:** Using multiple GCMs and addressing downscaling uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Single GCM; stationarity of predictor-predictand relations assumed.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Residual corrective diffusion modeling for km-scale atmospheric downscaling](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-025-02042-5)
Mardani et al. (2023), *Communications Earth & Environment*. 232 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides cost-effective km-scale downscaling of coarse global data as an alternative to expensive km-scale simulation.
- **Architecture:** CorrDiff: two-step model in which a UNet regresses the conditional mean and a score-based diffusion model generates the residual.
- **Data:** 25 km ERA5 as input and 2 km operational regional WRF output over Taiwan as target; about three years of training data with a held-out year for testing.
- **Main result:** Good deterministic and probabilistic skill, recovers power-law spectra and distributions, sharpens cold fronts, intensifies typhoons, and synthesizes rainbands.
- **Open work:** Better calibration of uncertainty and coupling with coarse global ML models for global-to-regional simulation.
- **Issues:** Uncertainty calibration remains challenging (under-dispersed); single region and short training record; target is a model, not observations.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Spatial downscaling of precipitation using adaptable random forests](https://doi.org/10.1002/2016wr019034)
He et al. (2016), *Water Resources Research*. 228 citations.

- **Main goal:** Statistically downscales precipitation to fine resolution with machine learning to support hydrological applications.
- **Architecture:** Prec-DWARF: random forest regression relating fine-resolution precipitation to coarse/fine covariates, in a single-RF and a double-RF (two independent random forests) version.
- **Data:** Hourly gauge-radar precipitation at 0.125 degrees from NLDAS-2, coarsened to 0.25, 0.5 and 1 degree for synthetic experiments.
- **Main result:** Prec-DWARF outperforms bilinear interpolation and reproduces spatial and temporal patterns; the double RF better captures extremes, but spatial and temporal variability are still strongly underestimated.
- **Open work:** Better representation of fine-scale variability and extremes, and application to real coarse model output.
- **Issues:** Single RF underestimates extremes; poor fine-scale structure at 1 degree; synthetic perfect-prognosis setup only.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Deep Learning for Daily Precipitation and Temperature Downscaling](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020wr029308)
Wang et al. (2021), *Water Resources Research*. 214 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales daily precipitation and temperature to local scale for impact assessment.
- **Architecture:** Super Resolution Deep Residual Network (SRDRN): deep CNN with residual blocks and batch normalization, plus data augmentation for imbalanced and extreme precipitation.
- **Data:** Synthetic experiments coarsening 4 km gridded data to 25, 50 and 100 km and downscaling back to 4 km; transfer to a second region.
- **Main result:** Captures spatial and temporal patterns and local extremes of precipitation and temperature; transfer learning to another region beats classic statistical downscaling.
- **Open work:** Apply to real GCM output and other Earth system variables.
- **Issues:** Synthetic coarsening setup avoids GCM biases and representativeness mismatch; deterministic outputs give no uncertainty.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Stochastic Super-Resolution for Downscaling Time-Evolving Atmospheric Fields With a Generative Adversarial Network](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2020.3032790)
Leinonen et al. (2020), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 213 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops stochastic, temporally consistent super-resolution (downscaling) of atmospheric fields that produces ensembles.
- **Architecture:** Recurrent conditional GAN (convolutional GRU-based generator and discriminator) generating ensembles of high-resolution image sequences from low-resolution sequences.
- **Data:** Swiss radar precipitation (MeteoSwiss) and GOES-16-derived cloud optical thickness.
- **Main result:** Generates realistic, temporally consistent sequences; rank statistics indicate near-correct ensemble spread; fully convolutional generator applies to larger domains and longer sequences.
- **Open work:** Apply to downscaling of model output (rather than coarsened observations) and to other variables.
- **Issues:** Trained on artificially coarsened observations, so performance on real model output is untested; GAN training stability and mode collapse are general risks.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Large-scale circulation anomalies conducive to extreme precipitation events and derivation of daily rainfall in northeastern Mexico and southeastern Texas](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(1999)012<1506:lscact>2.0.co;2)
Cavazos (1999), *Journal of Climate*. 204 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies large-scale circulation anomalies associated with extreme precipitation in northeastern Mexico and southeastern Texas and derives daily station rainfall from them, a statistical downscaling problem.
- **Architecture:** Principal component analysis combined with a self-organizing map (Kohonen network) to classify circulation patterns, plus a feed-forward artificial neural network to downscale daily rainfall.
- **Data:** NCEP-NCAR reanalysis atmospheric fields as predictors and daily station precipitation records in the study region; exact period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Distinct circulation anomaly types are linked to extreme rainfall events, and the neural network reproduces daily rainfall variability, though magnitudes of extremes are harder to capture.
- **Open work:** Testing on other seasons and regions, and applying the downscaling to climate model output for scenario projections.
- **Issues:** Downscaling relationships are calibrated on a limited reanalysis period and assume stationarity; extremes are rare in the training sample.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Generative Deep Learning Approach to Stochastic Downscaling of Precipitation Forecasts](https://doi.org/10.1029/2022ms003120)
Harris et al. (2022), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 202 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves the accuracy and resolution of global NWP precipitation forecasts, since key precipitation processes are sub-grid.
- **Architecture:** Conditional GAN and VAE-GAN that downscale and correct precipitation forecasts stochastically, producing ensembles of high-resolution fields.
- **Data:** ECMWF IFS forecast fields as inputs and high-resolution UK radar (NIMROD) precipitation as ground truth.
- **Main result:** Matches the statistical skill of state-of-the-art pointwise postprocessing while producing spatially coherent high-resolution maps. Compares favourably on pixelwise and pooled CRPS, power spectra and rank histograms, including heavy rain.
- **Open work:** Extend to other regions (for example East Africa), longer lead times and better calibration for extremes.
- **Issues:** Limited to one region and lead range. GAN training can be unstable, and calibration for rare extremes is challenging.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Multi-site downscaling of heavy daily precipitation occurrence and amounts](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2005.02.020)
Harpham et al. (2005), *Journal of Hydrology*. 198 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales heavy daily precipitation occurrence and amounts at multiple sites from large-scale atmospheric predictors for climate impact studies.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks (multilayer perceptron and radial basis function networks) compared with the regression-based Statistical DownScaling Model (SDSM).
- **Data:** NCEP/NCAR reanalysis predictors and daily precipitation from station networks in several UK regions.
- **Main result:** Both neural networks and SDSM capture some heavy precipitation statistics, with skill differing by method, region and index.
- **Open work:** Improve representation of inter-site correlation and extremes and apply to GCM scenarios.
- **Issues:** Heavy precipitation remains underestimated; trained on reanalysis so inherits its biases; results region-dependent.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Intercomparison of machine learning methods for statistical downscaling: the case of daily and extreme precipitation](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00704-018-2613-3)
Vandal et al. (2017), *Theoretical and Applied Climatology*. 191 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether modern ML methods improve statistical downscaling of daily and extreme precipitation from GCMs.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of perfect-prognosis methods (OLS, Elastic-Net, SVM, multi-task sparse structure learning, autoencoders) and a hybrid MSSL+BCSD approach.
- **Data:** Reanalysis predictors and gridded observed daily precipitation over the United States (details not confirmed).
- **Main result:** No method is consistently best; L1 sparsity helps; MSSL+BCSD improves daily to annual predictability over BCSD but worsens extremes.
- **Open work:** Developing methods that capture extremes and remain reliable under nonstationary climate.
- **Issues:** Limited set of methods and regions; perfect-prognosis evaluation does not test performance in future climates.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Downscaling Precipitation and Temperature with Temporal Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/jhm409.1)
Coulibaly et al. (2005), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 188 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales daily precipitation and temperature for climate change impact studies using temporal neural networks.
- **Architecture:** Time-lagged feed-forward neural network (TLFN) compared with a regression-based statistical downscaling model (SDSM).
- **Data:** NCEP/NCAR reanalysis predictors and station data in the Chute-du-Diable basin, Quebec, Canada.
- **Main result:** The TLFN downscales precipitation and temperature more accurately than SDSM.
- **Open work:** Apply to GCM scenarios and evaluate extremes.
- **Issues:** Trained on reanalysis so inherits its biases; single region.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Temporal neural networks for downscaling climate variability and extremes](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2006.01.003)
Dibike et al. (2005), *Neural Networks*. 188 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales climate variability and extremes using temporal neural networks.
- **Architecture:** Time-lagged feed-forward neural network (TLFN) for statistical downscaling, compared with regression approaches.
- **Data:** Large-scale predictors (reanalysis and GCM outputs) and station data in Quebec, Canada; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The temporal neural network reproduces daily variability and some extremes.
- **Open work:** Evaluate extremes further with GCM scenarios.
- **Issues:** Conference paper with limited evaluation details.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Downscaling Extremes—An Intercomparison of Multiple Statistical Methods for Present Climate](https://doi.org/10.1175/jcli-d-11-00408.1)
Bürger et al. (2012), *Journal of Climate*. 184 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares how well multiple statistical downscaling methods reproduce climate extremes in the present climate, to guide method choice for impact studies.
- **Architecture:** Intercomparison of statistical downscaling methods, including bias-correction (BCSD, BCCA), regression-based and expanded downscaling approaches; not a single ML model.
- **Data:** Reanalysis predictors downscaled to station observations in British Columbia, Canada, evaluated with ETCCDI-type climate extreme indices.
- **Main result:** Methods differ substantially in their skill at reproducing extreme indices, with no single method best for all indices; methods that preserve variance and temporal structure perform better for extremes.
- **Open work:** Extending the evaluation to future-climate (non-stationary) conditions and more regions is needed.
- **Issues:** Present-climate evaluation only cannot test stationarity; single region; results depend on the chosen indices and predictors.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Evaluating machine learning approaches for the interpolation of monthly air temperature at Mt. Kilimanjaro, Tanzania](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.spasta.2015.05.008)
Appelhans et al. (2015), *Spatial Statistics*. 177 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces high-resolution maps of monthly air temperature on the southern slopes of Mt. Kilimanjaro for scaling plot-based biodiversity research.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of 14 machine learning algorithms (stochastic gradient boosting, Cubist, random forest, model-averaged neural networks, linear and nonlinear regression) against kriging, plus Cubist with residual kriging.
- **Data:** Monthly air temperature from a network of observation plots on Mt. Kilimanjaro, Tanzania, with 10-fold cross-validation.
- **Main result:** Tree-based models perform best, led by stochastic gradient boosting, then Cubist and random forest; ML beats kriging quantitatively, but maps are visually ambiguous, so Cubist plus residual kriging is preferred.
- **Open work:** Including more physically meaningful predictors and denser station networks would improve maps.
- **Issues:** Small station network on complex terrain; good cross-validation scores do not guarantee realistic maps.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Model output statistics downscaling using support vector machine for the projection of spatial and temporal changes in rainfall of Bangladesh](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2018.06.006)
Pour et al. (2018), *Atmospheric Research*. 167 citations.

- **Main goal:** Projects spatial and temporal rainfall changes in Bangladesh by downscaling GCM output.
- **Architecture:** Model output statistics downscaling using support vector machine (support vector regression), with GCM ensemble selection by past performance and envelope methods.
- **Data:** CMIP5 GCMs under four RCPs, with GPCC gauge-based gridded monthly rainfall as reference.
- **Main result:** SVM-MOS reproduces GPCC variability; annual rainfall changes range from -4.2% to 24.6%, increasing more in the drier west and during monsoon.
- **Open work:** Daily-scale downscaling and extremes, and CMIP6 updates.
- **Issues:** Monthly scale only; stationarity assumption of statistical downscaling.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Simulating climate change scenarios using an improved K-nearest neighbor model](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2005.10.015)
Sharif et al. (2006), *Journal of Hydrology*. 145 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generates plausible daily weather series under climate change scenarios for hydrological impact studies.
- **Architecture:** Improved K-nearest neighbour (KNN) resampling weather generator with a perturbation step so that simulated values can fall outside the historical record; not a neural method.
- **Data:** Daily precipitation and temperature observations from stations in the Upper Thames River basin, Ontario, Canada.
- **Main result:** The modified KNN generator reproduces observed statistics and can produce extremes beyond the historical range under altered scenarios.
- **Open work:** Coupling with GCM-based scenarios and hydrological models for impact assessment.
- **Issues:** Scenarios are imposed by conditioning or perturbation rather than physically consistent climate projections; abstract unavailable so details are uncertain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [High‐resolution multisite daily rainfall projections in India with statistical downscaling for climate change impacts assessment](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgrd.50280)
Salvi et al. (2013), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 140 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces high-resolution multisite daily rainfall projections over India for climate change impact assessment through statistical downscaling.
- **Architecture:** Statistical downscaling combining clustering and classification of rainfall states (CART) with kernel regression of daily rainfall at multiple sites.
- **Data:** Gridded daily rainfall from the India Meteorological Department, large-scale predictors from NCEP/NCAR reanalysis, and GCM projections for future scenarios.
- **Main result:** The method reproduces observed rainfall statistics reasonably and projects changes in daily rainfall across Indian regions; exact values not recalled.
- **Open work:** Using multiple GCMs and scenarios to quantify projection uncertainty, and testing for nonstationarity of predictor-predictand links.
- **Issues:** Assumes stationary statistical relationships under climate change; projections depend on the driving GCM.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A comparative study of convolutional neural network models for wind field downscaling](https://doi.org/10.1002/met.1961)
Höhlein et al. (2020), *Meteorological Applications*. 134 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscale short-range near-surface (100 m) wind forecasts quickly from coarse to high resolution over complex terrain.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of four CNN architectures against multilinear regression, plus a proposed U-Net-based DeepRU model; tests adding atmospheric predictors and static fields like topography and land-sea mask.
- **Data:** Short-range forecasts from ERA5 initial conditions at 31 km as input, ECMWF HRES 9 km forecasts as target, over the Alpine region.
- **Main result:** DeepRU infers situation-dependent wind structures that other models miss; inference takes under 10 ms on a GPU versus minutes to hours for higher-resolution simulation.
- **Open work:** Extend to other variables, levels, and regions, and to probabilistic downscaling.
- **Issues:** Target is a model forecast (HRES), not observations; deterministic CNNs may smooth small-scale variability.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A semiparametric multivariate and multisite weather generator](https://doi.org/10.1029/2006wr005714)
Apipattanavis et al. (2007), *Water Resources Research*. 134 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generates multisite, multivariate daily weather sequences for agricultural and hydrological risk assessment.
- **Architecture:** Semiparametric weather generator: Markov chain for precipitation occurrence with K-nearest neighbour (KNN) bootstrap resampling of daily weather vectors; not a neural method.
- **Data:** Daily precipitation, temperature and solar radiation from stations in the Argentine Pampas.
- **Main result:** The generator reproduces daily statistics, spatial correlation and dependence between variables at multiple sites.
- **Open work:** Conditioning on climate indices or forecasts.
- **Issues:** Resampling cannot produce values outside the historical record.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [High-resolution downscaling with interpretable deep learning: Rainfall extremes over New Zealand](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wace.2022.100525)
Rampal et al. (2022), *Weather and Climate Extremes*. 133 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscale rainfall, especially extremes, to high resolution over New Zealand with an interpretable deep-learning approach.
- **Architecture:** Deep-learning (likely convolutional) statistical downscaling model with interpretability analysis; details not available from an abstract.
- **Data:** Not reported in the abstract; presumably coarse reanalysis predictors and high-resolution gridded New Zealand rainfall.
- **Main result:** Abstract not available; the title suggests skillful high-resolution reproduction of rainfall extremes with interpretable predictor relationships.
- **Open work:** Application to climate-model projections and assessment of extrapolation under climate change.
- **Issues:** Summary inferred from the title only; regional focus and possible underestimation of extremes typical of regression-based downscaling.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Spatial Downscaling Algorithm for Satellite-Based Precipitation over the Tibetan Plateau Based on NDVI, DEM, and Land Surface Temperature](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs8080655)
Jing et al. (2016), *Remote Sensing*. 133 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales satellite precipitation to 1 km over the Tibetan Plateau for ecological and hydrological modelling.
- **Architecture:** Random forest (RF) and support vector machine (SVM) regression using NDVI, DEM and land surface temperature predictors.
- **Data:** Yearly TRMM 3B43 V7 precipitation (25 km), MODIS NDVI and land surface temperature, DEM; validated with meteorological station observations.
- **Main result:** RF and SVM outperform exponential and multiple linear regression and the original TRMM; adding LST improves accuracy, especially for RF.
- **Open work:** Apply at monthly or weekly scales where the precipitation–LST relationship is more instantaneous.
- **Issues:** Annual scale only; sparse stations on the plateau limit validation.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A statistical downscaling method for monthly total precipitation over Turkey](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.997)
Tatlı et al. (2004), *International Journal of Climatology*. 132 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales large-scale atmospheric fields to monthly total precipitation over Turkey.
- **Architecture:** Statistical downscaling using principal components of large-scale predictors with a neural network-based transfer function; the specific network type is not specified here.
- **Data:** NCEP/NCAR reanalysis predictors and monthly precipitation from Turkish stations.
- **Main result:** The method reproduces monthly precipitation variability at stations with useful skill; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Applying to GCM scenarios for climate projections.
- **Issues:** Stationarity of predictor-predictand relations assumed; monthly scale only.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Least square support vector and multi‐linear regression for statistically downscaling general circulation model outputs to catchment streamflows](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.3493)
Sachindra et al. (2013), *International Journal of Climatology*. 130 citations.

- **Main goal:** Statistically downscales general circulation model outputs to catchment streamflow for climate impact assessment.
- **Architecture:** Least squares support vector machine regression compared with multi-linear regression.
- **Data:** Large-scale atmospheric predictors from reanalysis and GCM outputs with observed catchment streamflow; specific products not reported in the record.
- **Main result:** LS-SVM is reported to perform better than multi-linear regression in reproducing streamflow; numbers not available in the record.
- **Open work:** Downscaling multiple GCMs and emission scenarios to quantify projection uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Assumes stationarity of predictor–predictand relationships; inherits GCM biases; no abstract available.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Improving Monsoon Precipitation Prediction Using Combined Convolutional and Long Short Term Memory Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.3390/w11050977)
Miao et al. (2019), *Water*. 126 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves GCM precipitation prediction in a monsoon region by statistical downscaling from well-resolved atmospheric dynamical fields.
- **Architecture:** Deep neural network combining a convolutional neural network (CNN) and an LSTM recurrent module; compared with quantile mapping, support vector machine and a plain CNN.
- **Data:** ERA-Interim reanalysis predictors and precipitation over the Xiangjiang River Basin, South China; applied to ECMWF retrospective forecasts; distributed hydrological model for evaluation.
- **Main result:** Outperforms ERA-Interim precipitation and benchmark downscaling at 1-day to 2-week leads (advantage declines with lead); hydrological NSE rises from 0.06 (ERA-Interim) to 0.64 vs 0.82 with observed precipitation.
- **Open work:** Applying the approach to other monsoon basins and to operational hydrological forecasting.
- **Issues:** Single basin; skill depends on the GCM's dynamical forecast skill and degrades at long leads; trained against reanalysis-era observations.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Role of predictors in downscaling surface temperature to river basin in India for IPCC SRES scenarios using support vector machine](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.1719)
Anandhi et al. (2009), *International Journal of Climatology*. 125 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales monthly surface temperature to a river basin in India for IPCC SRES scenarios and examines how the choice of predictors affects projections.
- **Architecture:** Least-squares support vector machine (SVM) statistical downscaling model relating large-scale atmospheric predictors to station temperatures, tested with different predictor sets.
- **Data:** NCEP/NCAR reanalysis predictors for calibration and CGCM3 GCM output for SRES A1B, A2, B1 and COMMIT scenarios; observed temperatures for the Malaprabha basin, India.
- **Main result:** Including additional predictors such as humidity-related variables changes and improves downscaled temperatures; projected maximum and minimum temperatures increase under the SRES scenarios.
- **Open work:** Using multiple GCMs and quantifying downscaling uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Single GCM and basin; assumes stationarity of predictor-predictand relationships; reanalysis biases propagate.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Statistical Downscaling of Precipitation Using Machine Learning with Optimal Predictor Selection](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)he.1943-5584.0000355)
Najafi et al. (2011), *Journal of Hydrologic Engineering*. 124 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales coarse climate model information to local precipitation, selecting the most informative large-scale predictors.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning statistical downscaling with support vector machine and relevance vector machine regressors plus an optimal predictor selection step.
- **Data:** Large-scale atmospheric predictors from reanalysis and GCM output with station precipitation; region and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Predictor selection improves downscaling skill and the machine learning models reproduce observed precipitation statistics reasonably; detailed scores not available here.
- **Open work:** Applying to future scenarios and quantifying downscaling uncertainty across GCMs.
- **Issues:** Stationarity assumption; precipitation extremes and occurrence are hard for regression-based downscaling.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Probabilistic Multisite Precipitation Downscaling by an Expanded Bernoulli–Gamma Density Network](https://doi.org/10.1175/2008jhm960.1)
Cannon (2008), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 123 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales daily precipitation at multiple sites probabilistically from synoptic-scale predictors, capturing occurrence, amounts and spatial relationships.
- **Architecture:** Expanded Bernoulli-gamma density network (EBDN): an artificial neural network (MLP) whose outputs are Bernoulli-gamma parameters, with a covariance constraint in the cost function and an autoregressive noise model.
- **Data:** Multisite daily precipitation dataset from coastal British Columbia, Canada, with synoptic-scale climate predictors.
- **Main result:** EBDN specifies the conditional precipitation distribution at each site, reproduces spatial relationships, generates realistic synthetic series, and predicts amounts beyond the observed record.
- **Open work:** Application to GCM scenarios and other regions and variables.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated in one region; parametric Bernoulli-gamma form may misrepresent extremes; assumes stationarity of predictor relationships.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Simulation of daily temperatures for climate change scenarios over Portugal: a neural network model approach](https://doi.org/10.3354/cr013045)
Trigo et al. (1999), *Climate Research*. 121 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales large-scale climate to daily maximum and minimum temperature at stations in Portugal to build local climate change scenarios.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (multilayer perceptron) statistical downscaling from large-scale circulation and temperature predictors, compared with linear regression.
- **Data:** Observed daily station temperatures in Portugal with large-scale predictors; applied to general circulation model output (HadCM2) for climate change scenarios.
- **Main result:** The neural network reproduces observed daily temperatures well and is applied to project local temperature changes under enhanced greenhouse forcing.
- **Open work:** Extending the approach to precipitation and to multiple GCMs, and assessing stationarity of the predictor-predictand relationship.
- **Issues:** Downscaling inherits GCM biases in predictors and assumes the trained relationship holds under a changed climate; single-model scenarios.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [DeepDownscale: A Deep Learning Strategy for High-Resolution Weather Forecast](https://doi.org/10.1109/escience.2018.00130)
Rodrigues et al. (2018), *IEEE International Conference on e-Science*. 114 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces high-resolution weather forecast fields from cheaper low-resolution model output, for users who cannot afford high-resolution runs.
- **Architecture:** Deep neural network trained in a supervised way to map low- to high-resolution forecasts; the exact network family is not stated in the abstract.
- **Data:** Low- and high-resolution numerical weather forecasts; region and model not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Significant improvement over standard practices such as interpolation, while remaining lightweight.
- **Open work:** Applying to more variables and regions and comparing with dynamical downscaling.
- **Issues:** Quantitative results and evaluation details are not reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Spatial Interpolation of Surface Air Temperatures Using Artificial Neural Networks: Evaluating Their Use for Downscaling GCMs](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(2000)013<0886:siosat>2.0.co;2)
Snell et al. (2000), *Journal of Climate*. 114 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates neural networks for spatial interpolation of surface air temperature as a tool for downscaling GCM output.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward artificial neural networks compared with conventional spatial interpolation methods.
- **Data:** Observed surface air temperature from station networks in the United States.
- **Main result:** Neural networks interpolate temperatures more accurately than conventional methods. Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Applying to GCM fields and other variables such as precipitation.
- **Issues:** Tested on observations rather than GCM output; stationarity of relationships assumed.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [SVM-PGSL coupled approach for statistical downscaling to predict rainfall from GCM output](https://doi.org/10.1029/2009jd013548)
Ghosh (2010), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 110 citations.

- **Main goal:** Statistically downscales GCM output to predict rainfall at regional scale for climate change impact assessment.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine (SVM) regression coupled with probabilistic global search Lausanne (PGSL) optimisation of its parameters.
- **Data:** Large-scale GCM output and reanalysis predictors with observed rainfall; region and models not reported here (no abstract available).
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; the title implies the SVM-PGSL approach yields skilful rainfall downscaling from GCM output.
- **Open work:** Applying to multiple GCMs and scenarios and representing downscaling uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Statistical downscaling assumes stationary predictor-predictand relations under climate change; inherits GCM biases.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Improved K-Nearest Neighbor Weather Generating Model](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)1084-0699(2007)12:1(42))
Sharif et al. (2007), *Journal of Hydrologic Engineering*. 106 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generates synthetic daily weather sequences for hydrologic studies, overcoming the inability of plain K-nearest neighbour resampling to produce unobserved values.
- **Architecture:** Nonparametric K-nearest neighbour (KNN) resampling weather generator with a perturbation step that generates values outside the historical record.
- **Data:** Daily precipitation and temperature records from stations in the Upper Thames River basin, Ontario, Canada.
- **Main result:** The improved generator preserves statistics of historical data while producing new extreme values not present in the record.
- **Open work:** Coupling with climate change scenarios and hydrologic models.
- **Issues:** Perturbation scheme parameters are subjective; spatial correlation preservation depends on station configuration.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Deep-Learning-Based Gridded Downscaling of Surface Meteorological Variables in Complex Terrain. Part II: Daily Precipitation](https://doi.org/10.1175/jamc-d-20-0058.1)
Sha et al. (2020), *Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology*. 103 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscale daily precipitation over complex terrain in western North America with deep learning.
- **Architecture:** UNet and a proposed Nest-UNet with deep-layer aggregation and nested skip connections; inputs include low-resolution precipitation, high-resolution precipitation climatology and elevation.
- **Data:** PRISM data from 0.25° to 4 km; training on south and central-western US 2015-2018, testing 2018-2019 on all domains; station observations for comparison.
- **Main result:** Both UNets generalize across regions and beat the BCSD baseline with lower error and finer textures; Nest-UNet shares the most information with stations and PRISM.
- **Open work:** Test with actual climate or NWP model inputs and assess extremes and probabilistic outputs.
- **Issues:** Deterministic output may underrepresent extremes; inputs are coarsened PRISM rather than model output; short training period.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Regional climate model emulator based on deep learning: concept and first evaluation of a novel hybrid downscaling approach](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-022-06343-9)
Doury et al. (2021), *Climate Dynamics*. 102 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a cheap emulator of a regional climate model (RCM) to enlarge high-resolution downscaled ensembles for uncertainty exploration.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid downscaling: a neural network (U-Net-type) learns the RCM's downscaling function from large-scale predictors to daily near-surface temperature at 12 km.
- **Data:** RCM simulations (CNRM-ALADIN over a European domain driven by a GCM) for historical and future climate.
- **Main result:** The emulator reproduces spatial structure and daily variability of the RCM well; training on future climate is key; training takes about 2 h on GPU and prediction under a minute.
- **Open work:** Better reproduction of temperature extremes and climate change intensity; extension to other regions, GCMs, RCMs and variables.
- **Issues:** Underestimates some extremes and climate change signal; single RCM/variable; emulates the RCM, so inherits its biases.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Neural Networks for Rainfall Forecasting by Atmospheric Downscaling](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)1084-0699(2004)9:1(1))
Olsson et al. (2004), *Journal of Hydrologic Engineering*. 101 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts local rainfall by statistically downscaling large-scale atmospheric variables, aiming to improve rainfall prediction in a monsoon region.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks (specific type not specified in the available information) mapping large-scale atmospheric predictors to local rainfall amounts or occurrence categories.
- **Data:** Large-scale atmospheric fields from reanalysis and rain-gauge observations in southern Japan (Kyushu) during the rainy season.
- **Main result:** The neural networks capture rainfall occurrence and intensity categories with useful skill, better for classification of rainy versus dry conditions than for amounts.
- **Open work:** Apply the downscaling to forecast model output and refine predictor selection.
- **Issues:** Rainfall amounts, especially extremes, are poorly reproduced; trained on reanalysis predictors so operational skill depends on forecast quality.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deep-Learning-Based Gridded Downscaling of Surface Meteorological Variables in Complex Terrain. Part I: Daily Maximum and Minimum 2-m Temperature](https://doi.org/10.1175/jamc-d-20-0057.1)
Sha et al. (2020), *Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology*. 99 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develop a generalizable deep learning downscaling of daily maximum and minimum 2 m temperature in complex terrain.
- **Architecture:** UNet modified into UNet-Autoencoder with an extra high-resolution elevation output branch, enabling semisupervised fine-tuning in unseen domains.
- **Data:** PRISM 4 km and 0.25° coarsened data with elevation; trained on south and central-western US 2015-2018; tested 2018-2019 including the unseen northwestern US.
- **Main result:** Original UNet lacks fine detail when transferred; UNet-AE reduces MAE by more than 10% relative to UNet.
- **Open work:** Apply to other variables (Part II covers precipitation) and to downscaling actual model output.
- **Issues:** Target is PRISM, itself an interpolated product; inputs are coarsened PRISM rather than real GCM or reanalysis output; short training period.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Weather Types and Rainfall over Senegal. Part II: Downscaling of GCM Simulations](https://doi.org/10.1175/2007jcli1624.1)
Moron et al. (2008), *Journal of Climate*. 99 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales GCM simulations of Senegal rainfall through daily weather types to improve simulation of local rainfall characteristics.
- **Architecture:** Weather-typing via k-means clustering of atmospheric patterns combined with stochastic rainfall simulation; statistical downscaling, not a neural network.
- **Data:** Daily station rainfall over Senegal, reanalysis circulation fields and ensemble GCM (ECHAM4.5) simulations forced by observed SST.
- **Main result:** Weather-type-based downscaling improves interannual rainfall amount and occurrence simulation over raw GCM output.
- **Open work:** Apply to seasonal forecasts and climate change projections.
- **Issues:** Skill limited by GCM circulation biases and the weak predictability of Sahelian rainfall.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Statistical downscaling of watershed precipitation using Gene Expression Programming (GEP)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2011.07.007)
Hashmi et al. (2011), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 99 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales watershed precipitation from large-scale climate predictors.
- **Architecture:** Gene Expression Programming (GEP), an evolutionary symbolic regression method.
- **Data:** Large-scale reanalysis predictors and watershed precipitation observations.
- **Main result:** GEP gives comparable or better downscaling than benchmark methods.
- **Open work:** Application to climate-change projections.
- **Issues:** Precipitation extremes and stationarity issues.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Physically constrained generative adversarial networks for improving precipitation fields from Earth system models](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-022-00540-1)
Hess et al. (2022), *Nature Machine Intelligence*. 96 citations.

- **Main goal:** Correct both local distributions and spatial patterns of precipitation simulated by an Earth system model, which conventional post-processing cannot do.
- **Architecture:** Physically constrained generative adversarial network (cycle-consistent, unpaired) with a layer preserving global precipitation sums.
- **Data:** Daily precipitation from the CM2Mc-LPJmL ESM, with reanalysis (ERA5) precipitation as the target; tested on future scenarios.
- **Main result:** Outperforms existing methods for local distributions, strongly improves spatial patterns and intermittency, removes the double ITCZ, and generalizes to unseen future scenarios via the constraint.
- **Open work:** Application to other ESMs and variables and multivariate consistency.
- **Issues:** Applied to one coarse ESM; correction is statistical and does not fix model dynamics; unpaired mapping complicates verification.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Spatio-temporal interpolation of climatic variables over large region of complex terrain using neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0304-3800(00)00406-3)
Antonić et al. (2001), *Ecological Modelling*. 95 citations.

- **Main goal:** Interpolates monthly climatic variables over complex terrain.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks (specific type not specified in the available information) using geographic coordinates, altitude and time as inputs.
- **Data:** Monthly meteorological station data over Croatia.
- **Main result:** Neural networks interpolate climatic variables with good accuracy across complex terrain.
- **Open work:** Add terrain-derived predictors and compare with geostatistics.
- **Issues:** Station density limits accuracy in mountains.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A comparison of three methods for downscaling daily precipitation in the Punjab region](https://doi.org/10.1002/hyp.8083)
Raje et al. (2011), *Hydrological Processes*. 95 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares methods for statistically downscaling daily precipitation from GCMs to the Punjab region.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of three statistical downscaling methods for daily precipitation; specific methods are not reported here.
- **Data:** GCM output and observed daily precipitation for Punjab; details are not reported here.
- **Main result:** Relative skill of the three downscaling methods is reported; values are not available here.
- **Open work:** Extending to multiple GCMs and scenarios.
- **Issues:** Downscaling assumes stationary relationships.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [TRU-NET: a deep learning approach to high resolution prediction of rainfall](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10994-021-06022-6)
Adewoyin et al. (2020), *Machine Learning*. 94 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predict high-resolution precipitation from coarse model-like fields, since climate models represent precipitation poorly at their low resolution.
- **Architecture:** TRU-NET (Temporal Recurrent U-Net), an encoder-decoder with convolutional-recurrent layers and a novel 2D cross-attention mechanism, trained with a non-stochastic conditional-continuous loss for zero-inflated rainfall.
- **Data:** Reanalysis weather fields as input (excluding local precipitation) and high-resolution precipitation observations as targets; specific products not named in the abstract.
- **Main result:** With the CC loss, TRU-NET attains lower RMSE and MAE than a common precipitation-downscaling DL model and outperforms a state-of-the-art dynamical weather model, robustly across seasons and regions.
- **Open work:** Application to climate model output for future projections and probabilistic extensions.
- **Issues:** Trained on reanalysis rather than climate model output, so applying it to climate models involves a domain shift; extremes are not specifically assessed in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A nonparametric nonhomogeneous hidden Markov model for downscaling of multisite daily rainfall occurrences](https://doi.org/10.1029/2004jd005677)
Mehrotra et al. (2005), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 94 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales multisite daily rainfall occurrence from large-scale atmospheric predictors while preserving spatial dependence between stations.
- **Architecture:** Nonhomogeneous hidden Markov model whose state and occurrence probabilities are estimated nonparametrically (kernel-density based) instead of parametric distributions; a statistical non-deep-learning method.
- **Data:** Multisite daily rain-gauge records with reanalysis-derived atmospheric predictors; the station network and period are not reported here.
- **Main result:** The nonparametric NHMM reproduces at-site and spatial rainfall occurrence statistics comparably to or better than parametric alternatives; detailed scores are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Extending the framework to rainfall amounts and applying it to GCM predictors for climate change projections.
- **Issues:** Covers occurrences only; nonparametric estimation needs long records and may extrapolate poorly under predictors outside the observed range.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Comparison of Different Regression Algorithms for Downscaling Monthly Satellite-Based Precipitation over North China](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs8100835)
Jing et al. (2016), *Remote Sensing*. 92 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales coarse satellite precipitation to 1 km for hydrologic and environmental applications.
- **Architecture:** Compares CART regression tree, k-nearest neighbors, support vector machine and random forest regression using land surface predictors.
- **Data:** Monthly TRMM 3B43 V7 (25 km) over North China; MODIS LST (day, night, difference), NDVI, DEM and geolocation; validation with meteorological stations.
- **Main result:** Random forest is most accurate, followed by SVM, CART and k-NN; accuracy is lower in July–September; LST features are more important than NDVI.
- **Open work:** Daily downscaling and use of newer products such as GPM IMERG.
- **Issues:** Errors grow with precipitation amount; SVM depends on residual correction; monthly scale only.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Genetic Programming for the Downscaling of Extreme Rainfall Events on the East Coast of Peninsular Malaysia](https://doi.org/10.3390/atmos5040914)
Pour et al. (2014), *Atmosphere*. 91 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales extreme rainfall indices on the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia for climate change assessment.
- **Architecture:** Genetic programming-based logistic regression, compared with multilayer perceptron neural network and SDSM linear regression downscaling.
- **Data:** NCEP reanalysis predictors at 42 grid points; daily station rainfall 1961–1990 for calibration and 1991–2000 for validation.
- **Main result:** GP predicts annual and seasonal extreme rainfall indices more accurately than ANN and SDSM.
- **Open work:** Application to GCM projections to estimate future extreme rainfall changes.
- **Issues:** Single region; evaluation on reanalysis-driven downscaling only; stationarity of predictor relations assumed.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Uncertainty analysis of statistical downscaling methods using Canadian Global Climate Model predictors](https://doi.org/10.1002/hyp.6084)
Khan et al. (2006), *Hydrological Processes*. 89 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses uncertainty of statistical downscaling methods for daily precipitation and temperature.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of SDSM (regression-based), LARS-WG (stochastic weather generator) and an artificial neural network downscaling model.
- **Data:** Station observations in northern Quebec, Canada (Chute-du-Diable basin), with NCEP reanalysis and CGCM1 predictors.
- **Main result:** SDSM reproduces observed statistics with least uncertainty, while the ANN shows larger deviations especially for precipitation; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Including more GCMs and downscaling methods to characterise total uncertainty.
- **Issues:** One basin and one GCM; uncertainty assessed mainly through statistic reproduction.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Statistical downscaling of daily temperature and precipitation over China using deep learning neural models: Localization and comparison with other methods](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.6769)
Sun et al. (2020), *International Journal of Climatology*. 88 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates CNN-based statistical downscaling of daily temperature and precipitation across China and compares with established methods.
- **Architecture:** CNN models with different configurations mapping large-scale reanalysis predictors to high-resolution grids, compared with GLM, BCSD and BCCI quantile-mapping methods.
- **Data:** ERA-Interim predictors and high-resolution gridded observations over China; calibration 1979-1999, validation 2000-2017.
- **Main result:** CNN adds value over ERA-Interim in seasonal means, seasonal cycle and extreme percentiles and beats GLM for precipitation; bias-correction methods remain best for biases and temporal correlation.
- **Open work:** Apply to GCM projections and improve temporal correlation and precipitation extremes.
- **Issues:** Perfect-prognosis setting with reanalysis predictors; extrapolation tested only within a modestly warmer period.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Multilayer perceptron neural network for downscaling rainfall in arid region: A case study of Baluchistan, Pakistan](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12040-015-0602-9)
Ahmed et al. (2015), *Journal of Earth System Science*. 85 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales rainfall in an arid region of Baluchistan, Pakistan, for local climate impact assessment.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network for statistical downscaling of rainfall from large-scale predictors.
- **Data:** Station rainfall in Baluchistan and large-scale predictors (reanalysis or GCM output); specific products not reported here.
- **Main result:** The MLP downscales rainfall with acceptable skill in the arid region; numbers are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Projecting future rainfall under climate scenarios and comparing with other downscaling methods.
- **Issues:** Arid rainfall is intermittent and hard to model; assumes stationarity of predictor-predictand relationships.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Clustering Methods for Statistical Downscaling in Short-Range Weather Forecasts](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0493(2004)132<2169:cmfsdi>2.0.co;2)
Gutiérrez et al. (2004), *Monthly Weather Review*. 84 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales short-range numerical weather forecasts to local precipitation at stations, improving on direct model output.
- **Architecture:** Clustering-based statistical downscaling (k-means and self-organizing map clustering of atmospheric patterns) combined with analog-type conditional probabilities.
- **Data:** ECMWF reanalysis and operational forecast fields over Iberia and daily precipitation from a Spanish station network.
- **Main result:** Clustering-based downscaling gives skilful probabilistic local precipitation forecasts, comparable to or better than standard analog methods and direct model output.
- **Open work:** Extending to other variables and longer lead times, and combining with ensemble forecasts.
- **Issues:** Results are for one region and network; cluster number and predictor domain choices affect skill.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [On the suitability of deep convolutional neural networks for continental-wide downscaling of climate change projections](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-021-05847-0)
Baño-Medina et al. (2021), *Climate Dynamics*. 82 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether CNN-based perfect-prognosis downscaling can be trusted for future climate projections, given its black-box nature and possible extrapolation artifacts.
- **Architecture:** Deep CNNs for downscaling temperature and precipitation over Europe, compared with generalized linear models. The authors examine whether the downscaled climate change signal preserves the raw GCM delta.
- **Data:** Reanalysis predictors (ERA-Interim) and gridded observations (E-OBS) over Europe for training; GCM historical and future scenario output for application.
- **Main result:** Compared with GLMs, CNNs depart less from the raw GCM climate change signal at the end of the century and give more spatially homogeneous patterns, so projections are more plausible.
- **Open work:** Test the other perfect prognosis assumption (GCM reproduction of predictors), and use more GCMs and scenarios.
- **Issues:** Plausibility judged by consistency with the GCM signal rather than a ground truth. A limited set of GCMs is used, and extrapolation remains unverifiable.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Dynamical-generative downscaling of climate model ensembles](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2420288122)
Lopez-Gomez et al. (2024), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences*. 81 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces the cost of regional downscaling of large climate projection ensembles while keeping the skill of physics-based regional models, to better sample regional uncertainty.
- **Architecture:** Two-stage hybrid: a regional climate model (WRF) downscales GCM output to an intermediate resolution, then a conditional diffusion model generates the final high-resolution fields.
- **Data:** CMIP6 GCM projections downscaled with WRF over the western United States; the diffusion model is trained on high-resolution WRF simulations.
- **Main result:** The hybrid matches or approaches full dynamical downscaling skill, captures extremes and compound events better than statistical baselines, and cuts cost substantially, enabling downscaling of multi-model ensembles.
- **Open work:** Extending to more regions, variables and GCMs and using the larger ensembles for impact-oriented risk assessment.
- **Issues:** Still requires a coarse RCM run for every GCM member; trained on a single RCM, so inherits WRF biases; generalization to unseen climates depends on the physics-based intermediate stage.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A XGBoost-Based Downscaling-Calibration Scheme for Extreme Precipitation Events](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2023.3294266)
Zhu et al. (2023), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 79 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves spatial resolution and accuracy of satellite precipitation during extreme events such as typhoons.
- **Architecture:** XGBoost gradient boosting trees used in both downscaling and calibration (XGBoost_DC), compared with spline-based variants.
- **Data:** Coarse satellite-derived precipitation with gauge observations during typhoon events; product names not specified in the abstract.
- **Main result:** XGBoost_DC gives the highest accuracy and reproduces occurrence and spatial distribution of typhoon precipitation; spline-downscaling variants underestimate spatial variability.
- **Open work:** Applying the scheme to other extreme event types and regions.
- **Issues:** Limited to typhoon cases; quantitative metrics not given in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Downscaling multi-model climate projection ensembles with deep learning (DeepESD): contribution to CORDEX EUR-44](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-15-6747-2022)
Baño-Medina et al. (2022), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 78 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assessing whether CNN-based perfect-prognosis downscaling can extrapolate to future climate and produce a multi-model ensemble of regional projections for CORDEX.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network (CNN) perfect-prognosis downscaling model (DeepESD) applied to the output of multiple GCMs.
- **Data:** Trained on reanalysis predictors (ERA-Interim) and E-OBS observations; applied to eight CMIP5 GCMs over the EUR-44 (0.5°) domain and compared with the EURO-CORDEX RCM ensemble.
- **Main result:** DeepESD reduces historical distributional biases, gives climate change signals broadly comparable to RCMs, preserves inter-model spread for temperature and reduces it for precipitation.
- **Open work:** Further evaluating extrapolation under strong warming and extending the approach to other domains and variables.
- **Issues:** Perfect-prognosis assumptions and stationarity of learned links under future climate cannot be fully verified; reduced precipitation spread may be an artefact.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Downscaling GCMs using the Smooth Support Vector Machine method to predict daily precipitation in the Hanjiang Basin](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00376-009-8071-1)
Chen et al. (2010), *Advances in Atmospheric Sciences*. 78 citations.

- **Main goal:** Statistically downscales general circulation model (GCM) output to predict daily precipitation in the Hanjiang Basin, China, for climate impact assessment.
- **Architecture:** Smooth Support Vector Machine (SSVM), a support vector machine variant, used as a statistical downscaling regression/classification model.
- **Data:** Large-scale predictors from reanalysis and GCM outputs with station daily precipitation in the Hanjiang Basin; specific products and periods not reported in the available information.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available information.
- **Open work:** Comparison with other downscaling methods and multiple GCMs and scenarios would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; daily precipitation downscaling typically underestimates extremes and inherits GCM biases.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Convolutional conditional neural processes for local climate downscaling](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-2020-420)
Vaughan et al. (2021), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 76 citations.

- **Main goal:** Multisite statistical downscaling of temperature and precipitation that can predict at arbitrary locations, including sites without training data.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional conditional neural process (convCNP), a deep learning model for off-the-grid spatio-temporal data.
- **Data:** VALUE intercomparison experiment over Europe, with reanalysis (ERA-Interim) predictors and station observations.
- **Main result:** The convCNP outperforms an ensemble of existing downscaling methods and a Gaussian-process interpolation baseline at unseen sites, with large gains for extreme precipitation.
- **Open work:** Applying to GCM projections for climate impact studies and further deep learning downscaling research.
- **Issues:** Evaluated in the perfect-prognosis reanalysis setting; behaviour under future climate and GCM biases is untested.

- **Main goal:** Asks whether nonlinear statistical downscaling methods improve on linear regression for daily temperature at European stations.
