- **Data:** Large-scale predictors from reanalysis (e.g., 500 hPa heights and 850 hPa temperature) and daily temperature series from European stations.
- **Main result:** Nonlinear neural network downscaling yields only small improvements over linear regression, mostly limited to certain seasons and stations; linear methods remain competitive.
- **Open work:** Assessing nonlinearity for other variables such as precipitation, for extremes, and under climate-change conditions.
- **Issues:** Conclusions depend on the predictor set and network configuration; small gains may not justify added complexity, and stationarity under future climates is untested.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Stochastic downscaling of precipitation with neural network conditional mixture models](https://doi.org/10.1029/2010wr010128)
Carreau et al. (2011), *Water Resources Research*. 46 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops stochastic statistical downscaling of daily precipitation that represents occurrence, intensity and heavy-tailed extremes conditional on large-scale atmospheric predictors.
- **Architecture:** Neural network conditional mixture model: an MLP outputs the parameters of a mixture distribution (dry-day mass plus continuous components for heavy-tailed rain amounts), from which precipitation is sampled.
- **Data:** Large-scale atmospheric predictors and daily station precipitation; specific stations and reanalysis product not reported here.
- **Main result:** No abstract is available; the method yields stochastic precipitation simulations conditional on large-scale fields, aiming to reproduce distribution and extremes better than simpler downscaling.
- **Open work:** Multi-site extension with spatial dependence and application to climate model projections.
- **Issues:** Abstract missing, so quantitative results unverified; station-wise model without spatial coherence; stationarity assumption for future climates.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Downscaling of surface moisture flux and precipitation in the Ebro Valley (Spain) using analogues and analogues followed by random forests and multiple linear regression](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-15-1895-2011)
Ibarra-Berastegi et al. (2011), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 46 citations.

- **Main goal:** Statistically downscales daily precipitation and surface moisture flux at two Ebro Valley observatories from large-scale reanalysis fields, testing whether machine learning adds value to analogues.
- **Architecture:** Three downscaling models: analogues alone, analogues followed by random forests, and analogues followed by multiple linear regression, with EOF-reduced predictors.
- **Data:** ERA-40 reanalysis predictor fields and observations at Zaragoza and Tortosa, Spain, 1961–2001; training 1961–1996 (about 300 analogues), test 1997–2001.
- **Main result:** Random forests after analogues do not clearly beat linear regression for moisture flux, and simple analogue averages are only slightly worse; for precipitation all three perform equally, so skill comes mainly from the analogue stage.
- **Open work:** Testing other predictors, larger station networks and application to climate model output.
- **Issues:** Only two stations; random forest adds little over analogues; evaluated on a short five-year test period.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Can AI be enabled to perform dynamical downscaling? A latent diffusion model to mimic kilometer-scale COSMO5.0_CLM9 simulations](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-18-2051-2025)
Tomasi et al. (2024), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 41 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether generative deep learning can emulate kilometer-scale dynamical downscaling at much lower cost.
- **Architecture:** Latent diffusion model (LDM) applied as a residual on a reference U-Net, compared with interpolation, a U-Net and a GAN.
- **Data:** ERA5 predictors over Italy as input; targets are 2 m temperature and 10 m wind from COSMO-CLM dynamical downscaling at 2 km.
- **Main result:** The LDM with residual approach outperforms all baselines in spatial error, frequency distributions and power spectra while preserving fine-scale realism.
- **Open work:** Apply to downscaling of climate projections and exploit ensemble generation for uncertainty quantification.
- **Issues:** Limited to temperature and wind over Italy; target is a regional model, so it inherits COSMO-CLM biases.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Evaluation of machine learning tools as a statistical downscaling tool: temperatures projections for multi-stations for Thames River Basin, Canada](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00704-011-0546-1)
Goyal et al. (2012), *Theoretical and Applied Climatology*. 39 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates machine learning tools for statistical downscaling of temperature projections at multiple stations in the Thames River Basin, Ontario, Canada.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of machine learning regression tools for statistical downscaling; the specific set of methods is not specified in the available information.
- **Data:** Large-scale reanalysis predictors and station temperatures in the Thames River Basin, Canada, with GCM output for projections; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** No abstract is available; the title indicates machine learning tools are evaluated as downscaling methods for multi-station temperature projections.
- **Open work:** Extension to precipitation and multi-model ensembles.
- **Issues:** Abstract missing; stationarity assumption in downscaling; results unverified.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Global spatio-temporal ERA5 precipitation downscaling to km and sub-hourly scale using generative AI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01103-y)
Glawion et al. (2024), *npj Climate and Atmospheric Science*. 38 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales global reanalysis precipitation to km and sub-hourly scales to capture intense local rainfall relevant to hazards.
- **Architecture:** spateGAN-ERA5, a spatio-temporal generative adversarial network (GAN) producing ensembles of high-resolution precipitation fields.
- **Data:** ERA5 precipitation (24 km, 1 h) to 2 km, 10 min targets; trained on radar-based data from Germany, validated in the US and Australia.
- **Main result:** Produces realistic spatio-temporal rainfall patterns and accurate rain rate distributions including extremes, and generalises to US and Australian climates including tropical regimes.
- **Open work:** Global on-demand generation of high-resolution precipitation for hydrological applications and further validation in data-poor regions.
- **Issues:** Trained only on German data; generalisation to all climates is not guaranteed; inherits ERA5 biases in timing and location of rain.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Deep Learning for Downscaling Tropical Cyclone Rainfall to Hazard‐Relevant Spatial Scales](https://doi.org/10.1029/2022jd038163)
Vosper et al. (2023), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 37 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales tropical cyclone rainfall from coarse to hazard-relevant scales to support flood risk assessment under climate change.
- **Architecture:** Three deep learning downscaling models compared, including a Wasserstein generative adversarial network (WGAN), which performs best.
- **Data:** MSWEP (Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation) TC rainfall coarsened to about 100 km as input, original about 10 km as target; most extreme storms held out.
- **Main result:** The WGAN captures realistic spatial structure and power spectra with mean biases within 5% of observations, and extrapolates well to the most extreme unseen storms.
- **Open work:** Applying the downscaling to low-resolution climate model TC simulations to estimate future rainfall hazard.
- **Issues:** Trained on coarsened observations (perfect-prognosis setting), so transfer to climate model biases is untested; extremes sampled by few storms.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [NN5: A neural network based approach for the downscaling of precipitation fields – Model description and preliminary results](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2008.12.017)
Tomassetti et al. (2009), *Journal of Hydrology*. 37 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscaling coarse precipitation fields to finer spatial resolution for hydrological applications, presenting the NN5 neural network approach.
- **Architecture:** Neural network based downscaling model (NN5); the specific network type and predictors are not specified here.
- **Data:** Precipitation fields and observations used for training and testing are not reported here.
- **Main result:** Preliminary results indicate the approach can produce finer-scale precipitation fields; quantitative skill is not available here.
- **Open work:** Fuller validation over more events and regions, and coupling with hydrological models.
- **Issues:** Preliminary study; performance for extreme precipitation and transferability are not established.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Conditional diffusion models for downscaling & bias correction of Earth system model precipitation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14416)
Aich et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 36 citations.

- **Main goal:** Simultaneously bias-corrects and downscales Earth system model precipitation to improve extremes and spatial structure.
- **Architecture:** Conditional diffusion model trained to reverse a mapping of observational and ESM fields to a shared unbiased embedding space.
- **Data:** Observational precipitation data for training only; applied to ESM precipitation; specific products not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Preserves spatial patterns above a chosen scale with statistical fidelity and outperforms statistical and deep learning baselines, especially for extremes.
- **Open work:** Applying to other ESMs, variables and regions without retraining; multivariate correction.
- **Issues:** Correction below the chosen spatial scale relies on the embedding assumption; evaluation against observations in historical period only.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Transferability and explainability of deep learning emulators for regional climate model projections: Perspectives for future applications](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03378)
Baño-Medina et al. (2023), *arXiv*. 36 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses transferability and physical consistency of deep learning emulators of regional climate models across periods, scenarios and driving GCMs.
- **Architecture:** Deep learning RCM emulators under Perfect Prognosis and Model Output Statistics training setups, analysed with explainable AI (XAI); specific network family not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Short regional climate model simulations driven by global climate models for training; future periods, scenarios and other GCMs for transfer tests.
- **Main result:** Both approaches reproduce some RCM climatological properties across periods and scenarios; PP learns physically meaningful patterns while MOS is GCM-dependent; both fail at transfer to other GCMs.
- **Open work:** Strategies to handle GCM-dependent biases so emulators can build multi-GCM RCM ensembles.
- **Issues:** Hard transferability fails due to GCM biases; limited emulator applicability for ensemble generation.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Hydrology and Earth System Sciences Discussions Comparison of Data-driven Methods for Downscaling Ensemble Weather Forecasts
Liu et al. (2006), *Venue not recorded*. 36 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscaling ensemble weather forecasts to local daily variables for hydrological forecasting by comparing data-driven methods.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of data-driven downscaling methods, including neural network approaches; the specific models are not specified here.
- **Data:** Ensemble numerical weather forecasts and local station observations in a Canadian watershed; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The comparison identifies which data-driven method downscales precipitation and temperature most skilfully; numbers are not available here.
- **Open work:** Using downscaled ensembles to drive hydrological ensemble streamflow forecasts.
- **Issues:** Downscaled precipitation is typically harder to reproduce than temperature; results are basin-specific.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Machine learning emulation of a local-scale UK climate model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16116)
Addison et al. (2022), *arXiv*. 33 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generate realistic high-resolution UK precipitation projections cheaply, since convection-permitting climate simulations needed for extreme rainfall are very computationally expensive.
- **Architecture:** Conditional diffusion model (score-based deep generative model) that samples high-resolution rainfall conditioned on low-resolution fields such as relative vorticity, with self-learnt location-specific inputs.
- **Data:** Met Office UK convection-permitting local-scale climate model (UKCP18 2.2 km) precipitation as target, conditioned on coarsened low-resolution variables from the same simulations.
- **Main result:** First ML model shown to produce realistic high-resolution rainfall samples from a convection-resolving physical model; sample quantiles and time means match the high-resolution simulation well.
- **Open work:** Condition on GCM output rather than coarsened CPM fields, add more predictors, and test the climate-change signal and extreme-event statistics more thoroughly.
- **Issues:** Early workshop-stage results in a perfect-model setting; transfer to real GCM inputs and preservation of future changes are not demonstrated, and sampling is costlier than deterministic emulators.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [On the suitability of a convolutional neural network based RCM-emulator for fine spatio-temporal precipitation](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-024-07350-8)
Doury et al. (2024), *Climate Dynamics*. 33 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assess whether a neural-network RCM-emulator can reproduce fine-scale daily precipitation, allowing cheap high-resolution ensembles of regional climate projections.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network RCM-emulator (U-Net-type architecture from Doury et al. 2023) trained with a novel asymmetric loss to reproduce the full precipitation distribution.
- **Data:** Simulations of a 12 km CNRM regional climate model (ALADIN) driven by several GCMs, in a perfect-model framework; low-resolution predictors from upscaled RCM fields, then a GCM downscaling showcase.
- **Main result:** Excellent spatio-temporal correlation with the RCM, good dry-day counts and 99th quantiles, transferability across driving GCMs, and clear added value over GCMs for heavy precipitation structure.
- **Open work:** Establish a relevant evaluation framework for applying the emulator directly to GCM simulations and recover missing highest-frequency spatial details.
- **Issues:** Evaluated mainly in perfect-model conditions; fine-scale details are smoothed and GCM application lacks a reference truth for validation.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Precipitation Downscaling with Spatiotemporal Video Diffusion](https://doi.org/10.52202/079017-1795)
Srivastava et al. (2023), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 32 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales precipitation while capturing the conditional distribution needed for reliable ensembles and unbiased extremes.
- **Architecture:** Deterministic downscaler followed by a temporally conditioned video diffusion model that adds stochastic high-frequency detail.
- **Data:** FV3GFS global atmosphere model output, coarse versus fine resolution; case regions include California and the Himalayas.
- **Main result:** Outperforms six state-of-the-art baselines in CRPS, MSE and precipitation distribution metrics.
- **Open work:** Applying to observations or other climate models and testing in climate change settings.
- **Issues:** Trained and evaluated within one model (perfect-model setting); computational cost of diffusion sampling; limited regions examined.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A simple hybrid statistical–dynamical downscaling method for emulating regional climate models over Western Europe. Evaluation, application, and role of added value?](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-022-06552-2)
Boé et al. (2022), *Climate Dynamics*. 32 citations.

- **Main goal:** Emulate regional climate models cheaply with a hybrid statistical-dynamical downscaling method that avoids the stationarity assumption of conventional statistical downscaling.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML statistical method: constructed analogues algorithm learned between low- and high-resolution climate projections, in GCM/RCM or RCM/RCM emulation modes.
- **Data:** Large ensemble of regional climate projections over Western Europe (EURO-CORDEX-type GCM/RCM pairs) in a perfect-model framework.
- **Main result:** Reproduces climate change signals very well and outperforms conventional constructed-analogue downscaling; RCM/RCM mode retains the GCM large-scale signal whereas GCM/RCM mode does not.
- **Open work:** Determine whether large-scale differences between RCMs and driving GCMs reflect real RCM added value or other causes.
- **Issues:** Results depend strongly on the GCM/RCM pair used for learning; evaluation is within a perfect-model framework.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [CliGAN: A Structurally Sensitive Convolutional Neural Network Model for Statistical Downscaling of Precipitation from Multi-Model Ensembles](https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202010.0502.v1)
Chaudhuri et al. (2020), *Water*. 31 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscale annual maximum precipitation from multi-model CMIP6 ensembles to regional gridded data, preserving spatial structure that point-based losses miss.
- **Architecture:** CliGAN, a Wasserstein generative adversarial network (GAN) with a convolutional encoder-dense decoder generator and similar critic, using adversarial, MS-SSIM structural and Nash-Sutcliffe content losses.
- **Data:** Annual maximum precipitation from multiple CMIP6 atmosphere-ocean GCMs as input; regional gridded observational precipitation as target (region not reported in the abstract).
- **Main result:** Structural loss helps reproduce regional precipitation characteristics; point-based error functions alone are insufficient for realistic regional patterns.
- **Open work:** Use structural loss functions more widely in CNN-based downscaling and extend to other precipitation indices.
- **Issues:** Targets only annual maxima; quantitative skill and performance under future climate extrapolation are not reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Machine Learning Emulation of Precipitation From km‐Scale UK Regional Climate Simulations Using a Diffusion Model](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025ms005140)
Addison et al. (2024), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 29 citations.

- **Main goal:** Emulates precipitation from an expensive 2.2 km convection-permitting regional climate model at much lower cost.
- **Architecture:** CPMGEM: conditional diffusion model downscaling 60 km GCM-scale inputs to 8.8 km daily precipitation, stochastic sampling.
- **Data:** UKCP Local simulations over England and Wales, 1980-2080, high-emissions scenario.
- **Main result:** Matches CPM spatial structure and intensity distribution, shows skill for extremes with return periods up to about 100 years, and transfers from perfect-model to GCM inputs.
- **Open work:** Applying to large GCM ensembles and other GCMs/scenarios to sample uncertainty, and correcting the climate change magnitude error.
- **Issues:** Exhibits error in the magnitude of 21st-century change; daily means only; single region and single emission scenario.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [On the limitations of deep learning for statistical downscaling of climate change projections: The transferability and the extrapolation issues](https://doi.org/10.1002/asl.1195)
Hernanz et al. (2023), *Atmospheric Science Letters*. 28 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assess the transferability and extrapolation of deep learning downscaling of climate projections when used as RCM emulators.
- **Architecture:** U-Net convolutional neural network (UNET) compared with interpolation and linear regression emulators in two pseudo-reality experiments.
- **Data:** RCA4 regional climate model at 0.11° over a complex Pyrenees domain driven by CNRM-CM5, with predictors from the upscaled RCM or the ESM; other ESMs for transfer tests.
- **Main result:** UNET generalizes poorly to ESMs other than the training one, as does the linear method; under extrapolation it shows warm-extreme biases up to 5°C, larger than linear regression.
- **Open work:** Develop training strategies with multiple ESMs and future climates to improve generalization and extrapolation.
- **Issues:** Single RCM and region and mainly temperature; results may not generalize to other variables or architectures.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Data-driven topo-climatic mapping with machine learning methods](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-008-9339-y)
Pozdnoukhov et al. (2009), *Natural Hazards*. 27 citations.

- **Main goal:** Maps climatic variables such as temperature over complex terrain, where relationships with topography are nonlinear and scale-dependent.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning regression including support vector regression (support vector machines) using many multi-scale topographic features derived from a digital elevation model.
- **Data:** Meteorological station measurements (e.g. temperature) in Switzerland with DEM-derived terrain features.
- **Main result:** Machine learning captures nonlinear terrain effects such as temperature inversions better than linear geostatistical approaches; exact scores not reproduced here.
- **Open work:** Extension to other variables, operational mapping and uncertainty estimation.
- **Issues:** Sparse stations in high terrain; feature selection affects results; limited uncertainty quantification.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Enabling Smart Dynamical Downscaling of Extreme Precipitation Events With Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020gl090309)
Shi (2020), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 24 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces the cost of kilometre-scale dynamical downscaling of extreme convective precipitation by selecting only the GCM periods likely to produce extremes.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) classifying large-scale circulation data to select a subset for dynamical downscaling (smart dynamical downscaling).
- **Data:** Circulation and precipitation data for three subtropical/tropical regions for training; tested on different reanalysis datasets.
- **Main result:** CNNs retain 92 to 98 % of extreme events (above 99th percentile) while filtering out 88 to 95 % of data; skill drops modestly in the subtropics and sharply in the deep tropics on other reanalyses, worst case 62 % retained.
- **Open work:** Improving generalization in the deep tropics and applying to GCM projections of future climate.
- **Issues:** Sensitivity to dataset shift, especially in the deep tropics; missed extremes bias downscaled statistics.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Relationship Between Monthly Atmospheric Circulation Patterns and Precipitation: Fuzzy Logic and Regression Approaches](https://doi.org/10.1029/96wr00289)
Özelkan et al. (1996), *Water Resources Research*. 23 citations.

- **Main goal:** Relates monthly atmospheric circulation patterns to precipitation to support downscaling and water resources assessment.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic rule-based model compared with regression approaches linking circulation pattern frequencies to precipitation.
- **Data:** Monthly atmospheric circulation pattern classifications and station precipitation records; region details not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; the fuzzy rule-based approach is compared with regression for reproducing monthly precipitation.
- **Open work:** Use for climate change downscaling and extension to other variables and regions.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; monthly aggregation hides extremes, and fuzzy rule definition involves subjective choices.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [On the use of convolutional neural networks for downscaling daily temperatures over southern South America in a climate change scenario](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-023-06912-6)
Balmaceda-Huarte et al. (2023), *Climate Dynamics*. 22 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses convolutional neural networks for statistical downscaling of daily temperatures over southern South America and their behaviour under climate change, as the title states.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural networks (CNN) for statistical downscaling; further architectural details are not available without the abstract.
- **Data:** Not reported here; likely large-scale predictors from reanalysis and GCM output with station or gridded temperature observations, but unconfirmed.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract (abstract unavailable).
- **Open work:** Not reported in the abstract.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; extrapolation of CNN downscaling to future warmer climates is a general concern for this approach.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Potential for machine learning emulators to augment regional climate simulations in provision of local climate change information](https://doi.org/10.1175/bams-d-24-0114.1)
Kendon et al. (2025), *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society*. 21 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses whether machine learning emulators can augment costly high-resolution regional climate simulations to produce local climate change information quickly and cheaply for climate services.
- **Architecture:** Review and perspective that explores the skill of ML-based regional climate model emulators across a range of architectures and proposes validation methods for them.
- **Data:** Regional and km-scale climate simulation ensembles from coordinated international initiatives; the specific simulations and domains are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** ML emulation shows promise to augment regional-to-local climate projections within 5-10 years, but issues remain with extremes, multivariate coherence, climate memory and transfer to out-of-sample global models.
- **Open work:** Integrate climate expertise into emulator development, run the highest-resolution and most complex simulations affordable for training, and sample the full range of conditions including high-end scenarios.
- **Issues:** Perspective paper with few quantitative results in the abstract; emulator readiness depends on unresolved extremes, multivariate consistency and out-of-sample GCM generalization.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [EnScale: Temporally‐Consistent Multivariate Generative Downscaling via Proper Scoring Rules](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025ms005593)
Schillinger et al. (2025), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 20 citations.

- **Main goal:** Emulates expensive regional climate models by learning the full conditional distribution of high-resolution RCM fields given coarse GCM output.
- **Architecture:** EnScale: a two-step generative model trained with the energy score (a proper scoring rule), first correcting large-scale GCM mismatch then super-resolving with sparse local stochastic layers; EnScale-t adds temporal consistency.
- **Data:** Multiple pairs of GCM and corresponding RCM simulations over Central Europe; variables are temperature, precipitation, solar radiation and wind.
- **Main result:** Competitive with state-of-the-art ML downscaling across calibration, spatial and temporal structure, extremes and multivariate dependence, at about one order of magnitude lower computational cost.
- **Open work:** Test transfer to other regions and GCM-RCM combinations, and use the evaluation framework as a common benchmark for RCM emulators.
- **Issues:** Restricted to Central Europe and to the GCM-RCM pairs seen in training; extrapolation to unseen GCMs and future climates is not demonstrated in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [2007 Special Issue: Nonlinear analog predictor analysis: A coupled neural network/analog model for climate downscaling](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2007.04.002)
Cannon (2007), *Neural Networks*. 20 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales climate variables by coupling a neural network with an analog model so that predictors are optimized for analog selection.
- **Architecture:** Nonlinear analog predictor analysis (NLAPA): a multilayer perceptron neural network whose outputs feed an analog (nearest neighbour) model, trained to maximize analog performance.
- **Data:** Synthetic test datasets and real climate downscaling datasets (station precipitation and temperature); details not reported.
- **Main result:** NLAPA outperforms analog models using raw or linearly transformed predictors and preserves realistic multivariate relationships.
- **Open work:** Extension to more variables and sites and assessment under climate change projections.
- **Issues:** Analog methods cannot produce values outside the historical record; training is computationally intensive.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Satellite Observations Guided Diffusion Model for Accurate Meteorological States at Arbitrary Resolution](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvpr52734.2025.02614)
Tu et al. (2025), *Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition*. 19 citations.

- **Main goal:** Obtains accurate high-resolution surface meteorological states at arbitrary locations by downscaling reanalysis with guidance from satellite and station observations.
- **Architecture:** SGD: a conditional diffusion model with attention-based fusion of satellite observations, zero-shot guided sampling with optimizable convolutional kernels for the upscaling operator, and patch-based sampling for arbitrary resolution.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis for pre-training conditioned on GridSat satellite observations; weather station observations used as sampling guidance.
- **Main result:** Achieves accurate downscaling of meteorological states to 6.25 km resolution; specific error statistics are not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Extend to more variables, regions and finer resolutions, and assess performance for extremes.
- **Issues:** Relies on ERA5 as training target and on station availability for guidance; diffusion sampling is computationally expensive.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Predicting Snowfall from Synoptic Circulation: A Comparison of Linear Regression and Neural Network Methodologies](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-011-1122-5_5)
McGinnis (1994), *Venue not recorded*. 19 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts snowfall from synoptic atmospheric circulation, comparing linear regression and neural network approaches for downscaling.
- **Architecture:** Neural network compared with linear regression mapping synoptic circulation fields to snowfall.
- **Data:** Synoptic circulation fields and station snowfall observations; details not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; the comparison assesses whether neural networks capture nonlinear circulation-snowfall relations better than regression.
- **Open work:** Use for climate change scenarios and other regions.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; downscaling assumes stationary circulation-snowfall relations.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Testing the performance of three nonlinear methods of time seriesanalysis for prediction and downscaling of European daily temperatures](https://doi.org/10.5194/npg-12-979-2005)
Mikšovský et al. (2005), *Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics*. 18 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares nonlinear time-series methods with linear regression for short-term prediction and statistical downscaling of European daily temperatures.
- **Architecture:** Local linear models, multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network and radial basis function (RBF) neural network, benchmarked against multiple linear regression.
- **Data:** Daily mean, minimum and maximum temperatures from 25 European stations as predictands; NCEP/NCAR reanalysis fields as downscaling predictors.
- **Main result:** No nonlinear method is clearly superior, but all beat linear regression in most cases; nonlinearity is strong over most of Europe, weak in the Mediterranean and North Africa, and stronger in winter.
- **Open work:** Testing other predictors and variables such as precipitation, and explaining the geographic and seasonal pattern of nonlinearity.
- **Issues:** Only temperature is studied and gains over linear regression are modest; MLPs suffer from practical training disadvantages, and downscaling is tested on reanalysis rather than GCM output.

### [Are Deep Learning Methods Suitable for Downscaling Global Climate Projections? An Intercomparison for Temperature and Precipitation over Spain](https://doi.org/10.1175/aies-d-24-0121.1)
González-Abad et al. (2024), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 16 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses whether deep learning perfect-prognosis downscaling models can plausibly extrapolate to future emission scenarios.
- **Architecture:** Intercomparison of existing deep learning downscaling models, mainly convolutional neural networks, under a common experimental framework with multiple training replicas.
- **Data:** Observation-based training for minimum and maximum temperature and precipitation over Spain; applied to global climate projections. Specific datasets are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Identifies differences in extrapolation capability and sensitivity to training replicas across models; detailed numbers are not given in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Develop methods that extrapolate more reliably to unseen future conditions and support operational use.
- **Issues:** Limited to Spain and three variables; extrapolation cannot be fully verified against future observations.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Neural network based daily precipitation generator (NNGEN-P)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-006-0184-y)
Boulanger et al. (2006), *Climate Dynamics*. 16 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generates realistic daily precipitation series consistent with given larger-scale or monthly climate information, for impact studies and downscaling.
- **Architecture:** Neural network based stochastic daily precipitation generator (NNGEN-P) using a neural network to estimate the parameters of daily precipitation distributions.
- **Data:** Daily station precipitation records (South America); details not reported here.
- **Main result:** NNGEN-P reproduces daily precipitation statistics such as wet-day frequency and intensity distribution; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Application to climate model projections for downscaling.

- *Basis: assessment*

### [Regional climate risk assessment from climate models using probabilistic machine learning](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-026-01308-7)
Wan et al. (2024), *Nature Machine Intelligence*. 15 citations.

- **Main goal:** Bridges the resolution gap between coarse climate projections and fine-scale information needed for regional climate risk assessment, including compound extremes, without temporally paired training data.
- **Architecture:** GenFocal, a probabilistic generative AI framework (diffusion-based generative model) that debiases and downscales coarse climate model output to fine-scale weather without paired simulated-observed events.
- **Data:** Coarse free-running climate model projections as input and fine-scale reanalysis or observations as target; specific products and resolutions are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Generates statistically accurate fine-scale weather, synthesizes long-lived hazards such as heatwaves and tropical cyclones even when poorly represented in coarse projections, and samples rare high-impact events more accurately than leading methods.
- **Open work:** Extend to more regions, variables and climate models, and use the generated ensembles for adaptation and resilience planning.
- **Issues:** Statistical (unpaired) training cannot be verified event by event; fidelity under future climates relies on distributional assumptions and on the quality of the reference data.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [ORBIT-2: Scaling Exascale Vision Foundation Models for Weather and Climate Downscaling](https://doi.org/10.1145/3712285.3771989)
Wang et al. (2025), *International Conference on Software Composition*. 15 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides robust, generalizable and scalable AI downscaling of weather and climate fields to hyper-resolution for regional decision making.
- **Architecture:** ORBIT-2, a vision transformer foundation model using a Residual Slim ViT (Reslim) with Bayesian regularization and TILES tile-wise sequence scaling that reduces self-attention cost from quadratic to linear.
- **Data:** Global climate and weather data for downscaling down to 0.9 km; evaluated on 7 km resolution benchmarks against observation data; specific datasets are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Scales to 10 billion parameters on 65,536 GPUs with up to 4.1 ExaFLOPS sustained and 74–98% strong scaling efficiency; reaches R2 of 0.98–0.99 against observations on 7 km benchmarks.
- **Open work:** Demonstrate generalization across variables and geographies in operational downscaling and evaluate physical consistency at hyper-resolution.
- **Issues:** Emphasis on computational scaling; R2 summarizes skill poorly for extremes and fine-scale structure; requires exascale resources.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Emerging AI-based weather prediction models as downscaling tools](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17977)
Koldunov et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 13 citations.

- **Main goal:** Uses existing AI weather prediction systems to perform global downscaling of low-resolution climate model output.
- **Architecture:** Off-the-shelf AI-NWP models run one day ahead from low-resolution initial conditions to produce high-resolution fields; specific models and network families are not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Smoothed ERA5 and low-resolution CMIP6 model fields as initial conditions; evaluated on 2-metre temperature over year-long periods.
- **Main result:** AI-NWP produces detailed fields resembling training-data resolution after one-day lead and may bias-correct climate model output toward observations.
- **Open work:** Use downscaled data for local climate information or as boundary conditions for dynamical downscaling.
- **Issues:** Only 2-metre temperature assessed; AI-NWP trained on present-day ERA5 may not represent future climates.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Downscaling with AI reveals the large role of internal variability in fine-scale projections of climate extremes](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-026-08269-y)
Rampal et al. (2025), *Climate Dynamics*. 12 citations.

- **Main goal:** Overcomes the cost of dynamical downscaling, which limits ensemble size, to characterise fine-scale future changes in rare precipitation extremes over New Zealand.
- **Architecture:** Generative-AI downscaling emulator of a regional climate model; the specific generative network family is not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Global climate model projections downscaled over New Zealand, trained against regional dynamical downscaling; exact GCM ensemble and RCM not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** End-of-century daily precipitation extremes increase about 5.6%/°C for annual extremes and 9%/°C for 100-year events; internal variability of extremes grows nearly twice Clausius-Clapeyron scaling and dominates uncertainty.
- **Open work:** Apply large AI-downscaled ensembles to other regions and variables, and quantify how many members are needed for robust fine-scale extreme projections.
- **Issues:** Single region; conclusions depend on the emulator faithfully reproducing the regional model's extreme tails under warming beyond the training climate.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Climate Analysis, Modelling, and Regional Downscaling Using Self‐Organizing Maps](https://doi.org/10.1002/9780470021699.ch8)
Hewitson (2008), *Venue not recorded*. 11 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews the use of self-organizing maps for climate analysis, modelling and regional downscaling.
- **Architecture:** Review of self-organizing maps (SOM) for climate classification and downscaling.
- **Data:** Examples using reanalysis and GCM output; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Self-organizing maps are presented as a useful tool for synoptic classification and downscaling.
- **Open work:** Broader application in climate change downscaling.
- **Issues:** Choice of map size and interpretation is subjective.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [An intercomparison of generative machine learning methods for downscaling precipitation at fine spatial scales](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13987)
Rampal et al. (2025), *arXiv*. 8 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares generative ML methods for downscaling daily precipitation, including their ability to reproduce climate change signals of extremes.
- **Architecture:** Intercomparison of generative adversarial networks (GANs), flow matching and diffusion models in multiple configurations, with higher-order ODE solvers to reduce sampling steps.
- **Data:** Regional climate model (RCM) daily precipitation simulations over New Zealand for present-day and future climates.
- **Main result:** All methods are competitive; diffusion and flow matching give higher fidelity and better-calibrated ensembles than under-dispersive GANs; most underestimate end-of-century extreme precipitation change, which only one GAN and one flow-matching setup reproduce.
- **Open work:** Improving extrapolation of climate change signals and evaluating across comprehensive metrics.
- **Issues:** Emulates a single RCM over one region; perfect-model framework; visual realism and standard skill do not guarantee correct change signals.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Downscaling large-scale circulation to local winter climate using neural network techniques
Perez et al. (1998), *Venue not recorded*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales large-scale atmospheric circulation to local winter climate variables for regional climate studies.
- **Architecture:** Neural network statistical downscaling model linking large-scale circulation predictors to local climate.
- **Data:** Large-scale circulation fields and local station winter climate records; specific region and datasets not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Reports that neural network downscaling captures local winter climate variability from circulation; skill figures not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Applying the downscaling to climate model scenarios.
- **Issues:** Stationarity of predictor-predictand relations is assumed; author and region metadata are unclear.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Universal Diffusion-Based Probabilistic Downscaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11893)
Molinaro et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Creates a single model-agnostic downscaler that turns deterministic coarse weather forecasts into probabilistic high-resolution forecasts without per-model fine-tuning.
- **Architecture:** Conditional diffusion model trained on paired coarse (~25 km) inputs and high-resolution targets, applied zero-shot to forecasts from multiple upstream models.
- **Data:** High-resolution (~5 km) regional reanalysis targets; downscaled forecasts from several AI and NWP systems evaluated against in situ station observations up to 90 h lead.
- **Main result:** Ensemble mean of downscaled forecasts consistently improves on each model's raw deterministic forecast, with larger gains in probabilistic skill (CRPS).
- **Open work:** Extend to more variables, longer leads and other regions, and combine with ensemble upstream forecasts.
- **Issues:** Focused on near-surface variables and one region; zero-shot transfer may degrade for upstream models with very different biases; regional reanalysis product not named in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [HourGlass: A probabilistic data-driven temporal downscaler for global and regional weather forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11457)
Ingstad et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces temporally consistent, realistic hourly forecasts from 6-hourly data-driven forecasting systems, avoiding error accumulation of direct hourly forecasting.
- **Architecture:** HourGlass, a probabilistic data-driven temporal downscaling model trained with CRPS-variant losses; network family not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Trained on forecast trajectories of ECMWF AIFS-Single and AIFS-ENS (global) and MET Norway's Bris stretched-grid ensemble (regional); verified against observations.
- **Main result:** Retains the skill of the underlying systems while producing temporally coherent hourly forecasts with realistic small-scale variability; precipitation extremes remain underestimated.
- **Open work:** Improving hourly precipitation extremes and operational deployment for regional and global products.
- **Issues:** Underestimates the most intense precipitation; skill bounded by the parent 6-hourly forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Intelligent Shanghai Typhoon Model (ISTM): A Diffusion‐Based Downscaling Emulator From AIFS to Kilometer‐Scale Regional Reanalysis for Typhoon Forecasts](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025jh001072)
Niu et al. (2026), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Machine Learning and Computation*. 2 citations.

- **Main goal:** Addresses the systematic underestimation of typhoon intensity by AI weather models trained on coarse ERA5 by downscaling their forecasts to kilometre scale.
- **Architecture:** Intelligent Shanghai Typhoon Model (ISTM): regression–residual emulator in which a deterministic network predicts the conditional mean and a conditional diffusion model stochastically generates residuals; compared with U-Net baselines.
- **Data:** Bespoke 9 km typhoon reanalysis (HiRes) built by dynamically downscaling ERA5 with the Shanghai Typhoon Model (SHTM); fine-tuned to downscale ECMWF AIFS forecasts.
- **Main result:** ISTM improves wind and precipitation intensity and organization over ERA5 and deterministic U-Net; downscaling AIFS keeps track errors comparable while reducing 72 h mean intensity error by about 39.5% relative to AIFS.
- **Open work:** Extending to longer lead times, other basins and ensemble downscaling of AI forecasts.
- **Issues:** Inherits the biases of the SHTM-based HiRes reanalysis used as truth; track errors are bounded by the driving AIFS forecasts; regional focus on typhoons affecting Shanghai's domain.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Applying a standardised benchmarking framework to evaluate AI methods for precipitation downscaling over Australia](https://doi.org/10.1175/aies-d-25-0048.1)
Hobeichi et al. (2025), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 1 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a standardised benchmarking framework to evaluate AI-based precipitation downscaling against regional climate models, which was previously lacking.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark evaluation of three ML downscaling models (generative diffusion model, vision transformer, recurrent neural network) against 24 regional climate model (RCM) simulations using minimum-standard metrics.
- **Data:** Observational precipitation data over Australia and 24 RCM simulations; specific observational products and periods not reported in the abstract. The study releases a benchmark dataset of ML and RCM outputs.
- **Main result:** All three ML models and ten RCMs meet minimum benchmarks for total precipitation, spatial distribution, seasonal cycle and trends; ML models perform comparably to RCMs at much lower computational cost.
- **Open work:** Using ML downscaling to enlarge projection ensembles and improve uncertainty quantification; applying the framework to new AI downscaling methods.
- **Issues:** Minimum-standard metrics focus on mean rainfall characteristics and may not capture extremes or physical consistency; Australia-only evaluation.
- *Basis: abstract*

<a id="da"></a>
## Data assimilation

### [Combining data assimilation and machine learning to emulate a dynamical model from sparse and noisy observations: a case study with the Lorenz 96 model](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-2019-136)
Brajard et al. (2019), *Journal of Computational Science*. 291 citations.

- **Main goal:** Emulate a hidden chaotic dynamical model and predict its future states when only sparse, noisy observations are available.
- **Architecture:** Iterative hybrid of data assimilation (ensemble Kalman filter) and a neural network surrogate: DA produces complete analyses that train the NN, which then serves as the model for the next DA cycle.
- **Data:** Synthetic observations from the 40-variable Lorenz 96 model with varying noise and observation density.
- **Main result:** Method converges and yields forecast skill up to about two Lyapunov times, recovers positive Lyapunov exponents and the power spectrum; skill degrades smoothly with noise but drops abruptly if less than half the domain is observed.
- **Open work:** Scaling to higher-dimensional, more realistic dynamics and merging DA and ML more tightly.
- **Issues:** Low-dimensional toy system; sensitivity to observation coverage; computational cost of iteration in large systems not addressed.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Learning earth system models from observations: machine learning or data assimilation?](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.2020.0089)
Geer (2021), *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences*. 194 citations.

- **Main goal:** Asks whether Earth system models should be learned from observations with ML or with data assimilation, and how the two fields can be unified.
- **Architecture:** Conceptual paper that maps DA and ML onto a common Bayesian network framework, for example showing that 4D-Var is equivalent to a recurrent neural network. Not a new model.
- **Data:** No new data; discussion grounded in operational DA practice (ECMWF) with real, sparse and indirect observations.
- **Main result:** Argues that DA treats uncertainty and prior physical knowledge more rigorously, while ML offers flexible learnable components. Bayesian networks give a practical framework to unify them.
- **Open work:** Build hybrid systems where DA learns model parameters or embedded ML components directly from observations.
- **Issues:** Perspective without quantitative demonstration. Full Bayesian solutions are computationally infeasible, so approximations are needed.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Combining data assimilation and machine learning to infer unresolved scale parametrization](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.2020.0086)
Brajard et al. (2020), *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences*. 158 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learn ML parametrizations of unresolved processes from sparse, noisy observations rather than from dense high-resolution simulations.
- **Architecture:** Two-step hybrid: ensemble Kalman filter data assimilation estimates the full state with a truncated model, then a neural network learns model error (unresolved tendency) as a function of state; the NN is added to the truncated model.
- **Data:** Two-scale Lorenz model and MAOOAM, a reduced-order coupled ocean-atmosphere model, with synthetic noisy and sparse observations.
- **Main result:** The hybrid model forecasts better than the truncated model in both systems and reproduces the attractor significantly better.
- **Open work:** Apply to higher-dimensional and realistic models and iterate DA and learning jointly.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated only in low-order toy models; performance depends on the observation network and DA quality.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Deep Data Assimilation: Integrating Deep Learning with Data Assimilation](https://doi.org/10.3390/app11031114)
Arcucci et al. (2021), *Applied Sciences*. 154 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learn the data assimilation correction so a dynamic model can be improved and used for prediction when observations are unavailable.
- **Architecture:** Deep Data Assimilation: a recurrent neural network trained on model states and DA results learns the misfit function, which is composed with the dynamical model.
- **Data:** Simulated data from a double integral mass-dot system and the Lorenz system.
- **Main result:** Proves the approach reduces model error at each iteration and validates it with examples and a sensitivity study.
- **Open work:** Application to real physics problems with other equations and state variables.
- **Issues:** Only low-dimensional toy systems; no comparison with realistic geophysical DA systems.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Score-based Data Assimilation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10574)
Rozet et al. (2023), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 142 citations.

- **Main goal:** Infers full state trajectories of high-dimensional stochastic dynamical systems from noisy, incomplete observations without relying on costly sequential use of transition dynamics, as needed for ocean and atmosphere data assimilation.
- **Architecture:** Score-based (diffusion) generative model of trajectories whose score is decomposed into scores over short overlapping segments; observations guide sampling only at inference, generating all states non-autoregressively.
- **Data:** Simulated trajectories of toy chaotic systems; the paper's experiments use Lorenz-63 and a 2D Kolmogorov (turbulent) flow.
- **Main result:** Theoretical and empirical evidence shows plausible posterior trajectories under a variety of zero-shot observation operators (e.g. sparse, coarse, or nonlinear observations) without retraining.
- **Open work:** Scaling to realistic, full-dimensional geophysical systems and real observation networks, and calibration checks of posterior uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated only on idealized systems with simulated data; diffusion sampling is computationally heavy and posterior calibration with approximate guidance is not guaranteed.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Bayesian inference of chaotic dynamics by merging data assimilation, machine learning and expectation-maximization](https://doi.org/10.3934/fods.2020004)
Bocquet et al. (2020), *Foundations of Data Science*. 135 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs high-dimensional chaotic dynamics from partial, noisy observations over long time series by combining data assimilation (DA) and machine learning.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian framework unifying DA and ML via expectation-maximization and coordinate descent, jointly estimating the surrogate model, state trajectory and model-error statistics; approximate implementations discussed.
- **Data:** Synthetic observations from two low-order chaotic models with distinct identifiability properties.
- **Main result:** The approach successfully recovers dynamics, states and error statistics in both test models.
- **Open work:** Scaling to realistic geophysical models and observation systems, and handling unresolved scales.
- **Issues:** Tested only on low-order models with synthetic data; computational cost and identifiability in high dimensions remain open.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Data Learning: Integrating Data Assimilation and Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jocs.2021.101525)
Buizza et al. (2021), *Journal of Computational Science*. 121 citations.

- **Main goal:** Integrates data assimilation and machine learning into a combined framework, termed Data Learning (inferred from title).
- **Architecture:** Combination of DA and ML methods; specific architecture not available.
- **Data:** Not reported (abstract unavailable).
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Not reported.
- **Issues:** Cannot be assessed without the abstract; details should be checked in the paper.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Learning Variational Data Assimilation Models and Solvers](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021ms002572)
Fablet et al. (2020), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 110 citations.

- **Main goal:** Uses physics-informed deep learning to revisit variational data assimilation by jointly learning the dynamical prior and the solver of the assimilation problem.
- **Architecture:** End-to-end differentiable variational DA framework: a trainable dynamical/prior model plus a learned (recurrent, gradient-based) solver for the variational cost, trained supervised or unsupervised via automatic differentiation.
- **Data:** Idealized experiments with Lorenz-63 and Lorenz-96 systems with partial, noisy observations.
- **Main result:** Significant gains over classical gradient-based minimization of the variational cost in reconstruction accuracy and optimization cost; variational models based on the true ODEs are not always the best-performing priors.
- **Open work:** Scale to high-dimensional geophysical problems (e.g., satellite sea surface fields) and explore learned assimilation models for operational design.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated only on low-dimensional toy systems; supervised training requires ground-truth states rarely available in practice.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [DiffDA: a diffusion model for weather-scale data assimilation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05932)
Huang et al. (2024), *International Conference on Machine Learning*. 103 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces global atmospheric initial conditions by data assimilation with a machine learning model, replacing costly variational/ensemble DA.
- **Architecture:** Denoising diffusion model whose backbone is the pretrained GraphCast graph neural network; sparse observations and a forecast background guide the sampling.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25°, with simulated sparse observations drawn from ERA5 (under 0.96% of grid points) and GraphCast 48-hour forecasts as background.
- **Main result:** Generates assimilated global states consistent with observations at 0.25°, the highest resolution for ML DA at the time; forecasts from these analyses lose at most 24 h of lead time versus ERA5 initial conditions.
- **Open work:** Applying the method to real, heterogeneous observations (satellite radiances, in situ) and to autoregressive DA cycling for building reanalyses.
- **Issues:** Observations are simulated from ERA5 rather than real instrument data, so observation operators, errors and biases are idealized; skill still trails operational DA.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Data assimilation as a learning tool to infer ordinary differential equation representations of dynamical models](https://doi.org/10.5194/npg-26-143-2019)
Bocquet et al. (2019), *Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics*. 92 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learn the dynamics of a model from partial, noisy observations using data assimilation instead of machine learning libraries, with a view to high-dimensional systems.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian data assimilation framework inferring an ordinary differential equation representation by recursive nonlinear regression, with a local space-wise representation; non-neural, though analogous to deep architectures.
- **Data:** Several chaotic discrete and continuous toy models of various dimensions (e.g. Lorenz-96-type), with and without observation noise.
- **Main result:** The method identifies or improves model dynamics, builds surrogate models and produces forecasts from observations alone; stability analysis clarifies its strengths and limits.
- **Open work:** Scaling to realistic geophysical models and combining with neural-network surrogates.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated only on low-order chaotic models; numerical stability limits the method.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Supervised learning from noisy observations: Combining machine-learning techniques with data assimilation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physd.2021.132911)
Gottwald et al. (2020), *Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena*. 87 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learns forecast models of chaotic systems from noisy observations by combining machine learning and data assimilation.
- **Architecture:** Random feature map surrogate model learned sequentially within an ensemble Kalman filter.
- **Data:** Synthetic noisy observations from low-dimensional chaotic and multi-scale systems (e.g. Lorenz-63).
- **Main result:** The learned model has remarkably good forecast skill and low cost, yields reliable probabilistic ensembles, and can learn effective closures in multi-scale systems.
- **Open work:** Scaling to high-dimensional systems, e.g. using localization.
- **Issues:** Low-dimensional toy systems only; random feature models may not scale to geophysical dimensions.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Machine Learning, Deepest Learning: Statistical Data Assimilation Problems](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.01415)
Abarbanel et al. (2017), *arXiv*. 83 citations.

- **Main goal:** Formulate a strong equivalence between machine learning and statistical data assimilation to transfer methods between the fields.
- **Architecture:** Theoretical framework mapping network layers to time in data assimilation, including a continuous-layer "deepest learning" limit with Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations; not a specific network family.
- **Data:** Simple illustrative models from both machine learning and data assimilation.
- **Main result:** Deeper networks correspond to finer temporal resolution; the Hamiltonian view justifies backpropagation, and data assimilation methods help find global minima.
- **Open work:** Applying the equivalence to large practical networks and geophysical data assimilation problems.
- **Issues:** Mostly theoretical with simple numerical tests; practical benefits at scale are not shown.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Latent space data assimilation by using deep learning](https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.4153)
Peyron et al. (2021), *Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society*. 82 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces the cost of data assimilation in the big-data era by performing assimilation in a low-dimensional learned latent space.
- **Architecture:** An autoencoder provides the latent space. An ensemble transform Kalman filter with model error (ETKF-Q) runs in that space, and a surrogate neural network propagates latent dynamics (ETKF-Q-L).
- **Data:** Synthetic experiments with an augmented Lorenz 96 system that has a known latent structure.
- **Main result:** ETKF-Q-L lowers computational cost and gives better accuracy than the standard ETKF-Q on the test system.
- **Open work:** Test on higher-dimensional, realistic geophysical models and on systems without a clean latent structure.
- **Issues:** The toy system is designed to have a latent structure, which favours the method; transfer to real NWP is undemonstrated.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Building Tangent‐Linear and Adjoint Models for Data Assimilation With Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021ms002521)
Hatfield et al. (2021), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 80 citations.

- **Main goal:** Simplifies construction of tangent-linear and adjoint models for 4D-Var by using differentiable neural network emulators of parameterizations.
- **Architecture:** Neural network emulator of the non-orographic gravity wave drag scheme, differentiated to obtain tangent-linear and adjoint versions.
- **Data:** ECMWF IFS parameterization inputs/outputs; 4D-Var assimilation experiments.
- **Main result:** NN-derived tangent-linear and adjoint models pass standard consistency tests and work successfully in 4D-Var data assimilation.
- **Open work:** Applying to more complex, nonsmooth schemes (convection, clouds) and operational maintenance.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated for a single, relatively smooth scheme; accuracy depends on emulator quality and smoothness of NN gradients.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Integrating Recurrent Neural Networks With Data Assimilation for Scalable Data‐Driven State Estimation](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021ms002843)
Penny et al. (2021), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 62 citations.

- **Main goal:** Perform fully data-driven state estimation by integrating ML surrogate models into the data assimilation cycle.
- **Architecture:** Recurrent neural networks (reservoir computing type) replace the forecast model, forecast error covariance, and tangent linear and adjoint models; DA updates the hidden/reservoir state; domain localization and parallelization for scaling.
- **Data:** Synthetic observations from chaotic test systems such as the Lorenz-96 model.
- **Main result:** RNN-DA can estimate the system state for repeated initialization of short-term forecasts without a numerical model, and scales to higher dimensions with localization.
- **Open work:** Application to realistic NWP-scale models and real observations.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated on idealized, low-dimensional systems with synthetic observations; robustness to model error and real observation networks untested.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Generative Data Assimilation of Sparse Weather Station Observations at Kilometer Scales](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024ms004505)
Manshausen et al. (2024), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 60 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether score-based generative data assimilation can map sparse weather-station observations to full km-scale atmospheric states.
- **Architecture:** Unconditional diffusion model trained on analysis snapshots, combined with Score-based Data Assimilation (SDA) to condition on sparse observations at inference without retraining.
- **Data:** High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) analyses over a central US testbed, and surface weather station observations.
- **Main result:** Generated precipitation and wind fields show plausible structures such as gust fronts; assimilating 40 stations gives about 10% lower RMSE at withheld stations than the HRRR baseline.
- **Open work:** Combining stronger regional state generators with more in situ, ground-based and satellite data streams, and improving ensemble calibration.
- **Issues:** Proof of concept with a small station network; ensemble DA estimates are under-dispersive; no time dimension or forecast cycling is shown.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [FuXi-DA: a generalized deep learning data assimilation framework for assimilating satellite observations](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01039-3)
Xu et al. (2024), *npj Climate and Atmospheric Science*. 57 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a deep-learning data assimilation framework that ingests satellite observations to improve analyses and forecasts of ML weather models.
- **Architecture:** Deep learning DA network that fuses a background field from the FuXi forecast model with satellite observations in feature space to produce an analysis increment.
- **Data:** Advanced Geosynchronous Radiation Imager (AGRI) radiances from Fengyun-4B, FuXi background forecasts, and ERA5 as reference.
- **Main result:** Assimilating AGRI data consistently reduces analysis errors and significantly improves FuXi forecast performance; analysis increments are consistent with atmospheric physics.
- **Open work:** Extending to additional observation types (microwave, conventional, polar orbiters) and cycling DA.
- **Issues:** Single geostationary instrument only; evaluated within the FuXi system against reanalysis rather than an operational DA comparison.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A comparison of combined data assimilation and machine learning methods for offline and online model error correction](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jocs.2021.101468)
Farchi et al. (2021), *Journal of Computational Science*. 57 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares ways of combining ML and data assimilation to learn corrections to a physical model's error, offline and online.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid surrogate models with a neural-network correction added either to the model resolvent (integrated step) or inside the tendencies (requires adjoint); online learning formulated as a weak-constraint 4D-Var variant.
- **Data:** Two-scale Lorenz model with sparse, noisy observations.
- **Main result:** Both corrections give similar long-range forecast accuracy, but tendency correction is much better in DA experiments; online learning extracts all information from sparse, noisy observations.
- **Open work:** Implement in operational systems (e.g., IFS) where adjoints exist.
- **Issues:** Toy model; the tendency correction needs an adjoint of the physical model.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Combining machine learning and data assimilation to forecast dynamical systems from noisy partial observations](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0066080)
Gottwald et al. (2021), *Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science*. 57 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learns the propagator of a dynamical system from partial, noisy observations cheaply.
- **Architecture:** RAFDA: random feature map network trained sequentially within an ensemble Kalman filter data assimilation procedure, using delay coordinates via Takens embedding.
- **Data:** Low-dimensional chaotic test systems (e.g., Lorenz-63) with partial noisy observations.
- **Main result:** RAFDA outperforms standard random feature maps trained on batch data in forecasting.
- **Open work:** Scale to high-dimensional geophysical systems.
- **Issues:** Toy problems only; random feature models may need many features in high dimensions.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Reduced Order Deep Data Assimilation model](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physd.2020.132615)
Casas et al. (2020), *Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena*. 55 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves CFD air-pollution forecasts with data assimilation at reduced cost by learning the DA correction with a neural network in a reduced space.
- **Architecture:** Reduced Order Deep Data Assimilation (RODDA): reduced-order model plus data assimilation, with a neural network (family not specified in the abstract) learning the model–DA misfit.
- **Data:** Fluidity CFD simulation of air pollution in South London (UK) with observed data assimilated.
- **Main result:** The coupled CFD+RODDA forecasts are closer to observations and faster than a classic prediction–correction cycle with standard DA; it can also predict future observations.
- **Open work:** Applying the workflow to other physical models and domains with sufficient temporal data.
- **Issues:** Single case study; the neural correction depends on the DA results it was trained on; validation details are limited in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Deep Generative Data Assimilation in Multimodal Setting](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw63382.2024.00050)
Qu et al. (2024), *2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)*. 54 citations.

- **Main goal:** Emulates data assimilation with deep generative models to fuse multimodal observations without linear-Gaussian assumptions.
- **Architecture:** SLAMS: score-based latent diffusion model for data assimilation, framing DA as observation-conditioned state generation.
- **Data:** In-situ weather station data and satellite imagery assimilated to calibrate global vertical temperature profiles; specific products not named in the abstract.
- **Main result:** SLAMS is robust in low-resolution, noisy and sparse data settings in ablations; described as the first deep generative multimodal DA on real-world data.
- **Open work:** Coupling with forecast models in cycled assimilation and extension to more variables for Earth system models.
- **Issues:** Workshop-scale study; comparison against operational DA systems and cycled forecast impact is not reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [FengWu-4DVar: Coupling the Data-driven Weather Forecasting Model with 4D Variational Assimilation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.12455)
Xiao et al. (2023), *arXiv*. 51 citations.

- **Main goal:** Couple a data-driven weather model with data assimilation so ML forecasting does not depend on traditional analysis systems.
- **Architecture:** FengWu-4DVar: the FengWu AI forecast model inside a 4D-Var assimilation cycle, using auto-differentiation instead of a hand-coded adjoint.
- **Data:** Simulated observations (derived from reanalysis) in cycling experiments.
- **Main result:** Generates reasonable analysis fields and accurate, efficient cycled forecasts without a physical model.
- **Open work:** Assimilating real observations and comparing against operational analyses.
- **Issues:** Tested only with simulated observations; background error covariance treatment and real-observation issues not addressed in the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Variational Data Assimilation with a Learned Inverse Observation Operator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11192)
Frerix et al. (2021), *International Conference on Machine Learning*. 49 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves variational data assimilation, which is hard to optimize because observations are not invertibly related to physical states.
- **Architecture:** Learned inverse observation operator (neural network mapping observations to states), used to initialize 4D-Var-type optimization and to reformulate the objective in physical space.
- **Data:** Lorenz 96 model and a two-dimensional turbulent fluid flow, with synthetic observations.
- **Main result:** Significantly improves forecast quality for these chaotic systems compared with standard variational DA.
- **Open work:** Scale to realistic NWP observation networks and models, and combine with background error statistics.
- **Issues:** Idealized systems and synthetic observations; requires training data of paired observations and states.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Using Data Assimilation to Train a Hybrid Forecast System that Combines Machine-Learning and Knowledge-Based Components](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0048050)
Wikner et al. (2021), *Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science*. 45 citations.

- **Main goal:** Trains hybrid ML and physics forecast models when only noisy, partial observations are available rather than full-state training data.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid model in which reservoir computing corrects an imperfect knowledge-based model. Training uses analyses from an Ensemble Transform Kalman Filter.
- **Data:** Synthetic observations from the Lorenz 1963 and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky systems, with model error introduced as a misspecified parameter.
- **Main result:** Training on DA analyses from partial measurements yields an ML correction that improves forecasts of the imperfect model.
- **Open work:** Scale to realistic atmospheric models (pursued in Arcomano et al. 2022) and iterate DA and training cycles.
- **Issues:** Low-dimensional toy systems and a simple parametric model error. Behaviour with realistic structural error is untested.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Surrogate modeling for the climate sciences dynamics with machine learning and data assimilation](https://doi.org/10.3389/fams.2023.1133226)
Bocquet (2023), *Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics*. 45 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews machine learning surrogate modeling at the intersection of geoscience dynamical systems, data assimilation and model error correction.
- **Architecture:** Review and perspective on neural network surrogate dynamics combined with data assimilation, covering subgrid parameterization, model error correction, model discovery and surrogate modeling.
- **Data:** Not applicable; perspective article surveying the literature, including low-order chaotic models and high-dimensional geophysical systems.
- **Main result:** Identifies technical obstacles to deploying combined ML and data assimilation in high-dimensional operational systems and highlights advances in physical model error correction.
- **Open work:** Short- versus long-term fidelity of surrogate dynamics, combined DA-ML methodology, and uncertainty quantification.
- **Issues:** Perspective rather than new results; reflects the author's own view of the field.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Attention-based Convolutional Autoencoders for 3D-Variational Data Assimilation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cma.2020.113291)
Mack et al. (2020), *Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering*. 45 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces the computational cost of 3D-Variational data assimilation without sacrificing accuracy.
- **Architecture:** Bi-Reduced Space 3D-Var using attention-based convolutional autoencoders to reduce both the state and the background covariance representation; proven equivalent to previous solutions.
- **Data:** Air pollution model of a site at Elephant and Castle, London, UK.
- **Main result:** Reduces the background covariance matrix representation by about O(10^3) and increases assimilation accuracy relative to existing reduced-space methods.
- **Open work:** Apply the approach to larger geophysical assimilation systems such as weather or ocean models.
- **Issues:** Tested on a single urban pollution application; generality to atmospheric or oceanic DA is not shown.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [3D‐Var data assimilation using a variational autoencoder](https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.4708)
Melinc et al. (2023), *Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society*. 40 citations.

- **Main goal:** Proposes neural network data assimilation that performs 3D-Var minimisation in a learned latent space, as an alternative to traditional variational and Kalman filter methods.
- **Architecture:** Variational autoencoder (VAE) whose reduced-order latent space hosts an autodifferentiable 3D-Var cost function fusing observations and an encoded persistence background.
- **Data:** Atmospheric fields with simulated observations and a short-range persistence forecast as background; specific reanalysis product and resolution not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The latent-space background-error covariance matrix is quasidiagonal while grid-point covariances are flow-dependent and seasonal; single-observation tests show B captures tropical and extratropical covariances simultaneously.
- **Open work:** Extending to many real observations, cycled assimilation with a real forecast model background, and comparison against operational 3D-Var or EnKF systems.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated mainly with single temperature observation experiments and a persistence background; no full cycling or operational-scale evaluation is reported.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Online learning of both state and dynamics using ensemble Kalman filters](https://doi.org/10.3934/fods.2020015)
Bocquet et al. (2020), *Foundations of Data Science*. 37 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learns both the system state and a surrogate dynamical model online, updating estimates as new partial noisy observations arrive.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble Kalman filter family (global, local and iterative EnKF) with state-parameter augmentation and a simple machine-learning surrogate representation of the dynamics.
- **Data:** Synthetic observations from one-scale and two-scale chaotic Lorenz models (Lorenz-96 type).
- **Main result:** Online learning of dynamics and state is numerically efficient and accurate across the EnKF variants, with specific algorithmic issues identified and addressed for each.
- **Open work:** Scaling to high-dimensional realistic models and richer surrogate representations.
- **Issues:** Idealized low-dimensional chaotic models only; simple surrogate representation; localization of model parameters raises design issues.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Data driven weather forecasts trained and initialised directly from observations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15586)
McNally et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 33 citations.
