- **Main result:** 92% accuracy with 1% false positives on the test set; first in-orbit demonstration of a deep neural network for on-board data processing.
- **Open work:** In-orbit performance assessment and extension to other on-board edge applications are planned.
- **Issues:** Trained on emulated rather than real sensor data; image-level binary classification only, not pixel-level cloud masks.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Comparison of Multiple Linear Regression, Cubist Regression, and Random Forest Algorithms to Estimate Daily Air Surface Temperature from Dynamic Combinations of MODIS LST Data](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs9050398)
Phan et al. (2017), *Remote Sensing*. 174 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates daily maximum, minimum and mean air temperature from MODIS land surface temperature in mountainous northwest Vietnam.
- **Architecture:** Compares multiple linear regression, Cubist regression and random forest using combinations of four MODIS LST datasets with or without auxiliary data.
- **Data:** MODIS LST (Aqua and Terra, day and night), elevation and Julian day; three climate stations, 2009-2013.
- **Main result:** With auxiliary data, Cubist or random forest give R2 above 0.93/0.80/0.89 and RMSE about 1.5/2.0/1.6 °C for Ta-max, Ta-min and Ta-mean.
- **Open work:** Testing with more stations and cloud-gap filling would support spatial mapping.
- **Issues:** Only three stations; MODIS LST gaps under cloud; spatial transferability not tested.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Cloud Classification of AVHRR Imagery in Maritime Regions Using a Probabilistic Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1994)033<0909:ccoaii>2.0.co;2)
Bankert (1994), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 170 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates cloud classification of satellite imagery over maritime regions to support analysts and forecasters.
- **Architecture:** Probabilistic neural network classifier using spectral and textural features from image samples, with feature selection to reduce the feature set.
- **Data:** AVHRR imagery samples over maritime regions labelled by experts into about ten cloud classes.
- **Main result:** The probabilistic neural network achieves overall classification accuracy of roughly 80% on independent samples, with confusion mainly between similar cloud types.
- **Open work:** Extending to other regions and sensors and adding multi-layer or nighttime classes.
- **Issues:** Relies on subjective expert labels and fixed-size sample boxes that may contain mixed cloud types.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Hydrometeor classification system using dual-polarization radar measurements: model improvements and in situ verification](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2004.843077)
Lim et al. (2005), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 168 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves dual-polarization radar hydrometeor classification and verifies it with in situ observations.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic hydrometeor classification using polarimetric variables, with refined membership functions.
- **Data:** CSU-CHILL S-band polarimetric radar observations with in situ hydrometeor observations for verification.
- **Main result:** The improved classifier matches in situ hydrometeor observations well.
- **Open work:** Applying to other radars and climates.
- **Issues:** Limited verification cases; membership functions tuned to S-band.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Global wind speed retrieval from SAR](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2003.814658)
Horstmann et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 167 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean surface wind speeds globally from synthetic aperture radar imagery.
- **Architecture:** Neural network inversion of a C-band geophysical model function using SAR backscatter and wind direction from image streaks.
- **Data:** ERS-2 SAR imagery worldwide compared with ECMWF model winds.
- **Main result:** SAR wind retrievals agree well with model winds globally.
- **Open work:** Improved direction retrieval and use of Envisat ASAR.
- **Issues:** Dependent on model function; validation against model winds.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Development of a sky imager for cloud cover assessment.](https://doi.org/10.1364/josaa.25.000029)
Cazorla et al. (2008), *Journal of the Optical Society of America A*. 167 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops an all-sky imager to assess cloud cover automatically.
- **Architecture:** Sky camera system with a neural network classifier optimized by a genetic algorithm.
- **Data:** Sky images from Granada, Spain.
- **Main result:** The imager estimates cloud cover in good agreement with observers.
- **Open work:** Cloud type classification.
- **Issues:** Sun glare and horizon effects.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Land surface and air temperature dynamics: The role of urban form and seasonality.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2023.167306)
Naserikia et al. (2023), *Science of The Total Environment*. 167 citations.

- **Main goal:** Quantifies how land surface temperature differs from air temperature in cities and what controls their relationship.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning analysis of LST–Ta relationships with urban form predictors; the specific algorithm is not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Crowdsourced air temperature in Sydney, Australia, satellite LST, high-resolution imagery, urban landscape data and Local Climate Zones.
- **Main result:** LST and Ta differ in space and season; dense built areas show insignificant or negative summer LST–Ta relations, so LST is an inappropriate proxy for urban thermal environment there.
- **Open work:** Extending to other cities and combining with canopy-layer modelling.
- **Issues:** Crowdsourced sensors have quality issues; single city.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Weather Radar Ground Clutter. Part II: Real-Time Identification and Filtering](https://doi.org/10.1175/2009jtecha1160.1)
Hubbert et al. (2009), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 166 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies ground clutter in weather radar data in real time so that clutter filtering is applied only where needed, avoiding bias in precipitation echoes from indiscriminate filtering.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic Clutter Mitigation Decision (CMD) algorithm combining clutter phase alignment and reflectivity texture/spin features, followed by a spectral clutter filter (GMAP) at flagged gates; not a trained ML model.
- **Data:** S-band research and operational Doppler radar time series (NCAR S-Pol and NEXRAD-type data); exact cases not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Selective clutter filtering guided by the fuzzy decision removes clutter while largely preserving weather echoes that overlap clutter regions.
- **Open work:** Extension to other radar wavelengths and scanning strategies and tuning of membership functions for different clutter environments.
- **Issues:** Hand-designed membership functions and thresholds; performance in mixed clutter-weather gates and anomalous propagation depends on site tuning.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Cloud detection methodologies: variants and development—a review](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40747-019-00128-0)
Mahajan et al. (2019), *Complex & Intelligent Systems*. 164 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews cloud detection methods for satellite remote sensing imagery published from 2004 to 2018.
- **Architecture:** Review of threshold-based classical algorithms and machine learning approaches for cloud/no-cloud, snow/cloud and thin/thick cloud detection.
- **Data:** Literature on cloud detection from multispectral satellite imagery; no new data.
- **Main result:** Threshold methods have poor universality across locations, and many models lack ground-based validation; a hybrid of ML, physical retrieval and ground validation is recommended.
- **Open work:** Developing hybrid physically informed ML methods with ground-based validation.
- **Issues:** Coverage stops at 2018 and predates most deep learning cloud masking; no quantitative benchmark.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Estimation of daily maximum and minimum air temperatures in urban landscapes using MODIS time series satellite data](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2018.01.018)
Yoo et al. (2018), *ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing*. 162 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates daily maximum and minimum air temperature in urban landscapes from satellite data where station networks are sparse.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning regression on MODIS time series predictors; the specific model type is not specified here.
- **Data:** MODIS time series (land surface temperature and related products) with weather station air temperature in urban areas; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; the title implies daily Tmax and Tmin can be estimated from MODIS time series in cities.
- **Open work:** Higher spatial resolution inputs and handling of cloud-related gaps.
- **Issues:** Abstract not available; MODIS LST gaps under clouds and 1 km resolution limit urban detail.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Pattern Recognition Technique for Distinguishing Surface and Cloud Types in the Polar Regions](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1987)026<1412:aprtfd>2.0.co;2)
Ebert (1987), *Journal of Climate and Applied Meteorology*. 156 citations.

- **Main goal:** Distinguishes clouds from snow and ice surfaces in polar satellite imagery, which is difficult with simple thresholds.
- **Architecture:** Pattern recognition classifier (maximum likelihood style supervised classification) using spectral and textural features of image samples.
- **Data:** AVHRR imagery over polar regions with expert-labelled samples covering many surface and cloud classes.
- **Main result:** Combining spectral and textural features separates most surface and cloud types in polar scenes with good accuracy; specific figures not reported here.
- **Open work:** Application to climatological cloud analysis and extension to more seasons and sensors.
- **Issues:** Depends on expert labelling and limited training scenes; low sun angles and thin cloud remain problematic.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [DABNet: Deformable Contextual and Boundary-Weighted Network for Cloud Detection in Remote Sensing Images](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2020.3045474)
He et al. (2021), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 156 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects clouds in optical remote sensing images accurately with low computation for onboard use, and sharpens cloud boundaries.
- **Architecture:** Lightweight convolutional neural network (DABNet) with a deformable context feature pyramid module and a boundary-weighted loss.
- **Data:** Public GF-1 WFV cloud detection benchmark and a self-built higher-resolution GF-2 cloud dataset.
- **Main result:** DABNet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with only 4.12M parameters and 8.29G multiply-adds, with clearer boundaries and fewer false alarms.
- **Open work:** Testing on other sensors and actual onboard deployment are natural next steps.
- **Issues:** Evaluated on Chinese GF sensors only; cloud versus snow and bright surfaces not discussed in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A two-parameter wind speed algorithm for Ku-band altimeters](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(2002)019<2030:atpwsa>2.0.co;2)
Gourrion et al. (2002), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 153 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves wind speed retrieval from Ku-band satellite altimeters by accounting for sea state, not only backscatter.
- **Architecture:** Two-parameter wind speed algorithm using backscatter coefficient and significant wave height, fitted with a small neural network.
- **Data:** Satellite altimeter data (TOPEX/Poseidon) collocated with scatterometer and buoy wind measurements.
- **Main result:** Including significant wave height reduces wind speed retrieval errors relative to single-parameter algorithms.
- **Open work:** Adapting the algorithm to other altimeters and bands.
- **Issues:** Calibration depends on collocated reference winds; sea-state effects beyond wave height not captured.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Fuzzy Logic Technique for Identifying Nonprecipitating Echoes in Radar Scans](https://doi.org/10.1175/jtech1914.1)
Berenguer et al. (2006), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 152 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies nonprecipitating echoes (ground clutter, anomalous propagation) in weather radar scans to improve radar rainfall estimates.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classification using reflectivity texture and vertical structure features from volume scans; not a trained ML model.
- **Data:** Single-polarization C-band radar volume scans in Catalonia, Spain.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy logic scheme effectively removes clutter and anomalous propagation echoes while keeping most precipitation.
- **Open work:** Including Doppler and dual-polarization variables and testing at other radars.
- **Issues:** Membership functions tuned for a specific radar and climate; misclassification of weak precipitation remains.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [The operational cloud retrieval algorithms from TROPOMI on board Sentinel-5 Precursor](https://doi.org/10.5194/amt-11-409-2018)
Loyola et al. (2017), *Atmospheric Measurement Techniques*. 152 citations.

- **Main goal:** Describes the operational cloud retrieval algorithms for TROPOMI on Sentinel-5 Precursor, needed to improve trace-gas retrievals and extend the oxygen A-band cloud record.
- **Architecture:** Two tandem algorithms: OCRA, a non-ML optical cloud fraction method in UV/VIS, and ROCINN, a neural network inversion of oxygen A-band radiances for cloud top height and optical thickness.
- **Data:** Prototype results in the UPAS processor using OMI and GOME-2 measurements before TROPOMI launch; radiative transfer simulations for training ROCINN.
- **Main result:** OCRA and ROCINN are integrated in the S5P operational processor UPAS and produce cloud fraction, cloud top pressure and optical thickness from OMI and GOME-2 data.
- **Open work:** Validate the TROPOMI cloud products after launch and address anticipated challenges such as higher spatial resolution and instrument effects.
- **Issues:** Pre-launch paper with no TROPOMI data; neural network accuracy depends on the radiative transfer training set and cloud model assumptions.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Rainfall Estimation from a Combination of TRMM Precipitation Radar and GOES Multispectral Satellite Imagery through the Use of an Artificial Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(2001)040<2115:refaco>2.0.co;2)
Bellerby et al. (2000), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 149 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall at high temporal resolution by combining satellite precipitation radar with geostationary imagery.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network trained to map GOES multispectral infrared and visible features to rainfall measured by the TRMM Precipitation Radar.
- **Data:** TRMM Precipitation Radar overpasses collocated with GOES multispectral imagery.
- **Main result:** The neural network produces rainfall estimates that improve on simple infrared-based techniques when validated against radar rainfall.
- **Open work:** Operational use and extension to other regions and sensors.
- **Issues:** Training limited to PR overpass samples; IR-based relations are weaker for warm rain.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Polar Cloud and Surface Classification Using AVHRR Imagery: An Intercomparison of Methods](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1992)031<0405:pcascu>2.0.co;2)
Welch et al. (1992), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 147 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares methods for classifying clouds and surface types in polar AVHRR imagery, where cloud and snow/ice are spectrally similar.
- **Architecture:** Intercomparison of classification methods, including statistical classifiers and a neural network, using spectral and textural features.
- **Data:** AVHRR imagery over polar regions with expert-labelled samples.
- **Main result:** Neural network and statistical classifiers achieve comparable and generally good accuracy; specific values not reported here.
- **Open work:** Combining methods and testing across seasons and regions.
- **Issues:** Limited labelled samples and subjective labels; results may depend on chosen feature sets.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Climatology of stratocumulus cloud morphologies: microphysical properties and radiative effects](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-14-6695-2014)
Mühlbauer et al. (2014), *Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics*. 145 citations.

- **Main goal:** Characterizes the global climatology, physical properties and radiative effects of marine stratocumulus cloud morphologies (mesoscale cellular convection types).
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network cloud classification scheme assigning scenes to closed, open or disorganized cellular MCC, combined with A-train observational analysis.
- **Data:** A-train satellite observations (e.g. MODIS imagery, CloudSat radar reflectivity) on a global scale.
- **Main result:** Closed MCC has mean cloud fraction of about 90%, versus 51% for open and 40% for disorganized MCC; morphologies differ markedly in drizzle, cloud top height and shortwave reflectance.
- **Open work:** Linking morphology changes to cloud feedbacks and evaluating model representation of MCC types follow from the results.
- **Issues:** Classification relies on a pre-trained ANN with limited categories; observational sampling and retrieval uncertainties affect the statistics.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A neural-network technique for the retrieval of atmospheric temperature and moisture profiles from high spectral resolution sounding data](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2005.855071)
Blackwell (2005), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 133 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves atmospheric temperature and moisture profiles quickly and accurately from hyperspectral infrared sounder radiances.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network applied to radiances compressed by projected principal components (PPC/NN).
- **Data:** Simulated and observed AIRS hyperspectral radiances with radiosonde and NWP-based profiles (e.g., NOAA88 sounding set).
- **Main result:** PPC/NN retrievals are more accurate than linear regression and comparable to iterative physical methods at much lower cost.
- **Open work:** Handling clouds and applying to other sounders such as IASI and CrIS.
- **Issues:** Partly simulated data; cloudy scenes and training-set representativeness remain challenges.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Neural Networks and Support Vector Machine Algorithms for Automatic Cloud Classification of Whole-Sky Ground-Based Images](https://doi.org/10.1109/lgrs.2014.2356616)
Taravat et al. (2015), *IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters*. 133 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automatically classifies cloud types from whole-sky ground-based images.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron neural network and support vector machine classifiers.
- **Data:** Whole-sky ground-based camera images; site and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available information.
- **Open work:** Add more cloud classes and test at other sites.
- **Issues:** Card based on the title only; small image datasets are typical.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [AIRS/AMSU/HSB precipitation estimates](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2002.808322)
Chen et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 131 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates global precipitation rates from the Aqua satellite microwave and infrared sounders (AIRS, AMSU, HSB), extending sounder-based retrievals to precipitation.
- **Architecture:** MLP neural network estimator using opaque microwave channels and principal components of sounder radiances as inputs, with physically motivated preprocessing.
- **Data:** AIRS/AMSU/HSB observations from the Aqua satellite; neural network trained and evaluated against NEXRAD radar precipitation estimates.
- **Main result:** The neural network retrievals agree reasonably with NEXRAD precipitation rates at sounder resolution, demonstrating useful precipitation estimates from sounding instruments; detailed scores not reproduced here.
- **Open work:** Global validation beyond radar-covered regions, snow and light-rain sensitivity, and adaptation to later sounders remain open.
- **Issues:** Training against NEXRAD over limited regions may not transfer to other climates or ocean areas; HSB failed early in the Aqua mission, limiting data.

### [A Deep Neural Network Modeling Framework to Reduce Bias in Satellite Precipitation Products](https://doi.org/10.1175/jhm-d-15-0075.1)
Tao et al. (2016), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 130 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces systematic bias in satellite infrared-based precipitation estimates, which suffer from a weak link between cloud-top properties and surface rain.
- **Architecture:** Deep neural network (stacked denoising autoencoder) that extracts features from satellite infrared imagery to correct precipitation estimates.
- **Data:** Geostationary infrared satellite imagery and the PERSIANN-CCS product, evaluated against radar-based precipitation over the central United States (details not confirmed).
- **Main result:** The deep network reduces bias in the satellite precipitation estimates relative to the baseline product. Specific numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Adding further channels such as water vapor and microwave data, and extending evaluation to other regions and seasons.
- **Issues:** Limited region and period; depends on radar reference data for training. Abstract unavailable.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Convective Boundary Layer Depth: Improved Measurement by Doppler Radar Wind Profiler Using Fuzzy Logic Methods](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(2002)019<1745:cbldim>2.0.co;2)
Bianco et al. (2002), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 130 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves automatic measurement of convective boundary layer depth from radar wind profilers, where simple signal-to-noise peak methods fail with clouds, birds or other contamination.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic method combining radar reflectivity (signal-to-noise ratio) and vertical velocity spectral width information to identify the boundary layer top; not a neural network.
- **Data:** 915-MHz Doppler radar wind profiler observations, verified against radiosonde-derived boundary layer depths.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy logic algorithm gives boundary layer depths in better agreement with radiosondes than the standard signal-to-noise peak method, reducing gross errors.
- **Open work:** Adding further input variables (e.g. RASS temperature) and operational real-time deployment are natural extensions.
- **Issues:** Tuned membership functions are site- and instrument-specific; performance under stable or multi-layer conditions is limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [PERSIANN-MSA: A Precipitation Estimation Method from Satellite-Based Multispectral Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1175/2009jhm1139.1)
Behrangi et al. (2009), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 129 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves satellite precipitation estimation by using multispectral geostationary imagery rather than infrared alone in the PERSIANN framework.
- **Architecture:** PERSIANN-MSA: self-organizing feature map (SOFM) clustering of multispectral cloud features, with principal component analysis of inputs, followed by mapping clusters to rain rates.
- **Data:** GOES-12 multispectral channels (visible and infrared bands) over the United States, with radar-based precipitation for training and validation.
- **Main result:** Using multispectral information improves rain/no-rain detection and rain-rate estimates relative to infrared-only estimation.
- **Open work:** Extending to newer geostationary imagers with more channels and merging with passive microwave data.
- **Issues:** Visible channels are only available in daytime; evaluated over a limited region and period.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Estimation of solar radiation using a neural network based on radiative transfer](https://doi.org/10.1029/2009jd013337)
Takenaka et al. (2011), *Journal of Geophysical Research*. 127 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates surface solar radiation quickly and accurately from satellite data by emulating radiative transfer calculations.
- **Architecture:** Neural network trained to emulate a radiative transfer model for fast solar radiation estimation.
- **Data:** Radiative transfer simulations for training, applied to geostationary satellite observations and validated with ground radiation measurements; details not reported in the record.
- **Main result:** The neural network reproduces radiative transfer results at much lower computational cost, enabling high-frequency solar radiation estimation; numbers not available in the record.
- **Open work:** Extending the emulator to more atmospheric conditions and sensors.
- **Issues:** Accuracy bounded by the radiative transfer model and cloud retrievals; no abstract available.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A neural network as a nonlinear transfer function model for retrieving surface wind speeds from the special sensor microwave imager](https://doi.org/10.1029/95jc00857)
Krasnopolsky et al. (1995), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*. 123 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean surface wind speed from satellite microwave radiometer data more accurately, including in cloudy conditions.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron neural network as a nonlinear transfer function from brightness temperatures to wind speed.
- **Data:** SSM/I brightness temperatures collocated with buoy wind measurements.
- **Main result:** The neural network gives lower wind speed errors than existing regression algorithms, with better performance under moderate cloudiness and at high winds.
- **Open work:** Operational implementation and extension to other variables.
- **Issues:** Validation limited to buoy matchups; heavy rain conditions remain difficult.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Precipitation observations near 54 and 183 GHz using the NOAA-15 satellite](https://doi.org/10.1109/36.868889)
Staelin et al. (2000), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 120 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates precipitation from passive microwave sounder observations near 54 and 183 GHz, exploiting opaque oxygen and water vapour channels that sense precipitation aloft.
- **Architecture:** Physically guided retrieval that combines channel signatures with a neural network trained to estimate precipitation rate.
- **Data:** NOAA-15 AMSU-A and AMSU-B brightness temperatures, evaluated against NEXRAD radar precipitation rates over the United States.
- **Main result:** Opaque-channel signatures detect and quantify precipitation, with neural network estimates agreeing reasonably with NEXRAD at about 15 km resolution; detailed scores are not reproduced here.
- **Open work:** Extending to more cases, seasons and regions and to later sounders such as AMSU on other satellites.
- **Issues:** Training and evaluation tied to radar over limited U.S. cases; weak sensitivity to light or warm rain; radar itself carries errors.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Atmospheric correction over coastal waters using multilayer neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2017.07.016)
Fan et al. (2017), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 120 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves atmospheric correction of ocean color imagery over optically complex coastal waters, where standard NIR-based algorithms fail.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer neural networks (MLP) trained to map top-of-atmosphere reflectances to water-leaving reflectance and aerosol properties.
- **Data:** Training on coupled atmosphere–ocean radiative transfer simulations; applied to SeaWiFS and MODIS-Aqua imagery and validated against AERONET-OC in situ measurements.
- **Main result:** The neural network correction retrieves remote-sensing reflectance in coastal waters more accurately than the standard SeaDAS algorithms, especially in turbid waters.
- **Open work:** Extension to other sensors and to absorbing aerosols, plus uncertainty estimates, are natural next steps.
- **Issues:** Relies on the realism of simulated training data; performance depends on coverage of aerosol and water types in the simulations.

### [Mean Map Kernel Methods for Semisupervised Cloud Classification](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2009.2026425)
Gómez-Chova et al. (2010), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 118 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves cloud screening of multispectral satellite images when labeled samples are scarce.
- **Architecture:** Semisupervised kernel methods using mean map kernels within support vector machine (SVM) classification, exploiting clusters of unlabeled pixels.
- **Data:** Multispectral satellite images (MERIS) with few labeled cloud and cloud-free samples.
- **Main result:** The semisupervised mean map kernel approach improves cloud classification accuracy over standard supervised SVM when labels are scarce.
- **Open work:** Extension to other sensors and to operational cloud masking.
- **Issues:** Few test scenes; performance depends on clustering quality and kernel parameter choices.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Distinguishing Cloud and Snow in Satellite Images via Deep Convolutional Network](https://doi.org/10.1109/lgrs.2017.2735801)
Zhan et al. (2017), *IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters*. 117 citations.

- **Main goal:** Distinguishes cloud from snow in satellite imagery, which have similar visible reflectance and are often confused in cloud masks.

- **Data:** Multispectral satellite images (Gaofen-1 wide field of view) with manually labeled cloud and snow.
- **Main result:** The deep CNN distinguishes cloud and snow more accurately than conventional threshold-based and classical classifier methods.
- **Open work:** Extension to other sensors and larger, more diverse labeled datasets.
- **Issues:** Limited training scenes and labels; restricted spectral bands without thermal infrared.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A neural network approach to real-time rainfall estimation for Africa.](https://doi.org/10.1175/1525-7541(2003)004<1119:annatr>2.0.co;2)
Grimes et al. (2003), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 114 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces real-time rainfall estimates over Africa where gauge networks are sparse.

- **Data:** Meteosat thermal infrared imagery, ECMWF model variables and rain gauge data in Africa (e.g. Zambia).
- **Main result:** Neural network estimates improve on infrared-only methods at daily scale. Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Extending to other regions and operational implementation.
- **Issues:** Gauge validation is sparse; NWP-dependent inputs.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [CloudSEN12, a global dataset for semantic understanding of cloud and cloud shadow in Sentinel-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01878-2)
Aybar et al. (2022), *Scientific Data*. 113 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a transparent, richly annotated global reference dataset to benchmark cloud and cloud shadow detection for Sentinel-2 imagery.

- **Data:** Copernicus Sentinel-2 level-1C and level-2A multispectral data, Sentinel-1 SAR data and auxiliary remote sensing products, globally distributed and multi-temporal.
- **Main result:** CloudSEN12 exceeds previous datasets in annotation richness, scene variability, geographic distribution, metadata, quality control and sample count.

### [Mapping Daily Air Temperature for Antarctica Based on MODIS LST](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs8090732)
Meyer et al. (2016), *Remote Sensing*. 113 citations.

- **Architecture:** Random forest, generalized boosted regression models (GBM) and Cubist compared with simple linear regression; Cubist-based forward feature selection.
- **Data:** MODIS land surface temperature at 1 km with auxiliary predictors and air temperature from 32 Antarctic weather stations; maps produced for 2013.
- **Main result:** GBM with LST and month performs best (leave-one-station-out R2 0.71, RMSE 10.51 °C), only slightly better than linear regression (R2 0.64, RMSE 11.02 °C).
- **Open work:** Extend training to more years to build air temperature time series from 2000 onward.
- **Issues:** Large RMSE; only clear-sky LST available; few stations; ML gains over linear regression are small.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Development of a neural network based algorithm for rainfall estimation from radar observations](https://doi.org/10.1109/36.551944)
Xiao et al. (1997), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 112 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates surface rainfall rate from radar observations, aiming to avoid the limitations of fixed reflectivity-rainfall (Z-R) relations.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward neural network (multilayer perceptron) mapping radar measurements (reflectivity and polarimetric variables) to rain rate.
- **Data:** Ground-based weather radar observations collocated with rain gauge measurements from a field campaign; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The neural network rainfall estimates agree better with gauges than conventional Z-R based estimates.

Cho et al. (2006), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 111 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies and removes ground clutter and anomalous propagation echoes from weather radar data, which contaminate quantitative precipitation estimates.

- **Main result:** Echo characteristics separate ground and anomalous propagation echoes from precipitation; quantitative skill not reported here.
- **Open work:** Testing across more radars, seasons and mixed precipitation-clutter situations.
- **Issues:** Evaluation details unknown; feature thresholds may be radar- and site-specific, and embedded clutter within precipitation remains difficult.

### [Cloud Detection for High-Resolution Satellite Imagery Using Machine Learning and Multi-Feature Fusion](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs8090715)
Bai et al. (2016), *Remote Sensing*. 108 citations.

Camps-Valls et al. (2006), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 107 citations.

- **Issues:** Limited number of storms and reliance on spotter hail reports with sampling biases.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Prediction of high spatio-temporal resolution land surface temperature under cloudy conditions using microwave vegetation index and ANN](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2016.03.011)
Shwetha et al. (2016), *ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing*. 100 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates land surface temperature at high spatio-temporal resolution under cloudy conditions, where thermal infrared retrievals fail.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network relating a passive microwave vegetation index and other inputs to land surface temperature.
- **Data:** Passive microwave observations (AMSR-E-derived microwave vegetation index) and MODIS land surface temperature.
- **Main result:** The ANN predicts cloudy-sky LST with reasonable accuracy; detailed scores are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Application to newer microwave sensors and other regions.
- **Issues:** Microwave and thermal resolutions differ; validation under cloud is difficult.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Automated Cloud Classification of Global AVHRR Data Using a Fuzzy Logic Approach](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1997)036<1519:accoga>2.0.co;2)
Baum et al. (1997), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 99 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies clouds automatically in global satellite imagery for climate studies.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classification of AVHRR pixels into clear, water cloud, ice cloud and multilayer categories.
- **Data:** Global AVHRR Global Area Coverage (GAC) data.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy logic approach classifies cloud types consistently, with accuracy comparable to expert analysis on test scenes.
- **Open work:** Application to longer records and improved multilayer cloud detection.
- **Issues:** Difficulty over snow, ice and at night; validation limited to expert-labelled scenes.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Remote sensing from the infrared atmospheric sounding interferometer instrument 2. Simultaneous retrieval of temperature, water vapor, and ozone atmospheric profiles](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001jd001591)
Aires et al. (2002), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 99 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves temperature, water vapour and ozone profiles simultaneously from IASI hyperspectral infrared radiances quickly and accurately.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron neural network applied to principal-component-compressed IASI spectra, retrieving all three profiles jointly.
- **Data:** Simulated IASI radiances from radiative transfer computations over a climatological atmospheric profile database (TIGR).
- **Main result:** The neural retrieval gives accurate profiles of temperature, water vapour and ozone, with joint retrieval exploiting correlations between variables.
- **Open work:** Apply to real IASI observations and add first-guess information and error characterization.
- **Issues:** Evaluated on simulated data; clear-sky assumption and dependence on representativeness of the training database.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Artificial intelligence techniques for clutter identification with polarimetric radar signatures](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2012.02.007)
Islam et al. (2012), *Atmospheric Research*. 99 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies clutter in weather radar data using polarimetric signatures.
- **Architecture:** Artificial intelligence classifiers; specific types are not stated in the title.
- **Data:** Polarimetric weather radar observations; radar site not reported here.
- **Main result:** Not reported here.
- **Open work:** Operational testing across radars.
- **Issues:** Limited events; labeled clutter may be imperfect.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Bag-of-Words and Object-Based Classification for Cloud Extraction From Satellite Imagery](https://doi.org/10.1109/jstars.2015.2431676)
Yuan et al. (2015), *IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing*. 97 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extracts clouds from high-resolution satellite imagery, where spectral thresholds struggle to separate clouds from bright surfaces.
- **Architecture:** Object-based classification that segments the image into objects and describes them with bag-of-words features before classifying cloud versus non-cloud; classifier type is not specified here.
- **Data:** Optical satellite imagery; sensors and scenes are not reported here.
- **Main result:** The approach is presented as extracting clouds more accurately than comparison methods; numbers are not available here.
- **Open work:** Extension to thin and semi-transparent clouds and other sensors.
- **Issues:** Thin clouds and bright surfaces such as snow remain difficult; evaluation scope unknown without the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Regularized Neural Net Approach for Retrieval of Atmospheric and Surface Temperatures with the Iasi Instrument](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(2002)041<0144:arnnaf>2.0.co;2)
Aires et al. (2013), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 97 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves atmospheric temperature profiles and surface temperature from IASI hyperspectral infrared radiances quickly and robustly.
- **Architecture:** Regularized multilayer perceptron neural network retrieval, with regularization and input compression to handle many correlated channels.
- **Data:** Simulated IASI radiances computed from a climatological atmospheric profile database (TIGR).
- **Main result:** The regularized neural network gives accurate temperature profile and surface temperature retrievals in simulation.
- **Open work:** Application to real IASI observations and comparison with physical retrievals.
- **Issues:** Trained and tested on simulated radiances; real-instrument noise and cloud contamination not fully addressed.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Modeling and Prediction of Rainfall Using Radar Reflectivity Data: A Data-Mining Approach](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2012.2210429)
Kusiak et al. (2013), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 95 citations.

- **Main goal:** Models and predicts rainfall at rain gauges from radar reflectivity using data mining.
- **Architecture:** Data-mining (machine learning) models relating radar reflectivity to gauge rainfall; the specific algorithm types are not specified here.
- **Data:** Weather radar reflectivity data and rain gauge measurements; details are not reported here.
- **Main result:** Data-mining models predict gauge rainfall from radar reflectivity with useful accuracy; values are not available here.
- **Open work:** Extension to longer lead times and more gauges.
- **Issues:** Limited gauges and region; radar-gauge representativeness errors.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Comparison of four machine learning algorithms for their applicability in satellite-based optical rainfall retrievals](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2015.09.021)
Meyer et al. (2016), *Atmospheric Research*. 95 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether the choice of machine learning algorithm matters for satellite-based optical rainfall retrievals.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of random forest, artificial neural network, support vector machine and gradient boosting machine.
- **Data:** MSG SEVIRI satellite data over Germany with RADOLAN radar-based rainfall as reference.
- **Main result:** The four algorithms perform similarly for rain area delineation and rain rate; algorithm choice matters less than predictors.
- **Open work:** Improving predictor information rather than algorithm choice.
- **Issues:** Single region; optical retrievals limited at night and for some cloud types.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Multifeature texture analysis for the classification of clouds in satellite imagery](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2003.815404)
Christodoulou et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 91 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies cloud types in satellite imagery automatically to support weather analysis.
- **Architecture:** Multifeature texture analysis (several texture feature sets) with self-organizing map neural networks and k-nearest neighbour classifiers, including combinations of classifiers.
- **Data:** Meteosat satellite images with expert-labelled cloud types, mainly over the eastern Mediterranean region.
- **Main result:** Combining multiple texture feature sets improves cloud classification accuracy over single feature sets; exact accuracies not reported here.
- **Open work:** Adding spectral channels and larger labelled datasets for more cloud classes.
- **Issues:** Small expert-labelled sample and texture-only features; class confusion among similar cloud types.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Automated ground-based cloud recognition](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10044-005-0007-5)
Singh et al. (2005), *Pattern Analysis and Applications*. 91 citations.

- **Main goal:** Recognizes cloud types automatically from ground-based sky images.
- **Architecture:** Texture feature extraction methods (e.g. co-occurrence, autocorrelation, edge frequency) with k-nearest neighbour and neural network classifiers.
- **Data:** Ground-based digital sky images labelled by cloud type; size of dataset not reported here.
- **Main result:** Texture features allow automated discrimination of cloud types with moderate accuracy; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Larger image sets and more cloud classes; combining colour and texture.
- **Issues:** Small dataset and visual labels; sensitivity to illumination conditions.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Global Millimeter-Wave Precipitation Retrievals Trained With a Cloud-Resolving Numerical Weather Prediction Model, Part I: Retrieval Design](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2007.908302)
Surussavadee et al. (2008), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 89 citations.

- **Main goal:** Designs global precipitation retrievals from millimeter-wave satellite sounders using a cloud-resolving NWP model as training truth.
- **Architecture:** Neural network retrieval estimators trained on simulated radiances and precipitation.
- **Data:** MM5 cloud-resolving simulations of about 122 global storms with radiative transfer for AMSU-A/B (and AMSU-like) channels.
- **Main result:** The trained networks retrieve precipitation rate and related variables with good agreement with model truth; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Validation against observations (Part II) and extension to other sensors.
- **Issues:** Training truth is model-based, so retrievals inherit model microphysics biases.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Land surface skin temperatures from a combined analysis of microwave and infrared satellite observations for an all-weather evaluation of the differences between air and skin temperatures](https://doi.org/10.1029/2002jd002301)
Prigent et al. (2003), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 86 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves land surface skin temperature under all-weather conditions to evaluate differences between surface air and skin temperatures, including cloudy situations missed by infrared-only methods.
- **Architecture:** Combined microwave and infrared inversion using a neural network retrieval scheme (developed by Aires and colleagues) to estimate skin temperature with other surface and atmospheric variables.
- **Data:** SSM/I passive microwave and ISCCP infrared satellite observations, with surface air temperature from weather stations and reanalysis for comparison; global land.
- **Main result:** All-weather skin temperatures are obtained, and skin minus air temperature differences show coherent diurnal, seasonal and cloud-dependent behavior, differing between clear and cloudy conditions.
- **Open work:** Using the all-weather skin temperatures to evaluate land-surface schemes in climate and weather models.
- **Issues:** Microwave emissivity and penetration depth complicate interpretation of skin temperature; retrieval accuracy depends on first-guess information.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Cloud Classification of Satellite Radiance Data by Multicategory Support Vector Machines](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(2004)021<0159:ccosrd>2.0.co;2)
Lee et al. (2004), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 86 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects clouds and classifies cloud types from satellite radiance profiles, a need of Earth Observing System algorithms that must know whether a profile is cloud free.
- **Architecture:** Multicategory support vector machine (MSVM) that extends binary SVMs symmetrically to many classes and handles unequal misclassification costs and nonrepresentative training sets.
- **Data:** Satellite radiance profiles labeled as clear or by cloud type, in the context of MODIS-type observations; details of the sample are only partly given in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The MSVM shows potential as an efficient cloud detection and classification algorithm and avoids failures of one-versus-rest binary decompositions.
- **Open work:** Applying the MSVM operationally to large volumes of satellite data and adding more cloud categories and surface types.
- **Issues:** Demonstration on a limited labeled dataset; quality depends on the reliability of training labels.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Cloud Properties Derived From GOME/ERS-2 Backscatter Data for Trace Gas Retrieval](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2007.901043)
Rodriguez et al. (2007), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 84 citations.

- **Main goal:** Derives cloud fraction, cloud-top height and cloud albedo from GOME backscatter data to correct trace-gas retrievals for cloud effects.
- **Architecture:** Cloud algorithms OCRA (optical cloud recognition) for cloud fraction and ROCINN, which uses neural networks to retrieve cloud-top height and albedo from the oxygen A-band.
- **Data:** GOME/ERS-2 spectral backscatter measurements, with radiative transfer simulations for training and comparison against independent cloud products.
- **Main result:** The retrieved cloud properties are consistent with independent data and improve trace-gas (e.g. ozone) column retrievals.
- **Open work:** Application to successor sensors such as SCIAMACHY and GOME-2.
- **Issues:** Large GOME pixels and simplified cloud models (Lambertian reflectors) limit accuracy; card partly relies on knowledge.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Ocean surface wind retrievals from special sensor microwave imager data with neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1029/93jc03042)
Stogryn et al. (1994), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*. 82 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean surface wind speed from satellite passive microwave data, aiming to improve on regression algorithms, especially in cloudy conditions.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural networks (multilayer perceptron) mapping brightness temperatures to wind speed, with separate networks for different atmospheric conditions.
- **Data:** SSM/I brightness temperatures collocated with in situ buoy wind observations.
- **Main result:** Neural network retrievals are more accurate than conventional regression algorithms; specific error statistics are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Extending retrievals to wind direction and heavier precipitation conditions is a natural continuation.
- **Issues:** Depends on collocation data quality and representativeness; performance degrades in rain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Supervised Fuzzy-Logic Classification of Hydrometeors Using C-Band Weather Radars](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2007.903399)
Marzano et al. (2007), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 82 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies hydrometeor types from C-band polarimetric weather radar observations, where attenuation and resonance effects complicate classification.
- **Architecture:** Supervised fuzzy-logic classifier whose membership functions are trained from scattering simulations of hydrometeor classes.
- **Data:** Simulated C-band polarimetric radar variables from microphysical and scattering models for training, applied to C-band polarimetric radar observations in Italy.
- **Main result:** The supervised fuzzy-logic scheme gives physically consistent hydrometeor classifications in case studies.
- **Open work:** Validation against in situ microphysical observations and attenuation correction before classification.
- **Issues:** Lack of ground truth limits quantitative validation; membership functions depend on simulation assumptions.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Neural Networks–Based Fusion Technique to Estimate Half-Hourly Rainfall Estimates at 0.1° Resolution from Satellite Passive Microwave and Infrared Data](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(2004)043<0576:annftt>2.0.co;2)
Tapiador et al. (2004), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 80 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces high-resolution (half-hourly, 0.1°) satellite rainfall estimates by fusing accurate but infrequent passive microwave data with frequent infrared data.
- **Architecture:** Neural network–based fusion technique that learns the relation between infrared brightness temperatures and microwave-derived rain rates.
- **Data:** Satellite passive microwave (e.g. SSM/I) rain estimates and geostationary infrared imagery, with validation against ground observations; details are not reported here (no abstract available).
- **Main result:** Not reported in detail; the method yields half-hourly 0.1° rainfall fields as stated in the title.
- **Open work:** Validation over more regions and seasons and use of additional microwave sensors.
- **Issues:** Infrared–rain relations are indirect, especially for warm rain; card relies on title and limited knowledge.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Retrieval of cirrus cloud optical thickness and top altitude from geostationary remote sensing](https://doi.org/10.5194/amt-7-3233-2014)
Kox et al. (2014), *Atmospheric Measurement Techniques*. 80 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects cirrus clouds and retrieves their optical thickness and top altitude day and night from geostationary imagery.
- **Architecture:** Backpropagation neural network (MLP) in the COCS algorithm trained on collocated SEVIRI and CALIOP measurements.
- **Data:** About 8 million coincident MSG SEVIRI and CALIPSO CALIOP measurements; validation with independent CALIOP data and airborne high spectral resolution lidar.
- **Main result:** Provides cirrus optical depth at 532 nm and top altitude every 15 min over about one-third of the globe, validated against independent lidar measurements.
- **Open work:** Extension to other geostationary sensors and use for cirrus climatologies and contrail studies.
- **Issues:** Trained on CALIOP so inherits its sensitivity limits; restricted to the SEVIRI disc.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A neural network approach to estimating rainfall from spaceborne microwave data](https://doi.org/10.1109/36.628775)
Tsintikidis et al. (1997), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 79 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall from spaceborne passive microwave observations, where the radiance-rainfall relationship is highly nonlinear.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network mapping microwave brightness temperatures to rain rate.
- **Data:** Satellite passive microwave brightness temperatures (SSM/I-type frequencies) with rainfall reference data; specific datasets not reported here.
- **Main result:** The neural network provides rainfall estimates competitive with conventional retrieval approaches; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Validation over more regimes and against independent ground radar would strengthen the method.
- **Issues:** Retrievals depend on the representativeness of training data and beam-filling assumptions.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Determination of Rainfall Rates from GOES Satellite Images by a Pattern Recognition Technique](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(1985)002<0314:dorrfg>2.0.co;2)
Wu et al. (1985), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 76 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall rates from geostationary satellite imagery, which offers broad coverage but only indirect cloud-top information.
- **Architecture:** Pattern recognition technique classifying visible and infrared image features (e.g. brightness and texture) into rain-rate categories; not a neural network.
- **Data:** GOES visible and infrared images with radar-derived rainfall for training and verification.
- **Main result:** The pattern recognition method yields rain rate estimates that agree reasonably with radar; specific statistics not reported here.
- **Open work:** Application to other regions and storm types would test generality.
- **Issues:** Indirect relationship between cloud-top properties and surface rain; limited training cases.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Hydrometeor classification with a C-band polarimetric radar](https://doi.org/10.1071/es03003)
Keenan (2003), *Australian Meteorological Magazine*. 76 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies hydrometeor types in convective storms from C-band polarimetric radar, where attenuation and resonance effects complicate schemes designed for S-band.
- **Architecture:** Empirically based fuzzy logic classification: two-dimensional membership functions on polarimetric power and differential phase variables plus a temperature membership function assign one of ten hydrometeor species.
- **Data:** C-band polarimetric radar observations of a tropical thunderstorm near Darwin and a subtropical severe thunderstorm near Sydney, Australia.
- **Main result:** The scheme produces realistic hydrometeor classifications for both storm cases.
- **Open work:** Quantitative validation against in situ microphysics and refinement of membership functions for attenuation-affected regions.
- **Issues:** Evaluation is qualitative on two case studies; membership functions are empirical and not independently validated.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Supervised Classification and Estimation of Hydrometeors From C-Band Dual-Polarized Radars: A Bayesian Approach](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2007.906476)
Marzano et al. (2008), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 74 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies hydrometeors and estimates their content from C-band dual-polarization radar, accounting for C-band scattering behaviour.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian supervised classification (maximum a posteriori) trained on simulated polarimetric radar signatures, with parametric estimators of hydrometeor content; not a neural network.
- **Data:** Scattering-model simulations of C-band polarimetric observables for training; C-band dual-polarized radar case studies in Italy for application.
- **Main result:** The Bayesian approach yields physically consistent hydrometeor classifications at C-band with associated content estimates.
- **Open work:** Including attenuation correction and in situ validation and adapting the method to other wavelengths.
- **Issues:** Training relies on simulated scattering with assumed microphysics; validation against ground truth is limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Predicting near-surface atmospheric variables from Special Sensor Microwave/Imager using neural networks with a first-guess approach](https://doi.org/10.1029/2009jd013099)
Roberts et al. (2010), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 73 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves near-surface atmospheric variables over the ocean (air temperature, humidity, wind speed) from passive microwave data to improve turbulent surface flux estimates.
- **Architecture:** Neural network retrieval using SSM/I brightness temperatures together with a first-guess estimate of the target variables as additional inputs.
- **Data:** Special Sensor Microwave/Imager observations matched with in situ ship and buoy measurements; details of periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** The first-guess neural network approach reduces retrieval errors of near-surface humidity and air temperature compared with earlier satellite retrieval methods.
- **Open work:** Extension to newer microwave sensors and use in global ocean surface flux products are natural next steps.
- **Issues:** Retrieval quality depends on the first-guess source and on in situ matchup coverage; performance in high-latitude and extreme conditions is less certain.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [The Passive microwave Neural network Precipitation Retrieval (PNPR) algorithm for AMSU/MHS observations: description and application to European case studies](https://doi.org/10.5194/amt-8-837-2015)
Sanò et al. (2014), *Atmospheric Measurement Techniques*. 73 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops an operational precipitation retrieval for cross-track passive microwave sounders that works over varied surfaces in Europe and the Mediterranean.
- **Architecture:** Neural network retrieval (PNPR) using AMSU-A and MHS brightness temperatures and 183.31 GHz channel differences, also giving precipitation phase and a confidence index.
- **Data:** Training on a cloud-radiation database from cloud-resolving model simulations coupled with radiative transfer; case-study evaluation with ground radar and rain gauges in Europe.
- **Main result:** PNPR detects and retrieves precipitation well over land, ocean, coast and snow surfaces and captures heavy convective rain, with larger uncertainty for light precipitation.
- **Open work:** Extension to ATMS and to Africa and the South Atlantic with TRMM radar validation is in progress.
- **Issues:** Evaluated on four case studies only; training relies on simulated databases, so model biases propagate, and light precipitation is less accurate.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Hydrometeor classification from polarimetric radar measurements: a clustering approach](https://doi.org/10.5194/amt-8-149-2015)
Grazioli et al. (2015), *Atmospheric Measurement Techniques*. 73 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies hydrometeors from polarimetric radar without predefining classes, letting the data determine how many distinct types can be identified.
- **Architecture:** Unsupervised clustering with criteria on data similarity and spatial smoothness, followed by human labelling of clusters into hydrometeor classes.
- **Data:** X-band polarimetric weather radar data from two field campaigns, about 50 precipitation events.
- **Main result:** Seven classes are found: light rain, rain, heavy rain, melting snow, ice crystals/small aggregates, aggregates and rimed ice.
- **Open work:** Applying the method to other radar frequencies and climates, and automating class labelling, are natural extensions.
- **Issues:** Cluster-to-class assignment relies on human interpretation; no direct in situ validation, and results depend on campaign locations and X-band attenuation.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Application of neural networks to AVHRR cloud segmentation](https://doi.org/10.1109/36.387575)
Yhann et al. (1995), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 72 citations.

- **Main goal:** Segments clouds in AVHRR satellite imagery, a prerequisite for surface and cloud retrievals.
- **Architecture:** Neural network classifier (feed-forward) applied to AVHRR image features for cloud segmentation.
- **Data:** NOAA AVHRR multispectral imagery with labelled cloud and clear-sky samples; regions not reported here.
- **Main result:** The neural network segments clouds effectively compared with conventional methods; quantitative results not reported here.
- **Open work:** Testing across seasons, regions and surface types would assess robustness.
- **Issues:** Dependent on labelled training samples; performance over difficult surfaces such as snow and sunglint is uncertain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Precipitation Estimates from MSG SEVIRI Daytime, Nighttime, and Twilight Data with Random Forests](https://doi.org/10.1175/jamc-d-14-0082.1)
Kühnlein et al. (2014), *Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology*. 72 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates precipitation rates from geostationary infrared and visible imagery consistently for daytime, nighttime and twilight conditions.
- **Architecture:** Random forest models for rain area delineation and rain rate estimation, using SEVIRI spectral channels and derived cloud properties.
- **Data:** MSG SEVIRI data over Germany with RADOLAN RW gauge-adjusted radar product as reference.
- **Main result:** Random forests give reasonable rain area detection and rain rate estimates, with better performance during daytime than at night or twilight.
- **Open work:** Adding further predictors and extending the approach to other regions are suggested.
- **Issues:** Rain rate estimation remains weaker than rain area detection; reference radar has its own errors, and the region is limited to Germany.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Segmentation of Satellite Imagery Using Hierarchical Thresholding and Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1994)033<0605:sosiuh>2.0.co;2)
Peak et al. (1994), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 70 citations.

- **Main goal:** Segments satellite imagery into cloud and surface regions as a step toward automated cloud classification.
- **Architecture:** Hierarchical thresholding combined with a neural network classifier for image segmentation.
- **Data:** Satellite imagery (e.g. AVHRR); specific scenes not reported here.
- **Main result:** The combined thresholding and neural network approach yields usable segmentations; quantitative results not reported here.
- **Open work:** Integration into automated cloud classification systems is the natural next step.
- **Issues:** Thresholds and training samples are scene-dependent; limited evaluation.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Development and Interpretation of a Neural Network-Based Synthetic Radar Reflectivity Estimator Using GOES-R Satellite Observations](https://doi.org/10.1175/jamc-d-20-0084.1)
Hilburn et al. (2020), *Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Make GOES-R observations usable in precipitating scenes for convective-scale data assimilation by converting them to synthetic radar reflectivity.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network mapping ABI radiances and GLM lightning to radar reflectivity, interpreted with channel/spatial withholding, layerwise relevance propagation and synthetic inputs.
- **Data:** GOES-16 ABI radiances and GLM lightning with collocated MRMS radar reflectivity over the central and eastern US.
- **Main result:** Spatial context in CNNs gives a major improvement over pixel-by-pixel methods; skill at high reflectivity comes from radiance gradients and lightning, with lightning pinpointing strong echoes.
- **Open work:** Assimilate the synthetic reflectivity in convective-scale models and extend to regions without radar.
- **Issues:** Trained where radar exists, so performance in data-sparse regions is unverified; high reflectivity is rare and harder to capture.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Combining Crowdsourcing and Deep Learning to Explore the Mesoscale Organization of Shallow Convection](https://doi.org/10.1175/bams-d-19-0324.1)
Rasp et al. (2019), *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Explore mesoscale organization of trade-wind shallow cumulus at scale by combining human labeling and deep learning.
- **Architecture:** Crowdsourced labeling of four patterns (Sugar, Flower, Fish, Gravel), then deep learning object detection/segmentation models to automate detection.
- **Data:** About 10,000 MODIS visible satellite images over trade-wind regions labeled by 67 scientists into almost 50,000 cloud clusters.
- **Main result:** Deep learning reproduces human labeling well enough to build global climatologies; the patterns partly overlap with open/closed cells but differ in important ways and relate to distinct large-scale environments.
- **Open work:** Studying the physical drivers and radiative effects of the patterns and their representation in models; dataset released for further work.
- **Issues:** Subjective pattern definitions with notable inter-labeler disagreement; labels limited to selected regions.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Analysis of Polar Clouds from Satellite Imagery Using Pattern Recognition and a Statistical Cloud Analysis Scheme](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1989)028<0382:aopcfs>2.0.co;2)
Ebert (1989), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 67 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyses polar clouds from satellite imagery, where cloud detection over snow and ice is difficult.
- **Architecture:** Pattern recognition classification using spectral and textural features into surface and cloud classes, followed by a statistical cloud analysis scheme to estimate cloud fraction; not a neural network.
- **Data:** AVHRR multispectral imagery over Arctic and Antarctic regions.
- **Main result:** The pattern recognition approach identifies polar surface and cloud types and estimates cloud amounts reasonably; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Validation against surface observations and extension to more seasons are natural next steps.
- **Issues:** Cloud-surface contrast over snow and ice remains challenging; limited independent validation.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Automatic Parameter Optimization for Support Vector Regression for Land and Sea Surface Temperature Estimation From Remote Sensing Data](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2008.2005993)
Moser et al. (2009), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 67 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates hyperparameter selection for support vector regression in retrieving land and sea surface temperature from satellite data.
- **Architecture:** Support vector regression (SVR) with automatic parameter optimization by minimizing an estimate of generalization error.
- **Data:** Satellite thermal infrared remote sensing data with in situ or reference LST/SST; sensor details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The automatic optimization yields SVR retrievals as accurate as or better than manual tuning and standard split-window approaches.
- **Open work:** Application to other geophysical retrieval problems.
- **Issues:** Abstract not available; specific sensors and accuracy figures uncertain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Contextual Pattern Recognition Applied to Cloud Detection and Identification](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.1985.289471)

### Cloud classification using whole-sky imager data
Buch et al. (1995), *Venue not recorded*. 64 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates classification of sky and cloud types from ground-based whole-sky imager photographs, to replace subjective human cloud observations.
- **Architecture:** Pattern-recognition classifier using spectral and texture features of sky images, based on binary decision trees.

- **Main result:** The automated classifier separates major cloud types with moderate accuracy; exact accuracy figures not reported here.

- **Issues:** Single-site imagery, subjective human labels as reference and confusion between similar cloud types.

### [Remote sensing from the infrared atmospheric sounding interferometer instrument 1. Compression, denoising, and first-guess retrieval algorithms](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001jd000955)
Aires et al. (2002), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 64 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops compression, denoising and first-guess retrieval algorithms for the high-spectral-resolution IASI infrared sounder to handle its thousands of channels efficiently.
- **Architecture:** Principal component analysis for spectral compression and denoising, followed by a neural network (MLP) first-guess retrieval of atmospheric and surface variables from the compressed radiances.
- **Data:** Simulated IASI spectra computed with a radiative transfer model over a climatological atmospheric profile database (TIGR-type); no real IASI data, as the instrument was not yet launched.
- **Main result:** PCA strongly compresses the spectra while reducing instrument noise, and the neural network gives accurate first-guess retrievals suitable to initialize variational schemes.
- **Open work:** Application to real IASI observations and coupling with physical/variational retrieval (addressed in companion papers).
- **Issues:** Trained and tested on simulated spectra, so real-instrument errors, cloud contamination and radiative transfer biases are not represented.

Zhang et al. (1997), *Neurocomputing*. 63 citations.

- **Main result:** The neural network group gives lower rainfall-estimation error than single networks or conventional techniques; exact figures not reported here.

- **Issues:** Limited cases and reference data; transferability to other regions and satellite sensors is unclear.

### [Remote sensing of the vertical distribution of atmospheric water vapor from the TOVS observations: Method and validation](https://doi.org/10.1029/98jd00045)
Chaboureau et al. (1998), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 62 citations.

### [Using deep learning to emulate and accelerate a radiative-transfer model](https://doi.org/10.1175/jtech-d-21-0007.1)
Lagerquist et al. (2021), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 60 citations.

- **Main goal:** Emulates the shortwave RRTM radiative transfer model at a fraction of its cost so it can serve as an NWP parameterization.
- **Architecture:** Knowledge-guided U-net++ networks that predict surface downwelling flux, TOA upwelling flux, net flux and heating-rate profiles.
- **Data:** RRTM calculations on atmospheric profiles from many sites. Experiment 1 trains on non-tropical sites and tests on tropical sites; Experiment 2 trains and tests on different sites from all regions.
- **Main result:** The models run about 10^4 times faster than RRTM. Experiment 2 fixes most deficiencies seen in Experiment 1, but large upper-stratospheric heating-rate errors remain.

- **Issues:** Shortwave only and offline. Biases remain for certain cloud configurations and low zenith angles.

- **Open work:** Adding more channels and moving from rain detection to rain-rate estimation.
- **Issues:** Regional study; depends on radar reference; abstract unavailable.

- **Main goal:** Estimates instantaneous precipitation from geostationary satellite infrared imagery, which lacks direct sensitivity to surface rain, using deep learning.
- **Architecture:** Multiscale encoder-decoder convolutional neural network that detects precipitating pixels and estimates rain rate.

- **Main result:** Detects precipitating pixels with POD 0.75 and FAR 0.3; estimates instantaneous rain rate with RMSE of 1.6 mm/h.

- **Issues:** Regional training over western Europe; infrared-only inputs limit skill for warm rain; gauge point measurements versus pixel-scale estimates introduce representativeness error.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Artificial neural network estimation of rainfall intensity from radar observations](https://doi.org/10.1029/2000jd900408)
Orlandini et al. (2000), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres*. 25 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies the radar reflectivity–rain rate (Z–R) relationship with neural networks, exploiting the vertical profile and recent history of reflectivity to improve rainfall intensity estimation.

### [SOM of space borne precipitation radar rain profiles on global scale](https://doi.org/10.1109/igarss.2004.1368559)
Zafar et al. (2004), *IGARSS 2004. 2004 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium*. 9 citations.

Yool et al. (1992), *Optics & Photonics*. 8 citations.

- **Architecture:** Neural network classifier for cloud discrimination; specific network configuration not reported in the available metadata.
- **Data:** Remotely sensed measurements of clouds; sensor and dataset not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Reports that the neural network can discriminate clouds; accuracy figures not reported in the available metadata.

Igata et al. (1994), *PROCEEDINGS OF HYDRAULIC ENGINEERING*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall from geostationary satellite imagery to fill gaps in ground-based rainfall observation.

### [MSWEP V3: Machine Learning-Powered Global Precipitation Estimates at 0.1$^\circ$ Hourly Resolution (1979-Present)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01436)
Wang et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces a global, near-real-time, hourly precipitation dataset from 1979 to present using machine learning to merge multiple sources.
- **Architecture:** Dataset paper: machine learning model stacks merge satellite and (re)analysis precipitation and temperature with static variables, followed by gauge-based correction; specific learner types not named in the abstract.
- **Data:** Trained on 15,959 hourly/daily gauges; corrected with 57,666 daily and 86,000 monthly stations; evaluated on 15,958 independent gauges against ERA5, IMERG-L V7, GSMaP V8, CHIRP and others.
- **Main result:** MSWEP V3 baseline reaches median daily KGE 0.69, beating ERA5 (0.61), IMERG-L (0.46), GSMaP (0.38) and CHIRP (0.31); gauge correction adds 0.09 to median daily correlation.
- **Open work:** Use for monitoring, forecasting and water-risk management; continued updates with ~2-hour latency.
- **Issues:** Gauge-sparse regions remain less constrained; evaluation at gauges may not reflect grid-scale accuracy; early-period skill depends on available inputs.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Retrieval of atmospheric thermal profiles from meteorological satellite soundings using neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.170005)
Bustamante et al. (1994), *Defense, Security, and Sensing*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves atmospheric temperature profiles from meteorological satellite sounder radiances as an alternative to physical or regression retrievals.
- **Architecture:** Neural network mapping satellite sounding radiances to vertical temperature profiles; the network family details are not reported in the available record.
- **Data:** Meteorological satellite sounding data with collocated reference temperature profiles; specific instrument and period are not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Indicates that neural networks can retrieve thermal profiles with accuracy competitive with conventional methods; quantitative errors are not reported in the available record.

- **Issues:** Retrieval accuracy depends on training-set representativeness; cloud contamination and limited vertical resolution not addressed in the available record.

Smotroff et al. (1990), *1990 IJCNN International Joint Conference on Neural Networks*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies meteorological features in satellite imagery by fusing multiple data channels with neural networks.
- **Architecture:** Neural network data fusion classifier combining multiple satellite image inputs; detailed architecture is not reported in the available record.
- **Data:** Meteorological satellite imagery with multiple channels; specific satellite and labelled samples are not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Reports that neural network fusion yields usable meteorological classifications of satellite scenes; accuracy figures not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Larger labelled datasets and comparison with conventional statistical classifiers.
- **Issues:** Early study with limited training data and evaluation; dependence on expert labelling.

### [SpecTf: Transformers enable data-driven imaging spectroscopy cloud detection](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2502903122)
Lee et al. (2025), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects clouds, including thin cirrus, in hyperspectral VSWIR imaging spectroscopy where clouds distort quantitative retrievals.

Buckles et al. (1996), *Venue not recorded*. 5 citations.

Torsum et al. (1999), *IJCNN'99. International Joint Conference on Neural Networks. Proceedings (Cat. No.99CH36339)*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates classification of cloud types from satellite images.

### [Evolving expert neural networks for meteorological rainfall estimations](https://doi.org/10.1109/iconip.1999.845660)
McCullagh et al. (1999), *ICONIP'99. ANZIIS'99 & ANNES'99 & ACNN'99. 6th International Conference on Neural Information Processing. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX378)*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves rainfall estimation from meteorological data, which single backpropagation networks handle poorly because of interference between sub-tasks.
- **Architecture:** Modular system of expert multilayer perceptrons (backpropagation neural networks), each specialising in a rainfall band (low, medium, high), with combined outputs; networks are evolved.

### Bayesian retrieval of scatterometer wind fields
Cornford et al. (1999), *Venue not recorded*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves consistent ocean surface wind fields from scatterometer data while handling the directional ambiguities of local inversions.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian framework combining neural network local models of the scatterometer inverse problem (mixture density networks) with a Gaussian process prior on wind fields.
