### [A CFCC-LSTM Model for Sea Surface Temperature Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1109/lgrs.2017.2780843)
Yang et al. (2018), *IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters*. 260 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts sea surface temperature by modelling both temporal evolution and spatial correlation of SST fields.
- **Architecture:** CFCC-LSTM: fully connected LSTM combined with a convolution layer to capture spatial and temporal information.
- **Data:** Satellite-based SST data over coastal seas of China (exact product not confirmed).
- **Main result:** The model outperforms comparison methods for short-range SST prediction. Specific errors not reported here.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times, larger domains and inclusion of atmospheric forcing.
- **Issues:** Purely data-driven regional model; limited lead times. Abstract unavailable.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A neural network-based estimate of the seasonal to inter-annual variability of the Atlantic Ocean carbon sink](https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-10-7793-2013)
Landschützer et al. (2013), *Biogeosciences*. 243 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimate the Atlantic Ocean CO2 sink and its seasonal to interannual variability from sparse surface pCO2 observations.
- **Architecture:** Two-step neural network approach: self-organizing map clustering into biogeochemical provinces followed by feed-forward networks per province to interpolate pCO2; fluxes from a gas-exchange parameterization.
- **Data:** SOCAT v1.5 surface ocean pCO2 observations, 1998-2007, with predictors such as SST, salinity, chlorophyll and mixed layer depth; independent check with time series and SOCAT v2.

### [Patterns of ocean current variability on the West Florida Shelf using the self-organizing map](https://doi.org/10.1029/2004jc002786)
Liu et al. (2005), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*. 241 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extracts patterns of ocean current variability on the West Florida Shelf.

### [Using self-organizing maps to identify patterns in satellite imagery](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pocean.2003.07.006)
Richardson et al. (2003), *Progress in Oceanography*. 241 citations.

- **Main goal:** Demonstrates self-organizing maps for identifying patterns in satellite imagery time series.

### [A spatiotemporal deep learning model for sea surface temperature field prediction using time-series satellite data](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2019.104502)
Xiao et al. (2019), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 236 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predict short- and mid-term daily SST fields while capturing spatial and temporal correlations.

Zheng et al. (2020), *Science Advances*. 227 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts sea surface temperature evolution associated with tropical instability waves, as a data-driven alternative to physics-based ocean models.

Sagawa et al. (2019), *Remote Sensing*. 218 citations.

Ali et al. (2019), *Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews*. 212 citations.

### [Source localization in an ocean waveguide using supervised machine learning](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5000165)

Rajasekaran et al. (2008), *Ocean Engineering*. 194 citations.

Mandal et al. (2006), *Ocean Engineering*. 179 citations.

### [Using Random forest and Gradient boosting trees to improve wave forecast at a specific location](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apor.2020.102339)
Callens et al. (2020), *Applied Ocean Research*. 178 citations.

### [Neural network for wave forecasting among multi-stations](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0029-8018(01)00112-3)
Tsai et al. (2002), *Ocean Engineering*. 169 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts waves at one station using records from neighbouring stations.
- **Architecture:** Back-propagation neural network (MLP) with multi-station inputs.
- **Data:** Wave records from coastal buoy stations in Taiwan.
- **Main result:** Multi-station neural network forecasts reproduce wave heights at target stations well.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and wind input.
- **Issues:** Dependent on station network; short records.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Coastal bathymetry from hyperspectral observations of water radiance](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0034-4257(98)00043-1)
Sandidge et al. (1998), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 166 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves shallow coastal water depth from airborne hyperspectral remote sensing of water-leaving radiance.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (backpropagation neural network) mapping hyperspectral radiance spectra to depth.
- **Data:** AVIRIS hyperspectral imagery over Florida coastal sites (e.g., Tampa Bay and the Florida Keys) with surveyed bathymetry for training and testing.
- **Main result:** The neural network retrieves depth in shallow waters with errors of a fraction of a metre over the training sites; specific values not reported here.
- **Open work:** Generalization across sites, water types and bottom types, and application to satellite sensors.
- **Issues:** Trained per site, so sensitive to water clarity and bottom reflectance; limited to optically shallow water.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [EddyNet: A Deep Neural Network For Pixel-Wise Classification of Oceanic Eddies](https://doi.org/10.1109/igarss.2018.8518411)
Lguensat et al. (2017), *IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium*. 165 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates detection and classification of ocean mesoscale eddies from altimetry.
- **Architecture:** EddyNet: convolutional encoder-decoder (U-Net-like) with pixel-wise classification into non-eddy, anticyclonic and cyclonic classes.
- **Data:** CMEMS sea surface height maps with labels from a conventional eddy detection algorithm.
- **Main result:** Produces pixel-wise eddy segmentation maps; code, data and weights are released. Quantitative accuracy not given in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Extending to 3D eddy structure, temporal tracking and other ocean variables.
- **Issues:** Labels come from a traditional detector, so the network inherits its definitions; limited to gridded altimetry resolution.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction and reconstruction of ocean wave heights based on bathymetric data using LSTM neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2021.109046)
Jörges et al. (2021), *Ocean Engineering*. 165 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs gaps and forecasts nearshore significant wave height off Norderney (North Sea), accounting for changing sandbank bathymetry, for coastal protection.
- **Architecture:** LSTM neural networks, including a parallel LSTM (P-LSTM), tuned with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and compared with deep feed-forward networks and other ML methods.
- **Data:** Sea state and weather time series from adjacent buoys and bathymetric surveys of the Ebb-Tidal Delta sandbanks, 2004–2017.
- **Main result:** Including bathymetry reduces RMSE by 16.7% for reconstruction and 7.4–11.7% and 8.8–9.1% for short- and long-term prediction; P-LSTM reaches 0.069 m RMSE for reconstruction.
- **Open work:** Transfer to other coasts with morphodynamic change and probabilistic prediction of extremes are open.
- **Issues:** Single site; bathymetry is sparse in time; extreme storm waves may be underrepresented in training.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [An Alternative to Static Climatologies: Robust Estimation of Open Ocean CO2 Variables and Nutrient Concentrations From T, S, and O2 Data Using Bayesian Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmars.2018.00328)
Bittig et al. (2018), *Frontiers in Marine Science*. 165 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates ocean carbonate system variables and nutrients from widely measured temperature, salinity and oxygen, as dynamic alternatives to static climatologies.
- **Architecture:** CANYON-B, a Bayesian neural network mapping with uncertainty estimates, plus CONTENT, which refines carbonate variables for chemical consistency.
- **Data:** GLODAPv2 bottle data for training; independent GO-SHIP bottle and sensor data for validation; applications to BGC-Argo and underway observations.
- **Main result:** Methods compare favourably with other mappings, resolve 40–120 d and 500–1500 km scales better than climatologies, and reveal a Revelle factor increase of 0.1–0.4 units per decade.
- **Open work:** Better surface pCO2 estimation in productive regions and integration across observing systems are open.
- **Issues:** pCO2 overestimated in highly productive surface waters due to O2–C decoupling; limited by training data coverage.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Automatic identification of oil spills on satellite images](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2004.11.010)
Keramitsoglou et al. (2006), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 163 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates detection of oil spills on satellite radar images to support marine pollution monitoring, replacing slow manual interpretation.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classification system that segments dark formations and scores them with geometric and contrast features to separate oil spills from look-alikes.
- **Data:** Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery over the Mediterranean; scene counts not reported here.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy system identifies most verified oil spills while discriminating many look-alike dark areas, offering a practical aid to operators.
- **Open work:** Larger validation sets, wind-condition dependence and integration into operational monitoring services.
- **Issues:** Look-alike phenomena (low wind, biogenic films) still cause false alarms; limited verified ground truth.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A fuzzy logic classification scheme for selecting and blending satellite ocean color algorithms](https://doi.org/10.1109/36.942555)
Moore et al. (2001), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 162 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves satellite chlorophyll retrieval across optically different waters by selecting and blending ocean color algorithms according to water type.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classification (fuzzy c-means memberships of remote-sensing reflectance spectra into optical water types) with membership-weighted blending of class-specific bio-optical algorithms.
- **Data:** In situ reflectance and chlorophyll data sets (SeaBASS-type collections) applied to SeaWiFS imagery.
- **Main result:** Membership-weighted blending yields smooth chlorophyll fields and lower retrieval errors than a single global algorithm across water types.
- **Open work:** Defining more water classes, especially for coastal Case 2 waters, and applying the scheme to other sensors.
- **Issues:** Class definitions depend on the in situ training set; coastal waters with sediments and CDOM remain poorly represented.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Sea water level forecasting using genetic programming and comparing the performance with Artificial Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cageo.2009.09.014)
Ghorbani et al. (2010), *Computers & Geosciences*. 158 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts sea water level for coastal engineering and management.
- **Architecture:** Genetic programming (symbolic regression) compared with artificial neural networks.
- **Data:** Tide gauge sea level time series; the station and period are not reported here.
- **Main result:** Genetic programming is reported to perform comparably to or better than ANNs for sea level forecasting; specific scores are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Longer horizons and multi-station tests would extend the comparison.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; single-station univariate forecasting ignores meteorological forcing.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Neural network prediction of a storm surge](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2005.04.012)
Lee (2006), *Ocean Engineering*. 153 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts storm surge during typhoons to support coastal warning in Taiwan.
- **Architecture:** Back-propagation neural network using wind speed, wind direction, pressure and astronomical tide as inputs.
- **Data:** Typhoon storm surge observations from tide gauges in Taiwan; number of events not reported here.
- **Main result:** The neural network predicts storm surge and its time series with good accuracy for the tested typhoons.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and more stations and events.
- **Issues:** Few typhoon events; site-specific; no uncertainty estimates.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Neural networks in ocean engineering](https://doi.org/10.1533/saos.2004.0005)
Jain et al. (2006), *Ships and Offshore Structures*. 153 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews applications of neural networks in ocean engineering to guide practitioners.
- **Architecture:** Review of neural network applications (mainly feedforward networks) for waves, tides, currents, structural response and related ocean engineering problems.
- **Data:** Review of published studies; no new data.
- **Main result:** Neural networks are found to be useful, accurate alternatives to conventional methods for many ocean engineering tasks.
- **Open work:** Better physical interpretability, uncertainty quantification and standardized comparisons.
- **Issues:** Narrative review; depth limited by available studies up to 2006.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Real-time wave forecasting using genetic programming](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2008.04.007)
Gaur et al. (2008), *Ocean Engineering*. 150 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts significant wave heights in real time at short lead times for offshore and coastal operations.
- **Architecture:** Genetic programming models using preceding wave observations, compared with artificial neural networks.
- **Data:** Wave buoy records from NDBC stations in the Gulf of Mexico.
- **Main result:** Genetic programming forecasts waves for leads of hours to a day with accuracy similar to or better than neural networks.
- **Open work:** Using wind inputs and longer lead times.
- **Issues:** Univariate inputs limit skill at longer leads; few buoys.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Neural network estimation of chlorophyll a from MERIS full resolution data for the coastal waters of Galician rias (NW Spain)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2010.09.021)
Vilas et al. (2011), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 148 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates chlorophyll-a in optically complex coastal waters where standard ocean colour algorithms perform poorly.

- **Data:** MERIS full-resolution imagery matched with in situ chlorophyll-a in the Galician rias, NW Spain.
- **Main result:** The neural network is reported to estimate chlorophyll-a better than standard MERIS products in these waters; metrics not available here.
- **Open work:** Validate on other coastal systems and sensors such as OLCI.
- **Issues:** Regional training limits transferability; small match-up dataset; details unverified without abstract.

### [Using SAR images to delineate ocean oil slicks with a texture-classifying neural network algorithm (TCNNA)](https://doi.org/10.5589/m09-035)
Garcia-Pineda et al. (2009), *Canadian Journal of Remote Sensing*. 145 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates delineation of oil slicks on the ocean surface in synthetic aperture radar imagery, replacing slow manual interpretation.
- **Architecture:** Texture-classifying neural network algorithm (TCNNA): a neural network that classifies SAR pixel textures, combined with edge detection and ancillary wind and beam-mode information.
- **Data:** RADARSAT and ENVISAT ASAR SAR scenes, mainly over the Gulf of Mexico including natural seep slicks.
- **Main result:** TCNNA delineates oil slicks consistently and much faster than manual analysis; detailed accuracy figures are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Extending to other SAR sensors and regions and reducing false positives from look-alikes such as low-wind areas.
- **Issues:** Look-alike features can confuse the classifier; performance depends on wind conditions; validation against independent slick truth is limited.

### [FathomNet: A global image database for enabling artificial intelligence in the ocean](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-19939-2)
Katija et al. (2021), *Scientific Reports*. 143 citations.

- **Main goal:** Addresses the lack of standardized, labeled underwater imagery that limits machine learning for ocean visual monitoring.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark dataset: FathomNet, an open-source image database aggregating expert-curated labeled imagery of marine animals, equipment and debris, demonstrated with object detection models.
- **Data:** Iconic and non-iconic underwater imagery from institutional archives such as MBARI video, with community contributions.
- **Main result:** FathomNet-trained models reduce annotation effort on other institutional video and enable automated tracking when integrated with robotic vehicles.
- **Open work:** Growing the database with more community-labeled data and taxa.
- **Issues:** Label coverage is uneven across taxa and regions; models may not generalize to new imaging systems.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [DINCAE 1.0: a convolutional neural network with error estimates to reconstruct sea surface temperature satellite observations](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-13-1609-2020)
Barth et al. (2019), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 138 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs missing sea surface temperature in cloud-affected satellite images, with error estimates.
- **Architecture:** DINCAE, a convolutional auto-encoder (CNN) that takes data and its error variance as input and outputs the reconstruction and its error variance, trained by maximum likelihood.
- **Data:** 25-year AVHRR sea surface temperature time series; validated by cross-validation and World Ocean Database in situ observations; compared with DINEOF.
- **Main result:** DINCAE has lower reconstruction error than DINEOF while preserving more variability.
- **Open work:** Multivariate inputs, other variables such as chlorophyll and better use of temporal context.
- **Issues:** Regional application; error estimates assume Gaussian errors; large gaps remain hard to fill.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Estimation of ocean subsurface thermal structure from surface parameters: A neural network approach](https://doi.org/10.1029/2004gl021192)
Ali et al. (2004), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 138 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates upper-ocean subsurface thermal structure from surface parameters measurable by satellite.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network mapping surface parameters to subsurface temperatures; the specific architecture is not specified here.
- **Data:** Moored buoy observations in the Arabian Sea of surface variables and temperature profiles.
- **Main result:** The neural network reproduces subsurface temperatures and thermal structure reasonably well from surface inputs; exact errors are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Applying with satellite inputs over wider regions.
- **Issues:** Single mooring region; training sample size small.

### [Predicting sea level variations with artificial neural networks at Hillarys Boat Harbour, Western Australia](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecss.2004.06.004)
Makarynskyy et al. (2004), *Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science*. 137 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts hourly sea level variations at a harbour for navigation and coastal management.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks (feed-forward) trained on past sea level observations.

- **Open work:** Including meteorological forcing to capture surges.
- **Issues:** Single gauge; non-tidal residuals are harder to predict.

Lee et al. (2002), *Ocean Engineering*. 137 citations.

- **Open work:** Long-term predictions and inclusion of non-astronomical effects.
- **Issues:** Single site; no storm-surge handling.

### [Regional ocean wave height prediction using sequential learning neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2016.10.033)
Kumar et al. (2017), *Ocean Engineering*. 136 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts regional ocean wave heights using neural networks that learn sequentially from streaming data.
- **Architecture:** Sequential learning neural networks of the radial basis function type that grow and prune neurons online (such as the minimal resource allocation network).
- **Data:** Buoy wave height observations from a regional network; region and period not recalled with confidence.

- **Open work:** Longer lead times and use of wind forecasts as inputs.
- **Issues:** Point buoy data only; performance details are not verified.

### [Review of the application of Artificial Neural Networks in ocean engineering](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2022.111947)
Juan et al. (2022), *Ocean Engineering*. 134 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews applications of artificial neural networks in ocean engineering.
- **Architecture:** Review of artificial neural network applications in ocean and coastal engineering, such as waves, tides and structures.
- **Data:** Review of published literature; no new data.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available information.
- **Open work:** Not reported; likely calls for deep learning and physics-informed approaches.

### [Prediction of sea surface temperature in the tropical Atlantic by support vector machines](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csda.2012.12.003)
Lins et al. (2013), *Computational Statistics & Data Analysis*. 131 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts sea surface temperature in the tropical Atlantic to support ocean-climate monitoring and forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine regression, with hyperparameters tuned by particle swarm optimization.
- **Data:** PIRATA moored buoy SST time series in the tropical Atlantic.
- **Main result:** The SVM model gives accurate SST predictions at the buoy sites; detailed skill numbers are not available in the record.
- **Open work:** Extending to multivariate predictors, longer lead times and spatial fields rather than point series.
- **Issues:** Point-wise univariate time-series setting; no uncertainty quantification; limited to buoy locations.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Estimation of subsurface temperature anomaly in the Indian Ocean during recent global surface warming hiatus from satellite measurements: A support vector machine approach](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2015.01.001)
Su et al. (2015), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 128 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates subsurface temperature anomalies in the Indian Ocean during the global surface warming hiatus from satellite surface observations.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine regression mapping surface variables to subsurface temperature anomalies at multiple depths.
- **Data:** Satellite sea surface height, temperature, salinity and wind observations, trained and validated with Argo profile data.
- **Main result:** SVM accurately estimates upper-ocean subsurface temperature anomalies and captures heat redistribution in the Indian Ocean during the hiatus; numbers not available in the record.

Karimi et al. (2013), *Computers & Geosciences*. 127 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts sea level in Darwin Harbor, Australia, for coastal management.
- **Architecture:** Adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system and artificial neural networks.
- **Data:** Sea level observations at Darwin Harbor, Australia; period not reported in the record.
- **Main result:** Neuro-fuzzy and neural network models are reported to forecast sea level accurately; comparison details not available in the record.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and inclusion of meteorological forcing.

### [Estimates of Water-Column Nutrient Concentrations and Carbonate System Parameters in the Global Ocean: A Novel Approach Based on Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmars.2017.00128)
Sauzède et al. (2017), *Frontiers in Marine Science*. 126 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates water-column nutrient and carbonate system variables globally from routinely measured hydrographic properties and oxygen, where direct biogeochemical observations are sparse.
- **Architecture:** CANYON: seven feed-forward neural networks (MLP), one per variable, taking temperature, salinity, pressure, oxygen, position and date as inputs.
- **Data:** GLODAPv2 bottle database, 80/20 random train/test split with eight 10°x10° zones withheld for independent validation; applied to the Hawaii Ocean Time-series (HOT).
- **Main result:** RMSEs of 0.93 µmol/kg NO3, 0.07 PO4, 3.0 Si(OH)4, 0.019 pH, 7 µmol/kg AT, 10 µmol/kg CT and 28 µatm pCO2; a 22-year HOT reconstruction agrees well with measurements.
- **Open work:** Combining CANYON with Biogeochemical-Argo oxygen profiles for large-scale, high-resolution biogeochemical estimates and model initialization or validation.
- **Issues:** Trained on GLODAPv2 so limited for coastal or poorly sampled regimes; no uncertainty per estimate and assumes stationary property relationships.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Retrieval of atmospheric and oceanic properties from MERIS measurements: A new Case‐2 water processor for BEAM](https://doi.org/10.1080/01431160701601774)
Schroeder et al. (2007), *International Journal of Remote Sensing*. 125 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves atmospheric and oceanic properties over optically complex Case-2 coastal waters from MERIS imagery, where standard algorithms fail.
- **Architecture:** Neural network (MLP) inversion of radiative transfer simulations for atmospheric correction and retrieval of water constituents (chlorophyll, suspended matter, yellow substance), implemented in the BEAM toolbox.
- **Data:** Radiative transfer simulations of coupled atmosphere-ocean system for training; ENVISAT MERIS measurements and in-situ data for evaluation.
- **Main result:** The processor provides atmospheric correction and Case-2 water constituent retrievals with reasonable agreement against in-situ measurements.
- **Open work:** Further validation in diverse coastal waters and regional tuning of inherent optical properties.
- **Issues:** Trained on simulations, so performance depends on the representativeness of the bio-optical model; validation data are limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Near-shore swell estimation from a global wind-wave model: Spectral process, linear, and artificial neural network models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.coastaleng.2006.11.007)
Browne et al. (2007), *Coastal Engineering*. 125 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates near-shore swell conditions economically by driving models from an offshore global wave model rather than running full nearshore simulations everywhere.
- **Architecture:** Data-driven linear regression and artificial neural network (nonlinear) models compared with the spectral wave simulation model SWAN.
- **Data:** NOAA WaveWatch3 global wind-wave model output offshore and near-shore wave observations at 17 locations around Australia over a 7-month period.
- **Main result:** The ANNs outperform SWAN and the nonlinear architecture consistently beats the linear method; performance variability is explained by local wave transformation complexity.
- **Open work:** Longer records, more sites and forecasting at longer horizons.
- **Issues:** Only 7 months of data; site-specific empirical models need local observations for training.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Global high resolution monthly pCO 2 climatology for the coastal ocean derived from neural network interpolation](https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-14-4545-2017)
Laruelle et al. (2017), *Biogeosciences*. 125 citations.

- **Main goal:** Quantifies coastal-ocean surface pCO2 and its seasonality, as continental shelf air–sea CO2 exchange is poorly constrained due to sparse sampling.
- **Architecture:** Modified two-step SOM-FFN neural network: self-organizing map clustering followed by feed-forward neural networks (MLP), with sea ice and wind speed added as predictors.

- **Main result:** Confirms a meridional pCO2 gradient on shelves and reveals strong basin differences in seasonality, larger at high latitudes and not explained by temperature alone.
- **Open work:** Merging with open-ocean pCO2 products into a seamless global climatology and estimating coastal air–sea CO2 fluxes.
- **Issues:** Coastal data remain sparse and heterogeneous, so interpolation uncertainty is large in undersampled shelves; predictor products carry their own biases.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Significant wave height forecasting using wavelet fuzzy logic approach](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2010.07.009)
Özger (2010), *Ocean Engineering*. 124 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts significant wave height for ocean engineering and coastal operations at multiple lead times.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid wavelet fuzzy logic: discrete wavelet decomposition of wave height series combined with a fuzzy logic inference model.
- **Data:** Significant wave height observations from ocean buoys; specific stations and periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** The wavelet fuzzy approach is reported to improve forecasts over plain fuzzy logic, especially at longer lead times.
- **Open work:** Adding wind forcing inputs and comparing with numerical wave models.
- **Issues:** Univariate buoy-based forecasts; non-causal wavelet decomposition can leak information; limited sites.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Stochastic‐Deep Learning Parameterization of Ocean Momentum Forcing](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021ms002534)
Guillaumin et al. (2021), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 123 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a stochastic, data-driven parameterization of mesoscale ocean eddy momentum forcing for coarse climate models.
- **Architecture:** CNN predicting mean and standard deviation of a Gaussian distribution of subgrid momentum forcing from coarse surface velocities, trained with a negative log-likelihood loss.
- **Data:** Coarse-grained surface velocities from selected subdomains of the high-resolution CM2.6 coupled climate model; tests on global ocean and increased-CO2 climate.
- **Main result:** Offline, the parameterization generalizes to the global ocean and to higher CO2 without retraining; implemented in an idealized eddy-permitting shallow water model it is stable and improves some flow statistics.
- **Open work:** Implementation in full ocean general circulation models and multi-layer settings; better spatial/temporal correlation of the stochastic noise.
- **Issues:** Surface-only training data; online test only in an idealized shallow water model; Gaussian, spatially uncorrelated noise assumption.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Back-propagation neural network for the prediction of the short-term storm surge in Taichung harbor, Taiwan](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2007.03.002)
Lee (2008), *Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence*. 123 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts short-term storm surge at Taichung harbor, Taiwan, during typhoons for coastal hazard warning.

Zamani et al. (2008), *Ocean Engineering*. 121 citations.

- **Data:** Buoy wind and wave observations; location and period not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Data-driven models forecast significant wave height with useful accuracy at short horizons, according to the authors.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and use of forecast winds from numerical weather prediction.

### [One-Day Wave Forecasts Based on Artificial Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/jtech1932.1)
Londhe et al. (2006), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 119 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides one-day-ahead significant wave height forecasts at buoy locations as a cheap alternative to numerical wave models.

### [Discrete wavelet neural network approach in significant wave height forecasting for multistep lead time](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2012.01.017)
Deka et al. (2012), *Ocean Engineering*. 116 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts significant wave height at multiple lead times for coastal and offshore operations.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid discrete wavelet transform plus artificial neural network (wavelet neural network): wave height series are decomposed into sub-series fed to an ANN.
- **Data:** Observed significant wave height time series from buoy records; location and period are not reported here.

### [Deep learning for ocean remote sensing: an application of convolutional neural networks for super-resolution on satellite-derived SST data](https://doi.org/10.1109/prrs.2016.7867019)
Ducournau et al. (2016), *2016 9th IAPR Workshop on Pattern Recogniton in Remote Sensing (PRRS)*. 114 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves the spatial resolution of satellite-derived sea surface temperature fields with deep learning.

### [Neural network‐based estimates of North Atlantic surface pCO2 from satellite data: A methodological study](https://doi.org/10.1029/2007jc004646)
Friedrich et al. (2009), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*. 113 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses how well neural networks can reconstruct North Atlantic surface pCO2 from satellite data given sparse ship sampling.
- **Architecture:** Neural network mapping satellite-observable variables to pCO2; the network type is not specified here.
- **Data:** Synthetic pCO2 and predictor fields from a North Atlantic biogeochemical model, sampled along ship tracks, with SST and chlorophyll as predictors.
- **Main result:** Neural networks reconstruct basin-scale pCO2 reasonably, with errors depending on sampling density and predictors.
- **Open work:** Applying to real observations and satellite products.
- **Issues:** Methodological study on model data; real-world errors likely larger.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [The OLCI Neural Network Swarm (ONNS): A Bio-Geo-Optical Algorithm for Open Ocean and Coastal Waters](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmars.2017.00140)
Hieronymi et al. (2017), *Frontiers in Marine Science*. 113 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean color products from Sentinel-3 OLCI across a wide range of optical water types, including extreme absorbing and scattering coastal waters.
- **Architecture:** Swarm of blended neural networks (MLP-type) specialized for 13 optical water classes, producing constituent concentrations, optical properties and uncertainty estimates.
- **Data:** Sentinel-3 OLCI reflectances; networks span chlorophyll up to 200 mg m-3, non-algae particles up to 1500 g m-3 and CDOM absorption up to 20 m-1.
- **Main result:** Baseline validation across water types indicates the algorithm is suitable for estimating water properties and constituents of most natural waters, with per-product uncertainties.
- **Open work:** Extend validation with more in situ matchups and refine atmospheric correction.
- **Issues:** Validation is a baseline; performance depends on atmospheric correction and on the simulated training data.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Comparison of statistical and artificial neural network techniques for estimating past sea surface temperatures from planktonic foraminifer census data](https://doi.org/10.1029/2000pa000562)
Malmgren et al. (2001), *Paleoceanography*. 111 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares methods for reconstructing past sea surface temperatures from planktonic foraminifer census counts, a key paleoclimate proxy transfer problem.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (feed-forward MLP) compared with statistical transfer techniques such as the modern analog technique and regression-based transfer functions.
- **Data:** Core-top planktonic foraminifer census data with modern sea surface temperatures (Atlantic calibration set); exact datasets not reported here.
- **Main result:** The artificial neural network gives the lowest prediction errors among the compared techniques for past sea surface temperature estimation.
- **Open work:** Applying the calibrated networks to downcore records and assessing no-analog conditions.
- **Issues:** Calibration set coverage limits reliability in no-analog past conditions; error estimates depend on cross-validation design.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Application of artificial neural networks to paleoceanographic data](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0031-0182(97)00031-x)

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs past sea surface temperatures from fossil planktonic foraminiferal assemblages for paleoceanography.

- **Data:** Core-top planktonic foraminiferal assemblages with modern SST for training; applied to down-core sediment data.
- **Main result:** Neural networks give SST estimates with errors comparable to or lower than conventional transfer functions.

### [Aerobic oxidation of methane significantly reduces global diffusive methane emissions from shallow marine waters](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-35082-y)
Mao et al. (2022), *Nature Communications*. 108 citations.

- **Main goal:** Quantifies aerobic methane oxidation in shallow marine waters and its role in limiting global ocean methane emissions.

- **Data:** Field observations in the East China Sea plus measured MOx rates, methane concentrations and other variables from a global database.
- **Main result:** About half of methane, 1.8 ± 2.7 Tg per year, is oxidised in global near-shore waters shallower than 50 m.

### [Reconstruction of regional mean sea level anomalies from tide gauges using neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1029/2009jc005630)
Wenzel et al. (2010), *Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans*. 107 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs regional and global mean sea level anomalies over the twentieth century from sparse tide gauge records.

- **Issues:** Short altimetry training period relative to reconstruction span; sparse, unevenly distributed gauges and stationarity assumption for the learned mapping.

- **Main result:** The neural network retrieves Kd(λ) accurately in both open and coastal waters, outperforming empirical band-ratio algorithms in turbid waters.

Hashemi et al. (2016), *Natural Hazards*. 106 citations.

- **Main result:** ANN outperforms SVM for extreme storms, with RMSE below 35 cm for observed and synthetic storms; about 200 storms are insufficient for a reliable model.

### [Neural network approximations for nonlinear interactions in wind wave spectra: direct mapping for wind seas in deep water](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ocemod.2003.12.008)
Tolman et al. (2005), *Ocean Modelling*. 83 citations.

- **Main goal:** Speeds up computation of the nonlinear four-wave interaction source term in spectral wind wave models, whose exact calculation is too expensive for operations.
- **Architecture:** Neural network (MLP) direct mapping from decomposed wave spectra to the nonlinear interaction term, using a parametric basis/EOF decomposition of inputs and outputs.
- **Data:** Deep-water wind-sea spectra and exact nonlinear interaction computations used for training and testing, in the context of the WAVEWATCH III model.
- **Main result:** The neural network approximates the exact interactions much better than the discrete interaction approximation for wind seas, at a fraction of the cost of exact computation.
- **Open work:** Extending the approach to finite depth, swell and complex multimodal spectra, and testing in full model integrations.
- **Issues:** Restricted to deep-water wind-sea spectra; behavior outside the training spectral shapes is not guaranteed.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Retrieval of oceanic chlorophyll concentration using support vector machines](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2003.819870)
Zhan et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 82 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves oceanic chlorophyll concentration from ocean-color remote-sensing reflectances more accurately than empirical band-ratio algorithms.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine (SVM) regression mapping remote-sensing reflectances to chlorophyll concentration.
- **Data:** In situ chlorophyll and remote-sensing reflectance pairs (the SeaBAM dataset at SeaWiFS bands).
- **Main result:** The SVM retrieval performs comparably to or better than standard band-ratio algorithms such as OC2 and OC4.
- **Open work:** Application to satellite imagery and to optically complex coastal (Case 2) waters.
- **Issues:** Trained on a limited in situ dataset dominated by open-ocean waters; card partly relies on knowledge.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Unsupervised neural method for temperature forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0954-1810(99)00007-2)
Corchado et al. (1999), *Artificial Intelligence in Engineering*. 81 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts temperature time series of oceanographic water masses in real time and extracts models of their thermal structure.
- **Architecture:** Unsupervised Negative Feedback Artificial Neural Network, compared with linear regression and ARIMA models.
- **Data:** Oceanographic temperature time series of water masses; source and period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The negative feedback network extracts the underlying model of the data and forecasts competitively with linear regression and ARIMA; numbers not reported.
- **Open work:** Further evaluation on other oceanographic variables and longer horizons is implied.
- **Issues:** Limited description of data and quantitative skill; univariate time-series approach without ocean physics.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deriving ocean color products using neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2013.02.015)
Ioannou et al. (2013), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 79 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean color products (inherent optical properties of seawater) from satellite remote sensing reflectance using neural networks, aiming at robust retrievals in coastal and open waters.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network (MLP) inversion mapping remote sensing reflectance at visible bands to inherent optical properties such as phytoplankton, CDOM and particle absorption/backscatter.
- **Data:** Trained on simulated (radiative-transfer-based) reflectance datasets and evaluated against in situ bio-optical data and MODIS satellite reflectance; exact sets and periods not confirmed here.
- **Main result:** The neural network retrievals agree reasonably with in situ data and compare favorably with standard ocean color algorithms; specific accuracies not reported here.
- **Open work:** Extending to optically complex coastal waters and other sensors would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** Trained largely on synthetic data, so performance depends on how representative the simulations are; atmospheric correction errors propagate to retrievals.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Wave forecasts using wind information and genetic programming](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2012.07.017)
Nitsure et al. (2012), *Ocean Engineering*. 78 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts ocean wave heights from wind information as a cheap alternative to numerical wave models.
- **Architecture:** Genetic programming (evolutionary symbolic regression) relating wind inputs to future wave parameters.
- **Data:** Wind and wave observations; sources, locations and periods not reported in the available information.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available information.
- **Open work:** Comparison with numerical wave models and longer lead times would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; site-specific empirical models may not generalize to other locations or extreme seas.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [DeepBlue: Advanced convolutional neural network applications for ocean remote sensing](https://doi.org/10.1109/mgrs.2023.3343623)
Wang et al. (2024), *IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine*. 77 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews how convolutional neural networks can process and analyze ocean remote sensing big data to solve practical oceanographic problems.
- **Architecture:** Review of convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures and variants applied to ocean remote sensing, including transfer learning and interpretability methods.
- **Data:** Review; covers ocean remote sensing data from multiple satellite sensors as used in the surveyed studies.
- **Main result:** CNNs meet most ocean remote sensing needs across six categories: 3D ocean field reconstruction, information extraction, image super-resolution, ocean phenomena forecast, transfer learning and interpretability.
- **Open work:** Authors summarize technical challenges and future research directions for CNN-based ocean remote sensing big data.
- **Issues:** Review focused on CNNs, so other architectures (transformers, diffusion models) receive less coverage.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Current Patterns on the West Florida Shelf from Joint Self-Organizing Map Analyses of HF Radar and ADCP Data](https://doi.org/10.1175/jtech1999.1)
Liu et al. (2007), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 76 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extracts the dominant joint surface and subsurface current patterns on the West Florida Shelf and their relation to wind forcing.
- **Architecture:** Self-organizing map applied jointly to surface current maps and moored velocity profiles to extract coupled spatial patterns; not a predictive model.
- **Data:** HF radar surface currents and moored ADCP velocity profiles on the West Florida Shelf, with local wind observations.
- **Main result:** The joint SOM identifies coherent current patterns, including upwelling- and downwelling-favourable responses linked to wind forcing, consistent between surface and subsurface.
- **Open work:** Longer records, seasonal stratification effects and use of the patterns to evaluate ocean circulation models.
- **Issues:** Short observational period and limited spatial coverage; SOM map size choices influence the extracted patterns.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Significant wave height and energy flux range forecast with machine learning classifiers](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2015.03.012)
Fernández et al. (2015), *Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence*. 75 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts ranges of significant wave height and wave energy flux for wave energy conversion using meteorological variables from numerical models.
- **Architecture:** Ordinal and nominal multi-class classifiers (machine learning classification), with ordinal classifiers as the proposed approach.
- **Data:** NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis variables at four points around two buoys (Gulf of Alaska and southeast United States) matched with buoy wave height and period.
- **Main result:** Ordinal classifiers give acceptable reconstructions and perform favorably relative to nominal ones for wave height and energy flux ranges.
- **Open work:** Testing with forecast (not reanalysis) inputs and more buoys would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** Coarse reanalysis inputs and only two buoys; class ranges give limited precision.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Characteristics of Global Ocean Abnormal Mesoscale Eddies Derived From the Fusion of Sea Surface Height and Temperature Data by Deep Learning](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021gl094772)
Liu et al. (2021), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 74 citations.

- **Main goal:** Maps the global distribution of abnormal mesoscale eddies (warm cyclonic, cold anticyclonic) by combining SSH and SST observations.
- **Architecture:** Deep learning framework fusing satellite SSH and SST to detect and classify eddies; architecture details not given in the abstract.
- **Data:** Global satellite SSH and SST data, 1996-2015.
- **Main result:** Abnormal eddies are about one third of all eddies, active along equatorial and unstable currents; seasonal contrasts by hemisphere; daily counts of normal (abnormal) eddies change by +9.68 (-11.80) per year.
- **Open work:** Investigate mechanisms behind abnormal eddies and their trends, including subsurface structure.
- **Issues:** Depends on detection accuracy and SST signal quality; trends may be affected by changing satellite sampling.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Marine-Radar Wind Sensor](https://doi.org/10.1109/igarss.2006.335)
Dankert et al. (2006), *2006 IEEE International Symposium on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 74 citations.

- **Main goal:** Measures marine surface wind vectors from nautical X-band radar sea-clutter images, offering a ship- or platform-based wind sensor.
- **Architecture:** Wind direction from wind-induced streaks in radar image sequences; wind speed from a neural network relating radar backscatter, direction and other parameters to speed.
- **Data:** Nautical X-band marine radar image sequences with in situ anemometer wind measurements from ship and platform deployments.
- **Main result:** Retrieved wind speed and direction agree well with in situ wind measurements over a range of conditions.
- **Open work:** Testing other radar systems and installations and combining with wave retrievals from the same radar.
- **Issues:** Calibration is installation specific; rain, low winds and platform effects degrade retrievals.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Application of machine-learning techniques toward the creation of a consistent and calibrated global chlorophyll concentration baseline dataset using remotely sensed ocean color data](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2003.818016)
Kwiatkowska et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 74 citations.

- **Main goal:** Creates a consistent, cross-calibrated global chlorophyll baseline from different ocean color sensors to support long-term records.
- **Architecture:** Machine-learning methods, mainly support vector machines and neural networks, mapping one sensor's radiances to another sensor's chlorophyll to remove inter-sensor differences.
- **Data:** SeaWiFS and MODIS ocean color observations with in situ chlorophyll used for comparison.
- **Main result:** Support vector machines and neural networks bring MODIS-derived chlorophyll into close agreement with SeaWiFS, supporting a merged baseline dataset.
- **Open work:** Extending to more sensors and longer periods and propagating uncertainty in merged products.
- **Issues:** Calibration to a reference sensor inherits its biases; generalization outside the training conditions is uncertain.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Significant wave height record extension by neural networks and reanalysis wind data](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ocemod.2015.08.002)
Peres et al. (2015), *Ocean Modelling*. 74 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extends short buoy records of significant wave height backwards in time by learning the relation between reanalysis winds and measured waves, to support coastal and wave-climate studies.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward artificial neural network that maps reanalysis wind fields over the generation area to significant wave height at a buoy location.
- **Data:** Reanalysis wind data (ERA-Interim) as inputs and buoy significant wave height observations in the Mediterranean (Sicily) as targets; exact periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** The neural network reproduces observed wave heights with good accuracy, allowing reconstruction of wave records for periods without buoy measurements.
- **Open work:** Testing at more buoys and sea basins, and comparing against physics-based wave hindcasts, would establish how general the approach is.
- **Issues:** Accuracy is bounded by reanalysis wind quality, particularly in coastal and storm conditions; extremes are sparse in training and may be underestimated.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Elucidating ecological complexity: Unsupervised learning determines global marine eco-provinces](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aay4740)
Sonnewald et al. (2020), *Science Advances*. 73 citations.

- **Main goal:** Objectively defining global marine ecological provinces to tame complexity of ecosystem model output and community structure.
- **Architecture:** Unsupervised learning (SAGE method): t-SNE dimensionality reduction, DBSCAN clustering, and a connectivity graph to aggregate eco-provinces.
- **Data:** Plankton community structure and nutrient flux output from a global ecosystem model (the MIT Darwin model).
- **Main result:** Over a hundred eco-provinces are identified and nested into robust aggregated eco-provinces, used to explore nutrient supply control on community structure.
- **Open work:** Model intercomparison and monitoring of marine ecosystems with observations.
- **Issues:** Based on model output rather than observations; clustering depends on hyperparameter choices.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Reconstruction of Subsurface Velocities From Satellite Observations Using Iterative Self-Organizing Maps](https://doi.org/10.1109/lgrs.2017.2665603)
Chapman et al. (2016), *IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters*. 73 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructing deep ocean current velocities from satellite surface observations.
- **Architecture:** Iterative, modified self-organizing maps (SOM) exploiting local data-space correlations.
- **Data:** Satellite surface velocity, sea surface height and sea surface temperature, with deep velocities from Argo floats at 1000 m.
- **Main result:** Speed RMSE of about 2.8 cm/s, more than a factor of two smaller than competing methods, with direction errors under 30°.
- **Open work:** Extending to other depths and regions.
- **Issues:** Limited by Argo float coverage; single depth.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Application of artificial neural networks to tide forecasting
Sun (2007), *Journal of Dalian University of Technology*. 73 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts tidal levels with artificial neural networks as an alternative to harmonic analysis.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network for tide forecasting; network type not reported here.
- **Data:** Tide-gauge records from Chinese coastal stations; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Neural networks produce accurate tide forecasts comparable to or better than harmonic analysis.
- **Open work:** Including meteorological effects and longer forecast periods.
- **Issues:** Details on data and validation are not available; surge-dominated events may not be captured.

### [Development of a Neural Network Algorithm for Retrieving Concentrations of Chlorophyll, Suspended Matter and Yellow Substance from Radiance Data of the Ocean Color and Temperature Scanner](https://doi.org/10.1023/b:joce.0000038345.99050.c0)
Tanaka et al. (2004), *Journal of Oceanography*. 72 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves chlorophyll, suspended matter and yellow substance from satellite ocean color radiances in optically complex waters.

- **Data:** Simulated top-of-atmosphere or water-leaving radiances from a radiative transfer model; ADEOS OCTS radiance data; in situ measurements for validation.
- **Main result:** The neural network retrieves the three constituents from OCTS radiances with reasonable agreement against in situ data.
- **Open work:** Applying the algorithm to other sensors and regions with regional bio-optical models.
- **Issues:** Accuracy depends on the bio-optical model behind the simulations; limited in situ validation.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Automatic classification of water-leaving radiance anomalies from global SeaWiFS imagery: Application to the detection of phytoplankton groups in open ocean waters.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2013.08.046)
Mustapha et al. (2014), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 72 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automatically identifies dominant phytoplankton groups in open-ocean waters from satellite ocean colour radiance anomalies.

- **Data:** Global SeaWiFS imagery, with phytoplankton group labels from in situ pigment-based observations.
- **Main result:** The automatic classification reproduces and extends PHYSAT phytoplankton group detection in open-ocean waters.
- **Open work:** Applying the method to other sensors and longer time series would allow analysis of phytoplankton community changes.
- **Issues:** Limited to open-ocean (Case 1) waters; in situ group labels are sparse, and anomaly signals can be confounded by other optical constituents.

### [Prediction models for tidal level including strong meteorologic effects using a neural network](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2007.12.006)
Liang et al. (2008), *Ocean Engineering*. 71 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts tidal levels including strong meteorological effects such as storm surges, where harmonic analysis alone fails.
- **Architecture:** Neural network models (type not specified) combining astronomical tide and meteorological inputs.
- **Data:** Tide-gauge and meteorological records from Chinese coastal stations; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Including meteorological factors in neural network models improves tidal level predictions during strong weather events.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and use of forecast meteorology.
- **Issues:** Few strong events; site-specific training.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Water Level Observations and Short-Term Predictions Including Meteorological Events for Entrance of Galveston Bay, Texas](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)0733-950x(2002)128:1(21))
Cox et al. (2002), *Journal of Waterway, Port, Coastal, and Ocean Engineering*. 70 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves short-term water level predictions at the entrance of Galveston Bay, where meteorological forcing makes astronomical tide tables inaccurate.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (feedforward) using past water levels and wind observations as inputs, compared with harmonic tide predictions.
- **Data:** Water level and meteorological observations from the Texas Coastal Ocean Observation Network stations near Galveston Bay.
- **Main result:** The neural network forecasts water levels for horizons of hours to about a day considerably better than tide tables, especially during frontal passages.
- **Open work:** Adding forecast winds and extending to other Texas coastal stations.
- **Issues:** Site-specific; skill decays with lead time; extreme storm surges are rare in training data.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Forecasting the SST Space‐time variability of the Alboran Sea with genetic algorithms](https://doi.org/10.1029/1999gl011226)
Alvarez et al. (1999), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts the space-time variability of sea surface temperature in the Alboran Sea using a nonlinear data-driven technique.
- **Architecture:** Genetic algorithm combined with empirical orthogonal function (EOF) analysis; the genetic algorithm finds equations describing each EOF temporal amplitude.
- **Data:** Sea surface temperature fields of the Alboran Sea (satellite-derived); period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The method enables global forecasting of the future SST variability of the basin; quantitative skill not reported in the abstract.

### [Short-term forecasting of the wave energy flux: Analogues, random forests, and physics-based models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2015.05.038)
Ibarra-Berastegi et al. (2015), *Ocean Engineering*. 69 citations.

### [Applying artificial neural network methodology to ocean color remote sensing](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0304-3800(99)00105-2)
Gross et al. (1999), *Ecological Modelling*. 67 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean properties such as chlorophyll concentration from satellite ocean colour reflectances, improving on empirical band-ratio algorithms.

### [Improved Quantification of Ocean Carbon Uptake by Using Machine Learning to Merge Global Models and pCO2 Data](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021ms002620)
Gloege et al. (2021), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 66 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improve estimates of surface ocean pCO2 and air-sea CO2 flux by combining mechanistic biogeochemical models with sparse observations.
- **Architecture:** LDEO-HPD: XGBoost learns the model-data pCO2 misfit from observed predictors, then corrects global ocean biogeochemical model fields.

Merwe et al. (2007), *Neural Networks*. 66 citations.

Manucharyan et al. (2020), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 65 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstruct continuous sea surface height from sparse altimetry and infer unobserved deep ocean currents from SSH.

Sonnewald et al. (2019), *Earth and Space Science*. 54 citations.

Dankert et al. (2003), *IGARSS 2003. 2003 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium. Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.03CH37477)*. 9 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean surface wind vectors from sequences of marine X-band nautical radar images, enabling wind measurement from ships and offshore platforms.
- **Architecture:** Wind direction is derived from wind-induced streaks in the radar images, and wind speed from the mean radar backscatter using a neural network model trained against in situ wind data.
- **Data:** X-band nautical radar image sequences from offshore platforms with collocated anemometer measurements; exact sites and period not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Retrieved wind speed and direction agree well with in situ reference measurements; exact error statistics are not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Validation at more sites and radar installations, and extension to rain and low-wind conditions.
- **Issues:** Retrieval depends on radar installation and calibration; low winds and rain degrade backscatter; trained against local in situ data, so transfer to other radars may need retraining.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Machine Learning‐Based Model Infers the Sea Surface Velocity of Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT)](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024gl110731)
Zhou et al. (2025), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 8 citations.

- **Main goal:** Infers total sea surface velocity, including ageostrophic components, from SWOT sea surface height for submesoscale studies.
- **Architecture:** Machine-learning model mapping SWOT-derived fields to drifter-observed velocities; model type not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** SWOT satellite sea surface height and geostrophic velocity with drifter velocities as targets; compared with reanalysis kinetic energy.
- **Main result:** Errors relative to drifter velocities are reduced by about 50% versus SWOT geostrophic velocity; kinetic energy agrees better with reanalysis, especially at low latitudes.
- **Open work:** Global application to produce high-resolution SSV products and study submesoscale dynamics.
- **Issues:** Drifters are sparse and include wind-driven components; short SWOT record; validation against reanalysis is indirect.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Online Learning in Idealized Ocean Gyres](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024ms004883)
Maddison (2024), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 8 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests online (end-to-end) learning of neural network eddy parameterizations in an idealized ocean gyre.
- **Architecture:** Neural network forcing an automatically differentiable barotropic dynamical solver, trained online through the hybrid system dynamics.
- **Data:** High-resolution simulations of the idealized barotropic Stommel-Munk wind-driven gyre as reference.
- **Main result:** A suitably trained NN yields a stable coarse model with reasonable mean state and intrinsic variability, with some generalization to modified wind forcing.
- **Open work:** Enforcing symmetries and extending online learning to more realistic baroclinic ocean models.
- **Issues:** Highly idealized barotropic setting; the NN parameterized model fails to respect an intrinsic symmetry of the system.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [ORCAst: Operational High-Resolution Current Forecasts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12054)
Garcia et al. (2025), *arXiv*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces operational, high-resolution global nowcasts and week-long forecasts of ocean surface currents from incomplete satellite and in situ observations.
- **Architecture:** Multi-stage, multi-arm encoder-decoder neural network (ORCAst) that first predicts sea surface height and geostrophic currents, then total surface currents.
- **Data:** Trained entirely on observations: nadir and SWOT altimetry for SSH and geostrophic currents, and sparse drifter velocities for surface currents; regional training variants.
- **Main result:** Achieves stronger nowcast and forecast skill for ocean surface currents than various state-of-the-art methods; region-specific training further improves performance.
- **Open work:** Integrate more observation types, extend lead times and improve global generalization without regional retraining.
- **Issues:** Drifter ground truth is sparse and unevenly distributed; quantitative gains and baselines are not detailed in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Artificial neural network-based inversion technique for extracting ocean surface wave spectra from SAR images](https://doi.org/10.1109/igarss.1997.606394)
Kasilingam et al. (1997), *IGARSS'97. 1997 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium Proceedings. Remote Sensing - A Scientific Vision for Sustainable Development*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extracts ocean surface wave spectra from synthetic aperture radar images, addressing the nonlinear inversion of SAR imaging of waves.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network trained as an inversion operator from SAR image spectra to ocean wave spectra.
- **Data:** SAR image spectra, likely simulated with a SAR imaging model, paired with wave spectra; specific datasets not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Reports that the neural network inversion recovers wave spectra from SAR images; accuracy figures not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Validation with real SAR data and buoy spectra, and handling azimuth cutoff effects.
- **Issues:** Training on modelled spectra may not represent real SAR imaging nonlinearity; limited validation.
- *Basis: assessment*

### Development of an Expert System for Interpretation of Oceanographic Images
Thomason et al. (1986), *Venue not recorded*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops an expert system to interpret oceanographic satellite images, automating identification of ocean features.
- **Architecture:** Expert system (rule-based) combining image processing with oceanographic knowledge to label image features.
- **Data:** Oceanographic satellite images, such as infrared imagery of ocean features; specific datasets not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Demonstrates prototype automated interpretation of oceanographic images; quantitative accuracy not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Expanding the knowledge base and testing on more image sequences.
- **Issues:** Cloud cover and ambiguous features challenge rule-based interpretation; limited evaluation.
- *Basis: assessment*

### Estimation of ocean surface currents from satellite imagery using a Hopfield neural network
Côté et al. (1996), *Marine Technology Society Journal*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates ocean surface currents from sequential satellite imagery by tracking feature displacements.
- **Architecture:** Hopfield neural network used as an optimization method to match features between image pairs and derive current vectors.
- **Data:** Sequential satellite images of the ocean surface, such as infrared imagery; specific datasets not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Reports that the Hopfield network yields surface current fields from image sequences comparable to conventional matching; figures not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Validation against in situ current measurements and operational application.
- **Issues:** Feature tracking fails in cloud-covered or featureless areas; only advective surface motion is captured.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Application of multilayered neural networks to ocean acoustic tomography inversions](https://doi.org/10.1080/174159796088027628)
Stéphan et al. (1996), *Inverse Problems in Engineering*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Inverts ocean acoustic tomography measurements to recover the ocean sound-speed structure, a nonlinear inverse problem.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (multilayered neural network) trained to map acoustic observables to parameters of the sound-speed field.
- **Data:** Simulated acoustic tomography data generated from ocean sound-speed profiles with an acoustic propagation model; details are not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Shows that multilayer networks can perform the tomographic inversion efficiently and with accuracy comparable to classical inversion; numbers not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Application to real tomography experiments and handling of measurement noise and range-dependent environments.
- **Issues:** Likely trained and tested on simulations; performance on real ocean data and outside the training distribution is uncertain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Data mining using example-based methods in oceanographic forecast models](https://doi.org/10.1049/ic:19980550)
Corchado et al. (1998), *Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts ocean thermal structure ahead of a moving research vessel by mining past examples rather than running a physical model.
- **Architecture:** Example-based methods: case-based reasoning combined with a radial basis function neural network that adapts retrieved cases to produce forecasts.
- **Data:** Oceanographic temperature measurements recorded along research cruise tracks in the Atlantic; exact cruises and sample sizes are not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Shows the hybrid case-based reasoning and neural network system forecasts water temperature more accurately than the compared statistical and single-method approaches.
- **Open work:** Extending the system to other variables and regions and automating case base maintenance.
- **Issues:** Forecasts are short-range and local to the ship track; performance depends on the coverage of past cases.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A deep learning global ocean forecasting model with sub-daily and eddy-resolving resolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01444-2)
Niu et al. (2026), *npj Climate and Atmospheric Science*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Delivers global ocean forecasts at sub-daily, eddy-resolving resolution with deep learning, independent of NWP atmospheric forcing.
- **Architecture:** Deep learning ocean forecasting model (FuXi-Ocean) that adaptively fuses forecasts across multiple temporal windows to limit autoregressive error growth; network family not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Global 1/12° ocean data to 1500 m depth at 6-hourly steps (likely an ocean reanalysis such as GLORYS); near-surface atmospheric variables for initialization; evaluation for 2022.
- **Main result:** Stable 10-day forecasts despite four times more autoregressive steps than daily models, outperforming WenHai for temperature, salinity, currents, SST and sea level anomaly.
- **Open work:** Extend lead times and fully couple with AI atmospheric models.
- **Issues:** Evaluated over a single year, likely against reanalysis; omits deeper ocean below 1500 m; NWP-independence limits use of atmospheric forecast information.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Neural prediction of Lagrangian drift trajectories on the sea surface](https://doi.org/10.1175/aies-d-24-0052.1)
Botvynko et al. (2025), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Simulates Lagrangian drift trajectories at the sea surface more accurately than model-based and learning-based methods.
- **Architecture:** DriftNet, a deep convolutional neural network inspired by the Eulerian Fokker-Planck representation, taking Eulerian surface currents and an encoded initial position.
- **Data:** Two benchmarks with fully simulated ocean data and one combining operational ocean reanalysis with in situ drifters; North East Pacific and Gulf Stream regions; SSH inputs from model and observations.
- **Main result:** DriftNet outperforms state-of-the-art model-based and learning-based drift methods; the study also quantifies the influence of SSH inputs on drift simulation.
- **Open work:** Extend to global domains, longer trajectories and observation-only inputs.
- **Issues:** Two regions only; depends on quality of input current fields; quantitative gains not given in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Development of the pattern recognition and the spatial integration filtering methods for analyzing satellite altimeter data](https://doi.org/10.1016/0034-4257(94)90137-6)
Yan et al. (1994), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extracts ocean features from satellite altimeter data, where signals are noisy and sampled along tracks.
- **Architecture:** Pattern recognition method combined with a spatial integration filtering technique applied to altimetric sea surface height; not a neural network approach.
- **Data:** Satellite altimeter sea surface height data; mission and region not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Shows the methods can identify and map oceanic features such as eddies or fronts from altimeter data; quantitative results not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Application to longer altimeter records and other ocean regions.
- **Issues:** Relies on along-track sampling and filtering choices; validation against in situ data not described in the available record.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [wasserstandsvorhersage mittels neuronaler netze](https://doi.org/10.1007/bf02765119)
Röske (1997), *Deutsche Hydrographische Zeitschrift*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts water levels (Wasserstandsvorhersage) with neural networks, as a data-driven alternative or complement to conventional water-level prediction methods.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network; the specific network type, inputs and training scheme are not reported in the available metadata.
- **Data:** Not reported in the abstract; the title implies observed water-level time series, but the gauges, region and period are unknown.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; no quantitative skill is available from the metadata.
- **Open work:** Comparison against operational hydrodynamic or statistical forecasts and extension to longer lead times and extreme water levels would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** German-language report with no abstract; data, lead times and evaluation are unknown, and early neural networks of this era were typically small and trained on limited records.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Data-driven global ocean model resolving atmospherically forced ocean dynamics](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aed1225)
Kim et al. (2025), *Science Advances*. 1 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a deep learning global 3D ocean model able to simulate oceanic responses to atmospheric forcing, as a step toward coupled DL climate models.
- **Architecture:** KIST-Ocean: a deep learning global three-dimensional ocean general circulation model forced by atmospheric fields; network family not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Global ocean reanalysis and atmospheric forcing data; specific products not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Shows robust, efficient ocean simulation and reproduces Kelvin and Rossby wave propagation and wind-stress-curl-driven vertical motions underlying ENSO.
- **Open work:** Coupling with DL atmosphere models toward integrated Earth system simulation and long-range climate prediction.
- **Issues:** Quantitative skill metrics and data sources are not given in the abstract; trained on reanalysis so inherits its biases; uncoupled ocean-only setting.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Estimate of significant wave height from non-coherent marine radar images by multilayer perceptrons](https://doi.org/10.1186/1687-6180-2012-84)
Vicen-Bueno et al. (2012), *EURASIP Journal on Advances in Signal Processing*. 0 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates significant wave height (Hs) from non-coherent X-band marine radar images, where the standard SNR-based linear method fails for swell-dominated seas.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptrons (MLP) using the square root of SNR, peak wavelength and mean wave period as inputs.
- **Data:** WaMoS II radar-derived sea state parameters from Ekofisk and FINO 1 platforms in the North Sea, with reference Hs.
- **Main result:** The MLP method outperforms the standard linear SNR method at both platforms regardless of environmental conditions, while keeping real-time capability.
- **Open work:** Test at more sites and radar configurations and quantify uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Only two platforms; error magnitudes are not given in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*
