## Air quality & chemistry

### [An ensemble-based model of PM2.5 concentration across the contiguous United States with high spatiotemporal resolution.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envint.2019.104909)
Di et al. (2019), *Environment International*. 683 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produce high-resolution daily PM2.5 estimates across the contiguous US for health and epidemiology studies.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble of neural network, random forest and gradient boosting combined by a geographically weighted generalized additive model; separate model for uncertainty.
- **Data:** Satellite AOD, meteorology, land use, elevation, chemical transport model output, reanalyses and monitor PM2.5, 2000-2015.
- **Main result:** 10-fold cross-validated R2 of 0.86 for daily and 0.89 for annual PM2.5 at 1 km; good performance up to 60 ug/m3; downscaled to 100 m with uncertainty estimates.
- **Open work:** Explore other ensemble formats to merge estimates from different models or groups.
- **Issues:** Weaker performance at very high concentrations; cross-validation may overstate skill in monitor-sparse areas; 100 m downscaling relies only on land use.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Improved 1 km resolution PM 2.5 estimates across China using enhanced space–time extremely randomized trees](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-20-3273-2020)
Wei et al. (2020), *Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics*. 680 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produce high-quality, 1 km daily surface PM2.5 maps over China to support air-pollution monitoring at urban scale, where satellite and ground data alone are insufficient.
- **Architecture:** Enhanced space-time extremely randomized trees (STET), a tree ensemble augmented with spatiotemporal information and auxiliary predictors.
- **Data:** MODIS MAIAC 1 km AOD plus meteorological, topographic, land-use and emission data, with ground-station PM2.5 as targets; daily maps for 2018 over mainland China (ChinaHighPM2.5).
- **Main result:** Out-of-sample (out-of-station) cross-validation R2 of 0.89 (0.88), RMSE 10.33 (10.93) ug/m3, MAE 6.69 (7.15) ug/m3; outperforms most previous models and supports historical estimation (monthly R2 0.80).
- **Open work:** Extending the dataset to longer periods and other pollutants, and improving estimates where AOD retrievals are missing.
- **Issues:** Depends on AOD availability (cloud and snow gaps); only one year evaluated in detail; cross-validation at stations may overstate skill in sparsely monitored regions.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Deep CNN-LSTM Model for Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Forecasting in Smart Cities](https://doi.org/10.3390/s18072220)
Huang et al. (2018), *Sensors*. 649 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts PM2.5 concentrations in smart cities for pollution control.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) model named APNet.
- **Data:** Historical PM2.5 concentration, cumulated rain hours and cumulated wind speed; location and period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** APNet achieves the best MAE, RMSE, correlation and index of agreement among compared machine learning methods.
- **Open work:** Applying the model to PM2.5 prevention and control and adding further meteorological inputs.
- **Issues:** Limited inputs; no spatial transfer test; numbers not given in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Long short-term memory neural network for air pollutant concentration predictions: Method development and evaluation.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2017.08.114)
Li et al. (2017), *Environmental Pollution*. 599 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts hourly air pollutant concentrations, especially PM2.5, by exploiting long-term temporal dependence and spatial correlation among monitoring stations.
- **Architecture:** Extended long short-term memory network (LSTME) that adds spatiotemporal correlations and auxiliary inputs such as meteorology and time stamps to a recurrent neural network.
- **Data:** Hourly PM2.5 concentrations from air quality monitoring stations in Beijing, China, with meteorological data; period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The LSTM-based model outperforms spatiotemporal deep learning, time-delay neural network, ARMA and support vector regression baselines in hourly PM2.5 prediction.
- **Open work:** Extension to other pollutants, longer lead times and other cities.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; single city; no emission or chemical transport inputs, so performance under unusual emission changes is untested.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A hybrid model for spatiotemporal forecasting of PM2.5 based on graph convolutional neural network and long short-term memory.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2019.01.333)
Qi et al. (2019), *Science of The Total Environment*. 567 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts spatiotemporal PM2.5 concentrations across monitoring stations up to 72 hours ahead.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid graph convolutional network and LSTM (GC-LSTM): stations form a spatiotemporal graph series whose node signals are processed by graph convolution and an LSTM.
- **Data:** Historical station air quality observations, meteorological factors, spatial terms and temporal attributes from ground monitoring stations; region and period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** GC-LSTM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines; for 72-h predictions recall is 68.45% and false alarm rate 4.65% at 115 μg/m3, with R2 of 0.72.
- **Open work:** Apply to other pollutants and regions; add emissions or chemical transport model inputs.
- **Issues:** Moderate skill at 72 h; station-only graph without explicit transport physics; single study region.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Tracking Air Pollution in China: Near Real-Time PM2.5 Retrievals from Multisource Data Fusion.](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.1c01863)
Geng et al. (2021), *Environmental Science & Technology*. 541 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides full-coverage, near real-time daily PM2.5 data over China for research, management and health studies.
- **Architecture:** Two-stage machine learning model with tree-based learners, synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) for high pollution, and a tree-based gap-filling method for missing AOD.
- **Data:** Ground observations, satellite AOD, operational chemical transport model simulations, meteorology, land use, population and elevation; daily 10 km PM2.5 since 2000 (TAP dataset).
- **Main result:** Out-of-bag cross-validation R2 averages 0.83, with improved performance at high pollution levels and gap-filled daily coverage.
- **Open work:** Extend TAP to other pollutants and support policy and health impact assessments.
- **Issues:** Out-of-bag CV can overstate skill in sparsely monitored areas; pre-2013 estimates rely on extrapolation where few ground stations existed.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Artificial neural networks forecasting of PM2.5 pollution using air mass trajectory based geographic model and wavelet transformation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2015.02.030)
Feng et al. (2015), *Atmospheric Environment*. 537 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves two-day-ahead forecasts of daily PM2.5 in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, especially of high pollution days.
- **Architecture:** MLP (back-propagation neural network) hybrid with an air-mass-trajectory-based geographic indicator and wavelet decomposition of the PM2.5 series into sub-series forecast separately.
- **Data:** 13 monitoring stations in the Jing-Jin-Ji area, September 2013 to October 2014, with daily meteorological forecasts and pollutant predictors.
- **Main result:** The hybrid reduces RMSE by up to 40% on average, and the detection rate of high PM2.5 days reaches about 90%.
- **Open work:** Apply the approach to other countries' air quality forecasting systems.
- **Issues:** About one year of data; wavelet decomposition may leak future information if not done causally; region-specific trajectory corridors.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [GeoMAN: Multi-level Attention Networks for Geo-sensory Time Series Prediction](https://doi.org/10.24963/ijcai.2018/476)
Liang et al. (2018), *International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence*. 536 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts geo-sensor readings several hours ahead, accounting for dynamic spatio-temporal correlations and external factors.
- **Architecture:** GeoMAN: multi-level attention-based recurrent neural network (encoder-decoder LSTM with local and global spatial attention and temporal attention) plus an external-factor fusion module.
- **Data:** Real-world air quality sensor data and water quality data, with meteorological and spatial data.
- **Main result:** Outperforms nine baseline methods on both air quality and water quality datasets.
- **Open work:** Extend to longer horizons and more sensor types; improve scalability to large networks.
- **Issues:** Single-sensor target forecasting; evaluated on limited cities and data periods.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Forecasting Fine-Grained Air Quality Based on Big Data](https://doi.org/10.1145/2783258.2788573)
Zheng et al. (2015), *Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining*. 534 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts fine-grained air quality at monitoring stations for the next 48 hours using big data, to support public warnings.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid data-driven system combining a linear-regression temporal predictor, a neural network spatial predictor, a dynamic aggregator and an inflection predictor for sudden changes.
- **Data:** Air quality, meteorological data and weather forecasts from monitoring stations in Chinese cities.
- **Main result:** The system outperforms classical baselines, notably in predicting sudden changes, and was deployed operationally; exact scores not reported here.
- **Open work:** Extend to more cities and pollutants and to longer horizons.
- **Issues:** Station-based forecasting without explicit chemistry; performance at long horizons and in extreme episodes is limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A machine learning method to estimate PM2.5 concentrations across China with remote sensing, meteorological and land use information.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2018.04.251)
Chen et al. (2018), *Science of The Total Environment*. 532 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates historical daily ground-level PM2.5 across China during 2005–2016 for exposure assessment.
- **Architecture:** Random forest regression compared with two traditional regression models.
- **Data:** Daily PM2.5 from 1479 stations (2014–2016), satellite AOD, meteorology and other predictors; national estimates at 0.1° for 2005–2016.
- **Main result:** Random forest explains most variability: 10-fold CV R2 = 83%, RMSE = 28.1 μg/m3 daily; up to 86% at monthly and annual scales (RMSE 10.7 and 6.9 μg/m3).
- **Open work:** Use the estimates for long-term health studies and validate pre-2014 back-extrapolation.
- **Issues:** Model trained on 2014–2016 but applied back to 2005, assuming stable relationships; random CV may overstate spatial skill.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Multiple linear regression and artificial neural networks based on principal components to predict ozone concentrations](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2005.12.002)
Sousa et al. (2007), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 524 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts next-day ozone concentrations for air quality forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Multiple linear regression and feedforward neural network (MLP) models using principal components as inputs.
- **Data:** Hourly ozone, other pollutant and meteorological measurements from Oporto, Portugal.
- **Main result:** Principal-component-based feedforward neural networks give the best ozone predictions.
- **Open work:** Other sites and pollutants; longer horizons.
- **Issues:** Single urban area; statistical models without chemistry.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A machine learning calibration model using random forests to improve sensor performance for lower-cost air quality monitoring](https://doi.org/10.5194/amt-11-291-2018)
Zimmerman et al. (2018), *Atmospheric Measurement Techniques*. 498 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves calibration of low-cost multipollutant air quality sensors affected by environmental conditions and cross-sensitivities.
- **Architecture:** Random forest calibration models compared with laboratory univariate and empirical multiple linear regression.
- **Data:** 16–19 RAMP sensor packages (CO, NO2, O3, CO2) collocated with reference monitors in Pittsburgh, PA, August 2016–February 2017.
- **Main result:** RF matches or beats other calibrations; MAE 38 ppb CO, 10 ppm CO2, 3.5 ppb NO2, 3.4 ppb O3, Pearson r above 0.8, and only RF meets EPA personal exposure data-quality guidance.
- **Open work:** Deploy dense calibrated networks and develop multipollutant sensor packages.
- **Issues:** Calibration may not transfer to other climates or concentration ranges; NO2 relative error remains about 29%.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Comparing Neural Networks and Regression Models for Ozone Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1080/10473289.1997.10463925)
Comrie (1997), *Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association*. 461 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares neural networks with regression for daily maximum ozone forecasting in air-quality management.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron neural network compared with multiple linear regression.
- **Data:** Meteorological variables and observed ozone concentrations from several US cities.
- **Main result:** Neural networks are somewhat better than regression, but the gain is modest and not consistent across cities.
- **Open work:** Better predictors and hybrid models for high ozone episodes.
- **Issues:** Limited improvement over regression; peak events remain hard to predict.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Deep Air Quality Forecasting Using Hybrid Deep Learning Framework](https://doi.org/10.1109/tkde.2019.2954510)
Du et al. (2018), *IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering*. 441 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts urban air quality (mainly PM2.5) from multivariate time series to support pollution early warning.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid deep model combining 1D CNNs for local trend and spatial features with bidirectional LSTMs for temporal dependencies.
- **Data:** Two real-world air quality datasets of pollutant and meteorological time series (Beijing-related data likely; not confirmed).
- **Main result:** The model forecasts PM2.5 with good accuracy and outperforms baseline methods. Numbers not given in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Longer forecast horizons, integration of meteorological forecasts and emissions.
- **Issues:** Station time-series focus without explicit chemistry or transport; limited datasets.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Multi-hour and multi-site air quality index forecasting in Beijing using CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, and spatiotemporal clustering](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2020.114513)
Yan et al. (2021), *Expert Systems with Applications*. 430 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts Beijing's air quality index at multiple hours and stations, accounting for spatiotemporal patterns of pollution.
- **Architecture:** Compares a back-propagation neural network (MLP), a convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) and a hybrid CNN-LSTM, combined with seasonal and spatial clustering of stations.
- **Data:** Multi-site hourly air quality index observations in Beijing; period and station count not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** For next-hour forecasts accuracy rises from BPNN to CNN to LSTM to CNN-LSTM; LSTM is best for multi-hour forecasts; cluster-based models improve forecasts for specific clusters.
- **Open work:** Adding meteorological and emission inputs and extending lead times.
- **Issues:** Single city; seasonal models give little gain; no uncertainty quantification.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Random forest meteorological normalisation models for Swiss PM 10 trend analysis](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-18-6223-2018)
Grange et al. (2018), *Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics*. 422 citations.

- **Main goal:** Remove the influence of meteorological variability on air-quality time series so that PM10 trends reflect emission and chemistry changes.
- **Architecture:** Random forest regression of daily PM10 on meteorological, synoptic, boundary-layer-height and time variables; normalised trends tested with the Theil-Sen estimator; partial dependence plots for interpretation.
- **Data:** Daily PM10 at 31 Swiss monitoring sites, 1997-2016, with surface meteorology, synoptic classes and boundary layer height.
- **Main result:** Significant normalised PM10 decreases between -0.09 and -1.16 ug/m3/yr, largest at urban traffic sites (mean -0.77 ug/m3/yr); two high-PM10 regimes identified: poor dispersion and photochemical secondary production.
- **Open work:** Application to other pollutants and regions, and quantification of uncertainty in normalised trends.
- **Issues:** Normalisation assumes the RF captures all meteorological effects; covariate shift over decades and correlated predictors can bias trends; single-country scope.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A hybrid ARIMA and artificial neural networks model to forecast particulate matter in urban areas: The case of Temuco, Chile](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2008.07.020)
Díaz-Robles et al. (2008), *Atmospheric Environment*. 410 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily particulate matter (PM10) concentrations in Temuco, Chile, a city with severe wood-smoke pollution, to support air quality episode management.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid model combining ARIMA and an artificial neural network, compared with ARIMA, neural network and linear regression alone.
- **Data:** Daily PM10 and meteorological observations from Temuco, Chile.
- **Main result:** The hybrid ARIMA-ANN model forecasts PM10 and exceedance episodes more accurately than the individual models.
- **Open work:** Application to other cities and pollutants, and longer forecast horizons.
- **Issues:** Single city and monitoring setup; emissions changes not modelled explicitly.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A novel spatiotemporal convolutional long short-term neural network for air pollution prediction.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2018.11.086)
Wen et al. (2019), *Science of The Total Environment*. 399 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts air pollutant concentrations by capturing spatiotemporal features across neighboring stations.
- **Architecture:** Spatiotemporal convolutional neural network combined with long short-term memory (C-LSTME), using adaptive k-nearest neighbor stations plus meteorological and aerosol data.
- **Data:** Hourly PM2.5 at 1233 monitoring stations in Beijing and China, 2016–2017, with meteorological and aerosol data.
- **Main result:** C-LSTME outperforms state-of-the-art models at different prediction times and regional scales.
- **Open work:** Improving long-term and sudden-change prediction and adding emissions data.
- **Issues:** Two-year record; few extreme events; no uncertainty quantification.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Estimating Ground‐Level PM2.5 by Fusing Satellite and Station Observations: A Geo‐Intelligent Deep Learning Approach](https://doi.org/10.1002/2017gl075710)
Li et al. (2017), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 384 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates ground-level PM2.5 across China by fusing satellite observations with station measurements, to monitor pollution where monitors are sparse.
- **Architecture:** Geo-intelligent deep belief network (Geoi-DBN) that adds geographical distance and spatiotemporally correlated neighbouring PM2.5 as inputs to a deep belief network.
- **Data:** Satellite observations (aerosol-related retrievals) and ground station PM2.5 measurements over China for 2015; out-of-sample cross-validation.
- **Main result:** Cross-validated R2 rises from 0.42 (traditional neural network) to 0.88 and RMSE falls from 29.96 to 13.03 μg/m3; over 80% of the Chinese population lives where annual PM2.5 exceeds 35 μg/m3.
- **Open work:** Extending to multiple years and other regions, and testing transfer to periods without station data.
- **Issues:** Single year of training data; reliance on neighbouring station PM2.5 limits use in station-free regions; satellite gaps not discussed in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A review of artificial neural network models for ambient air pollution prediction](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2019.06.014)
Cabaneros et al. (2019), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 383 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews how artificial neural network models for ambient air pollution prediction are developed, given their black-box nature and uncertainty.
- **Architecture:** Review applying the Maier et al. (2010) ANN development protocol to assess published air pollution forecasting studies; covers MLP and ensemble-type neural networks.
- **Data:** Journal papers on ANN forecasting of outdoor PM10, PM2.5, nitrogen oxides and ozone, mostly using meteorological and emission predictors.
- **Main result:** Most studies use ad hoc input selection, data splitting and structure selection; multilayer perceptrons and ensembles dominate.
- **Open work:** Systematic protocols for input selection, data division, model structure and validation of ANN air quality models.
- **Issues:** Review predates widespread deep learning in the field; assessment limited to the reviewed sample and protocol criteria.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Ground-level gaseous pollutants (NO2, SO2, and CO) in China: daily seamless mapping and spatiotemporal variations](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-23-1511-2023)
Wei et al. (2023), *Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics*. 373 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generates seamless daily maps of surface NO2, SO2 and CO across China to support air pollution and health studies.
- **Architecture:** Artificial-intelligence (machine learning) model combining big data sources; the specific model type is not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Ground observations over China with satellite and auxiliary data, 2013–2020 at 10 km; validated by cross-validation against stations.
- **Main result:** Daily CV R2 (RMSE) of 0.84 (7.99 µg/m3) for NO2, 0.84 (10.7 µg/m3) for SO2 and 0.80 (0.29 mg/m3) for CO; concentrations fell 12%, 55% and 17% from 2013 to 2020.
- **Open work:** Use in short-term exposure and health studies, and extension to finer resolution and later years.
- **Issues:** Input sources and model details not given in the abstract; accuracy may degrade in station-sparse western China.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Air Pollution Forecasts: An Overview](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph15040780)
Bai et al. (2018), *International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health*. 346 citations.

- **Main goal:** Gives an overview of methods for forecasting air pollution.
- **Architecture:** Review of statistical, artificial intelligence (neural network) and numerical forecasting methods and their hybrids.
- **Data:** Published air pollution forecasting studies; no new data.
- **Main result:** Hybrid models improve accuracy; the review compares advantages and disadvantages of each class.
- **Open work:** Better hybrid models and systematic comparisons.
- **Issues:** Broad narrative review without quantitative synthesis.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [From low-cost sensors to high-quality data: A summary of challenges and best practices for effectively calibrating low-cost particulate matter mass sensors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaerosci.2021.105833)
Giordano et al. (2021), *Journal of Aerosol Science*. 341 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews the challenges of calibrating low-cost particulate matter mass sensors so that their data can support quantitative air quality assessment, especially in low and middle-income countries.
- **Architecture:** Review of calibration and correction methods for low-cost PM sensors, from simple linear and quadratic regression to complex machine learning algorithms, plus a set of best practices.
- **Data:** Literature on low-cost optical PM sensors co-located with reference-grade monitors; no new dataset.
- **Main result:** Identifies biases from meteorology, sensor age, aerosol source, composition and refractive index, and presents best practices for obtaining high-quality data from low-cost sensors.
- **Open work:** Transferable calibrations across sites and aerosol types, long-term drift handling, and calibration where reference monitors are scarce.
- **Issues:** Narrative review without a quantitative meta-analysis; machine learning calibrations may not generalize beyond their co-location conditions.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [An Ensemble Machine-Learning Model To Predict Historical PM2.5 Concentrations in China from Satellite Data.](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.8b02917)
Xiao et al. (2018), *Environmental Science & Technology*. 337 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs historical daily PM2.5 across China from satellite aerosol data, addressing poor accuracy when predicting outside the training period.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble of random forest, generalized additive model and XGBoost trained per spatial cluster, combined by a generalized additive ensemble model after multiple imputation of missing satellite data.
- **Data:** Satellite aerosol optical depth with meteorological and land-use predictors, and ground PM2.5 monitors across China split into seven regions.
- **Main result:** Cross-validation R2 0.79 (RMSE 21 µg/m3); out-of-range hindcast R2 0.58 daily and 0.76 monthly; cluster-based models improve R2 by about 0.05.
- **Open work:** Extending hindcasts further back and improving daily out-of-range skill.
- **Issues:** Daily out-of-period skill is moderate; depends on satellite AOD imputation; monitoring network is sparse before 2013.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model for Forecasting Particulate Matter (PM2.5)](https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2020.2971348)
Li et al. (2020), *IEEE Access*. 334 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts next-24-hour PM2.5 concentration in Beijing to support health protection.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid CNN-LSTM in which a convolutional neural network extracts air quality features and an LSTM models the time series; compared with univariate and multivariate LSTM variants.
- **Data:** Air quality data from the previous 7 days in Beijing as input and next-day PM2.5 as target.
- **Main result:** The multivariate CNN-LSTM gives the lowest MAE and RMSE and shorter training time; values are not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Adding meteorological forecasts and testing at more cities and longer leads.
- **Issues:** Single city, limited baselines, no uncertainty, and quantitative results absent from the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Neural networks and periodic components used in air quality forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/s1352-2310(00)00385-x)
Kolehmainen et al. (2001), *Atmospheric Environment*. 332 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts urban air pollutant (NO2) concentrations and tests whether removing periodic components helps neural network models.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (MLP) and self-organizing map (SOM) models, combined with or without periodic (Fourier-type) component removal.
- **Data:** Hourly NO2 concentrations and meteorological data from Stuttgart, Germany.
- **Main result:** The MLP applied directly to the original data gives the best forecasts; removing periodic components brings little benefit.
- **Open work:** Testing other pollutants and sites and adding meteorological forecast inputs.
- **Issues:** Single city; short-term forecasts only; models do not represent emissions or transport explicitly.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Shapley additive explanations for NO2 forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecoinf.2019.101039)
García et al. (2020), *Ecological Informatics*. 332 citations.

- **Main goal:** Interprets a deep learning model that forecasts NO2 concentrations so that forecasters can understand individual predictions.
- **Architecture:** Deep neural network forecaster explained with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), compared with two other explanation methods.
- **Data:** NO2 air quality time series from Madrid, Spain, with associated predictors.
- **Main result:** SHAP gives per-feature contributions to each prediction and is judged suitable for air quality data, giving insight into model behavior.
- **Open work:** Using explanations to improve model design and extending to other pollutants and cities.
- **Issues:** Focus on interpretability rather than accuracy; explanation fidelity is hard to verify and correlated inputs complicate SHAP attributions.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Cluster analysis: A technique for estimating the synoptic meteorological controls on air and precipitation chemistry—Method and applications](https://doi.org/10.1016/0960-1686(92)90110-7)
Dorling et al. (1992), *Atmospheric Environment. Part A. General Topics*. 316 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a cluster analysis technique to estimate how synoptic meteorological conditions control air and precipitation chemistry at a receptor site.
- **Architecture:** Non-hierarchical (k-means-type) cluster analysis of air-mass back trajectories; unsupervised statistical method, not a neural network.
- **Data:** Back trajectories arriving at Eskdalemuir, Scotland, combined with measurements of precipitation and air chemistry at the site.
- **Main result:** Trajectory clusters separate air flows with distinct pollutant concentrations, showing that synoptic flow type explains much of the variability in deposition chemistry.
- **Open work:** Application to other sites and longer records to examine trends and source-receptor relationships.
- **Issues:** Results depend on trajectory accuracy and on the subjective choice of the number of clusters; clustering on trajectories alone ignores vertical mixing and wet removal processes.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A neural network forecast for daily average PM10 concentrations in Belgium](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2005.01.050)
Hooyberghs et al. (2005), *Atmospheric Environment*. 310 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts next-day daily average PM10 concentrations in Belgium for operational air quality warnings.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward artificial neural network (MLP) using meteorological predictors and PM10 observations as inputs.
- **Data:** PM10 monitoring network data in Belgium with meteorological forecast variables such as boundary layer height.
- **Main result:** Boundary layer height is the most important input; the neural network improves on persistence and is used operationally.
- **Open work:** Better meteorological inputs and handling of episodes with transboundary transport.
- **Issues:** Skill for high-concentration episodes remains limited; depends on quality of meteorological forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Using meteorological normalisation to detect interventions in air quality time series.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2018.10.344)
Grange et al. (2019), *Science of The Total Environment*. 309 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects the effect of air quality interventions in pollutant time series by removing the confounding influence of meteorology.
- **Architecture:** Meteorological normalisation based on a random forest regression of concentrations on meteorological and time variables, followed by resampling of meteorology.
- **Data:** Routine air quality monitoring observations: SO2 at Dover (port city, England) and NOx/NO2 at London Marylebone Road, with associated meteorological data.
- **Main result:** Normalised series clearly show SO2 drops from stricter marine fuel sulfur limits at Dover and NO2/NOx changes tied to primary NO2 emissions at Marylebone Road, not visible in raw data.
- **Open work:** Applying the technique to other interventions and pollutants, and formal change-point or uncertainty analysis of normalised trends.
- **Issues:** Only two sites; attribution depends on the meteorological covariates captured and gives no formal uncertainty on intervention effects.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Forecasting air quality time series using deep learning](https://doi.org/10.1080/10962247.2018.1459956)
Freeman et al. (2018), *Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association*. 294 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts air quality time series to support pollution warnings.
- **Architecture:** Recurrent neural network with long short-term memory units, with decision trees used for input selection.
- **Data:** Hourly air quality and meteorological monitoring data; specific network not confirmed here.
- **Main result:** The LSTM model is reported to forecast 8-hour average ozone up to 72 hours ahead with reasonable accuracy.
- **Open work:** Adding emissions and meteorological forecasts as inputs.
- **Issues:** Error grows with forecast horizon; limited stations.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Recursive neural network model for analysis and forecast of PM10 and PM2.5](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apr.2016.12.014)
Biancofiore et al. (2017), *Atmospheric Pollution Research*. 293 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyses and forecasts PM10 and PM2.5 concentrations for air quality management.
- **Architecture:** Recursive (recurrent) neural network compared with multiple linear regression and feedforward neural network.
- **Data:** PM10, PM2.5 and meteorological data from a coastal site in central Italy (Pescara).
- **Main result:** The recurrent network gives better PM forecasts than the comparison models.
- **Open work:** Extend to other sites and longer horizons.
- **Issues:** Single site, limited period.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Air pollutants concentrations forecasting using back propagation neural network based on wavelet decomposition with meteorological conditions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apr.2016.01.004)
Bai et al. (2016), *Atmospheric Pollution Research*. 292 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily air pollutant concentrations using meteorological conditions to support urban air quality warning.
- **Architecture:** Back-propagation neural network (MLP) combined with wavelet decomposition of pollutant series, with meteorological inputs.
- **Data:** Daily pollutant concentrations and meteorological observations from urban monitoring stations in China; exact stations and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Wavelet decomposition is expected to improve the BP network over the undecomposed version; quantitative results not reported here.
- **Open work:** Testing at more sites and longer horizons and comparing with deep sequence models.
- **Issues:** Abstract missing; data, pollutants and gains not verified; wavelet decomposition can leak future information if applied to full series.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A neural network-based method for short-term predictions of ambient SO2 concentrations in highly polluted industrial areas of complex terrain](https://doi.org/10.1016/0957-1272(93)90007-s)
Božnar et al. (1993), *Atmospheric Environment. Part B. Urban Atmosphere*. 286 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts short-term SO2 concentrations in a polluted industrial area of complex terrain, where dispersion models perform poorly.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron trained with backpropagation on meteorological and emission-related inputs.
- **Data:** Automatic monitoring network measurements of SO2 and meteorology around the Šoštanj thermal power plant in Slovenia.
- **Main result:** The neural network gives useful half-hourly SO2 forecasts and captures pollution episodes better than simple alternatives.
- **Open work:** Improved input selection and extension to other pollutants and sites.
- **Issues:** Site-specific model; limited ability to extrapolate to unusual emission or meteorological conditions.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Regression and multilayer perceptron-based models to forecast hourly O3 and NO2 levels in the Bilbao area](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2004.07.008)
Agirre-Basurko et al. (2006), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 286 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts hourly ozone and nitrogen dioxide levels in the Bilbao area to support air-quality warnings.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural networks compared with multiple linear regression models.
- **Data:** Hourly air-quality, meteorological and traffic variables from monitoring stations in the Bilbao area, Spain.
- **Main result:** The MLP models outperform linear regression for most forecast horizons and stations, and traffic variables add useful information.
- **Open work:** Extending to other pollutants and sites and using meteorological forecasts as inputs for operational use.
- **Issues:** Local station-based models with limited transferability; no abstract available, so quantitative scores are not reported here.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [An LSTM-based aggregated model for air pollution forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apr.2020.05.015)
Chang et al. (2020), *Atmospheric Pollution Research*. 286 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves PM2.5 forecasting at 1–8 h horizons by using information from nearby industrial and external pollution source stations.
- **Architecture:** Aggregated LSTM (ALSTM) combining three LSTM networks for local, nearby industrial and external source stations.
- **Data:** Taiwan Environmental Protection Agency monitoring data with 17 attributes, 2012–2017 training, 2018 testing.
- **Main result:** ALSTM improves accuracy over SVR, gradient boosted tree regression and a single LSTM in MAE, RMSE and MAPE.
- **Open work:** Extending to more regions, longer horizons and including meteorological forecasts.
- **Issues:** Single region; specific numbers not given in the abstract; no uncertainty estimates.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Air Pollution Forecasting Using a Deep Learning Model Based on 1D Convnets and Bidirectional GRU](https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2019.2921578)
Tao et al. (2019), *IEEE Access*. 284 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts short-term PM2.5 concentration from meteorological factors.
- **Architecture:** CBGRU, combining 1D convolutional neural networks (CNN) with bidirectional gated recurrent units (GRU).
- **Data:** Beijing PM2.5 data set from the UCI Machine Learning Repository.
- **Main result:** CBGRU yields lower errors and better prediction than traditional models.
- **Open work:** Testing on more cities and multi-site data and longer horizons.
- **Issues:** Single public benchmark dataset; quantitative gains not stated in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Air pollution prediction with machine learning: a case study of Indian cities](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13762-022-04241-5)
Kumar et al. (2022), *International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology*. 275 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyzes and predicts air quality in Indian cities using machine learning.

### [A hybrid model for PM₂.₅ forecasting based on ensemble empirical mode decomposition and a general regression neural network.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2014.07.051)
Zhou et al. (2014), *Science of The Total Environment*. 274 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts PM2.5 concentrations one day ahead in Xi'an, China, to support rapid air-quality warning systems.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid EEMD-GRNN: ensemble empirical mode decomposition splits the PM2.5 series into intrinsic mode functions, each predicted by a general regression neural network; inputs are selected with principal component regression.

- **Main result:** EEMD-GRNN outperforms a plain GRNN, multiple linear regression, PCR and ARIMA for one-day-ahead PM2.5 prediction; no headline numbers given in the abstract.

### [Low-Cost Outdoor Air Quality Monitoring and Sensor Calibration](https://doi.org/10.1145/3446005)
Concas et al. (2019), *ACM Transactions on Sensor Networks*. 272 citations.

- **Main goal:** Surveys low-cost outdoor air-quality sensors and their in-field calibration, which is needed because the sensors drift and suffer cross-sensitivities.
- **Architecture:** Review of low-cost sensor technologies and machine learning calibration methods (regression, neural networks and other learners) for air-quality monitoring.
- **Data:** Literature survey; no new dataset. Covers studies co-locating low-cost sensors with reference monitoring stations.
- **Main result:** Machine-learning-based calibration is promising for in-field recalibration, but cross-sensitivity, environmental effects and sensor ageing remain key obstacles.

### [Spatiotemporal continuous estimates of PM2.5 concentrations in China, 2000-2016: A machine learning method with inputs from satellites, chemical transport model, and ground observations.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envint.2018.11.075)
Xue et al. (2019), *Environment International*. 271 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds complete daily PM2.5 estimates across China for 2000–2016, extending exposure records before the 2013 national monitoring network.

- **Data:** Satellite AOD and other satellite covariates, meteorological variables and chemical transport model simulations; trained on in-situ PM2.5 from 2013–2016 with year-wise held-out cross-validation.
- **Main result:** Cross-validated R2 of 0.61 (daily), 0.68 (monthly) and 0.75 (annual); gap-filled R2 0.55/0.71/0.77. Population-weighted PM2.5 rose 2.10 μg/m3/yr in 2000–2007 and fell 4.51 μg/m3/yr in 2013–2016.
- **Open work:** Use the product in epidemiological studies and validate pre-2013 hindcasts against independent historical observations.
- **Issues:** Pre-2013 estimates rely on extrapolation in time; daily accuracy is moderate, especially after gap filling; errors in AOD and CTM inputs propagate.
- *Basis: abstract*

- **Data:** Ozone, precursor pollutant and meteorological data from a monitoring station in Kuwait.
- **Main result:** The combined model predicts ozone better than PCR or regression alone.
- **Open work:** Testing the combined approach at other sites and seasons and for forecasting rather than simulation.
- **Issues:** Single monitoring site; no uncertainty estimates; abstract unavailable.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Development of a stacked ensemble model for forecasting and analyzing daily average PM2.5 concentrations in Beijing, China.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2018.04.040)
Zhai et al. (2018), *Science of The Total Environment*. 206 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts and explains daily PM2.5 concentrations in Beijing.
- **Architecture:** Stacked ensemble: LASSO, AdaBoost, XGBoost and GA-optimized MLP at level 0, combined by support vector regression at level 1.
- **Data:** Daily air pollutant and meteorological data for Beijing and surrounding cities (e.g. Zhangjiakou, Chengde).
- **Main result:** R2 0.90 and RMSE 23.69 μg/m3; NO2 and CO in Zhangjiakou are the most important features; grade classification accuracy 73.93%.
- **Open work:** Improving performance on high-pollution days.
- **Issues:** Weaker on heavily polluted days; single city target; feature engineering is case-specific.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Air Pollution Prediction Using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Deep Autoencoder (DAE) Models](https://doi.org/10.3390/su12062570)
Xayasouk et al. (2020), *Sustainability*. 205 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts fine particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) concentrations in Seoul to provide fine dust forecasts relevant to urban health.
- **Architecture:** Long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network and deep autoencoder (DAE) models, compared via RMSE with tuned learning rate, epochs and batch sizes.
- **Data:** Hourly air quality data from 25 monitoring stations in Seoul, South Korea, 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2018; prediction of the following 10 days.
- **Main result:** Both models predict fine PM concentrations effectively, with the LSTM slightly outperforming the deep autoencoder in RMSE.
- **Open work:** Adding meteorological and emission predictors and extending evaluation to longer test periods and other cities.
- **Issues:** Very short 10-day test window; comparison limited to two deep models without strong statistical or chemical-transport baselines; meteorological inputs not described in the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Separating emission and meteorological contributions to long-term PM2.5 trends over eastern China during 2000–2018](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-21-9475-2021)
Xiao et al. (2021), *Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics*. 203 citations.

- **Main goal:** Quantifies how meteorology and emissions contributed to long-term PM2.5 trends over eastern China during 2000 to 2018, informing air quality management.
- **Architecture:** Two-stage machine learning PM2.5 model with synthetic minority oversampling for polluted days, plus a generalized additive model and the WRF/CMAQ chemical transport model for meteorological attribution.
- **Data:** Satellite-based full-coverage daily PM2.5 retrievals with ground measurements, meteorological fields and WRF/CMAQ simulations, 2000 to 2018, eastern China.
- **Main result:** GAM and CMAQ meteorological contributions agree monthly (r 0.53 to 0.72); emissions dominate trends, while meteorology contributes -3.9% to 2.8% of annual mean PM2.5 in eastern China and up to -25.6% to 12.3% in the Pearl River Delta.
- **Open work:** Stricter clean air actions are needed given worsening meteorology in northern China; future climate-driven changes merit study.
- **Issues:** Attribution depends on statistical and model assumptions; satellite-based PM2.5 uncertainty, especially early years and polluted days.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Spatiotemporal distributions of surface ozone levels in China from 2005 to 2017: A machine learning approach.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envint.2020.105823)
Liu et al. (2020), *Environment International*. 203 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconstructs long-term nationwide surface ozone in China back to 2005, when in-situ measurements are scarce, to support health and trend studies.
- **Architecture:** XGBoost (gradient boosted trees) predicting daily maximum 8-hour average ozone.
- **Data:** MDA8 observations 2013 to 2017 with satellite ozone retrievals, aerosol reanalysis, meteorology and land use; external tests with 2005 to 2012 regional and 2018 national data; 0.1° output.
- **Main result:** Daily cross-validation R2 of 0.61 to 0.78 and external monthly R2 of 0.60 to 0.87; BTH ozone rose 1.37 μg/m3/year in 2013 to 2017 and 26.24% of the population exceeded standards in 2017.
- **Open work:** Applying the product to long-term health impact studies and pollution control policy.
- **Issues:** Hindcasts before 2013 rely on few validation sites; only monthly means before 2013; tree models do not extrapolate beyond training conditions.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Spatial estimation of urban air pollution with the use of artificial neural network models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2018.07.058)
Alimissis et al. (2018), *Atmospheric Environment*. 202 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates urban air pollutant concentrations at unmonitored locations to produce accurate pollution fields for health risk assessment.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks (MLP) for spatial interpolation compared with multiple linear regression.
- **Data:** Urban air quality monitoring network of the greater Athens area, Greece, for NO2, NO, O3, CO and SO2.
- **Main result:** Neural networks are significantly superior in most cases, especially where network density is limited and spatial correlation among sites is lower.
- **Open work:** Adding meteorological and land use predictors and testing in other cities.
- **Issues:** Limited number of monitoring sites; no uncertainty estimates; no quantitative values in abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Deep Learning for Air Quality Forecasts: a Review](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40726-020-00159-z)
Liao et al. (2020), *Current Pollution Reports*. 200 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews deep learning methods for air quality forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Review of deep learning approaches for air quality forecasts, such as recurrent, convolutional and hybrid networks.
- **Data:** Literature survey; no new data.
- **Main result:** Summarizes progress of deep learning in air quality forecasting; specific conclusions not available without the abstract.
- **Open work:** Not reported; open problems in this area include interpretability, integration with chemical transport models and generalization.
- **Issues:** Abstract not available, so the card is inferred from the title.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Point-surface fusion of station measurements and satellite observations for mapping PM 2.5 distribution in China: Methods and assessment](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2017.01.004)
Li et al. (2016), *Atmospheric Environment*. 200 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates spatially continuous ground-level PM2.5 across China by fusing station measurements and satellite observations, and assesses competing models.
- **Architecture:** Generalized regression neural network (GRNN) compared with linear regression, multiple linear regression, semi-empirical model, geographically weighted regression and back-propagation neural network.
- **Data:** National monitoring network PM2.5 measurements and 3 km MODIS aerosol optical depth over China.
- **Main result:** GRNN performs best; advanced models reach R 0.61 to 0.82 and RMSE 20.93 to 28.68 μg/m3 versus R 0.49 to 0.55 for conventional models.
- **Open work:** Improving accuracy further and supporting global PM2.5 monitoring.
- **Issues:** MODIS AOD gaps limit coverage; only yearly and seasonal means mapped.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction of hourly air pollutant concentrations near urban arterials using artificial neural network approach](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trd.2008.10.004)
Cai et al. (2009), *Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment*. 198 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts hourly concentrations of traffic-related pollutants near urban arterial roads for air quality management.
- **Architecture:** Backpropagation feed-forward neural network (MLP) using traffic, meteorological and background inputs, compared with multiple linear regression and the CALINE4 dispersion model.
- **Data:** Hourly CO, NO2, PM10 and O3 measurements near arterial roads in Guangzhou, China, with traffic and weather data.
- **Main result:** The neural network predicts hourly concentrations more accurately than multiple regression and CALINE4.
- **Open work:** Test at more sites and for forecasting rather than estimation, and add emission factors.
- **Issues:** Few monitoring sites and a short period; site-specific training limits transferability.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Mapping urban air quality using mobile sampling with low-cost sensors and machine learning in Seoul, South Korea](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envint.2019.105022)
Lim et al. (2019), *Environment International*. 197 citations.

- **Main goal:** Maps street-level PM2.5 in Seoul using low-cost mobile sensors to enable cheap high-resolution air quality monitoring.
- **Architecture:** Land use regression comparing linear regression, random forest and a stacked ensemble of multiple machine learning algorithms.
- **Data:** 169 hours of mobile PM2.5 measurements from seven AirBeam low-cost sensors over five routes in about three weeks, plus OpenStreetMap geospatial predictors.
- **Main result:** Cross-validated R2 is 0.63 for linear regression, 0.73 for random forest and 0.80 for the stacked ensemble, and pollution hotspots are identified.
- **Open work:** Application to citizen science and data-poor regions such as developing countries.
- **Issues:** Short three-week campaign; low-cost sensor accuracy and calibration issues; limited temporal representativeness.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction of the Level of Air Pollution Using Principal Component Analysis and Artificial Neural Network Techniques: a Case Study in Malaysia](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11270-014-2063-1)
Azid et al. (2014), *Water, Air, & Soil Pollution*. 195 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts the air pollution index in Malaysia to support air quality management.
- **Architecture:** Principal component analysis for input selection combined with artificial neural networks.
- **Data:** Air quality and meteorological monitoring data from Malaysian stations; details are not reported here.
- **Main result:** The title indicates PCA-ANN predicts the air pollution level; quantitative results are not available here.
- **Open work:** Extension to forecasting horizons and other regions.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; station-based model with limited transferability.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Daily urban air quality index forecasting based on variational mode decomposition, sample entropy and LSTM neural network](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scs.2019.101657)
Wu et al. (2019), *Sustainable Cities and Society*. 194 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily urban air quality index to protect public health.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid of variational mode decomposition, sample entropy recombination of sub-series and LSTM neural network forecasting of each component.
- **Data:** Daily AQI series from Beijing and Baoding, China.
- **Main result:** The VMD-SE-LSTM model outperforms single and other hybrid models and achieves a high rate of correct AQI class forecasts.
- **Open work:** Inclusion of meteorological and emission predictors and multi-step forecasts.
- **Issues:** Univariate series; decomposition of full series can leak future information; quantitative metrics not given in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction of air pollution index (API) using support vector machine (SVM)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jece.2019.103208)
Leong et al. (2020), *Journal of Environmental Chemical Engineering*. 194 citations.

- **Main goal:** Models the air pollution index more efficiently than complex conventional calculation methods.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine regression, comparing kernel functions including radial basis function.
- **Data:** Air pollution data; location and period are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The RBF-kernel SVM gives R2 of 0.9843 for air pollution index modeling.
- **Open work:** Tuning penalty and regularization parameters, which were not investigated.
- **Issues:** Only kernel type explored; dataset details and validation design not described.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [An integrated neural network model for PM10 forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2006.01.010)
Pérez et al. (2006), *Atmospheric Environment*. 193 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily PM10 concentrations in Santiago, Chile to support air quality episode warnings.
- **Architecture:** Integrated feed-forward neural network (MLP) model using forecast meteorological variables and measured concentrations, compared with linear regression and persistence.
- **Data:** PM10 monitoring network data and meteorological observations and forecasts for Santiago, Chile.
- **Main result:** The neural network predicts the next-day maximum of 24-h average PM10 better than linear and persistence models.
- **Open work:** Improve forecasts of extreme episodes and incorporate more meteorological forecast information.
- **Issues:** Depends on meteorological forecast quality; few extreme episodes for training.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Forecasting of the daily meteorological pollution using wavelets and support vector machine](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2006.10.008)
Osowski et al. (2007), *Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence*. 191 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily air pollution levels using wavelet decomposition and support vector machines.
- **Architecture:** Wavelet decomposition of time series followed by support vector machine regression for each component.
- **Data:** Daily pollutant (e.g. NO2, SO2, CO, dust) and meteorological data from a monitoring station in northern Poland.
- **Main result:** The wavelet-SVM approach improves forecasting accuracy over direct SVM and neural network approaches.
- **Open work:** Extend to longer lead times and more stations.
- **Issues:** Single region; wavelet decomposition choice is empirical.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Modeling PM2.5 Urban Pollution Using Machine Learning and Selected Meteorological Parameters](https://doi.org/10.1155/2017/5106045)
Deters et al. (2017), *Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering*. 191 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts urban PM2.5 concentrations in Quito, Ecuador, from meteorological variables, as complex terrain and urban factors complicate physics-based air quality forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning classification and regression models using wind speed, wind direction and precipitation as predictors; the specific algorithm family is not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Six years of meteorological and PM2.5 monitoring data from Quito, Ecuador.
- **Main result:** Classification of low versus moderate PM2.5 levels is highly reliable; regression predicts PM2.5 better under extreme conditions (strong winds, heavy precipitation), with high correlation in the wet season.
- **Open work:** Adding further predictors such as emissions, boundary-layer height or traffic, and testing other cities, would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** Only three meteorological predictors; weaker skill under ordinary conditions; single-city study with limited details on model validation.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Air Quality Index and Air Pollutant Concentration Prediction Based on Machine Learning Algorithms](https://doi.org/10.3390/app9194069)
Liu et al. (2019), *Applied Sciences*. 187 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts the Air Quality Index and pollutant concentrations to support air pollution warnings.
- **Architecture:** Support vector regression (SVR) and random forest regression (RFR).
- **Data:** Public datasets: Beijing AQI and NOx concentrations in an Italian city.
- **Main result:** SVR is best for Beijing AQI (RMSE 7.666, R2 0.978), RFR best for NOx (RMSE 83.67, R2 0.840).
- **Open work:** Testing additional algorithms, longer horizons and more cities would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** Forecast horizon and lagged-input setup are unclear; only two datasets; no uncertainty.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A new method for prediction of air pollution based on intelligent computation](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00500-019-04495-1)
Al_Janabi et al. (2019), *Soft Computing*. 185 citations.

- **Main goal:** Proposes a new intelligent-computation method to predict concentrations of air pollutants for air quality management.
- **Architecture:** Intelligent computation forecasting method; the specific model family is not specified here.
- **Data:** Not reported in the abstract. The title implies air pollutant concentration records.
- **Main result:** The proposed method is presented as improving air pollution prediction; quantitative results not available here.
- **Open work:** Validation across more cities, pollutants and longer horizons would be needed to assess robustness.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; method, data and metrics could not be verified from the record.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A novel optimal-hybrid model for daily air quality index prediction considering air pollutant factors.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2019.05.288)
Wu et al. (2019), *Science of The Total Environment*. 185 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts the daily air quality index (AQI) accurately for public health protection while accounting for influential pollutant factors.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid secondary decomposition model: wavelet decomposition plus sample-entropy-improved VMD, LSTM neural network for high-frequency components and Bat-algorithm-optimized least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) for the low-frequency component.
- **Data:** Daily AQI series for Beijing and Guilin, China, from 1 December 2016 to 31 December 2018, with PM2.5, PM10, SO2, CO, NO2 and O3 as factors.
- **Main result:** The optimal-hybrid model captures AQI series characteristics and achieves high accuracy in forecasting AQI classes, outperforming comparison models across several indices.
- **Open work:** Extending to multi-step horizons, more cities and meteorological predictors would test generality.
- **Issues:** Only two cities and about two years of data; decomposition over the full series may leak future information; one-day-ahead focus without uncertainty.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [The Impact of the Wuhan Covid-19 Lockdown on Air Pollution and Health: A Machine Learning and Augmented Synthetic Control Approach](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10640-020-00483-4)
Cole et al. (2020), *Environmental and Resource Economics*. 182 citations.

- **Main goal:** Quantifies the effect of the Wuhan Covid-19 lockdown on air pollution and associated health outcomes.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning weather normalisation of pollutant concentrations followed by an augmented synthetic control method; ML model type not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Concentrations of NO2, PM10, SO2 and CO in Wuhan and control cities in China, with weather data.
- **Main result:** NO2 fell by up to 24 µg/m3 (63%) and PM10 by a similar amount for a shorter period; no effect on SO2 or CO; NO2 reduction may have prevented up to 10,822 deaths in China.
- **Open work:** Extending to other cities and pollutants and refining health impact functions are natural steps.
- **Issues:** Health estimates depend on assumed concentration-response functions; control cities may be affected by spillovers.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Extreme gradient boosting model to estimate PM2.5 concentrations with missing-filled satellite data in China](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2019.01.027)
Chen et al. (2019), *Atmospheric Environment*. 181 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates daily ground PM2.5 across China while handling the large share of missing satellite AOD retrievals.
- **Architecture:** Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) with a non-linear exposure-lag-response model, after two-step AOD gap filling with a mixed-effect model and inverse distance weighting.
- **Data:** Satellite AOD at 3 km resolution and ground PM2.5 monitors across China, 2014–2015.
- **Main result:** Gap filling cuts missing AOD from 87.91% to 13.83%; PM2.5 cross-validation gives R2 0.86, RMSE 14.98 and MAPE 23.72%.
- **Open work:** Extending to more years and evaluating gap-filled areas independently are natural steps.
- **Issues:** Only two years; interpolated AOD may be less reliable in persistently cloudy regions; cross-validation may be optimistic.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Comparison of Machine Learning and Land Use Regression for fine scale spatiotemporal estimation of ambient air pollution: Modeling ozone concentrations across the contiguous United States.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envint.2020.105827)
Ren et al. (2020), *Environment International*. 179 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares machine learning and land use regression for fine-scale ozone estimation across the contiguous US for exposure assessment.
- **Architecture:** Thirteen algorithms from nine categories, including linear land use regression, random forest and extreme gradient boosting.
- **Data:** Daily maximum 8-hour ozone with chemistry-transport model predictions, meteorology, land use and emissions at census tract level across the contiguous US.
- **Main result:** Nonlinear ML reduces RMSE by about 10–40% versus LUR; tuned sample weights reduce cross-validated RMSE by about 30%; RF and XGBoost perform best.
- **Open work:** Careful hyperparameter tuning and validation design remain crucial.
- **Issues:** Ozone only; results depend on validation strategy; potential overfitting.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [PM10 concentration forecasting in the metropolitan area of Oviedo (Northern Spain) using models based on SVM, MLP, VARMA and ARIMA: A case study.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2017.11.291)
Nieto et al. (2018), *Science of The Total Environment*. 178 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts monthly PM10 concentrations in the Oviedo metropolitan area (Spain) to support air-quality management and health protection.
- **Architecture:** Compares support vector machine regression (SVM), multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network, and statistical VARMA and ARIMA models.
- **Data:** Seven years of monthly averaged air-pollutant measurements, including PM10, from monitoring stations in Oviedo, northern Spain.
- **Main result:** SVM regression outperforms MLP, VARMA and ARIMA for forecasts one month ahead and for the following seven months.
- **Open work:** Using meteorological predictors and daily resolution would make the forecasts more operationally useful.
- **Issues:** Monthly averages from a single city give a small sample; no meteorological drivers; limited out-of-sample evaluation details.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Comparative assessment of neural networks and regression models for forecasting summertime ozone in Athens.](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0048-9697(03)00335-8)
Chaloulakou et al. (2003), *Science of The Total Environment*. 176 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily maximum summertime ozone concentrations in Athens for air quality warnings.
- **Architecture:** Neural network (MLP) compared with multiple linear regression.
- **Data:** Meteorological and ozone monitoring data from Athens, Greece, summer seasons.
- **Main result:** Neural networks outperform regression models, especially when previous-day ozone is included as a predictor.
- **Open work:** Better prediction of exceedance episodes and use of forecast meteorology.
- **Issues:** Single city; few extreme ozone episodes; uses observed rather than forecast meteorology.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Air Pollution Forecasting Using RNN with LSTM](https://doi.org/10.1109/dasc/picom/datacom/cyberscitec.2018.00178)
Tsai et al. (2018), *2018 IEEE 16th Intl Conf on Dependable, Autonomic and Secure Computing, 16th Intl Conf on Pervasive Intelligence and Computing, 4th Intl Conf on Big Data Intelligence and Computing and Cyber Science and Technology Congress(DASC/PiCom/DataCom/CyberSciTech)*. 175 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts PM2.5 concentrations across Taiwan to support air pollution warning.

### [Forecasting air pollutant indicator levels with geographic models 3 days in advance using neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2010.05.093)
Kurt et al. (2010), *Expert Systems with Applications*. 175 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts air pollutant indicator levels in Istanbul three days ahead to support public warnings.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural networks combined with geographic models that use data from neighboring districts as inputs.
- **Data:** Air pollutant (e.g., SO2, PM10, CO) and meteorological measurements from monitoring stations in Istanbul districts; period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract; including geographic neighborhood information is reported to reduce forecast errors relative to non-geographic models.

- **Issues:** No abstract available to confirm data and scores; city-specific model.

### [Air quality index forecast in Beijing based on CNN-LSTM multi-model.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chemosphere.2022.136180)
Zhang et al. (2022), *Chemosphere*. 174 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts Beijing's air quality index to support environmental management decisions.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid CNN-LSTM: a convolutional neural network extracts features, which an LSTM uses to learn temporal dynamics; compared with ARMA, SARIMA, RNN, LSTM and GRU.
- **Data:** Beijing air quality index time series; period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** CNN-LSTM is most accurate; relative to SARIMA, MAE and RMSE drop 3.17% and 5.46% and R2 rises 8.45%.

### [The Forecasting of PM2.5 Using a Hybrid Model Based on Wavelet Transform and an Improved Deep Learning Algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2019.2944755)
Qiao et al. (2019), *IEEE Access*. 174 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves PM2.5 concentration forecasting for haze management, addressing LSTM gradient issues and arbitrary choice of wavelet order and decomposition levels.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid WT-SAE-LSTM: wavelet transform decomposition into frequency components, each predicted by a stacked autoencoder plus LSTM, then reconstructed.

### [Mapping real-time air pollution health risk for environmental management: Combining mobile and stationary air pollution monitoring with neural network models.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2015.12.012)
Adams et al. (2016), *Journal of Environmental Management*. 172 citations.

- **Main goal:** Maps real-time intra-urban air pollution health risk where fixed monitoring networks are sparse.

### [Progress in developing an ANN model for air pollution index forecast](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2003.10.066)
Jiang et al. (2004), *Atmospheric Environment*. 170 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a neural network model to forecast the air pollution index operationally.
- **Architecture:** Neural network (MLP) using meteorological and pollution predictors.
- **Data:** Air pollution index and meteorological data from a Chinese city.

### [Separating Daily 1 km PM2.5 Inorganic Chemical Composition in China since 2000 via Deep Learning Integrating Ground, Satellite, and Model Data](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.3c00272)
Wei et al. (2023), *Environmental Science & Technology*. 170 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates daily 1 km PM2.5 inorganic chemical composition across China since 2000 given sparse surface observations and chemical model uncertainty.
- **Architecture:** Four-dimensional spatiotemporal deep forest (4D-STDF), a cascade tree-ensemble (random forest based) deep forest model.

### [Evaluation of gap-filling approaches in satellite-based daily PM2.5 prediction models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2020.117921)
Xiao et al. (2021), *Atmospheric Environment*. 168 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates gap-filling strategies for missing satellite AOD in daily 1 km PM2.5 prediction.
- **Architecture:** Random forest PM2.5 model combined with four gap-filling strategies (multiple imputation, decision tree, ordinary kriging, generalized additive mixed model).

### [An ensemble long short-term memory neural network for hourly PM2.5 concentration forecasting.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chemosphere.2019.01.121)
Bai et al. (2019), *Chemosphere*. 167 citations.

- **Main goal:** Hourly PM2.5 concentration forecasting for public health early warning.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble LSTM (E-LSTM): EEMD decomposition into modes, an LSTM per mode with meteorological inputs, and inverse EEMD integration.
- **Data:** PM2.5 and meteorological data from two environmental monitoring stations in Beijing, China.
- **Main result:** E-LSTM beats single LSTM and feed-forward networks, with MAPE 19.6% and 16.9%, RMSE 12.1 and 14.0 µg m-3 and correlation 0.994 and 0.991.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and more stations.
- **Issues:** Only two stations; EEMD on full series may leak future information; one-hour-ahead only.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [The use of random forests in modelling short-term air pollution effects based on traffic and meteorological conditions: A case study in Wrocław.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2018.03.094)
Kamińska (2018), *Journal of Environmental Management*. 166 citations.

- **Main goal:** Models how traffic flow and meteorological conditions drive short-term NO2, NOx and PM2.5 concentrations at an urban roadside site.
- **Architecture:** Random forest regression with predictor importance analysis, fitted separately for nine seasonal and climatic time subsets.
- **Data:** Hourly NO2, NOx and PM2.5, wind speed and direction, temperature, pressure, humidity, temporal variables and traffic flow at a station 40 m from a large intersection in Wrocław, Poland, 2015–2016.
- **Main result:** Fit is best for the warm season and summer; traffic flow dominates nitrogen oxide concentrations, while temperature, wind speed and direction dominate PM2.5; temporal variables are largely unimportant.
- **Open work:** Extending to multiple stations, other pollutants and forecasting rather than explanatory modelling would broaden the findings.
- **Issues:** Single station and two years; explanatory rather than predictive validation; importance measures can be biased by correlated predictors.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Forecasting peak air pollution levels using NARX models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2009.04.002)
Pisoni et al. (2009), *Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence*. 162 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily peak air pollution levels (notably ozone) to support warning systems in a polluted urban region.
- **Architecture:** Nonlinear autoregressive models with exogenous inputs (NARX) identified from data, using meteorological and pollutant predictors.
- **Data:** Air quality monitoring and meteorological data from Northern Italy; stations and periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** NARX models give useful next-day peak pollution forecasts, competitive with alternative statistical approaches.
- **Open work:** Including forecast meteorology, more stations and probabilistic exceedance forecasts.
- **Issues:** Site-specific models; performance on extreme episodes and transferability are uncertain.

### [A novel hybrid-Garch model based on ARIMA and SVM for PM2.5 concentrations forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apr.2017.01.003)
Wang et al. (2017), *Atmospheric Pollution Research*. 162 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts PM2.5 concentrations by capturing linear, nonlinear and volatility components of the series.

- **Issues:** Abstract not available; univariate inputs; single location.

### [Recurrent Neural Network and random forest for analysis and accurate forecast of atmospheric pollutants: A case study in Hangzhou, China](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2019.05.319)
Feng et al. (2019), *Journal of Cleaner Production*. 161 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyzes and forecasts atmospheric pollutants in Hangzhou, China, ahead of the 2022 Asian Games.
- **Architecture:** Random forest for feature importance analysis and a recurrent neural network (RNN) coupled to WRF for 24 h forecasts and source identification.
- **Data:** Pollutant (SO2, NO2, CO, PM2.5, PM10, O3) and meteorological observations in Hangzhou plus WRF meteorological fields.
- **Main result:** CO plays an important role in shaping O3, NO2 and PM; dew-point deficit matters more than relative humidity; the WRF/RNN method forecasts pollutants 24 h ahead.
- **Open work:** Evaluating emission-source attribution and applying to other cities.
- **Issues:** Quantitative skill not given in the abstract; ML ignores emission inventories and chemistry.
- *Basis: abstract*

Zhu et al. (2018), *Atmospheric Environment*. 161 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily PM2.5 concentrations including meteorological factors for air quality warnings.

- **Data:** Daily PM2.5 and meteorological data for Chongqing, Harbin and Jinan, China.
- **Main result:** The hybrid model outperforms six comparison models.
- **Open work:** Multi-step forecasts and inclusion of emission data.
- **Issues:** No quantitative metrics in the abstract; complex pipeline.

### [Comparative Analysis of Multiple Deep Learning Models for Forecasting Monthly Ambient PM2.5 Concentrations: A Case Study in Dezhou City, China](https://doi.org/10.3390/atmos15121432)
He et al. (2024), *Atmosphere*. 157 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts monthly ambient PM2.5 in Dezhou City, China, to support air pollution prevention and control.
- **Architecture:** Eight deep learning models compared, including ANN, CNN, GRU, LSTM and hybrid CNN-GRU-LSTM (convolutional plus recurrent).
- **Data:** Air pollution data for Dezhou City, January 2014 to December 2023.
- **Main result:** CNN-GRU-LSTM performs best (R 0.9686, RMSE 4.6491 μg/m3), 34.28% more accurate than ANN; CNN, GRU and LSTM RMSE are 32.78–57.00% higher.
- **Open work:** Adding meteorological and emission predictors and testing other cities would extend the work.

### [Himawari-8-derived diurnal variations in ground-level PM2.5 pollution across China using the fast space-time Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM)](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-21-7863-2021)
Wei et al. (2021), *Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics*. 157 citations.

- **Main goal:** Captures diurnal variation of ground-level PM2.5 across China using geostationary satellite data rather than polar-orbiter snapshots.
- **Architecture:** Space-time LightGBM (STLG), a gradient boosting decision tree model incorporating spatiotemporal features.
- **Data:** Himawari-8/AHI aerosol products plus environmental variables, with 1,415,188 hourly ground PM2.5 samples in China; output ChinaHigh PM2.5 at 5 km.
- **Main result:** Hourly estimates reach CV-R2 0.85, RMSE 13.62 and MAE 8.49 μg/m3; PM2.5 peaks near 10:00 local time and declines until sunset.
- **Open work:** Extending to nighttime and other geostationary sensors would broaden coverage.

- *Basis: abstract*

### [Real-Time Profiling of Fine-Grained Air Quality Index Distribution Using UAV Sensing](https://doi.org/10.1109/jiot.2017.2777820)
Yang et al. (2017), *IEEE Internet of Things Journal*. 156 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds fine-grained real-time air quality index maps with UAV-mounted sensors while limiting battery use.

- **Data:** UAV-sensed AQI measurements in a 2-D roadside park and a 3-D building courtyard.
- **Main result:** GPM-NN gives higher AQI prediction accuracy than existing models while the adaptive algorithm greatly reduces power consumption.
- **Open work:** Scaling to larger urban areas and multiple UAVs would extend the system.
- **Issues:** Small local test scenarios; quantitative accuracy not given in the abstract.

### [Identifying dominant environmental predictors of freshwater wetland methane fluxes across diurnal to seasonal time scales](https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.15661)
Knox et al. (2021), *Global Change Biology*. 155 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies dominant environmental controls on freshwater wetland methane fluxes across diel, synoptic and seasonal scales to reduce uncertainty in the global methane budget.
- **Architecture:** Statistical and machine learning analysis in a wavelet multi-resolution framework: correlation analysis, generalized additive models, mutual information and random forests.
- **Data:** Eddy covariance methane flux and environmental measurements from 23 freshwater wetland sites (FLUXNET-CH4 network).
- **Main result:** Temperature dominates seasonally where water table varies little, while water table depth dominates elsewhere; seasonal fluxes lag water table by about 17 days; pressure drops trigger releases at peat sites.
- **Open work:** Incorporating identified predictors and lags into process-based wetland methane models and expanding site coverage.
- **Issues:** Limited number of sites with uneven representation of wetland types; correlative analysis does not establish causality.

### [Atmospheric urban pollution: applications of an artificial neural network (ANN) to the city of Perugia](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0304-3800(01)00434-3)
Viotti et al. (2002), *Ecological Modelling*. 154 citations.
