### [Wind speed forecasting approach using secondary decomposition algorithm and Elman neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2015.08.014)
Liu et al. (2015), *Applied Energy*. 278 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves wind speed forecasting through secondary decomposition of the wind series.
- **Architecture:** Secondary decomposition (wavelet packet decomposition followed by ensemble empirical mode decomposition) with Elman recurrent neural networks.
- **Data:** Measured wind speed time series; sites not reported here.
- **Main result:** Secondary decomposition is reported to improve accuracy over single decomposition and Elman network alone; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Multi-step and probabilistic forecasting and comparison with deep sequence models.
- **Issues:** Abstract missing; decomposition-based setups can leak future information.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Forecasting daily urban electric load profiles using artificial neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enconman.2004.01.006)
Beccali et al. (2004), *Energy Conversion and Management*. 277 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily electric load profiles of an urban area using weather information to support utility operations.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network; the network type is not specified here.
- **Data:** Measured electric load and meteorological data for an urban area in Italy (Palermo); details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The neural network reproduces daily load profiles with useful accuracy using weather inputs.
- **Open work:** Testing over more years and seasons and using weather forecasts rather than observations as inputs.
- **Issues:** Single urban area; no abstract available, so error figures are not reported here.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A review and taxonomy of wind and solar energy forecasting methods based on deep learning](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.egyai.2021.100060)
Alkhayat et al. (2021), *Energy and AI*. 274 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews deep learning methods for wind and solar energy forecasting to support power system operation.
- **Architecture:** Review and taxonomy of deep learning wind and solar forecasting over five years, including hybrid models, RNN (LSTM, GRU) and CNN.
- **Data:** Published studies; discusses datasets, preprocessing, and deterministic and probabilistic methods.
- **Main result:** Hybrid models are most used, followed by LSTM/GRU recurrent networks and CNNs; probabilistic and multistep forecasting are gaining attention.
- **Open work:** Current challenges and future directions, including probabilistic and multistep forecasting.
- **Issues:** Limited to five years of literature; no quantitative benchmark across studies.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Long short term memory–convolutional neural network based deep hybrid approach for solar irradiance forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2021.117061)
Kumari et al. (2021), *Applied Energy*. 273 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves hourly global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting to support integration of variable solar power into grids and energy markets.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid LSTM-CNN: an LSTM extracts temporal features from irradiance time series and a convolutional neural network extracts spatial features from correlation matrices of meteorological variables at the target and neighboring sites.
- **Data:** Hourly meteorological data (temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, cloud cover, etc.) and GHI at 23 locations in California, USA; evaluated over one year, by season and under three sky conditions.
- **Main result:** Forecast skill score improves by about 37–45% over smart persistence, SVM, ANN, standalone LSTM, CNN and other hybrid models across seasons and sky conditions.
- **Open work:** Test longer horizons and other climates, and incorporate satellite or numerical weather prediction inputs.
- **Issues:** Single-region study; deterministic forecasts only with no uncertainty quantification; short-term horizon; sensitivity to the choice of neighboring sites not fully explored.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Empirical and machine learning models for predicting daily global solar radiation from sunshine duration: A review and case study in China](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2018.10.018)
Fan et al. (2019), *Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews*. 273 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews and benchmarks empirical and machine learning models that estimate daily global solar radiation from sunshine duration, for solar energy system design.
- **Architecture:** Review plus benchmark of 12 empirical sunshine-based model forms and 12 machine learning algorithms, including ANFIS, extreme learning machine, LSSVM, MARS, XGBoost, M5Tree, GRNN and MLP.
- **Data:** Daily station observations of sunshine duration and global solar radiation across four climatic zones of China (temperate continental, temperate monsoon, mountain plateau, subtropical monsoon).
- **Main result:** Machine learning models (RMSE 2.06–2.75 MJ m−2 d−1, R2 0.84–0.94) generally beat empirical ones (RMSE 2.12–3.54); ANFIS is recommended overall, with MARS and XGBoost as accurate, cheap alternatives.
- **Open work:** Extend to other input combinations, sub-daily scales and regions outside China; assess spatial transferability between stations.
- **Issues:** Gains over the best empirical models are modest; results are station-based and China-specific; model hyperparameter tuning effort may differ across methods.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Mid-to-long term wind and photovoltaic power generation prediction based on copula function and long short term memory network](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2019.01.193)
Han et al. (2019), *Applied Energy*. 273 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts mid-to-long term wind and photovoltaic power generation with limited historical samples, for grid planning and complementary dispatch.
- **Architecture:** Copula functions select key meteorological drivers from nonlinear and tail dependence; LSTM networks then forecast wind, PV and joint wind-PV generation, benchmarked against persistence and support vector machine models.
- **Data:** Actual generation and meteorological data from wind farms and photovoltaic power stations in China and the United States; record lengths not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Independent and joint LSTM models outperform persistence and SVM baselines; no headline error values are given in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Couple with longer-range weather or climate forecasts as inputs and test on more plants and longer records.
- **Issues:** Mid-to-long term skill depends on weather predictability that the method does not address directly; limited samples raise overfitting risk; quantitative gains not stated.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [ANFIS, SVM and ANN soft-computing techniques to estimate daily global solar radiation in a warm sub-humid environment](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jastp.2017.02.002)
Quej et al. (2017), *Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics*. 273 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates daily horizontal global solar radiation from routinely measured meteorological variables in the warm sub-humid Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of three soft computing methods: adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), artificial neural network (MLP-type ANN) and support vector machine (SVM) regression.
- **Data:** Daily station meteorology in the Yucatán Peninsula (maximum and minimum air temperature, rainfall) plus extraterrestrial radiation; number of stations and years not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** SVM using maximum and minimum temperature, extraterrestrial radiation and rainfall performs best by RMSE, MAE and R2.
- **Open work:** Test transferability to other climates and stations and include humidity or cloud-related predictors.
- **Issues:** Regional, station-based study; numerical skill and train/test split not stated in the abstract; no comparison to satellite radiation products.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A generalized knowledge-based short-term load-forecasting technique](https://doi.org/10.1109/59.260833)
Rahman et al. (1993), *IEEE Transactions on Power Systems*. 272 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a generalized knowledge-based short-term load forecasting technique transferable across utilities and weather regimes.
- **Architecture:** Expert system (rule-based) using weather-load relationships and forecaster knowledge, not a neural network.
- **Data:** Historical load and weather data from several utilities in different regions.
- **Main result:** The technique gives accurate forecasts across different utilities with limited site-specific tuning.
- **Open work:** Automatic adaptation of rules and combination with learning methods.
- **Issues:** Rule base requires expert knowledge and maintenance; performance on unusual days depends on rule coverage.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Very Short-Term Nonparametric Probabilistic Forecasting of Renewable Energy Generation— With Application to Solar Energy](https://doi.org/10.1109/tpwrs.2015.2502423)
Golestaneh et al. (2016), *IEEE Transactions on Power Systems*. 272 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces very short-term probabilistic forecasts of renewable generation, demonstrated for solar power, without assuming a parametric predictive distribution.
- **Architecture:** Nonparametric quantile forecasting based on extreme learning machines (single-hidden-layer feedforward networks) to give fast predictive densities.
- **Data:** Solar power generation data; site and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The method yields reliable and sharp predictive quantiles at very short lead times with low computational cost, compared favourably with benchmark probabilistic methods.
- **Open work:** Extend to multi-site and spatio-temporal settings and to wind power.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; details of data and scores could not be confirmed. Quantile crossing and calibration at extreme quantiles are typical concerns.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Short-Term Wind Speed Interval Prediction Based on Ensemble GRU Model](https://doi.org/10.1109/tste.2019.2926147)
Li et al. (2020), *IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy*. 271 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides short-term wind speed prediction intervals for wind power production, where variability makes reliable intervals difficult.
- **Architecture:** Variational mode decomposition plus gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks: an interval model for the main mode, point models for other modes, and a GRU error-correction model, combined in an ensemble.
- **Data:** Wind speed time series from two wind fields, eight test cases; sites and periods not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The method gives higher prediction-interval coverage probability and narrower interval width than compared approaches.
- **Open work:** Extend to wind power directly and to longer horizons with NWP inputs.
- **Issues:** Univariate, data-driven setup; decomposition over the whole series may leak information; limited number of sites.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Short-term PV power forecasting using hybrid GASVM technique](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2019.02.087)
Vandeventer et al. (2019), *Renewable Energy*. 270 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts short-term power output of a residential-scale PV system under variable weather.
- **Architecture:** Genetic-algorithm-optimized support vector machine (GASVM): an SVM classifies weather conditions and a genetic algorithm tunes the ensemble.
- **Data:** PV output and data from a local weather station installed with the PV system at Deakin University, Australia.
- **Main result:** GASVM improves on a conventional SVM by about 670 W in RMSE and 98.8% in MAPE.
- **Open work:** Test on more systems, seasons and with NWP forecast inputs.
- **Issues:** Single small system; very large MAPE improvement suggests a weak baseline; data length not stated.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [An Integration of ANN Wind Power Estimation Into Unit Commitment Considering the Forecasting Uncertainty](https://doi.org/10.1109/tia.2007.908203)
Methaprayoon et al. (2007), *IEEE Transactions on Industry Applications*. 267 citations.

- **Main goal:** Integrates wind power forecasts and their uncertainty into unit commitment scheduling of power systems.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network for wind power estimation, coupled to a unit commitment optimization that accounts for forecast uncertainty.
- **Data:** Wind and wind-farm power data and a test power system; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Accounting for wind forecast uncertainty in unit commitment yields more reliable and economical scheduling than ignoring it.
- **Open work:** Probabilistic forecasts and larger systems with high wind penetration.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; forecast accuracy and system details are not reported here.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Prediction of wind speed and wind direction using artificial neural network, support vector regression and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.seta.2018.01.001)
Khosravi et al. (2018), *Sustainable Energy Technologies and Assessments*. 267 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts wind speed and wind direction for wind energy applications.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of artificial neural network (MLP), support vector regression and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) models.
- **Data:** Wind measurements from a wind site; location and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** Results not available here; the paper compares the three methods' accuracy for speed and direction.
- **Open work:** Extend to multi-step horizons and to power forecasting.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; details unconfirmed. Wind direction is circular and needs care in regression.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Short term load forecasting of Taiwan power system using a knowledge-based expert system](https://doi.org/10.1109/59.99372)
Ho et al. (1990), *IEEE Transactions on Power Systems*. 266 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts short-term electric load of the Taiwan power system by encoding operator knowledge into an expert system.
- **Architecture:** Expert system (rule-based) built from operator heuristics and load-weather relationships, not a neural network.
- **Data:** Historical hourly load and weather data from the Taiwan Power Company.
- **Main result:** The expert system produces accurate hourly load forecasts, comparable to or better than conventional statistical methods.
- **Open work:** Automatic rule learning and handling of special days.
- **Issues:** Knowledge acquisition is labor-intensive and rules are system specific.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Day-ahead power forecasting in a large-scale photovoltaic plant based on weather classification using LSTM](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.energy.2019.07.168)
Gao et al. (2019), *Energy*. 266 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts the day-ahead power output time series of a large PV plant, treating ideal and non-ideal weather separately.
- **Architecture:** LSTM networks: for ideal weather driven by next-day meteorological data; for non-ideal weather adding adjacent-day series and weather-type information, with daily totals from a discrete grey model used for correction.
- **Data:** Power output and meteorological data from a large-scale PV plant; location and period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** RMSE reaches 4.62% under ideal weather, and the proposed methods beat traditional algorithms under non-ideal weather.
- **Open work:** Use NWP forecasts directly and test on more plants and seasons.
- **Issues:** Relies on correct weather-type classification for the next day; single plant; error for non-ideal weather not quantified in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Estimation of monthly average daily global solar irradiation using artificial neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.solener.2007.06.003)
Mubiru et al. (2008), *Solar Energy*. 265 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates monthly average daily global solar irradiation where pyranometer data are lacking.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (feedforward) using meteorological and geographical inputs.
- **Data:** Meteorological records (sunshine duration, temperature, cloud cover) and irradiation measurements from stations in Uganda.
- **Main result:** The neural network estimates monthly average daily global irradiation with good agreement against measurements and outperforms empirical models.
- **Open work:** More stations and validation in other tropical climates.
- **Issues:** Few stations and monthly averages only; no abstract available, so error figures are not reported here.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A new strategy for wind speed forecasting using artificial intelligent methods](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2008.04.017)
Monfared et al. (2009), *Renewable Energy*. 265 citations.

- **Main goal:** Proposes a wind speed forecasting strategy for wind energy applications with lower computational cost.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks and fuzzy logic models applied to preprocessed wind speed series.
- **Data:** Wind speed time series; site and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The proposed strategy improves forecast accuracy and reduces computation time compared with classic neural network forecasting.
- **Open work:** Testing at multiple sites and forecast horizons.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; site, horizons and error statistics are not reported here.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Short-term wind power prediction based on LSSVM–GSA model](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enconman.2015.05.065)
Yuan et al. (2015), *Energy Conversion and Management*. 265 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts short-term wind power to support grid operation with variable wind generation.

- **Data:** Wind power data from a wind farm; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The LSSVM-GSA model is reported to improve accuracy over compared models; specific numbers not available here.
- **Open work:** Add NWP inputs and test probabilistic variants.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; data and results unconfirmed. Single-site, point-forecast setting.

### [Forecasting wind speed using empirical mode decomposition and Elman neural network](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2014.06.027)
Wang et al. (2014), *Applied Soft Computing*. 264 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts wind speed despite its chaotic, nonstationary nature.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid EMD-ENN: empirical mode decomposition into intrinsic mode functions, each forecast by an Elman recurrent neural network, with input size set by partial autocorrelation.
- **Data:** Four wind speed prediction cases; sites and periods not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** EMD-ENN has the lowest MAE, MSE and MAPE compared with persistence, a back-propagation neural network and plain ENN.
- **Open work:** Test multi-step horizons and add meteorological inputs.
- **Issues:** Decomposition of the full series can leak future information; univariate; limited cases.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Machine learning-based energy management and power forecasting in grid-connected microgrids with multiple distributed energy sources](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-70336-3)
Singh et al. (2024), *Scientific Reports*. 264 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts solar PV and wind generation in grid-connected microgrids to improve energy management.
- **Architecture:** Support vector regression using historical generation, weather and grid conditions, compared with linear regression and coupled to an energy management scheme.
- **Data:** Historical energy production, weather and grid condition data for a microgrid; site and period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** RMSE of 1.415 (solar) and 1.749 (wind); 8.4% lower operating costs, 15% lower peak load and 12% more renewable use.
- **Open work:** Test with deep learning and probabilistic forecasts and on real deployments.
- **Issues:** Only a linear regression baseline; units and data source unclear; system-level gains may be simulation-based.

### [Solar Irradiance Forecasting Using Deep Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.procs.2017.09.045)
Alzahrani et al. (2017), *Procedia Computer Science*. 264 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts solar irradiance for planning and operation of photovoltaic systems.
- **Architecture:** Deep recurrent neural network (stacked RNN), compared with support vector regression and feedforward neural networks.
- **Data:** Real solar irradiance data from Natural Resources Canada.
- **Main result:** The deep RNN outperforms the compared methods on performance tests; numbers not given in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Extend to multi-horizon forecasts and additional meteorological inputs.
- **Issues:** Short conference paper; data length, horizon and metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [An LSTM Short-Term Solar Irradiance Forecasting Under Complicated Weather Conditions](https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2019.2946057)
Yu et al. (2019), *IEEE Access*. 263 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts global horizontal irradiance one hour and one day ahead, especially on cloudy days where forecasts fail.

### [Short-term reforecasting of power output from a 48 MWe solar PV plant](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.solener.2014.11.017)
Chu et al. (2015), *Solar Energy*. 263 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves intra-hour forecasts of power output from a 48 MWe solar PV plant by reforecasting baseline forecasts.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network reforecasting of baseline models (such as persistence and other time-series models), with sky-image features and genetic-algorithm optimization.
- **Data:** Power output from a 48 MWe PV plant and ground-based sky imager data; site and period not confirmed here.
- **Main result:** Reforecasting improves forecast skill over the baseline models at short horizons; exact values not confirmed here.

Zhang et al. (2017), *Energy Conversion and Management*. 262 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts wind speed with an optimized compound extreme learning machine model.

- **Main result:** Reported to outperform compared benchmark models; numbers not available here.
- **Open work:** Test probabilistic outputs and other sites.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; data and results unconfirmed. Univariate, site-specific setup.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deterministic wind energy forecasting: A review of intelligent predictors and auxiliary methods](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enconman.2019.05.020)
Liu et al. (2019), *Energy Conversion and Management*. 260 citations.

- **Main goal:** Surveys intelligent predictors for deterministic wind speed and wind power forecasting.

### [Solar resource estimation using artificial neural networks and comparison with other correlation models](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0196-8904(03)00009-8)
Reddy et al. (2003), *Energy Conversion and Management*. 259 citations.

### [Direct Quantile Regression for Nonparametric Probabilistic Forecasting of Wind Power Generation](https://doi.org/10.1109/tpwrs.2016.2625101)
Wan et al. (2017), *IEEE Transactions on Power Systems*. 257 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces nonparametric probabilistic forecasts of wind power by directly estimating quantiles, avoiding distributional assumptions and costly two-stage interval construction.

Cao et al. (2012), *European Journal of Operational Research*. 257 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether recurrent neural networks forecast wind speed better than conventional time-series models, for wind energy planning.

Agga et al. (2021), *Renewable Energy*. 256 citations.

Doucoure et al. (2016), *Renewable Energy*. 254 citations.

Benghanem et al. (2009), *Energy Conversion and Management*. 253 citations.

Abdoos (2016), *Neurocomputing*. 253 citations.

### [Wind speed prediction method using Shared Weight Long Short-Term Memory Network and Gaussian Process Regression](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2019.04.047)
Zhang et al. (2019), *Applied Energy*. 252 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides reliable deterministic and probabilistic wind speed predictions for wind power integration with reduced training cost.

### [Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Multi-Site PV Power Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1109/tste.2021.3125200)
Simeunović et al. (2021), *IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy*. 252 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts multi-site PV power at fine spatial and temporal resolution, exploiting the dense network of PV systems as virtual weather stations.

- **Data:** Production data from 304 real PV systems and simulated production from 1000 PV systems across Switzerland, one year each.

- **Open work:** Adding NWP and satellite inputs to extend skill to longer horizons.
- **Issues:** Production-only inputs limit longer-horizon skill; one year of data; deterministic forecasts only.

### [A critical review of the models used to estimate solar radiation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2016.11.124)
Zhang et al. (2017), *Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews*. 252 citations.

- **Issues:** Literature-based; cross-study comparisons uneven.

Andrade et al. (2017), *IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy*. 252 citations.

Liu et al. (2019), *Applied Sciences*. 251 citations.

### [A current perspective on the accuracy of incoming solar energy forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pecs.2018.10.003)
Blaga et al. (2019), *Progress in Energy and Combustion Science*. 250 citations.

### [Short-term offshore wind power forecasting - A hybrid model based on Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), and deep-learning-based Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2021.12.100)
