- **Issues:** Limited years of training data.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Robust Model Predictive Control of Irrigation Systems With Active Uncertainty Learning and Data Analytics](https://doi.org/10.1109/tcst.2019.2916753)
Shang et al. (2018), *IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology*. 89 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates irrigation control that keeps soil moisture safe while reducing water use under uncertain evapotranspiration and precipitation forecasts.
- **Architecture:** Data-driven robust model predictive control combining a mechanistic soil moisture model with uncertainty sets learned from historical forecast errors (support vector clustering for evapotranspiration, tailored set for precipitation) and affine decision rules.
- **Data:** Historical evapotranspiration and precipitation forecasts and observations used for real-data case studies; specific products not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Maintains soil moisture above safety levels and cuts total water consumption by 40% relative to tuned open-loop control, outperforming rule-based and certainty-equivalent MPC.
- **Open work:** Field deployment and extension to multiple fields, crops and longer weather-forecast horizons.
- **Issues:** Simulation case studies rather than field trials; performance depends on representativeness of historical forecast errors.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Assessment and prediction of index based agricultural drought vulnerability using machine learning algorithms.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2023.161394)
Kafy et al. (2023), *Science of The Total Environment*. 89 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses and predicts agricultural drought vulnerability in the drought-prone Barind Tract of Bangladesh.
- **Architecture:** Cellular Automata–Artificial Neural Network (CA-ANN) model to project the Vegetation Health Index built from VCI and TCI.
- **Data:** Landsat imagery 1996–2021 with NDVI, MNDWI, soil moisture content, TCI, VCI and VHI; projections for 2026 and 2031.
- **Main result:** Healthy vegetation fell 19% and surface water 26% with >5 °C warming; extreme drought rose from 2% to 7%; projected extreme and severe drought reaches 18% and 24% by 2031.
- **Open work:** Using projections to plan drought mitigation and community preparedness.
- **Issues:** Projections extrapolate past land-cover trends without climate scenario forcing; validation of future predictions is not possible; Landsat temporal sampling is coarse.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Linear regressions and neural approaches to water demand forecasting in irrigation districts with telemetry systems](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biosystemseng.2007.03.003)
Pulido-Calvo et al. (2007), *Biosystems Engineering*. 88 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily water demand in irrigation districts equipped with telemetry systems to support operation.
- **Architecture:** Linear regression models compared with neural network approaches (feed-forward neural networks, including hybrid variants).
- **Data:** Daily water demand and climatic records from irrigation districts in southern Spain with telemetry.
- **Main result:** Neural approaches forecast irrigation water demand more accurately than linear regressions; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Inclusion of crop and weather forecast information.
- **Issues:** Limited districts and seasons; demand depends on management decisions not captured.
- *Basis: assessment*

Matsumura et al. (2014), *The Journal of Agricultural Science*. 88 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts maize yield in Jilin Province, China.

- **Data:** Maize yield and predictor data for Jilin; details not reported.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Adding remote sensing predictors and testing at finer scales.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; short yield records limit ANN training.

### [MMST-ViT: Climate Change-aware Crop Yield Prediction via Multi-Modal Spatial-Temporal Vision Transformer](https://doi.org/10.1109/iccv51070.2023.00531)
Lin et al. (2023), *IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision*. 86 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts county-level crop yields across the United States accounting for both growing-season weather variation and long-term climate change.

- **Data:** Satellite remote sensing imagery and short-term meteorological data for over 200 US counties; dataset and code released.
- **Main result:** MMST-ViT outperforms competing models on three performance metrics for county-level yield prediction.

- **Issues:** Evaluated over about 200 counties only; climate change effects are learned from limited historical years and are hard to verify.

### [The response of maize, sorghum, and soybean yield to growing-phase climate revealed with machine learning](https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ab7b22)
Hoffman et al. (2020), *Environmental Research Letters*. 84 citations.

- **Main goal:** Characterizes how maize, sorghum and soybean yields depend on climate in crop-specific developmental phases, to understand climate change impacts on food systems.
- **Architecture:** Random forest used as a diagnostic tool with phase-specific climate variables and a time trend for technology.
- **Data:** County yields and climate variables for the US plains, 1980–2016, aggregated by establishment, critical window and grain-filling phases.
- **Main result:** Random forest explains 71–86% of yield variance; yields fall sharply above ~29°C (maize) and 30°C (soybean) maximum temperature, while sorghum tolerates up to 32.5°C; maize is sensitive to low humidity during flowering.
- **Open work:** Projecting shifts in optimal growing regions under warming with soil productivity and adaptation included.
- **Issues:** Correlative county-level analysis; technology represented only by a time trend; extrapolation to future warming is uncertain.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [DeepCropNet: a deep spatial-temporal learning framework for county-level corn yield estimation](https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ab66cb)
Lin et al. (2020), *Environmental Research Letters*. 82 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates county-level corn yield from meteorological conditions while capturing temporal cumulative effects and spatial heterogeneity.
- **Architecture:** DeepCropNet: attention-based long short-term memory (LSTM) for temporal features with multi-task learning output layers for regional spatial features.
- **Data:** US Corn Belt county yields 1981–2016 with growing degree days, killing degree days and precipitation time series.
- **Main result:** RMSE of 0.82 Mg/ha versus 1.14 for LASSO and 1.05 for random forest; attention reveals consistent cumulative temporal patterns.
- **Open work:** Adding soil, management and remote-sensing inputs and testing under future climate.
- **Issues:** Only three meteorological inputs; no explicit technology or management variables; spatial generalization outside the Corn Belt untested.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Forecasting of Crop Yield using Remote Sensing Data, Agrarian Factors and Machine Learning Approaches](https://doi.org/10.9734/jerr/2023/v24i12858)
Bharadiya et al. (2023), *Journal of Engineering Research and Reports*. 81 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews crop yield forecasting with remote sensing, agrarian factors and machine learning to support food policy and disaster response.
- **Architecture:** Review of machine learning and deep learning approaches using vegetation indices and environmental variables for crop yield prediction.
- **Data:** Literature from 2011-2022; most reviewed studies use satellite data, mainly MODIS vegetation indices.
- **Main result:** Satellite remote sensing, especially MODIS, is the most used data source and vegetation indices are the most common predictors; pros and cons of techniques are compared.
- **Open work:** Filling gaps in applying deep learning with remote sensing in specific regions.
- **Issues:** Narrative review with no quantitative synthesis; selection criteria are loosely described.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Comparative Analysis of Statistical and Machine Learning Techniques for Rice Yield Forecasting for Chhattisgarh, India](https://doi.org/10.3390/su15032786)
Satpathi et al. (2023), *Sustainability*. 80 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies the best weather-based model for forecasting rice yield in three agro-climatic zones of Chhattisgarh, India.
- **Architecture:** Stepwise multiple linear regression, artificial neural network (ANN), LASSO, elastic net and ridge regression, with ensembles built using GLM, random forest, cubist and elastic net.
- **Data:** 21 years of district rice yield statistics and weather data for Raipur, Surguja and Bastar; 80% calibration and 20% validation.
- **Main result:** ANN performs best for Raipur and Surguja, LASSO and elastic net for Bastar; ensembles beat individual models, with random forest ensemble best for Bastar (R2 0.85 calibration, 0.81 validation).
- **Open work:** Adding remote sensing and soil inputs and testing other crops.
- **Issues:** Very short records (21 years) and near-perfect ANN scores suggest overfitting risk.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A generalized regression neural network and its application for leaf wetness prediction to forecast plant disease](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0169-7439(99)00006-4)
Chtioui et al. (1999), *Chemometrics and Intelligent Laboratory Systems*. 79 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts leaf wetness, a key driver of plant disease infection, to support disease forecasting from weather data.

- **Data:** Field weather observations and leaf wetness measurements; site and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The GRNN predicts leaf wetness with useful accuracy for disease forecasting; quantitative results are not reported here.

- **Issues:** Local data-driven model; transferability to other climates and canopies is uncertain.

### [Applied Deep Learning-Based Crop Yield Prediction: A Systematic Analysis of Current Developments and Potential Challenges](https://doi.org/10.3390/technologies12040043)
Meghraoui et al. (2024), *Technologies*. 79 citations.

- **Main goal:** Systematically reviews deep learning for crop yield prediction to synthesize crops, models, inputs and challenges.

- **Data:** Studies from DOAJ, IEEE, MDPI and ScienceDirect over eight years using satellite imagery, UAV data and other inputs.
- **Main result:** CNN and LSTM are the dominant architectures, cereals such as wheat and corn are most studied, and UAV data use is growing alongside satellite imagery.
- **Open work:** Continual updates of the review and addressing data and generalization challenges.
- **Issues:** Limited to four databases; results may differ with other sources.

Marj et al. (2011), *International Journal of Remote Sensing*. 78 citations.

- **Open work:** Testing longer lead times and other regions would follow naturally.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; teleconnection-based predictability is regionally limited and short records constrain ANN training.

### [Yield prediction for crops by gradient-based algorithms](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0291928)
Mahesh et al. (2024), *PLOS ONE*. 71 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts crop yields to support farmers and agricultural policy decisions.

### [Demand Forecasting for Irrigation Water Distribution Systems](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)0733-9437(2003)129:6(422))
Pulido-Calvo et al. (2003), *Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering*. 70 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily water demand in irrigation distribution systems to support operation of pumping and distribution networks.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward computational neural networks compared with multiple linear regression and univariate time-series (ARIMA-type) models.
- **Data:** Daily water demand and climatic records from an irrigation district in southern Spain.
- **Main result:** Neural networks give lower forecast errors for daily irrigation demand than the regression and time-series models.

### [Crop Yield Forecasting Using Artificial Neural Networks: A Comparison between Spatial and Temporal Models](https://doi.org/10.1155/2014/857865)
Guo et al. (2014), *Mathematical Problems in Engineering*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares spatial and temporal neural network models for forecasting wheat yield.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks: a spatial feed-forward NN versus temporal nonlinear autoregressive (NARNN) and NARX (NARXNN) recurrent networks.
- **Data:** Historic wheat yield, plantation area, rainfall and temperature records; region and period not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The spatial NN predicts wheat yield for a given plantation area with high accuracy, outperforming NARNN and NARXNN, but only within normal yield ranges; NARNN/NARXNN are inconsistent between training and forecasting.

### [Deep Learning for Multi-Source Data-Driven Crop Yield Prediction in Northeast China](https://doi.org/10.3390/agriculture14060794)
Lu et al. (2024), *Agriculture*. 65 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts maize, rice and soybean yields in Northeast China from multi-source data to support food security and agricultural planning.
- **Architecture:** CNN-LSTM-Attention hybrid (convolutional neural network, LSTM and attention mechanism) compared with random forest, XGBoost and a CNN.
- **Data:** Multi-source data 2014-2020: vegetation indices including kNDVI, environmental variables and photosynthetically active parameters, with yield statistics for Northeast China.
- **Main result:** The CNN-LSTM-Attention model gives significantly more accurate yields than the traditional models, and kNDVI proves an effective predictor for multiple crops; numbers not given in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Extending to other regions and longer records, and using the model for in-season yield forecasting.
- **Issues:** Short seven-year record limits temporal generalization; no uncertainty estimates; gains over baselines not quantified in the abstract.

Balls et al. (1996), *New Phytologist*. 64 citations.

- **Main goal:** Examines how microclimatic conditions modify visible ozone injury in subterranean clover, to relate ozone exposure to crop damage better than exposure indices alone.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network relating ozone exposure and microclimate variables to leaf injury, used to explore the influence of each variable.

### [Artificial Neural Network Model for Subsurface-Drained Farmlands](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)0733-9437(1997)123:4(285))
Yang et al. (1997), *Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering*. 64 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a data-driven model of subsurface-drained farmland hydrology, such as water table depth and drain outflow, as a fast alternative to process-based drainage models.

### [Accurate Wheat Yield Prediction Using Machine Learning and Climate-NDVI Data Fusion](https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2024.3376735)
Ashfaq et al. (2024), *IEEE Access*. 64 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts district-level wheat yield in Multan, Punjab, Pakistan, and clarifies the contribution of climate, soil, socioeconomic and remote sensing inputs.

Hoque et al. (2024), *IEEE Access*. 60 citations.

### [Probabilistic assessments of climate change impacts on durum wheat in the Mediterranean region](https://doi.org/10.5194/nhess-11-1293-2011)
Ferrise et al. (2011), *Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences*. 56 citations.

Aghajanloo et al. (2012), *Neural Computing and Applications*. 55 citations.

Ding et al. (2023), *ACM Transactions on Sensor Networks*. 49 citations.

Arshad et al. (2023), *Field Crops Research*. 47 citations.

Shin et al. (2020), *Agricultural and Forest Meteorology*. 46 citations.

Saikai et al. (2023), *PLOS Water*. 45 citations.

Singh et al. (2008), *Agricultural Economics Research Review*. 44 citations.

### [How can machine learning help in understanding the impact of climate change on crop yields?](https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/acb164)
Sidhu et al. (2023), *Environmental Research Letters*. 43 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates whether machine learning improves estimation of crop yield response to climate change compared with linear regression.

### [Machine Learning Crop Yield Models Based on Meteorological Features and Comparison with a Process-Based Model](https://doi.org/10.1175/aies-d-22-0002.1)

Liu et al. (2024), *Earth's Future*. 37 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses crop yield sensitivity to climate change in Northeast China while accounting for vegetation and groundwater memory that is only observed in the satellite era.
- **Architecture:** ReGen-Net reconstruction module extends NDVI and groundwater anomaly records back to 1981; a GATAE-TFT model (graph attention plus Temporal Fusion Transformer) predicts yields, with YieldTransformer baseline and SHAP attribution.
- **Data:** Crop yield records since 1981 in Northeast China, NDVI, groundwater storage anomalies (GRACE-era), drought indices; bias-adjusted ISIMIP projections 2017–2060 under SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5.
- **Main result:** Test R2 of 0.857, 0.777, 0.798 and 0.837 for maize, rice, soybean and wheat; projections show gradual declines in maize, rice and wheat and stable soybean.
- **Open work:** Incorporate management and CO2 effects and extend to other regions.
- **Issues:** Reconstructed predictors add uncertainty; statistical projections assume stationary relationships under future climate; adaptation and CO2 fertilization are not explicitly represented.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [NeuralCrop: Combining physics and machine learning for improved crop yield projections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20177)
Lin et al. (2025), *arXiv*. 0 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves crop yield projections under climate change by combining process-based global gridded crop models with machine learning that generalizes out of distribution.
- **Architecture:** NeuralCrop, a differentiable hybrid global gridded crop model combining an advanced process-based GGCM with neural network components; first trained to emulate a GGCM, then fine-tuned on observations.
- **Data:** Emulation of a process-based GGCM, then fine-tuning on observed yields; site-level and large-scale simulations including European wheat regions and the US Corn Belt.
- **Main result:** Accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art GGCMs, better reproduction of yield anomalies especially under drought extremes, and orders of magnitude faster for large-scale long-term runs.
- **Open work:** Extend to more crops and regions and use for climate-impact risk assessment.
- **Issues:** Out-of-distribution reliability under future climates remains to be demonstrated; inherits parent GGCM structure; observational yield data quality limits fine-tuning.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Seasonal Pre‐Planting Drought Impact‐Based Forecasting of Crop Yield in India](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025ef007128)
Shyrokaya et al. (2026), *Earth's Future*. 0 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts standardized crop yields in India before planting from drought indices to support impact-based early warning.
- **Architecture:** Random Forest, XGBoost (gradient boosting) and artificial neural networks (MLP) linking observed and forecast drought indices to yields, at district and cluster levels.
- **Data:** District-level historical paddy rice and wheat yields in India, observed drought indices at multiple accumulation periods, and ECMWF SEAS5 seasonal forecasts.
- **Main result:** District models beat cluster models with Random Forest best; over 80% of wheat and 70% of rice districts reach RMSE below 0.2; SEAS5 enables rice predictions up to 6 months ahead; CRPS confirms skill including for extremely low yields.
- **Open work:** Operationalize for anticipatory action and include non-climatic drivers such as irrigation and management.
- **Issues:** Short yield records per district; standardized yields remove trends; skill varies with yield variability and lead time.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Evaluating and improving crop-yield forecasting methods during extreme drought](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17971)
Gupta et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 0 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates crop-yield forecasting models under the extreme 2012 US Corn Belt drought, when conditions lie outside the training distribution.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of non-deep ML models with sample weighting and feature selection against the VITA deep learning model.
- **Data:** County-level US corn yields with 16 meteorological drivers; 2012 drought year as test.
- **Main result:** Sample weighting and feature selection improve the ML models, VITA gains little from them but still outperforms the ML models.
- **Open work:** Develop methods robust to distribution shift and spatial/temporal sparsity for extreme years.
- **Issues:** Single extreme year and single crop; limited predictors; quantitative skill not reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [MODELLING THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON THE HUNGARIAN WINE REGIONS USING RANDOM FOREST](https://doi.org/10.15666/aeer/1002_121140)
Gaál et al. (2012), *Applied Ecology and Environmental Research*. 0 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses how climate change may affect the Hungarian wine regions by modelling climatic suitability.
- **Architecture:** Random forest classification relating climate variables to wine region occurrence, projected under future climate.
- **Data:** Observed climate data for Hungary and regional climate change scenarios; details not reported.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the record.
- **Open work:** Include grape variety-specific responses and multiple climate model ensembles.
- **Issues:** Correlative niche modelling ignores adaptation and assumes stationary climate-suitability relations. No abstract available; details of data, validation and skill cannot be confirmed from the record.
- *Basis: assessment*

<a id="benchmarks"></a>
## Benchmarks & datasets

### [The ERA5 global reanalysis](https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.3803)
Hersbach et al. (2020), *Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society*. 26,664 citations.

- **Main goal:** Documents ERA5, ECMWF's fifth-generation global reanalysis replacing ERA-Interim.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML: 4D-Var data assimilation with IFS Cy41r2 at about 31 km, hourly output, plus a 10-member ensemble (3-hourly, half resolution) for uncertainty.
- **Data:** Global observations from 1950 onwards (paper focuses on 1979 onwards); atmosphere, land surface and ocean waves.
- **Main result:** Re-forecasts gain up to one day of skill over ERA-Interim; better tropospheric fit to radiosondes and much better wave heights; correlation with GPCP monthly precipitation rises from 67% to 77%.
- **Open work:** Complete the back extension to 1950 and address stratospheric and other known biases.
- **Issues:** No improvement in stratospheric fit; ensemble spread reflects observing-system changes. As the main training set for ML weather models, its biases propagate into them.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [WeatherBench: A Benchmark Data Set for Data‐Driven Weather Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020ms002203)
Rasp et al. (2020), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 797 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a common benchmark for data-driven medium-range (3-5 day) global weather forecasting to enable fair comparisons.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark dataset with evaluation metrics (latitude-weighted RMSE, mainly Z500 and T850) and baselines: persistence, climatology, linear regression, CNNs, and IFS physical models at coarse resolutions.
- **Data:** ERA5 regridded to 5.625, 2.8125 and 1.40625 degrees, 1979-2018, with 2017-2018 as test years.
- **Main result:** Simple deep learning baselines trail operational IFS by a wide margin, establishing a reference point for later models.
- **Open work:** Higher-resolution, probabilistic evaluation and more variables (later addressed by WeatherBench 2).
- **Issues:** Coarse resolution and few headline variables; deterministic RMSE favours smooth forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [WeatherBench 2: A Benchmark for the Next Generation of Data‐Driven Global Weather Models](https://doi.org/10.1029/2023ms004019)
Rasp et al. (2023), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 469 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a common, updated benchmark to compare data-driven and physical global medium-range weather models fairly.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark: open-source evaluation framework, public training, ground-truth and baseline data, headline scores, and a continuously updated website.
- **Data:** ERA5 and operational analyses as ground truth; forecasts from IFS HRES and ENS and ML models such as Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and others, mainly for 2020.
- **Main result:** Defines headline scores following operational practice and presents results for state-of-the-art physical and ML models.
- **Open work:** Better probabilistic and extreme-event evaluation, observation-based verification, and handling of caveats such as differing initial conditions.
- **Issues:** Verification against reanalysis or each model's own analysis can bias comparisons; standard metrics reward smooth forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### SEVIR : A Storm Event Imagery Dataset for Deep Learning Applications in Radar and Satellite Meteorology
Veillette et al. (2020), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 230 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a curated, co-registered dataset of storm events to support deep learning in radar and satellite meteorology.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark dataset (SEVIR) with baseline deep learning models for tasks such as nowcasting and synthetic weather radar generation from satellite.
- **Data:** More than 10,000 events, each 4 hours at 5-minute steps over 384 km x 384 km patches across the US, with GOES-16 visible and infrared channels, NEXRAD vertically integrated liquid, and GLM lightning.
- **Main result:** Supplies standardized data and baseline results (e.g., U-Net style models) that became a widely used nowcasting benchmark.
- **Open work:** Benchmark more advanced generative and probabilistic nowcasting models and expand coverage beyond the US.
- **Issues:** US-only, event-centred sampling biases toward storms; abstract unavailable here, so details are from knowledge of the paper.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [ClimateBench v1.0: A Benchmark for Data‐Driven Climate Projections](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021ms002954)
Watson-Parris et al. (2022), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 112 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a benchmark for ML emulators of climate model responses to emissions, so scenario space can be explored cheaply beyond pattern scaling.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark framework with baseline emulators (Gaussian process, random forest, neural network models) that map emissions and concentrations of CO2, CH4 and aerosols to climate fields.
- **Data:** NorESM2 simulations from ScenarioMIP, AerChemMIP and DAMIP. Targets are annual mean temperature, diurnal temperature range, precipitation and extreme precipitation.
- **Main result:** Baseline emulators predict global annual-mean fields for unseen scenarios with reasonable skill. Temperature is emulated much better than precipitation.
- **Open work:** Include physical constraints such as energy conservation directly in emulators, and use emulators for detection and attribution.
- **Issues:** Based on a single ESM, so the benchmark reflects its biases. Annual means only; held-out test scenario is limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [EarthNet2021: A large-scale dataset and challenge for Earth surface forecasting as a guided video prediction task](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00124)
Requena-Mesa et al. (2021), *2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)*. 82 citations.

- **Main goal:** Frames Earth surface forecasting as guided video prediction: predicting future satellite imagery conditioned on future weather, to capture localized impacts of extreme weather.
- **Architecture:** Dataset and challenge for model intercomparison rather than a single model. Baselines include persistence and video prediction networks.
- **Data:** Sentinel-2 imagery at 20 m, matched topography and mesoscale (1.28 km) E-OBS-style meteorological variables over Europe, packaged into about 32,000 samples.
- **Main result:** Releases a large ML-ready dataset with evaluation tracks (including out-of-distribution and seasonal tests), aiming at more than 50x finer resolution than numerical models.
- **Open work:** Develop models that exploit the weather conditioning, and link the forecasts to impacts such as crop yield, forest health and biodiversity.
- **Issues:** Cloud contamination and gaps in optical imagery. The meteorological guidance comes from observations or reanalysis rather than real forecasts, so operational skill is untested.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [ClimateLearn: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Weather and Climate Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.01909)
Nguyen et al. (2023), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 76 citations.

- **Main goal:** Addressing poor reproducibility and inconsistent setups in ML for weather and climate by providing a standard open library.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark library (ClimateLearn, PyTorch) with data pipelines, deep learning models such as transformers (ViT), ResNets and U-Nets plus baselines, and standard evaluation for forecasting and downscaling.
- **Data:** ERA5 (including WeatherBench-style data), CMIP6 and PRISM datasets.
- **Main result:** Provides holistic pipelines and documentation and showcases comprehensive forecasting and downscaling experiments; described as the first large-scale open effort of its kind.
- **Open work:** Community growth, more tasks, models and datasets, and probabilistic evaluation.
- **Issues:** A software resource rather than a new method; experiments are illustrative and at coarse resolution.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [ChaosBench: A Multi-Channel, Physics-Based Benchmark for Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Climate Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.00712)
Nathaniel et al. (2024), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 61 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provide a benchmark for extending data-driven weather emulators to subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) timescales.
- **Architecture:** ChaosBench: multi-channel benchmark with deterministic, probabilistic and physics-based metrics, and operational physics-based baselines; evaluates ViT/ClimaX, Pangu-Weather, GraphCast and FourCastNetV2.
- **Data:** ERA5 atmosphere plus ocean, sea-ice and land reanalyses spanning over 45 years; S2S forecasts from four national weather agencies as baselines.
- **Main result:** Weather-scale ML models collapse to unskilled climatology at S2S leads; ensembles, error-propagation control and physics-informed models extend predictability somewhat.
- **Open work:** Developing coupled Earth-system emulators and probabilistic methods that retain skill at S2S leads.
- **Issues:** Benchmark findings depend on chosen metrics and baselines; ML models evaluated largely as designed for weather scales rather than retrained for S2S.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [ClimateSet: A Large-Scale Climate Model Dataset for Machine Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03721)
Kaltenborn et al. (2023), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 47 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a large, consistent, ML-ready multi-model climate dataset, since most ML emulation, downscaling and prediction work relies on output from a single climate model.
- **Architecture:** Dataset and modular retrieval/preprocessing pipeline; benchmarks several ML emulators (forcing-to-climate mapping) and a multi-model 'super emulator'.
- **Data:** Forcing inputs from Input4MIPs and outputs of 36 CMIP6 climate models across scenarios; pipeline can add further models and scenarios.
- **Main result:** Emulator benchmarks show that ML model performance and generalization vary substantially across climate models; training on several models at once is feasible.
- **Open work:** Extending to more variables, models and tasks (downscaling, prediction) and assessing whether super emulators generalize to unseen scenarios and models.
- **Issues:** Benchmarks are emulation of model output, so they inherit CMIP6 biases; coarse resolution and limited scenario set constrain conclusions about generalization.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [The EUPPBench postprocessing benchmark dataset v1.0](https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-15-2635-2023)
Demaeyer et al. (2023), *Earth System Science Data*. 43 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a common benchmark dataset so that statistical postprocessing methods for medium-range forecasts can be compared fairly for operational choices.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark dataset of time-aligned forecasts and observations with proposed evaluation methods; first benchmark compares several postprocessing methods for 2 m temperature.
- **Data:** ECMWF ensemble forecasts and reforecasts paired with station observations and gridded data over a central European domain (EUMETNET), distributed via climetlab and Zenodo.
- **Main result:** Releases the public EUPPBench v1.0 dataset with download examples, evaluation protocol and a first intercomparison of 2 m temperature correction methods.
- **Open work:** Extending to more variables (wind, precipitation), longer periods and larger domains, and broader method intercomparisons.
- **Issues:** Version 1 focuses on 2 m temperature and a limited region, so conclusions may not transfer to other variables or climates.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Digital Typhoon: Long-term Satellite Image Dataset for the Spatio-Temporal Modeling of Tropical Cyclones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02665)
Kitamoto et al. (2023), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 39 citations.

- **Main goal:** Supplies a long-term, homogeneous satellite image dataset of tropical cyclones for benchmarking spatio-temporal ML models.
- **Architecture:** Dataset with a processing workflow (typhoon-centered infrared crops in Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection, inter-satellite calibration) and benchmark tasks for analysis, forecasting and reanalysis of intensity.
- **Data:** Over 40 years of geostationary infrared imagery of western North Pacific typhoons, aligned with best track data.
- **Main result:** Benchmarks show the intensity tasks remain challenging for recent deep learning models, with performance sensitive to many design choices.
- **Open work:** Developing models for track and intensity forecasting, societal impact and climate change tasks using the dataset.
- **Issues:** Single infrared channel and western Pacific basin only; best track labels contain agency-dependent uncertainties.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [CRA5: Extreme Compression of ERA5 for Portable Global Climate and Weather Research via an Efficient Variational Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03376)
Han et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 39 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces the storage and transmission cost of reanalysis data so AI weather research is accessible to resource-limited researchers.
- **Architecture:** Neural codec VAEformer: a low-complexity variational autoencoder transformer producing a quantized Gaussian latent for entropy coding.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis (226 TB) compressed to the CRA5 dataset (0.7 TB); downstream training of global weather forecasting models on CRA5.
- **Main result:** Compression ratio above 300 while outperforming prior compression methods; forecasting models trained on CRA5 match accuracy of models trained on original ERA5.
- **Open work:** Compressing other variables and datasets, and assessing impact on extremes and fine-scale analyses.
- **Issues:** Lossy compression may degrade extremes or small-scale features; utility shown mainly through forecasting accuracy rather than all scientific uses.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [SubseasonalClimateUSA: A Dataset for Subseasonal Forecasting and Benchmarking](https://doi.org/10.52202/075280-0349)
Mouatadid et al. (2021), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 34 citations.

- **Main goal:** Streamlines data curation for subseasonal (2-6 week) forecasting in the US, where dynamical models have limited skill.
- **Architecture:** Curated dataset and benchmark comparing operational dynamical models, classical baselines and ten ML/deep learning methods.
- **Data:** Multi-source US subseasonal data (temperature, precipitation, climate indices and dynamical forecasts) at regular grid, accessible via a Python package.
- **Main result:** Benchmarks suggest simple, effective ways (e.g. learned corrections and ensembling) to improve on operational models.
- **Open work:** Regular updates, expansion to more targets and regions, and testing new deep learning methods on the benchmark.
- **Issues:** US-only domain; subseasonal skill is low overall so differences between methods may be small and period-dependent.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [WeatherBench Probability: A benchmark dataset for probabilistic medium-range weather forecasting along with deep learning baseline models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00865)
Garg et al. (2022), *arXiv*. 32 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extend WeatherBench to probabilistic medium-range forecasting so that ML uncertainty estimates can be compared with standard metrics and an operational ensemble.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark dataset with probabilistic metrics plus deep learning baselines (ResNet-type convolutional neural networks) using Monte Carlo dropout, parametric and categorical predictions.
- **Data:** WeatherBench ERA5 reanalysis at coarse resolution; ECMWF IFS ensemble forecasts as operational baseline; CRPS, spread-skill ratio and rank histograms.
- **Main result:** Monte Carlo dropout severely underestimates uncertainty; parametric and categorical models are fairly reliable and similar, but none match the skill of the IFS ensemble.
- **Open work:** Develop stronger probabilistic ML methods, such as generative ensembles, and evaluate them with the benchmark.
- **Issues:** Coarse resolution and limited variables; baselines are simple, and per-gridpoint distributions do not provide spatially coherent ensemble members.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [ClimART: A Benchmark Dataset for Emulating Atmospheric Radiative Transfer in Weather and Climate Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14671)
Cachay et al. (2021), *NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks*. 32 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provide a standard benchmark for ML emulation of atmospheric radiative transfer, which is expensive in weather and climate models and hard to compare across prior studies.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark dataset, ClimART, with baselines including MLP, convolutional neural networks and graph neural networks for emulating radiative fluxes and heating rates.
- **Data:** More than 10 million samples from present, pre-industrial and future climate conditions based on the Canadian Earth System Model radiation code, with multiple out-of-distribution test sets.
- **Main result:** Baselines reveal shortcomings of datasets and architectures used in prior work and highlight trade-offs between accuracy and inference speed.
- **Open work:** Develop emulators that generalize out of distribution, respect physical constraints, and remain stable when coupled online.
- **Issues:** Offline benchmark only; emulators are not evaluated when coupled in a climate model, and data come from a single model's radiation scheme.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [RainBench: Towards Data-Driven Global Precipitation Forecasting from Satellite Imagery](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i17.17749)
Witt et al. (2021), *AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence*. 26 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a benchmark dataset for data-driven global precipitation forecasting, aimed at extreme precipitation in the developing world.
- **Architecture:** Multimodal benchmark dataset plus PyRain, a data-processing library, with baseline neural network models for medium-range precipitation forecasting.
- **Data:** Simulated satellite data (SimSat), selected ERA5 reanalysis variables and IMERG precipitation.
- **Main result:** Releases the dataset and library and reports baseline results for two medium-range forecasting tasks; the abstract does not give quantitative skill.
- **Open work:** Use real satellite observations and probabilistic models, and improve skill for extremes.
- **Issues:** Uses simulated rather than real satellite imagery. Baselines are coarse, and skill relative to NWP is not established in the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [ENS-10: A Dataset For Post-Processing Ensemble Weather Forecast](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.14786)
Ashkboos et al. (2022), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 25 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a dataset for ML post-processing of ensemble weather forecasts, which otherwise requires costly simulations to obtain.
- **Architecture:** Dataset and benchmark task (48 h prediction correction) with baseline post-processing models, including extreme event evaluation.
- **Data:** Ten ECMWF ensemble members (reforecasts), 1998-2017, 11 pressure levels plus surface at 0.5 degree, lead times 0, 24, 48 h, twice weekly.
- **Main result:** Baselines improve 48 h forecasts of three key variables and are evaluated for extreme events.
- **Open work:** More members, lead times and variables, and stronger architectures for ensemble post-processing.
- **Issues:** Only 10 members and twice-weekly initializations; limited lead times; targets are ERA5 rather than observations.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Probabilistic measures afford fair comparisons of AIWP and NWP model output](https://doi.org/10.1175/aies-d-25-0054.1)
Gneiting et al. (2025), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 14 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a fair way to compare single-valued output from AI and physics-based weather models, since pre-specified loss functions can favour some competitors.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML statistical method: potential continuous ranked probability score (PCRPS), computed by post-processing deterministic forecasts with isotonic distributional regression and taking the mean CRPS.
- **Data:** WeatherBench 2 forecasts including GraphCast, ECMWF HRES, GenCast and the operational ECMWF ensemble.
- **Main result:** GraphCast outperforms ECMWF HRES under PCRPS; PCRPS for HRES and GenCast aligns very well with the mean CRPS of the ECMWF ensemble and GenCast ensemble.
- **Open work:** Use PCRPS in benchmarks and other application domains where loss functions are not pre-specified.
- **Issues:** Measures potential rather than realized skill and is invariant to monotone transformations, so it ignores calibration and bias of raw output; requires enough training data for the post-processing.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A Benchmark Dataset for Tornado Detection and Prediction using Full-Resolution Polarimetric Weather Radar Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16437)
Veillette et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 14 citations.

- **Main goal:** Supports development of ML tornado detection and prediction from radar, where rare events make training dataset design critical.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark dataset (TorNet) with ML baselines, including a deep learning convolutional neural network that processes raw polarimetric radar imagery, plus non-DL and operational baselines.
- **Data:** Full-resolution polarimetric Level-II WSR-88D (NEXRAD) radar data sampled from 9 years of reported storm events.
- **Main result:** The DL baseline, without manual feature engineering, shows higher detection performance than non-DL and operational baselines; dataset, code and weights are released.
- **Open work:** Use TorNet for tornado prediction (lead time) and improved architectures, and examine robustness for operational acceptance.
- **Issues:** Labels depend on storm reports, which are incomplete and biased; tornadoes remain rare, and detection skill is still limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Accelerating Community-Wide Evaluation of AI Models for Global Weather Prediction by Facilitating Access to Model Output](https://doi.org/10.1175/bams-d-24-0057.1)
Radford et al. (2024), *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society*. 13 citations.

- **Main goal:** Facilitates community evaluation of AI weather prediction models by providing open access to their outputs.
- **Architecture:** Dataset and visualization resource: reforecast archive and real-time web display of FourCastNet v2-small, Pangu-Weather and GraphCast Operational alongside GFS and IFS.
- **Data:** Twice-daily 10-day reforecasts since September 2020 initialized from GFS and IFS initial conditions, hosted on Amazon S3 via NOAA's Open Data Dissemination program.
- **Main result:** Delivers a growing three-year reforecast archive and a real-time comparison web page (aiweather.cira.colostate.edu).
- **Open work:** Use the archive for feature-based verification of impactful phenomena and assess whether AIWP models belong in operations.
- **Issues:** Resource paper without verification results; limited to three models.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [AIMIP Phase 1: systematic evaluations of AI weather and climate models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06944)
Henn et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 12 citations.

- **Main goal:** Establishes an intercomparison project for AI weather and climate models to identify how frameworks and architectures affect behaviour and to build trust through open data and evaluation.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark and intercomparison protocol (AIMIP Phase 1) specifying a common AMIP-style experiment, output format and training constraints; participating models span several AI architectures.
- **Data:** Models trained on historical reanalysis and forced with observed sea surface temperatures over 1979–2024; compared with a conventional physics-based atmosphere model; dataset publicly released.
- **Main result:** AI models simulate historical climate and response to forcing as well as a physics-based model, but some underestimate historical warming trends and predictions diverge in out-of-sample generalization tests.
- **Open work:** Later phases with more demanding forcing scenarios and further community evaluations of the released Phase 1 dataset.
- **Issues:** Training on reanalysis restricts experiments to the historical period; out-of-sample warming tests reveal divergent and potentially unreliable extrapolation.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Extreme Weather Bench: A framework and benchmark for evaluation of high-impact weather](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01126)
McGovern et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a standardized way to verify AI and NWP weather models on high-impact hazards rather than only global-mean scores or hand-picked cases.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark framework and open-source code (Extreme Weather Bench) containing curated case studies, observational data and impact-based metrics; not a forecast model.
- **Data:** Standard set of high-impact event case studies spanning multiple spatial and temporal scales and hazard types, with associated observational datasets; specific products not listed in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Introduces EWB as a community-driven benchmark enabling like-for-like comparisons across AI and NWP models on specific high-impact phenomena.
- **Open work:** Add more phenomena, test cases and metrics together with the forecast verification community.
- **Issues:** Case-study-based evaluation has limited sample sizes per hazard; results depend on chosen cases, observations and metrics; no benchmark results are reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Can AI Weather Models Predict Beyond Two Weeks? A Quantitative Benchmark and Analysis of Long Rollouts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30184)
Lehmann et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Characterizes why AI weather models become unstable when rolled out beyond two weeks and establishes a taxonomy of failure modes.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark and analysis of nine state-of-the-art AI weather models in year-long rollouts, with ablations on Vision Transformer (ViT) architectural design choices.
- **Data:** Year-long autoregressive rollouts of pretrained AI weather models; training and verification data presumably ERA5 reanalysis, not specified in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Failures fall into blow-up, drift and loss of seasonality; stable models damp high-frequency energy and act as denoisers yet still produce distinct trajectories conditioned on initial state.
- **Open work:** Use the taxonomy and spectral diagnostics to design architectures that remain stable for subseasonal to climate time scales.
- **Issues:** Ablations limited to ViT-style architectures; seasonality and drift diagnostics do not establish climate fidelity; models lack ocean coupling or forcing changes.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Machine Learning: Defining Worldwide Cyclone Labels for Training](https://doi.org/10.23919/icif.2018.8455276)
Bonfanti et al. (2018), *Fusion*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Creates a worldwide labeled dataset of tropical and extratropical cyclones to train deep learning detection networks.
- **Architecture:** Rule-based heuristic labeling using time, pressure, vorticity and gradient thresholds without terrain cut-off; not an ML model itself, the labels are intended for deep learning training.
- **Data:** Gridded meteorological fields for labeling, applied to GOES-15 water vapor imagery to build the training dataset.
- **Main result:** Outputs cyclone centers and regions of interest per time stamp as a global labeled dataset for deep learning applications.
- **Open work:** Training and evaluating deep learning cyclone detectors on the labeled imagery.
- **Issues:** Labels depend on hand-tuned thresholds; no validation against best-track or expert-labeled datasets reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [PhysMetrics.Weather: An Evaluation Framework for Physical Consistency in ML Weather Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10642)
Kasteleyn et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a way to assess physical consistency of ML weather prediction models beyond pixel-wise error metrics such as RMSE.
- **Architecture:** Evaluation framework (PhysMetrics.Weather) with conservation, spectral and dynamical metrics; open-source code, not a forecast model.
- **Data:** Applied to MLWP model forecasts; specific models and datasets not listed in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Introduces a tool quantifying physical realism of MLWP forecasts to guide physics-informed architecture development and operational reliability assessment.
- **Open work:** Extend metrics and apply systematically across MLWP models to inform physics-informed design.
- **Issues:** Abstract reports no quantitative findings; physical metrics depend on reference datasets and diagnostic choices.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [WP-MIP: An Artificial Intelligence, Hybrid, and Physically Based Model Intercomparison Project for Weather Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1175/bams-d-26-0012.1)
McTaggart-Cowan et al. (2026), *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society*. 4 citations.

- **Main goal:** Establish a systematic intercomparison of AI, hybrid and physics-based weather prediction models to assess physical consistency and skill across all forecast fields and conditions.
- **Architecture:** Model intercomparison project (WP-MIP) supported by the WMO: a centralized database of physically based, machine-learning and hybrid global deterministic forecasts; not a new ML model.
- **Data:** Global deterministic forecasts contributed by institutions on six continents, using center-specific and common initializations.
- **Main result:** Describes the project design; aims to develop AI-ready verification techniques and best-practice guidance for model developers and national weather centres.
- **Open work:** Extending to ensemble and other forecast types and publishing results of the distributed evaluation.
- **Issues:** Project overview without results yet; first phase limited to deterministic global forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [CORDEX-ML-Bench: A Benchmark for Data-Driven Regional Climate Downscaling -Experiment Design and Overview](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29172)
Rampal et al. (2026), *arXiv*. 4 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provide standardised training and evaluation protocols for ML regional climate downscaling across multiple domains, enabling intercomparison and operational readiness under CMIP7.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark (CORDEX-ML-Bench) with perfect-model design evaluating 40 ML configurations: traditional ML, convolutional U-Nets, vision transformers, graph neural networks, diffusion, flow matching and generative adversarial networks.
- **Data:** CORDEX-aligned regional climate model simulations driven by GCMs, downscaling daily maximum temperature and precipitation to about 10 km (20x) over the European Alps, New Zealand and Southern Africa; historical and future periods.
- **Main result:** Generative models outperform deterministic ones for precipitation, especially fine-scale variability and extremes; for temperature deterministic models remain competitive. Historically trained models underestimate future climate-change signals.
- **Open work:** Further benchmark phases with more regions, variables and rigorous extrapolation testing to support operational use.
- **Issues:** Perfect-model framework does not test transfer to real observations; only two variables and three pilot regions.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [NNJA—a curated archive of Earth system observations from 1970s to present for reanalysis and data-driven model development](https://doi.org/10.1175/bams-d-25-0157.1)
Frolov et al. (2026), *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society*. 0 citations.

- **Main goal:** Creates a curated, publicly accessible archive of historical Earth system observations to support reanalysis production and AI model development.
- **Architecture:** Dataset paper describing NNJA (NOAA-NASA Joint Archive) and its ML-ready companion NNJA-AI in Apache Parquet format, with a three-tier verification process.
- **Data:** Satellite radiances, conventional atmospheric observations, in-situ ocean profiles, sea ice concentration and freeboard and land observations from over 60 sensors, 1979 to near-real time, distributed on AWS.
- **Main result:** Atmospheric records grow from about 10^6 per day in 1979 to about 10^8 today; data are verified and come with channel-level quality lists compatible with data assimilation systems.
- **Open work:** Supporting next-generation U.S. reanalyses and end-to-end AI forecasting from observations.
- **Issues:** Authors document known limitations in coverage and quality; historical satellite records are inhomogeneous over time.
- *Basis: abstract*

<a id="methods"></a>
## Core ML methods

### [Physics-informed neural networks: A deep learning framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving nonlinear partial differential equations](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcp.2018.10.045)
Raissi et al. (2019), *Journal of Computational Physics*. 21,648 citations.

- **Main goal:** Solve forward and inverse problems for nonlinear PDEs using neural networks that respect physical laws.
- **Architecture:** Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs): networks trained with PDE residuals via automatic differentiation in continuous-time and discrete-time (implicit Runge-Kutta) forms.
- **Data:** Classical benchmark problems: Burgers, Schrodinger, Allen-Cahn, Navier-Stokes, Korteweg-de Vries and shallow-water waves.
- **Main result:** Accurate data-efficient solutions and identification of PDE parameters from sparse data across the benchmarks.
- **Open work:** Scaling to high-dimensional, multiscale and chaotic problems; training robustness.
- **Issues:** Training can be difficult for stiff or multiscale problems; computational cost versus classical solvers; geophysical applications not demonstrated here.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.08895)
Li et al. (2020), *International Conference on Learning Representations*. 5,244 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learn solution operators of parametric PDEs (mappings between function spaces) so a whole family of PDE instances can be solved quickly, instead of one instance at a time.
- **Architecture:** Fourier Neural Operator: stacked layers that parameterize the integral kernel in Fourier space (FFT, learned weights on truncated low modes, inverse FFT) plus a pointwise linear path and nonlinearity.
- **Data:** Numerically generated solutions of 1D Burgers' equation, 2D Darcy flow and 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes (vorticity form, including turbulent regime) at varying resolutions.
- **Main result:** State-of-the-art accuracy among neural PDE surrogates on all benchmarks and up to three orders of magnitude faster than traditional solvers; discretization-invariant, enabling zero-shot super-resolution.
- **Open work:** Extending to irregular geometries, non-periodic boundaries and real geophysical systems; long autoregressive rollouts; it became the basis of FourCastNet-style weather emulators.
- **Issues:** Truncated Fourier modes limit representation of fine-scale features; FFT assumes regular periodic grids; tested on idealized PDE data with a single fixed setting, not on observations.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Machine Learning for Fluid Mechanics](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-fluid-010719-060214)
Brunton et al. (2019), *Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics*. 3,057 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews how machine learning can extract knowledge from large fluid-mechanics datasets and support modelling, optimization and control of flows.
- **Architecture:** Review of ML methods for fluid mechanics, spanning supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning, including neural networks, dimensionality reduction and data-driven modelling of flows.
- **Data:** No new data; draws on experimental, field and large-scale simulation data used in the reviewed fluid-mechanics studies.
- **Main result:** Argues that ML offers a powerful information-processing framework that can augment and possibly transform fluid-mechanics research and industrial applications.
- **Open work:** Identifies emerging opportunities in combining domain knowledge with ML for understanding, modelling and controlling flows.
- **Issues:** Broad review not specific to geophysical flows; discusses strengths and limitations qualitatively rather than benchmarking methods.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Data-driven discovery of partial differential equations](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.1602614)
Rudy et al. (2016), *Science Advances*. 1,827 citations.

- **Main goal:** Discovers the governing partial differential equations of spatiotemporal systems directly from measurement data, where first-principles derivations are intractable.
- **Architecture:** Sparse regression (PDE-FIND) over a library of candidate nonlinear and partial derivative terms, with Pareto analysis to select parsimonious models; not a neural network.
- **Data:** Simulated time series from canonical systems including Navier-Stokes, the quantum harmonic oscillator, diffusion, Burgers and Korteweg-de Vries equations, in Eulerian and Lagrangian frames.
- **Main result:** Correctly recovers the governing equations of a range of canonical PDEs and can disambiguate non-unique dynamics, such as distinguishing linear wave from Korteweg-de Vries, using multiple initial conditions.
- **Open work:** Extension to parameterized systems, noisy real-world measurements and systems where the candidate library is unknown.
- **Issues:** Relies on accurate numerical derivatives, so it is sensitive to noise; requires the true terms to be present in the candidate library.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Deep learning for universal linear embeddings of nonlinear dynamics](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-07210-0)
Lusch et al. (2017), *Nature Communications*. 1,822 citations.

- **Main goal:** Finds coordinate transformations that make strongly nonlinear dynamics approximately linear, enabling prediction and control with linear theory via Koopman eigenfunctions.
- **Architecture:** Modified autoencoder neural network that learns Koopman eigenfunctions, with an auxiliary network parameterizing continuous eigenvalue frequencies.
- **Data:** Simulated low-dimensional dynamical systems; specific test systems are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Learns parsimonious, interpretable embeddings on which dynamics are globally linear, including systems with continuous spectra.
- **Open work:** Scaling the approach to high-dimensional systems and using the embeddings for estimation and control.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated on low-dimensional toy systems; not tested on realistic geophysical flows.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Neural Operator: Learning Maps Between Function Spaces With Applications to PDEs
Kovachki et al. (2023), *Journal of machine learning research*. 1,737 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generalizes neural networks to learn operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces, providing fast surrogates for PDE solution operators.
- **Architecture:** Neural operator framework built from linear integral operators and nonlinear activations, with graph neural operator, multipole, low-rank and Fourier neural operator (FNO) parameterizations.
- **Data:** Synthetic PDE datasets including Burgers, Darcy flow and Navier-Stokes equations.
- **Main result:** Proves universal approximation and discretization invariance, and shows neural operators outperform prior ML baselines while being orders of magnitude faster than conventional solvers.
- **Open work:** Applying neural operators to larger, more complex physical systems such as weather and climate, and improving data efficiency.
- **Issues:** Abstract not available; card relies on knowledge of the paper and its 2021 arXiv version. Benchmarks are idealized PDEs.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Learning to Simulate Complex Physics with Graph Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09405)
Sanchez-Gonzalez et al. (2020), *International Conference on Machine Learning*. 1,723 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a general learned simulator for complex particle-based physics (fluids, rigid and deformable materials).
- **Architecture:** Graph Network-based Simulators (GNS): particles as graph nodes, encoder-processor-decoder with learned message passing, trained on single-step predictions with input noise injection.
- **Data:** Particle-based simulations of fluids (water, sand, goop), rigid solids and deformable materials from various physics solvers.
- **Main result:** Generalizes from single-step training with thousands of particles to thousands of rollout steps, new initial conditions and at least 10x more particles; long-term accuracy depends mainly on the number of message-passing steps and noise injection.
- **Open work:** Apply to inverse problems and larger-scale scientific simulations.
- **Issues:** Not an atmospheric study; Lagrangian particle setting differs from gridded geophysical models, and no physical conservation is enforced.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.03409)
Pfaff et al. (2020), *International Conference on Learning Representations*. 1,544 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learns fast surrogate simulators for mesh-based physical simulations, which are costly and require per-system tuning.
- **Architecture:** MeshGraphNets: graph neural network encoder-processor-decoder that passes messages on the simulation mesh (mesh-space and world-space edges) and learns to adapt mesh resolution during rollout.
- **Data:** Simulated trajectories from conventional solvers for aerodynamics (incompressible and compressible flow), structural mechanics and cloth.
- **Main result:** Accurately predicts dynamics across domains, generalizes to larger and more complex state spaces at test time, and runs 1-2 orders of magnitude faster than the source simulator.
- **Open work:** Extension to larger 3D systems and longer horizons; the GNN-on-mesh design later underpins global weather models such as GraphCast.
- **Issues:** Not an atmospheric application; trained on the simulator it emulates, so accuracy is bounded by it, and long rollouts can still accumulate error.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Machine learning–accelerated computational fluid dynamics](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2101784118)
Kochkov et al. (2021), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences*. 1,351 citations.

- **Main goal:** Accelerates fluid simulations without losing accuracy by embedding ML inside traditional numerical solvers rather than replacing them.
- **Architecture:** End-to-end trained, differentiable CFD solver (JAX) with learned interpolation and learned correction components inside a finite-volume scheme.
- **Data:** Two-dimensional turbulent flows (for example forced Kolmogorov flow) from high-resolution direct numerical simulation and large-eddy simulation.
- **Main result:** Matches baseline solvers at 8 to 10x finer resolution in each dimension, giving 40 to 80x speedups. Stays stable over long runs and generalizes to new forcings and Reynolds numbers.
- **Open work:** Extend to 3D flows, more complex geometries, and atmospheric or climate models.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated only on 2D idealized turbulence. Requires differentiable solvers and gains may shrink for 3D or multi-physics flows.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Model-Free Prediction of Large Spatiotemporally Chaotic Systems from Data: A Reservoir Computing Approach.](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevlett.120.024102)
Pathak et al. (2018), *Physical Review Letters*. 1,256 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts large spatiotemporally chaotic systems from data alone, without a physical model.
- **Architecture:** Parallel reservoir computing: many local reservoirs, each predicting a spatial patch with overlapping neighbor inputs.
- **Data:** Simulated data from the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation on large domains.
- **Main result:** The parallel scheme predicts the state for several Lyapunov times and reproduces long-term statistics, scaling to large systems.
- **Open work:** Application to weather and other real, partially observed spatiotemporal systems.
- **Issues:** Idealized 1D system with full noise-free observations. Abstract unavailable.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Learning Partial Differential Equations](https://doi.org/10.1145/3648506)
Li et al. (2021), *ACM / IMS Journal of Data Science*. 1,023 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learns solution operators of parametric PDE families while overcoming both the optimization difficulty of PINNs and the data demands of purely data-driven neural operators.
- **Architecture:** Physics-informed neural operator (PINO): Fourier neural operator (FNO) trained with coarse-resolution data plus PDE residual constraints at higher resolution, with instance-wise fine-tuning using physics only.
- **Data:** Synthetic PDE problems including Burgers, Darcy flow, Navier-Stokes and Kolmogorov flows.
- **Main result:** Accurately approximates solution operators with no degradation under zero-shot super-resolution, needs few or no data, and solves long transient and Kolmogorov flows where PINN and other baselines fail.
- **Open work:** Authors point to applications such as weather forecasting, airfoil design and turbulence control.
- **Issues:** Tested on idealized PDE benchmarks only; requires known governing equations to impose constraints.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Universal Differential Equations for Scientific Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-55125/v1)
Rackauckas et al. (2020), *arXiv*. 902 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reconciles mechanistic scientific models with data without requiring big data, by embedding learnable components into differential equations.
- **Architecture:** Universal differential equations (UDEs): differential equation models augmented with neural networks or other universal approximators, trained with open-source differentiable solver software (Julia SciML).
- **Data:** Diverse examples including biological systems, physics-informed neural network training and large-eddy simulation closures; specific datasets not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** UDEs discover unknown governing equations, extrapolate beyond training data and accelerate simulations in a time- and data-efficient manner.
- **Open work:** Applying UDEs to more complex scientific models, including climate and fluid closures.
- **Issues:** Mostly demonstration examples; performance on large, noisy real-world systems is not established.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Using machine learning to replicate chaotic attractors and calculate Lyapunov exponents from data.](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5010300)
Pathak et al. (2017), *Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science*. 700 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates Lyapunov exponents and reproduces the long-term climate of chaotic systems from data without a model.
- **Architecture:** Reservoir computing (echo-state recurrent network) with linear regression for output weights, run autonomously to reproduce the attractor.
- **Data:** Simulated time series from the Lorenz system and the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation.
- **Main result:** The autonomous reservoir reproduces the attractor's climate and gives accurate Lyapunov exponent estimates, including for the high-dimensional KS system.
- **Open work:** Applying to higher-dimensional and real-world systems such as weather and climate.
- **Issues:** Idealized low-dimensional or 1D systems with clean data; success is not guaranteed for every training run.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Neural Operator: Learning Maps Between Function Spaces](https://doi.org/10.5555/3648699.3648788)
Kovachki et al. (2021), *arXiv*. 698 citations.

- **Main goal:** Generalizes neural networks to learn operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces, providing fast surrogates for PDE solution operators.
- **Architecture:** Neural operator: composition of linear integral operators and nonlinear activations, with graph neural operator, multipole graph, low-rank and Fourier neural operator (FNO) parameterizations.
- **Data:** Synthetic PDE data for Burgers, Darcy subsurface flow and Navier-Stokes equations.
- **Main result:** Proves universal approximation and discretization invariance; outperforms prior ML methods and is orders of magnitude faster than conventional PDE solvers.
- **Open work:** Scaling to complex real-world systems and improving data efficiency.
- **Issues:** Evaluated on idealized PDE benchmarks; needs solver-generated training data.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Physics-guided Neural Networks (PGNN): An Application in Lake Temperature Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.11431)
Daw et al. (2017), *arXiv*. 689 citations.

- **Main goal:** Combines physics-based models with neural networks to improve generalization and physical consistency of lake temperature predictions.
- **Architecture:** Physics-guided neural network (PGNN): a feedforward neural network taking physics-based model outputs plus observational features, trained with a loss penalizing violations of the temperature-density-depth relationship.
- **Data:** Lake temperature observations and physics-based lake model (GLM) simulations; specific lakes not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** PGNN gives lower errors and physically consistent predictions with better generalizability than pure data-driven or physics-based models.
- **Open work:** Extending physics-guided learning to other physical constraints and environmental systems.
- **Issues:** Physics constraint covers only density-depth monotonicity; tested on limited lakes.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Learning data-driven discretizations for partial differential equations](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1814058116)
Bar-Sinai et al. (2018), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences*. 648 citations.

- **Main goal:** Learns accurate coarse-grid discretizations of PDEs so that solutions remain accurate at much lower resolution.
- **Architecture:** Neural networks that estimate spatial derivative coefficients, trained end to end within the numerical solver.
- **Data:** High-resolution solutions of 1D nonlinear PDEs (Burgers, Korteweg-de Vries, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky) coarse-grained for training.
- **Main result:** Learned discretizations allow time integration at 4x to 8x coarser resolution than standard finite-difference methods.
- **Open work:** Extending to 2D/3D problems and atmospheric or oceanic flows.
- **Issues:** Only 1D model equations; generalization to new regimes and higher dimensions not shown.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### Multicategory Support Vector Machines , Theory , and Application to the Classification of Microarray Data and Satellite Radiance Data
Lee (2004), *Venue not recorded*. 605 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops multicategory support vector machines and applies them to classification problems including satellite radiance data.
- **Architecture:** Multicategory support vector machine (SVM) theory and algorithms, with tuning methods.
- **Data:** Microarray gene expression data and satellite radiance data (MODIS) for cloud classification.
- **Main result:** The multicategory SVM performs well and handles multiple classes in a single framework.
- **Open work:** Feature selection and extensions to nonstandard settings.
- **Issues:** Thesis-style preprint; atmospheric results limited to one cloud classification application.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Data-driven forecasting of high-dimensional chaotic systems with long short-term memory networks](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.2017.0844)
Vlachas et al. (2018), *Proceedings of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences*. 587 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts high-dimensional chaotic systems in a reduced-order space using data alone.
- **Architecture:** LSTM networks in reduced-order space, and a hybrid mean stochastic model plus LSTM (MSM-LSTM) to ensure convergence to the invariant measure.
- **Data:** Time series from Lorenz 96, the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation and a prototype barotropic climate model.
- **Main result:** LSTMs outperform Gaussian processes in short-term accuracy in all cases; the hybrid improves long-term statistical behaviour.
- **Open work:** Scaling to more realistic, higher-dimensional systems and quantifying forecast uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Toy systems; reduced-order truncation; long-term forecasts can drift without the hybrid stochastic component.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Backpropagation algorithms and Reservoir Computing in Recurrent Neural Networks for the forecasting of complex spatiotemporal dynamics](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2020.02.016)
Vlachas et al. (2019), *Neural Networks*. 535 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares training strategies for recurrent neural networks forecasting high-dimensional chaotic spatiotemporal dynamics, including reduced-order settings.
- **Architecture:** Recurrent neural networks: reservoir computing (echo state networks) versus gated RNNs (LSTM, GRU) trained with backpropagation through time, with parallel implementations.
- **Data:** Simulated Lorenz-96 and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky systems, using full-state and reduced-order observations.
- **Main result:** With full-state data, reservoir computing beats BPTT in accuracy and long-term statistics at much lower training cost; with reduced-order data, BPTT RNNs are more stable and accurate. Lyapunov spectrum of KS is recovered with BPTT.
- **Open work:** Scaling to real, partially observed geophysical systems and improving the stability of large reservoirs are natural next steps.
- **Issues:** Idealized chaotic test systems only; large reservoir models can diverge on reduced-order data.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Towards Physics-informed Deep Learning for Turbulent Flow Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1145/3394486.3403198)
Wang et al. (2019), *Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining*. 462 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts turbulent flow dynamics with deep learning while incorporating physical principles, relevant to turbulence and climate modelling.
- **Architecture:** Turbulent-Flow Net: trainable spectral filters inspired by a coupled RANS–LES decomposition, followed by a specialized U-Net for prediction.
- **Data:** Velocity fields from large-scale turbulent fluid flow simulations (two-dimensional Rayleigh–Bénard convection).
- **Main result:** Significantly lower error than state-of-the-art baselines for predictions 60 frames ahead, with better mass conservation and turbulent kinetic energy spectra.
- **Open work:** Extending to 3D turbulence, longer horizons and hard physical constraints.
- **Issues:** Trained and tested on a single simulated flow configuration; conservation is encouraged rather than guaranteed.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### Integrating Physics-Based Modeling with Machine Learning: A Survey
Willard et al. (2020), *Venue not recorded*. 452 citations.

- **Main goal:** Surveys methods that integrate physics-based modelling with machine learning to improve accuracy, consistency and data efficiency in scientific applications.
- **Architecture:** Review/survey organized by objective (e.g. surrogates, downscaling, parameterization, inverse modelling) and by method (physics-guided loss, initialization, architecture design, residual and hybrid models).
- **Data:** Covers studies across environmental and engineering sciences, including hydrology, climate and fluid dynamics; no new data.
- **Main result:** Provides a taxonomy of physics–ML integration strategies and catalogs applications for each.
- **Open work:** Open questions include uncertainty quantification, generalization, and principled combination of multiple integration strategies.
- **Issues:** Survey without quantitative comparison; abstract unavailable in the metadata.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators: Efficient Token Mixers for Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13587)
Guibas et al. (2021), *arXiv*. 430 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides an efficient token mixer for vision transformers on high-resolution inputs, where self-attention scales quadratically.
- **Architecture:** Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNO): token mixing as a global convolution in the Fourier domain with block-diagonal channel mixing, adaptive weight sharing and soft-thresholded frequency modes.
- **Data:** Computer vision benchmarks such as few-shot segmentation and Cityscapes segmentation.
- **Main result:** Quasi-linear complexity and linear memory; outperforms other efficient attention mechanisms, handling sequences of 65k tokens.
- **Open work:** Applications to scientific data; AFNO became the backbone of FourCastNet for global weather forecasting.
- **Issues:** Evaluated only on vision tasks here; FFT-based mixing assumes periodic, regular grids, which is awkward for the sphere.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Attractor reconstruction by machine learning.](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5039508)
Lu et al. (2018), *Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science*. 417 citations.

- **Main goal:** Explains when reservoir computing can learn a model of a chaotic system that both forecasts short term and reproduces its long-term ergodic behaviour.
